key_components: skill-conditioned multi-teacher pool
outcome-validated teacher polarity
robust support estimation (masking/clipping/thresholding)
bounded gated distillation objective
online skill bank update

2605.28791.novelty: Formulates skill-based self-distillation as teacher hypothesis validation rather than unconditional imitation, using verifier outcomes to determine polarity of skill-conditioned teachers and a bounded gated loss to suppress extreme/uninformative signals

on_policy_mechanism.evidence_quote: The student is the plain-prompt policy p_S(· | x) = π_θ(· | x), which samples y ∼ p_S(· | x). After generation, an answer verifier gives a scalar outcome r ∈ {−1, 1}.

opd_classification.reasoning: Core contribution is a self-distillation method where privileged information (skill bank) conditions the teacher, with verifier outcomes validating teacher polarity—PI-based on-policy self-distillation with environment feedback.

key_findings: On Qwen3-1.7B, SGSD improves the average score across AIME24, AIME25, and HMMT25 from 37.4% to 43.7%, outperforming GRPO by 6.2% and OPSD by 1.7%.
Skill injection alone is not sufficient; Base+Skill can underperform the plain base model.
Removing teacher polarity yields short-term gain but eventual collapse.
Full-vocabulary distillation consistently outperforms Top-100 support distillation.
SGSD shows more stable training dynamics than OPSD, which degrades after mid-training.
2605.28791.ablations_summary: Token masking, clipping, and thresholding each improve stability; removing all three causes performance below base at step 100. Polarity is essential to prevent late-stage collapse. Multi-teacher pool outperforms single teacher. Gated loss outperforms forward KL, JSD, and matches/beats reverse KL. Live synchronized teacher outperforms frozen/periodic/EMA teachers.
limitations: Evaluated mainly on mathematical reasoning with automatic answer verification; extensions to open-ended generation may require a calibrated judge.
Simple cold-start construction and rank-wise pairing; more adaptive retrieval/pairing strategies may improve the teacher pool.
Reports best checkpoint among recorded steps rather than held-out model selection.
Most ablations conducted only on Qwen3-1.7B to control computational cost.
failure_modes: Adding answer PI to SGSD causes large performance drop and collapse on both AIME24 and AIME25.
SGSD underperforms OPSD on Qwen3-8B, suggesting weaker PI assumption may not fully close the gap at larger scale.
Skill injection without polarity gating introduces misleading supervision leading to collapse.

theory.theoretical_claim: Gated loss gradient is sign-consistent, bounded by 1/sqrt(e*tau_g), locally approximates reverse-KL up to constant scale 1/(2*tau_g), and exponentially damps extreme gaps
theory.proof_sketch: Derivative g_tau(Delta) = Delta / (tau_g * (1 + exp(Delta^2/(2*tau_g)))) is shown to have matching sign, bounded magnitude, linear local behavior matching reverse-KL second-order expansion, and exponential decay for |Delta|->infinity

2605.28791.relevance_to_opd: Directly proposes an on-policy self-distillation method where the student generates rollouts, skill-conditioned self-teachers provide dense token-level logit supervision, and verifier outcomes validate teacher polarity—a novel OPD framework with environment-gated PI.

2606.00147.title: RAFT: Data Refinement and Adaptive Distillation for Domain Fine-Tuning with Alleviated Forgetting
2606.00147.summary: Two-stage framework coupling data refinement with on-policy distillation to mitigate forgetting in domain SFT

method.training_loop: Stage1: self-rewrite+filter+fuse answers offline. Stage2: student generates trajectories, teacher (original model conditioned on fused answer) provides soft targets, optimize L_SFT + EMA-weighted L_KL
method.loss_formulation: L = L_SFT + λ(s) * L_KL, where λ(s) = mhat_SFT / (mhat_KL + ε), L_KL = (T^2/N) Σ KL(q̃ ∥ p̃)
method.data_source: Domain QA pairs extracted from CCL4.0 and Common Corpus, ~2000 per domain across 5 domains
key_components: self-conditioned rewriting
cosine similarity semantic filtering
multi-expert fusion
answer-conditioned on-policy distillation
top-K temperature distillation
EMA-based adaptive loss balancing

2606.00147.novelty: Combines offline data refinement (self-rewrite + filter + fuse) with answer-conditioned on-policy distillation where teacher is conditioned on fused answer for informed guidance, plus EMA-based adaptive balancing; prior methods address only data or training constraints alone

on_policy_mechanism.evidence_quote: At each training step, the model first generates trajectories via autoregressive sampling. The original instruction-tuned model (teacher) then provides soft supervision through Answer-Conditioned On-Policy Distillation

opd_classification.reasoning: The core contribution is an adaptive on-policy distillation objective with answer-conditioned teacher and EMA-based adaptive weighting, making it primarily about adaptive divergence/loss formulation for on-policy distillation.

training_setup.compute_budget: ~1000 GPU-hours (A100), total including preliminary trials ≤2000 hours

key_findings: RAFT improves average domain accuracy by 23.2% over standard SFT across 3 models and 5 domains
RAFT recovers 18.2% relative improvement on MS-Bench and 10.2% on IFEval compared to SFT
RAFT improves average MS-Bench retention from 76.8% to 89.2% and IFEval retention from 91.2% to 99.5%
EMA-based adaptive balancing achieves best D-Acc (19.7%) and MS-Bench (65.0%) vs all fixed-coefficient baselines on SmolLM3-3B Open Culture
Cosine similarity threshold τ=0.8 provides optimal balance between semantic fidelity and distribution adaptation
2606.00147.ablations_summary: Data fusion alone improves D-Acc by 7-20.5% and MS-Bench by 3.2-6.4% over original data SFT; adding adaptive on-policy distillation provides further 31-33% D-Acc gains; EMA adaptive balancing outperforms fixed λ∈{0.1,1.0}; Top-K=512 optimal; temperature T=1.5 best for MS-Bench; τ=0.8 best similarity threshold
limitations: Evaluation focused on small-scale language models (~3B); scalability to larger models unverified
Training data diversity is relatively constrained; performance on code generation, multilingual, or significantly larger corpora unexplored
failure_modes: RAFT does not dominate every individual model-domain setting
On some specific domains (e.g., Phi-4-mini on Open Culture), RAFT's MS-Bench drops below base model
2606.00147.relevance_to_opd: Directly proposes on-policy distillation where student generates trajectories at each training step and the original instruction-tuned model (self-teacher) provides soft logit targets conditioned on fused answers, with adaptive KL loss balancing

2606.00305.title: Bridging Reasoning Trajectories in On-Policy Distillation via Near-Future Guidance
2606.00305.summary: Trajectory-aware OPD using OT-based near-future guidance to fix token-level reasoning correction failures

method.training_loop: Stage1: off-policy forward-KL KD on teacher responses. Stage2: student rollouts on-policy, reverse-KL OPD + OT-based trajectory loss on detected divergent points within short windows.
method.loss_formulation: L_TOPD = L_OPD + λ * L_traj, where L_traj = sum_i KL(ỹ_{t+i} || p_S(· | c_{t+i}))
method.data_source: OpenThoughts3 math prompts
key_components: trajectory-aware divergence detection via short-window OT distance
OT-based trajectory-level teacher signal injection
downweighting low-OT high-loss false alarms
two-stage training with off-policy warmup then on-policy distillation

2606.00305.novelty: Identifies token-by-token learning trap in OPD where local reverse-KL correction fails to redirect reasoning trajectories; proposes short-window OT alignment to inject near-future trajectory guidance into token-level distillation loss.

on_policy_mechanism.evidence_quote: In Stage 2, the student performs on-policy sampling on a separate set of 50k prompts. For each prompt, we sample 4 student rollouts and optimize the student on its own trajectories using reverse KL distillation

opd_classification.reasoning: Core contribution is a new trajectory-aware objective (OT-based loss) that augments the standard reverse-KL OPD loss with near-future trajectory alignment, making it primarily a novel loss/objective for on-policy distillation.

key_findings: TOPD improves average accuracy from 47.8% (standard OPD) to 52.2% across three competitive math benchmarks.
About 29.23% of high-loss tokens fall within the low-divergence regime, indicating false alarms in standard OPD.
Suppressing low-OT high-loss tokens (false alarms) improves OPD from 47.8% to 48.2%, while suppressing high-OT tokens drops to 42.1%.
TOPD reduces mean local OT distance from 0.538 (original) to 0.204 vs 0.350 for standard OPD, showing stronger trajectory repair.
TOPD introduces only 1.41× training time overhead compared to standard OPD.
2606.00305.ablations_summary: Downweighting bottom 30% low-OT high-loss tokens improves OPD by +0.4%; downweighting matched high-OT tokens drops performance by -5.7%; TOPD with full trajectory guidance achieves +4.4% over baseline OPD, showing both divergence detection and trajectory injection are needed.
limitations: Additional computational cost from short-window continuation generation and OT computation
Analysis focuses on short-horizon trajectory divergence; some reasoning errors may emerge over longer contexts
Experiments mainly on mathematical reasoning benchmarks; validation needed for code and open-ended reasoning
OT distance measures trajectory proximity but does not always capture semantic equivalence
failure_modes: Different reasoning paths can lead to same correct answer but OT cannot capture semantic equivalence
Long-range reasoning errors beyond the short window (K=50) may not be addressed
2606.00305.relevance_to_opd: Directly addresses limitations of standard on-policy distillation by identifying token-by-token learning trap and proposing trajectory-aware OT-based guidance to improve reasoning trajectory correction during on-policy training.

2606.00564.title: Decomposed On-Policy Distillation for Vision-Language Reasoning: Steering Gradients for Visual Grounding
2606.00564.summary: Decomposes VLM on-policy distillation into language prior and visual grounding, steering gradients toward visual subspace

method.training_loop: Sample rollout τ from student VLM policy; compute multimodal and unimodal logits from teacher/student; decompose loss into language prior + visual grounding; steer gradient toward visual subspace with norm normalization; add language preservation regularizer on high-VDS tokens
method.loss_formulation: L = η_VGS(γ) · E_{τ~p^θ_S(·|I,x)} [ℓ_Standard(τ) + γ·ℓ_Vis(τ) + λ·ℓ_LP(τ)]
method.data_source: Vision-SR1-47K dataset
key_components: Visual Gradient Steering (VGS)
Decomposition into Language Prior and Visual Grounding objectives
Visual Dependency Score (VDS)
Language Preservation regularizer
Gradient norm normalization

2606.00564.novelty: First gradient-level analysis showing language and vision gradients are orthogonal in VLM on-policy distillation; proposes steering the gradient update toward the visual subspace to break the passive compromise trajectory of standard monolithic objectives

on_policy_mechanism.evidence_quote: On-Policy Distillation via the Reverse KL Divergence... by sampling τ ∼ pθ S, the student learns from its own rollouts (on-policy), effectively closing the training-inference gap.

opd_classification.reasoning: The core contribution is a new decomposed loss formulation for on-policy distillation that separates visual grounding from language prior and steers the optimization objective toward the visual subspace, constituting a novel objective/divergence design.

stabilization_tricks: language preservation regularizer on high-VDS tokens

key_findings: VGS improves average Acc@1 from 43.74% to 46.10% (+2.37%) for 2B student distilled from 8B teacher across 7 multimodal benchmarks.
Language and visual gradients are nearly orthogonal (≈92°) for high visual dependency tokens, revealing a fundamental tension in standard monolithic distillation.
VGS combined with GRPO achieves 47.20% average accuracy vs 45.41% for GRPO+Standard-KD (+1.79%) on 2B student.
Adaptive token-level VGS further improves average to 46.53% for 2B student.
Steering toward language prior degrades performance while steering toward visual subspace consistently improves it, validating the asymmetric maturity hypothesis.
2606.00564.ablations_summary: Key ablations: (1) Visual vs Language steering direction validates visual grounding as bottleneck; (2) γ sensitivity shows robustness across wide range; (3) λ=0.01 language preservation prevents language prior unlearning; (4) Adaptive token-level VGS provides additional marginal gain; (5) GRPO+VGS outperforms GRPO+Standard-KD and pure GRPO.
limitations: 1.375× training time overhead per step due to additional non-image-conditioned forward pass
Dependence on teacher calibration: if teacher has mode collapse where visual input has no influence on output distribution, VGS reduces to standard distillation
failure_modes: When teacher model suffers from perceptual blindness (visual input exerts no influence on output distribution), VGS cannot rectify it
VisualPuzzles benchmark for 4B student shows slight degradation (-0.44%) in one setting

theory.theoretical_claim: Bayesian decomposition of VLM log-likelihood into language prior + visual likelihood; gradient orthogonality analysis showing standard loss acts as passive bisector
theory.proof_sketch: Applies Bayes' Rule to factor multimodal log-probability into language prior and visual likelihood terms; constructs tractable visual target distribution q*_T via log-space substitution; empirically validates near-orthogonality of decomposed gradients

2606.00564.relevance_to_opd: Directly advances on-policy distillation for VLMs by decomposing the monolithic reverse-KL objective into language and visual components, revealing geometric pathology in standard OPD and proposing gradient steering to prioritize visual grounding

2606.01039.title: OPD+: Rethinking the Advantage Design for On-Policy Distillation
2606.01039.summary: Corrects advantage estimation in on-policy distillation via f-divergence gradient analysis

method.training_loop: Sample rollouts from student policy, compute f-divergence reward w_f(u) = -f(u) + u*f'(u) instead of stop-gradient -f(u), update student via policy gradient
method.loss_formulation: L = -E_{y~p_θ} Σ ∇_θ log p_θ(y_n|y_{<n},x) * w_f(u_{θ,n}) where w_f(u) = -f(u) + u*f'(u)
method.data_source: DeepMath rollouts for math; ToolAlpaca for tool use
key_components: corrected advantage w_f(u) = -f(u) + u*f'(u)
f-divergence framework for OPD
gradient-faithful weight replacing stop-gradient reward

2606.01039.novelty: Shows stop-gradient in OPD yields biased gradients for general f-divergences (not reverse KL), derives corrected advantage w_f(u) = -f(u) + u*f'(u) that rescues forward KL and JSD from collapse and improves reverse KL

on_policy_mechanism.evidence_quote: In OPD, we distill a Qwen3-8B teacher into a Qwen3-8B-Base student model which has been initialized by supervised fine-tuning (SFT). For competition mathematics, the student trains for 100 on-policy steps (with a total batch size of 64 groups).

opd_classification.reasoning: Core contribution is a new corrected objective/divergence formulation for on-policy distillation, deriving gradient-faithful advantage for general f-divergences.

key_findings: OPD+ with JSD achieves 50.42% on AIME25 vs 48.54% for standard Reverse KL, rescuing previously collapsed divergences
Forward KL and JSD with stop-gradient collapse to baseline (0% on ToolUse), while OPD+ corrected versions achieve 59.01% and 60.29% respectively
Reverse KL+ improves over standard Reverse KL on ToolUse (61.44% vs 59.97%) despite theoretically equivalent gradients, due to variance reduction
Only one line of code change is needed to implement OPD+ over standard OPD
2606.01039.ablations_summary: Comparison of stop-gradient advantage (-f(u)) vs corrected advantage (w(u)) across three f-divergences (Forward KL, Reverse KL, JSD) shows corrected version eliminates training collapse for Forward KL and JSD and improves Reverse KL via variance reduction baseline effect
limitations: No detailed model scaling analysis across different model sizes
Limited to Qwen3 model family only
No comparison of single token performance with logit distillation for various divergences
failure_modes: Standard Forward KL and JSD with stop-gradient suffer catastrophic collapse to 0% accuracy on tool use

theory.theoretical_claim: Stop-gradient in OPD leads to biased gradient estimates for general f-divergences; Reverse KL is special case where bias reduces to constant baseline
theory.proof_sketch: Differentiating true objective yields score-function term plus direct reward-gradient term u*f'(u)*∇log p_θ; for reverse KL f(u)=-log u so u*f'(u)=-1 is constant baseline vanishing under score identity; for general f the correction is non-constant hence stop-gradient is biased

2606.01039.relevance_to_opd: Directly advances on-policy distillation by correcting the advantage estimation formula, providing a principled f-divergence framework that expands viable divergence choices beyond reverse KL

2606.01249.title: Trust Region On-Policy Distillation
2606.01249.summary: Trust-region OPD with outlier estimation and off-policy guidance for stable reasoning distillation

method.training_loop: Student generates rollouts; tokens split into trust-region (K1 RKL) and outlier (top-k FKL) via adaptive acceptance ratio; off-policy teacher prefixes with FKL imitation annealed to zero
method.loss_formulation: J_TrOPD = -I[x~π_S] M_x Σ π_T,v log(π_T,v/π_S,v) - I[x~π_S] M̄_x log(π_S/π_T) - β I[x~π_T] log(π_T/π_S)
method.data_source: OpenThoughts3 prompts (math, code, science domains)
key_components: adaptive trust region via speculative decoding acceptance ratio
top-k FKL outlier estimation
off-policy teacher prefix guidance with cosine annealing
K1 reverse-KL estimator for trust region

2606.01249.novelty: Partitions student-generated tokens into trust region (reliable K1 RKL supervision) and outlier region (top-k FKL estimation) using speculative-decoding acceptance probability, plus annealed off-policy teacher prefixes, addressing unreliable policy gradients in reasoning OPD

on_policy_mechanism.evidence_quote: On-policy distillation instead trains on student of generations (SoGs) to mitigate exposure bias. In reverse KL divergence (RKL)-based OPD, the sequence-level objective can be written as

opd_classification.reasoning: Core contribution is an adaptive trust-region divergence objective that selectively applies RKL in reliable regions and FKL in outlier regions during on-policy distillation, fitting adaptive objective formulation.

key_findings: TrOPD improves over OPD by +3.34 (AIME25), +4.00 (LiveCodeBench), +5.11 (IFBench), and +6.18 (GPQA Diamond) on Qwen3-SFT-1.7B.
Single-domain TrOPD outperforms REOPOLD by 1.99 and 1.84 points in math and general domains respectively on DeepSeek-1.5B.
FKL outlier estimation recovers informative supervision that masking/clipping discards, yielding +1.28 avg over Mask Outlier.
Off-policy guidance complements all outlier strategies, with TrOPD FKL achieving the best overall score of 49.85 avg in single-domain.
2606.01249.ablations_summary: Mask Outlier and Clip Outlier both improve over vanilla OPD; FKL Outlier further improves over both; off-policy guidance adds +1-2 points on top of each outlier strategy; combining TrOPD with concurrent AOPD yields additional +1.04 avg gain.
limitations: Lack of practical deployment studies on small reasoning models
No mid-training or pre-training stages explored which may constrain reasoning performance upper bound
Focused only on OPD post-training with DeepSeek-Qwen2.5-1.5B and Qwen3-SFT-1.7B
failure_modes: Standalone top-k FKL completely fails (near 0% accuracy) due to biased vocabulary approximation
Entropy-based token selection can degrade performance by discarding informative ordinary tokens
2606.01249.relevance_to_opd: Directly proposes a novel OPD method (TrOPD) that addresses the core challenge of unreliable teacher supervision under distribution mismatch in on-policy distillation for reasoning LLMs, with trust-region partitioning and adaptive divergence objectives.

2606.01476.title: OmniOPD: Logit-Free On-Policy Distillation via Speculative Verification
2606.01476.summary: Logit-free on-policy distillation using chunk-level Monte Carlo semantic verification from black-box teachers

method.training_loop: Student generates on-policy trajectory → peak-entropy selects M chunks → teacher generates N MC rollouts per chunk → Bayesian-smoothed semantic similarity scores chunks → student updated with chunk loss + KL anchor on unaudited tokens
method.loss_formulation: L = -sum_c [pi_hat_teacher^(c) * sum_{t in c} log pi_theta(y_t|x,y_{<t})] + beta * sum_{t in U} D_KL(pi_ref || pi_theta)
method.data_source: DAPO-Math-17K for math, PRIME-RL compilation (APPS, CodeContests, TACO, Codeforces) for code
key_components: peak-entropy chunk scheduling
Monte Carlo semantic similarity estimation
Dirichlet-Multinomial Bayesian smoothing
trust-region KL anchor on unaudited tokens

2606.01476.novelty: Replaces token-level logit matching in OPD with chunk-level semantic similarity estimated via Monte Carlo rollouts from black-box teachers, enabling logit-free on-policy distillation that is tokenizer- and style-invariant

on_policy_mechanism.evidence_quote: Generate student reasoning trajectory y =(y 1 ,...,y T )∼π θ (·|x) ... Query black-box teacher π t ∗ eacher with prefix y <c for N rollouts {y t ( e i) acher }N i=1

opd_classification.reasoning: Core contribution is enabling on-policy distillation from black-box teachers without logit access, using chunk-level semantic verification as the supervision signal.

stabilization_tricks: trust-region KL anchor on unaudited tokens

key_findings: OmniOPD outperforms SFT by up to +45.31% relative on math and +18.52% relative on code
OmniOPD surpasses standard white-box OPD by up to +28.64% on mathematical reasoning (72.32% vs 56.22% with Qwen3-30B-A3B teacher)
With Claude-4.5-Haiku and Gemini-2.5-Flash teachers, OmniOPD achieves +9.54% relative over open-weight teacher, surpassing GRPO (75.67% vs 70.24%)
Removing KL anchoring causes catastrophic collapse from 69.08% to 8.28%
Sparse configuration M=5 retains 99% accuracy (68.38% vs 69.08%) at 0.88x SFT cost
2606.01476.ablations_summary: KL anchoring is critical (removal causes collapse to 8.28%); Bayesian smoothing contributes +0.45%; entropy selection contributes +0.63%; chunk size C=25 catastrophically degrades performance; N=10→20 rollouts gives diminishing returns (+0.49%); M=5→10→20 scales smoothly
failure_modes: On competitive programming with larger student (Qwen3-4B), OmniOPD slightly underperforms white-box OPD, hypothesized due to code's syntactic rigidity making token-level matching more directly meaningful
When teacher capability margin over student is small, self-exploratory GRPO remains competitive (OmniOPD 60.67% vs GRPO 62.41% for Qwen3-1.7B with Qwen3-32B teacher)

theory.theoretical_claim: Bounded gradient stability (Thm 4.1), sub-Gaussian concentration of chunk estimator at O(1/N) rate (Thm 4.2), trust-region bound on unaudited tokens (Thm 4.3), tokenizer/style invariance of chunk-level loss (Thm 4.4)
theory.proof_sketch: Bayesian estimator lower-bounded by alpha*pi_bar/(N+alpha)>0 preventing gradient collapse; Hoeffding inequality gives sub-Gaussian concentration; Pinsker inequality bounds TV distance on unaudited tokens; semantic similarity function induces equivalence class invariance

2606.01476.relevance_to_opd: Directly proposes a novel on-policy distillation framework that removes the logit-access requirement of standard OPD, enabling distillation from black-box proprietary teachers while maintaining chunk-level dense supervision on student-generated trajectories

2606.02372.title: COMAP: Co-Evolving World Models and Agent Policies for LLM Agents
2606.02372.summary: Co-evolving textual world models and agent policies via on-policy self-distillation and future-aware reflection

method.training_loop: Draft action → world model predicts future state → future-aware reflection refines action → execute → on-policy self-distillation updates world model with EMA teacher; iterate co-evolving rounds
method.loss_formulation: L_WM = E[-log p_S(s^env_{t+1}|s_t,a_t) + η L_WMSD]; L_policy = L^exp + L^ref + α E[-log p_θ(a^tgt|x^ref)] + β E[BCE(p_t, y^ref_t)]
method.data_source: On-policy trajectories from agent-environment interaction across ALFWorld, ScienceWorld, WebShop, StableToolBench
key_components: on-policy self-distillation for world model with EMA teacher
future-aware reflection with action gate
world-state gate curriculum
suffix-based refinement initialization

2606.02372.novelty: Introduces closed-loop co-evolution where agent on-policy trajectories update the world model via self-distillation while the world model's future predictions guide policy refinement, unlike prior static world models

on_policy_mechanism.evidence_quote: the student first generates an on-policy next-state rollout sˆS t+1 ∼ pS ϕ (· | s t ,a t ), while the teacher observes the same input together with senv t+1 and provides a soft target for this student rollout

opd_classification.reasoning: The core contribution is on-policy self-distillation of the world model using the student's own rollouts with an EMA teacher providing soft targets—a pure self-distillation mechanism without external teacher models.

key_findings: COMAP achieves +16.75% relative improvement with Qwen3-4B over prior best world-modeling baseline (51.52→60.15 average)
Qwen3-8B with COMAP (72.11%) surpasses GPT-5.4 with ReAct (67.83%) on agent tasks
Freezing world model after warm-up causes 26.9-29.1% Delta-F1 drop, validating co-evolution necessity
WMSD reduces change-token NLL from 2.02 to 1.45 (4B) and 1.80 to 1.38 (8B) vs off-policy SFT
World model Delta-F1 reaches 90.29% on Qwen3-8B, slightly surpassing GPT-5.4's 89.05%
2606.02372.ablations_summary: Removing future-state input causes largest policy drop (9.8-24.1%). Frozen WM causes 26.9-29.1% Delta-F1 drop. Expert SFT warmup, action gate, online reflection, world-state gate, and WMSD all contribute positively.
limitations: Assumes text-representable environments; may not cover multimodal settings with visual/spatial/auditory signals
Requires additional world-model call at inference time, affecting latency-sensitive applications
failure_modes: Inaccurate early future states may mislead reflection
Unnecessary refinements may harm already good draft actions
2606.02372.relevance_to_opd: Self-distillation of the world model uses on-policy student rollouts with EMA teacher soft targets, directly implementing on-policy distillation for world-model adaptation to the evolving agent's state-action distribution

2606.02530.title: SafeSteer: Localized On-Policy Distillation for Efficient Safety Alignment
2606.02530.summary: Localized on-policy distillation confined to safety tokens via activation steering teacher

method.training_loop: Construct safety teacher via activation steering; select safety tokens by contrastive log probability voting; student generates on-policy rollouts on harmful prompts; minimize reverse KL restricted to safety token subset S
method.loss_formulation: L(θ_s) = E_{b,m} [1/T_{b,m} Σ_t Σ_{v∈S} p_s(v) log(p_s(v)/p_t(v))]
method.data_source: 100 harmful samples from PKU-SafeRLHF, 160 harmless instructions from Alpaca
key_components: activation-steered safety teacher
contrastive log probability voting for safety token selection
token-level localized reverse KL
on-policy student rollouts

2606.02530.novelty: Restricts on-policy distillation penalty to a sparse safety token subset identified via contrastive log probability voting between activation-steered teacher and base model, eliminating alignment tax without general-purpose data or auxiliary reward models

on_policy_mechanism.evidence_quote: During alignment, π_s generates trajectories on harmful instructions x ∈ D_harmful, sampled from PKU-SafeRLHF. Then π_s is optimized by restricting the reverse KL penalty to the safety token subset S.

opd_classification.reasoning: Core contribution is token-level weighting (restricting KL to safety tokens) within on-policy distillation using a self-constructed teacher via activation steering

train: Alpaca (160 harmless samples for token selection)

key_findings: SafeSteer reduces average ASR on Qwen3-4B from 2.87% to 0.91% with only 0.29 points general capability degradation
SafeSteer achieves 2.5× ASR reduction over strongest baseline BFPO on Qwen2.5-7B (1.48% vs 3.75%)
Only 100 harmful training samples required, less than 1% of data used by baselines
Activation-steered teacher consistently drives ASR to near 0% vs system prompt baseline
Removing safety token restriction degrades MATH and HumanEval, confirming global penalty harms general capabilities
2606.02530.ablations_summary: Forward KL underperforms reverse KL; removing safety token restriction hurts general capabilities (especially MATH/HumanEval); re-normalization of probability slices causes severe capability degradation; using base model π_0 instead of steered π_t for rollouts causes catastrophic safety failure (JBB ASR: 1% → 75%); response length H controls depth of safety alignment (H=1 captures superficial refusal tokens, H=7 captures semantic safety concepts)
limitations: Relies on base model already possessing refusal capability (not applicable to purely pretrained checkpoints)
Experiments limited to models ≤10B parameters
Only evaluated on text-only autoregressive LLMs, not VLMs or diffusion-based language models
failure_modes: Using base model π_0 for rollouts instead of steered π_t causes catastrophic safety failure on models with shallow safety alignment
Re-normalization of probability slices over S causes optimizer to inflate safety logits and crowd out general capability distribution
2606.02530.relevance_to_opd: Directly proposes an on-policy distillation method for safety alignment, with student generating on-policy rollouts and minimizing reverse KL against a self-constructed activation-steered teacher, restricted to safety-critical tokens to preserve general capabilities

2605.31490.title: Are Full Rollouts Necessary for On-Policy Distillation?
2605.31490.affiliation_primary: Institute of Automation, Chinese Academy of Sciences
2605.31490.summary: Horizon-control strategies (POPD, TOPD) improve OPD efficiency by truncating rollouts

method.training_loop: Student generates rollouts (full or truncated), compute token-level log-ratio between teacher and student on rollout, update student via policy gradient with log-ratio signal; POPD progressively expands horizon, TOPD permanently truncates
method.loss_formulation: E[g_topd] = E_{x, y~pi_theta} [sum_{t=1}^{H} r_t s_t], where r_t = log pi_g(y_t|y_{<t},x) - log pi_theta(y_t|y_{<t},x)
method.data_source: DAPO-Math-17K dataset
key_components: Progressive horizon expansion (POPD)
Truncated rollout distillation (TOPD)
Token-level OPD (short log-ratio horizon)

2605.31490.novelty: Identifies rollout horizon as key bottleneck in OPD and proposes two simple strategies (progressive and truncated) that match full-rollout OPD performance using only 10% of rollout horizon, reducing training time by up to 82%

on_policy_mechanism.evidence_quote: Standard OPD requires the student to generate a full rollout and then computes log-ratio signals between teacher and student over the generated rollout.

opd_classification.reasoning: Core contribution is a compute-efficiency technique (horizon control) for on-policy distillation, falling under efficiency/stability techniques for OPD.

key_findings: POPD improves training efficiency of OPD by up to 3× on AIME24
TOPD with ρ=0.25 improves AIME24 from 49.3 to 51.3 while reducing training time from 29.7h to 10.2h
TOPD with ρ=0.10 retains most performance (50.7 on AIME24) using only 5.3h vs 29.7h for full OPD
Early rollout segments provide more effective supervision than late segments, which can degrade below initial policy
Sequence-level OPD accumulates future noise with error growing as O(T^3) for the first token
2605.31490.ablations_summary: Segment-level distillation shows early/middle segments provide better supervision; prefix-continuation analysis confirms TOPD works through genuine parameter updating not prefix activation; reverse distillation confirms truncated rollouts provide strong optimization signal; autoregressive control task shows TOPD fails when teacher exhibits phase-dependent behaviors across rollout stages
limitations: Only simple horizon-control strategies explored; adaptive mechanisms (based on KL divergence, entropy, confidence) left for future work
TOPD fails in tasks where teacher exhibits phase-dependent behaviors across different rollout stages
failure_modes: TOPD fails in autoregressive control tasks where useful teacher characteristics are horizon-dependent (0% success at ρ=0.10 and ρ=0.20)

theory.theoretical_claim: Sequence-level OPD advantage MSE grows as O(T^3) for first token due to accumulated future noise
theory.proof_sketch: Decompose log-ratio signal into ideal signal plus position-dependent noise; accumulate variance over future positions with discount factor γ=1 and linearly growing noise scale σ_k=δk; sum of squares yields cubic growth

2605.31490.relevance_to_opd: Directly studies efficiency of on-policy distillation by proposing horizon control strategies (POPD and TOPD) that reduce rollout length while maintaining distillation quality, demonstrating full rollouts are unnecessary for effective OPD

2605.30251.title: Same Evidence, Different Answers: Canonical-Context On-Policy Distillation for Multi-Turn Language Models
2605.30251.summary: On-policy self-distillation aligning RAW-SHARDED multi-turn answers with FULL-context teacher behavior

method.training_loop: Student rollouts final answer from RAW-SHARDED history; frozen same-backbone teacher scores student prefixes under FULL prompt; minimize answer-masked reverse KL
method.loss_formulation: L = E_{(c,h)} E_{y~pi_theta(.|h)} [ 1/|T_ans(y)| sum_{t in T_ans} D_KL(pi_theta(.|h,y_{<t}) || pi_0(.|c,y_{<t})) ]
method.data_source: GSM8K and GSM8K-Aug sharded math conversations
key_components: on-policy student rollout from RAW-SHARDED history
frozen same-backbone FULL-context teacher
answer-masked reverse KL objective
same-prefix canonical relabeling

2605.30251.novelty: Uses on-policy distillation not to import knowledge from a stronger teacher but to enforce presentation invariance between task-equivalent FULL and RAW-SHARDED contexts using the same backbone as both teacher and student

on_policy_mechanism.evidence_quote: Given a retained pair (c,h), the current student produces a final-answer rollout yˆ ∼ π θ (· | h), and T ans (yˆ) denotes the token positions belonging to that final assistant continuation. These prefixes are the on-policy states for distillation

opd_classification.reasoning: Core contribution is self-distillation where the same backbone serves as both frozen FULL-context teacher and trainable RAW-SHARDED student, with on-policy rollouts and reverse-KL alignment—pure self-distillation for presentation invariance.

stabilization_tricks: answer-mask to avoid leaking future evidence

key_findings: CCOPD yields 32% average relative improvement on RAW-SHARDED over unmodified base model across math and five zero-shot OOD task families
Math RAW-SHARDED accuracy improves from 66.0 to 82.5 (+16.5 points) while FULL remains at 90.3
Math-only training transfers: non-math RAW-SHARDED average improves from 36.8 to 49.7 (+12.9 points)
Under assistant-side pollution stress test, base collapses from 90.3 to 33.0 while CCOPD remains at 89.3
Reverse KL outperforms forward KL (82.5 vs 79.0 on math RAW-SHARDED)
Same-backbone teacher is sufficient; larger 14B teacher does not consistently outperform self-distillation
2605.30251.ablations_summary: Teacher source ablation shows same-backbone is sufficient (4B worse, 14B not better); KL direction matters (reverse > forward); SFT and GRPO baselines yield smaller RAW-SHARDED gains; OPSD (privileged supervision) performs worse; neutral-placeholder and SAAR probes confirm reduced self-anchored drift
limitations: Experiments limited to 8B scale with LoRA adapter trained on thousands of pairs
Does not establish behavior for substantially larger models or closed-source systems
RAW-SHARDED setting is a controlled approximation; real conversations have evolving intents, clarifications, corrections
Cannot correct errors made by the FULL teacher itself
Does not directly train earlier-turn behaviors such as clarification or abstention
failure_modes: Cannot fix tasks where the FULL-conditioned base model itself fails
SummHay (long-context summarization) shows non-significant improvement
Lightweight test-time modes slightly reduce CCOPD accuracy, suggesting potential interaction effects

theory.theoretical_claim: On-policy chain rule decomposes sequence-level KL into expected sum of same-prefix token KL terms; Pinsker's inequality bounds answer-event probability difference
theory.proof_sketch: Lemma 1 shows D_KL(P_theta^h || P_0^c) = E[sum d_t(y)] via autoregressive factorization; Proposition 1 uses Pinsker to get |P_theta^h(E) - P_0^c(E)| <= sqrt(epsilon/2)

2605.30251.relevance_to_opd: Directly proposes an on-policy distillation method where the student generates rollouts from contaminated multi-turn histories and is supervised by token-level KL from a frozen same-backbone teacher conditioned on a clean canonical context

2605.29584.title: GAPD: Gold-Action Policy Distillation for Agentic Reinforcement Learning in Knowledge Base Question Answering
2605.29584.affiliation_primary: University of Science and Technology of China
2605.29584.summary: Token-level distillation from gold-action-conditioned self-teacher during on-policy KBQA RL

method.training_loop: GRPO rollout → execute student actions → entity-anchor match student states to gold states → condition current policy on aligned gold action as self-teacher → compute token-level log-prob gap → fuse with GRPO advantage → PPO-style clipped update
method.loss_formulation: L_fuse = -(1/Z) sum min(r_ik * A_hat_ik, clip(r_ik,1-eps,1+eps)*A_hat_ik), A_hat_ik = A_grpo_i + lambda_gapd * A_gapd_ik
method.data_source: GrailQA, WebQSP, GraphQ training sets with gold logical form annotations over Freebase KB
key_components: entity-anchor matching
gold-action-conditioned self-teacher
token-level advantage fusion with GRPO
stop-gradient self-teacher distribution

2605.29584.novelty: Uses entity-anchor matching to align on-policy student states with gold execution states, then conditions the current policy on aligned gold actions to create a self-teacher whose token-level log-prob gap is fused with GRPO advantage as dense guidance during RL

on_policy_mechanism.evidence_quote: GRPO samples the student rollout, executable gold logical forms are aligned to the student's execution state, and the added distillation signal is applied only to matched turns.

opd_classification.reasoning: The self-teacher is the current policy conditioned on gold-action information (PI of ground truth), providing token-level distributional supervision on student-generated rollouts fused with RL reward.

key_findings: GAPD improves GrailQA overall EM/F1 from 83.9/86.1 to 87.8/89.5 (+4.6%/+3.9% relative) over outcome-only RL baseline KBQA-R1.
On WebQSP, GAPD improves F1 from 83.4 to 86.1 (+3.2% relative).
Self-teacher (gold-action-conditioned same policy) outperforms external Qwen3-32B teacher variant (86.1 vs 84.8 on WebQSP).
Turn-index alignment without entity-anchor matching drops WebQSP F1 to 79.3, showing state-based alignment is critical.
GAPD achieves higher F1 with fewer interactions per query (76.9 avg F1, 2.68 calls) vs baseline (74.4 F1, 2.91 calls).
2605.29584.ablations_summary: Outcome reward only is consistently lower; external Qwen3-32B/14B teachers improve over baseline but trail self-teacher GAPD; turn-index alignment without entity-anchor matching sharply reduces F1; first-turn-only supervision recovers much but trails full GAPD; lambda_gapd is stable in 0.1-1.0 range.
limitations: Training is ~1.5× slower than outcome-only RL due to self-teacher scoring on supervised spans
failure_modes: When student execution state cannot be aligned to any gold state (low Jaccard similarity), no distillation signal is provided
2605.29584.relevance_to_opd: GAPD is a direct application of on-policy distillation in agentic RL: the student generates rollouts via GRPO, and a self-teacher (current policy conditioned on aligned gold actions) provides token-level distributional supervision on those student-generated tokens, closely following the GKD/MiniLLM paradigm but in a structured action environment.

2605.30833.title: Your Teacher Can't Help You Here: Combating Supervision Fidelity Decay in On-Policy Distillation
2605.30833.affiliation_primary: University of Chinese Academy of Sciences
2605.30833.summary: Identifies Supervision Fidelity Decay in OPD and proposes Lookahead Group Reward to combat it

method.training_loop: Student generates rollout; at high-entropy positions, evaluate teacher confidence on top-K candidates one step ahead via tree-attention; compute group-normalized confidence reward; combine with reverse-KL advantage; update student
method.loss_formulation: L^{LGR}_t = A_t + \gamma \cdot r_{conf}(x_t), where A_t = 1 + \log \pi_\theta(x_t|x_{<t}) - \log \pi_T(x_t|x_{<t})
method.data_source: Polaris dataset (math), DeepScaler code dataset (code)
key_components: Supervision Fidelity Decay analysis
Lookahead Group Reward (one-step-ahead teacher confidence)
Group normalization of confidence reward
Entropy-triggered tree-attention mechanism

2605.30833.novelty: Identifies that teacher supervision quality degrades monotonically along student-generated prefixes (SFD) and proposes a one-step lookahead confidence reward that evaluates which candidate token preserves future teacher supervision, orthogonal to divergence choice

on_policy_mechanism.evidence_quote: Generate x=(x_1,...,x_L) ~ π_θ(·|c) //Student rollout ... Run teacher forward pass with tree mask M //Single pass for all positions

opd_classification.reasoning: Core contribution is an adaptive supervision signal (lookahead confidence reward) that addresses degradation of teacher signal quality during on-policy distillation, modifying the effective objective based on student state

key_findings: LGR improves mean@8 by 2.57 points over OPD for 7B student across six benchmarks
Gains increase with generation length: +4.92 points on AIME-26 at 39k tokens
At short lengths (3k) where SFD is minimal, LGR provides no advantage, confirming the mechanism
Stabilization methods (JSD, REOPOLD) do not address SFD and perform comparable or worse than OPD
Max-p confidence metric outperforms alternatives (PPL, entropy, sampled-p) as reward signal
2605.30833.ablations_summary: Max-p metric best among 4 candidates (46.67 vs 43.75 for sampled-p on AIME-24); optimal γ=1.0-1.5 (γ=10 causes reward hacking); entropy-triggered activation is near-lossless; gains grow monotonically with max generation length from 3k to 39k
limitations: Requires white-box access to teacher model logits
Confidence reward assumes teacher's relative ranking remains informative even in OOD regions
Fixed number of candidates K and static entropy threshold τ rather than dynamic adjustment
Not validated on multi-modal reasoning settings
failure_modes: At short generation lengths (3k) where SFD is minimal, LGR provides no advantage
High γ (10.0) causes reward hacking with repetitive tokens that inflate teacher confidence without solving tasks
May weaken for extremely OOD student trajectories or poorly calibrated teachers

theory.theoretical_claim: Teacher signal vanishes under SFD (Prop 1), drift compounds self-reinforcingly under reverse-KL (Prop 2), one-step-ahead discriminability survives local supervision failure (Prop 3)
theory.proof_sketch: Variance of teacher log-prob bounded by log²|V| - Ent(π_T)², so as teacher entropy increases under SFD, discriminative signal ∆_T→0; one-step-ahead comparison is independent of local entropy

2605.30833.relevance_to_opd: Directly addresses a fundamental failure mode of on-policy distillation (supervision quality degradation along student trajectories) and proposes a principled lookahead reward that maintains teacher supervision capability during on-policy training

2606.00424.title: Weak Critics Make Strong Learners: On-Policy Critique Distillation for Scalable Oversight
2606.00424.summary: On-policy critique distillation using weak model critiques to improve strong models

method.training_loop: Each epoch: strong model generates on-policy answers, weak model critiques them, filter high-quality critiques via outcome+rubric checks, distill critic-conditioned self-teacher into student (same model without critique) via token-level KL
method.loss_formulation: L_OPCD(θ) = (1/|S_e|) Σ_{(x,y,f)∈S_e} Σ_{t=1}^{|y|} KL(π_θ(·|x,y_{<t}) || stopgrad[π_θ(·|x,f,y_{<t})])
method.data_source: GPQA main split (non-Diamond) for reasoning; Magpie alignment corpus for alignment
key_components: weak-model critique generation
outcome+rubric-based critique filtration
self-teacher with critique conditioning
progressive on-policy distillation
token-level KL divergence loss

2606.00424.novelty: Uses weak model as critic (not labeler/judge) and distills critic-conditioned self-teacher behavior into the same strong model without critique access, progressively updating on-policy across epochs

on_policy_mechanism.evidence_quote: In each epoch, the current strong model generates on-policy answers, and the weak model critiques these answers. We then use an outcome- and rubric-based quality metric to keep only useful critiques.

opd_classification.reasoning: Core contribution is on-policy self-distillation where the teacher is the same strong model conditioned on weak critique (privileged information), making it a self-teacher with external critique as privileged signal.

key_findings: OPCD improves IFEval mean@8 from 61.60% to 68.74% (+7.14) and pass@8 from 75.97% to 80.41% (+4.44) using weak Phi-4-mini critiques
OPCD improves GPQA mean@8 from 38.22% to 42.67% (+4.45) and pass@8 from 70.25% to 76.86% (+6.61) using weak Qwen3-1.7B critiques
Weak critique at inference time improves strong model on GPQA Diamond from 83.84 to 90.40 at pass@16
Critique quality is central: best-critic selection outperforms random and worst-critic baselines consistently
2606.00424.ablations_summary: Critique quality ablations (best/random/worst critic) show high-quality critiques are essential; alignment vs reasoning training dynamics differ substantially with reasoning being noisier
limitations: Reasoning training signals are noisy and high-variance compared to alignment
Method relies on critique quality estimation which could be further improved
Only tested on limited task domains (GPQA, IFEval)
failure_modes: Misleading weak critiques can hurt performance below no-critique baseline
Reasoning training loss increases rather than decreases, indicating unstable optimization
2606.00424.relevance_to_opd: Directly proposes on-policy distillation where student generates rollouts each epoch, a self-teacher conditioned on weak critique provides dense token-level logit supervision, and the student learns to internalize critique-guided behavior without critique at test time

2605.31159.title: Trust-Region Behavior Blending for On-Policy Distillation
2605.31159.summary: Trust-region warmup for on-policy distillation via teacher-guided behavior policy under student-centered KL constraint

method.training_loop: Sample prefixes from behavior policy µ* (closest-to-teacher inside student-centered KL trust region), apply reverse-KL OPD loss on those prefixes, anneal KL budget to zero after warmup horizon K
method.loss_formulation: L_OPD(θ) = E_{h~P_πS}[D_KL(π_θ(·|h) || π_T(·|h))]
method.data_source: 25,600 training prompts from OpenThoughts3-1.2M corpus
key_components: per-prefix trust-region solver
student-centered KL constraint
annealed warmup schedule
closed-form geometric mixture behavior policy

2605.31159.novelty: Introduces a constrained behavior policy optimization during early OPD warmup that moves sampling toward teacher within a student-centered KL trust region, unlike prior work that changes the target distribution or loss after prefixes are already visited

on_policy_mechanism.evidence_quote: On-policy distillation (OPD) trains a student on prefixes sampled from its own policy while matching a stronger teacher. This addresses the prefix mismatch of offline distillation

opd_classification.reasoning: Core contribution is a curriculum/warmup technique (annealed trust-region behavior blending) that improves early-stage on-policy distillation stability

key_findings: TRB attains the strongest average score in both model-pair settings: 33.2% (vs 32.3% vanilla OPD) for 1.7B and 44.4% (vs 44.0%) for 0.6B
Annealed warmup outperforms persistent fixed-ε blending, suggesting teacher-guided off-policy behavior is not equally useful throughout training
TRB prefixes yield higher continuation success rates than vanilla-OPD prefixes at step 0 for both teacher (+50%) and student (+26%) continuations at length 64
2605.31159.ablations_summary: Comparison of annealed vs fixed-ε budget shows annealing is critical; sweep over ε₀ ∈ {0.001-0.05} and K ∈ {15,25,50} shows moderate budgets (ε₀=0.01-0.02) with short warmup (K=15-25) work best; SFT warmup and temperature warmup underperform TRB
limitations: Scoped to two math-reasoning OPD settings with Qwen3-Base student-teacher pairs only
Does not claim warmup schedules transfer unchanged to other domains or teacher-student gaps
Increases training-time cost during warmup due to online teacher decoding and co-residency
Batched teacher pass in vanilla OPD can be faster in wall-clock time than TRB's online teacher decoding
failure_modes: On AIME25 benchmark, TRB (6.9%) slightly underperforms vanilla OPD (7.1%)
Some baselines win individual benchmark columns though none matches TRB on overall average

theory.theoretical_claim: Token-level KL trust regions induce rollout-level control: D_KL(P_µ||P_S) ≤ Tε; small budget ε buys teacher-closeness improvement of order √ε while paying behavior-KL cost ε
theory.proof_sketch: Autoregressive chain rule decomposes sequence KL into sum of per-step local KLs under behavior policy; monotonicity of D_KL(µ_β||π_S) in β proven via variance of log-ratio being non-negative

2605.31159.relevance_to_opd: Directly addresses the early-training brittleness of on-policy distillation by proposing a principled warmup mechanism that controls the behavior policy during student rollout collection without changing the per-prefix OPD objective

2606.02684.title: Filter, Then Reweight: Rethinking Optimization Granularity in On-Policy Distillation
2606.02684.summary: Dual-granularity OPD with trajectory filtering and soft token reweighting

method.training_loop: Student generates rollouts; teacher scores trajectories; filter bottom p% by teacher log-prob; compute token weights from teacher confidence × student confusion; optimize PPO-clipped loss with weighted advantages
method.loss_formulation: L_FiRe-OPD = -1/T sum_t min(r_t * a_tilde_t, clip(r_t, 1-eps, 1+eps) * a_tilde_t) where a_tilde_t = w_t / (1/T sum w_t') * a_t
method.data_source: DeepMath-103K (difficulty level 6) for math; multi-teacher dataset from Yang et al. 2026b for multi-teacher
key_components: trajectory-level filtering by teacher log-probability
soft token-level reweighting combining teacher confidence and student confusion
PPO-style clipped objective with weighted advantages

2606.02684.novelty: Jointly applies trajectory-level hard filtering and token-level soft reweighting in OPD, combining teacher confidence and student confusion multiplicatively for continuous importance weights rather than hard token selection used in prior work

on_policy_mechanism.evidence_quote: At each training iteration, the student generates rollouts from its current policy given a set of prompts: y ~ π_θ(·|x). The teacher then provides token-level supervision on these student-generated trajectories.

opd_classification.reasoning: Core contribution is a token-level and trajectory-level weighting/filtering scheme for on-policy distillation, which is an efficiency/stability technique for selective supervision (token weighting + curriculum-like filtering).

train: multi-teacher math+code dataset from Yang et al. 2026b

key_findings: FiRe-OPD achieves +6.25 on AIME 2024 and +2.13 avg over standard OPD in strong-to-weak setting
Multi-teacher setting shows +18.81 on MinervaMATH and +9.77 on HumanEval+ over OPD
Hard trajectory filtering + soft token weighting (60.83) outperforms all other combinations including Hard+Hard (58.23) and Soft+Soft (58.68)
Student confusion is the dominant token-level signal (removing it causes -2.24 drop) while teacher confidence is complementary (-0.96 drop)
2606.02684.ablations_summary: Removing student confusion causes largest drop (-2.24), followed by trajectory filtering (-1.84), then teacher confidence (-0.96). Optimal filtering percentile is p=20%. α robust for ≥1.0, β shows minimal sensitivity. Hard+Soft strategy (60.83) beats all other granularity combinations.
limitations: Treats each token independently without modeling how erroneous prefixes degrade subsequent teacher signals
Does not explore intermediate granularities such as step-level or segment-level weighting aligned with chain-of-thought structure
failure_modes: Over-filtering (p=40%) discards useful training signals, hurting challenging benchmarks significantly
Small α values (≤0.5) degrade performance by under-weighting teacher confidence
2606.02684.relevance_to_opd: Directly proposes a novel OPD method that jointly optimizes trajectory-level filtering and token-level soft reweighting, addressing granularity isolation and hard selection limitations in existing OPD approaches

2606.03603.title: World Models Meet Language Models: On the Complementarity of Concrete and Abstract Reasoning
2606.03603.summary: On-policy self-distillation using privileged future videos to teach MLLMs when to invoke/verify/rely on world-model rollouts

method.training_loop: Stage 1: protocol SFT on structured trajectories from Gemini teacher. Stage 2: student generates on-policy trajectories, privileged evaluator scores with ground-truth future video/answer, advantage-weighted KL distillation back to student.
method.loss_formulation: L = L_SFT + L_disc + L_text + λ_call * E[N_sim], where L_disc = D_KL(sg[q_t^*] || π_θ) and L_text = -Σ sg[w_{t,k}] log π_θ(a_k)
method.data_source: VRQABench (4000 train puzzles from VR-Bench) and OpenWorldQA (3904 train real-world anchor-frame questions)
key_components: privileged future evaluator with ground-truth video/answer
on-policy trajectory generation
advantage-weighted distillation at intermediate decision nodes
simulation decision gating
rollout verification and reliance control

2606.03603.novelty: Uses ground-truth future videos as teacher-side privileged context only during training to score on-policy concrete-reasoning trajectories at intermediate simulation-control decision nodes, enabling advantage-weighted self-distillation for world-model invocation/verification/reliance without requiring true futures at test time.

on_policy_mechanism.evidence_quote: For each training example, the student first generates a base trajectory τ_s under the student-view context c = (o,q,options), which excludes the ground-truth future v∗ and answer y∗. At each decision node t with prefix h^s_t, we build a candidate set C_t.

opd_classification.reasoning: The core contribution is on-policy self-distillation using privileged information (ground-truth future videos/answers) as teacher-side context to calibrate student's own trajectories—distillation IS the method.

key_findings: PF-OPSD improves over SFT baseline by 10.6% on VRQABench and 10.9% on OpenWorldQA
Workflow Agent with world-model access but no PF-OPSD training performs worse than image-only supervised model
PF-OPSD reduces rollout acceptance from 92.5% for high-quality rollouts to 5.2% for corrupted ones, demonstrating learned verification
Removing advantage weighting drops accuracy by 6.0% on VRQABench and 5.3% on OpenWorldQA
Cross-world-model transfer shows PF-OPSD with Helios outperforms always-simulate with stronger Wan 2.2 model
2606.03603.ablations_summary: Removing simulation decision forces all samples through noisy rollouts (-3.9%/-3.3%). Removing rollout verification causes largest drop (-7.2%/-5.7%). Removing rollout reliance (-4.6%/-4.0%). Removing advantage weighting (-6.0%/-5.3%). Answer-only distillation without intermediate node supervision (-7.9%/-6.7%).
limitations: Conclusions most applicable when world model can produce partially relevant futures
Experiments do not exhaust all forms of physical reasoning or all world-model designs
Specialized domains, longer temporal horizons, and interactive environments may require additional coverage
Depends on availability and alignment of training-time privileged signals (ground-truth future videos)
failure_modes: Multi-attempt retry cases (2-3 attempts) show lower accuracy and higher misjudgment rate
When rollouts are poorly aligned with input scene, model cannot fully compensate
Simulation Inertia: models under-invoke world model even when simulation would help
Forced-Simulation Paradox: providing rollouts unconditionally can hurt performance
2606.03603.relevance_to_opd: Directly implements on-policy self-distillation where the student generates trajectories during training and a privileged evaluator (with ground-truth future context) provides advantage-weighted targets for intermediate decision nodes, exemplifying OPD with privileged information.

2606.03089.title: Constitutional On-Policy Safe Distillation
2606.03089.summary: Two-stage on-policy distillation framework mitigating safety-expressiveness collapse via Cross-SFT teacher calibration

method.training_loop: Stage 1: Cross-SFT cold-start calibrates teacher on mixed safety+expressiveness data. Stage 2: Student rollouts evaluated by constitution-conditioned teacher providing token-level reverse-KL rewards, optimized via clipped surrogate (GRPO-style).
method.loss_formulation: L = E[sum_t min(rho_t * A_hat(i,t), clip(rho_t, 1-eps, 1+eps) * A_hat(i,t))] where r(i,t) = log P_S(y_t|x,y<t) - log P_T(y_t|x,c_safe,y<t)
method.data_source: 9K multi-objective dataset: BeaverTails-V (2K), SPA-VL (2K), MM-RLHF Safety (1K), MMPR (2K), MM-RLHF General (1K), 300 over-refusal queries
key_components: Cross-SFT Cold-Start teacher calibration
Constitution-conditioned on-policy distillation
Token-level reverse-KL reward
Hybrid outcome-weighted advantage variant
Geometric leakage analysis

2606.03089.novelty: Identifies that safety OPSD collapses via geometric leakage (not shortcut copying as in reasoning tasks) where safety boundary pressure spills into expressiveness dimension through non-orthogonal coupling, and resolves it with Cross-SFT teacher calibration before on-policy distillation

on_policy_mechanism.evidence_quote: Sample queries x ∼ D and collect G trajectories {y(i) 1:T}G i=1 ∼ π_old(·|x). Compute token-level Reverse KL distillation penalty: r(i,t) = −(log π_old(y(i)_t|x,y(i)<t) − log π_T(y(i)_t|x,C,y(i)<t))

opd_classification.reasoning: Core contribution is on-policy self-distillation with privileged information (safety constitution) as the teacher signal source; the distillation IS the method and removing it eliminates the contribution.

key_findings: COPSD(Standard) achieves +27.8% safety and +31.3% helpfulness win-rate gains on BeaverTails-V for Qwen3-VL-4B while limiting MathVista reasoning loss to 2.1% vs 17.5% for GRPO
Safety OPSD collapses through geometric leakage rather than shortcut copying, with lexical overlap remaining below 0.08 across all variants
COPSD student surpasses its own SFT teacher on both safety and effectiveness metrics, breaking the teacher ceiling
COPSD(Standard) on Qwen2.5-VL-7B achieves +40.5% safety and +43.3% helpfulness on BeaverTails-V
2606.03089.ablations_summary: Teacher SFT epochs: 2-epoch optimal, 5-epoch causes diversity collapse and safety drops from 77.76% to 55.69%. Self-generated data removal maintains safety but degrades MathVista from 72.70% to 64.60%. Constitution ratio in RL data has limited effect; teacher distribution geometry is the main bottleneck.
limitations: Framework explored primarily on multimodal VLMs (Qwen3-VL-4B and Qwen2.5-VL-7B)
Teacher SFT requires careful epoch tuning to avoid over-optimization
Mixed-teacher distillation underperforms single calibrated teacher
failure_modes: Over-training SFT teacher (5 epochs) causes catastrophic collapse of safety scores
Removing self-generated data leads to geometric misalignment between teacher patterns and model's internal reasoning manifolds
Hybrid teacher configuration slows convergence rather than providing coherent alignment direction

theory.theoretical_claim: Safety OPSD collapse is caused by geometric leakage: safety boundary pressure transfers into expressiveness dimension through non-orthogonal coupling ρ>0, formalized as v_H ≈ -ρβλ/(1-ρ²) ReLU(y_S - y_S_limit)
theory.proof_sketch: Model teacher as energy-based distribution in non-orthogonal 2D semantic subspace (safety, expressiveness). Natural gradient descent under metric tensor G with off-diagonal coupling ρ shows safety boundary gradient leaks into expressiveness axis via inverse metric, unlike verifiable tasks where Mahalanobis attractor cancels cross-coupling exactly.

2606.03089.relevance_to_opd: Directly addresses on-policy self-distillation for safety alignment, identifying a novel failure mode specific to safety (geometric leakage vs shortcut copying in reasoning), and proposes a teacher calibration stage (Cross-SFT) to fix the teacher distribution before performing standard on-policy distillation

2606.03532.title: When Should the Teacher Move? Temporal Coupling and Stability in Self On-Policy Distillation
2606.03532.summary: Adaptive teacher refresh gating for stable self on-policy distillation

method.training_loop: GRPO policy gradient + KL(student||self-teacher) distillation; teacher is a frozen copy of student refreshed only when isolation, reward-improvement, and length-tail gates all pass
method.loss_formulation: L_t = -E_{x~pi_theta}[r(x)] + lambda * KL(pi_theta || pi_phi)
method.data_source: SciKnowEval (Chemistry, Biology, Physics) and ToolAlpaca
key_components: isolation gate (minimum freeze period)
reward gate (ratchet improvement threshold)
length-tail gate (seqlen tail ratio safety)
hard teacher refresh conditioned on consolidation

2606.03532.novelty: Identifies isolation periods (not teacher age) as the key stability property for self on-policy distillation, uncovers state-oblivious collapse in fixed-interval hard refresh, and proposes CGTR which gates each teacher refresh on joint reward-improvement and length-tail safety evidence

on_policy_mechanism.evidence_quote: Self on-policy distillation trains a student policy against a teacher derived from its own parameter history, yet the teacher's update schedule—which governs the temporal coupling between teacher and student—has not been systematically studied

opd_classification.reasoning: Core contribution is a curriculum/scheduling mechanism (CGTR) that adaptively controls when the self-teacher refreshes during on-policy distillation, making it primarily a stability/scheduling technique (§6.2) for self-distillation (§5.3.2) with an adaptive objective component (§4.2).

key_findings: M=50 fixed refresh collapses catastrophically at step 189 (test mean@16 → 0.000) while CGTR achieves 0.806 with zero collapse on Chemistry 300-step training

Isolation periods, not teacher age, are the structural property enabling stable self on-policy distillation (lag-aligned EMA α=0.04 matches M=50 age but produces worse entropy stability: 0.727 vs 0.499)
CGTR achieves best final score on all four tasks (Chemistry 0.806, Biology 0.485, Physics 0.703, ToolUse 0.536) with a single shared parameter set and no per-dataset tuning
State-oblivious collapse is mechanistically distinct from EMA's chronic contamination and invisible under short-horizon evaluation
2606.03532.ablations_summary: Removing reward gate causes collapse at step 218 (testfin=0.000); removing isolation gate quadruples refresh rate (12 vs 3) and degrades final score to 0.731; removing length-tail gate allows one premature refresh dropping final score by 0.035. Hyperparameter sensitivity on Biology shows testfin varies only 0.022 across all threshold variants with zero collapse.
limitations: Experiments on single model family (Qwen3-8B) across four tasks at moderate scale
Reward gate relies on binary correctness signal; denser or learned rewards not explored
Extension to larger models, longer horizons, and broader task types remains open
failure_modes: State-oblivious collapse: fixed-interval hard refresh copies transiently drifting student into teacher irreversibly
Reference collapse: tight synchronization (M≤2) makes KL penalty vacuous
Chronic contamination: EMA accumulates student drift unboundedly over long horizons
2606.03532.relevance_to_opd: Directly studies the teacher update schedule in self on-policy distillation, identifying structural requirements (isolation periods + state awareness) and proposing an adaptive gating mechanism (CGTR) that stabilizes long-horizon self-distillation training

2606.03620.title: Physics-Guided Policy Optimization with Self-Distillation
2606.03620.summary: Adaptive step-size modulation for self-distilled policy optimization via mutual-information signal

method.training_loop: SDPO loop: student generates rollouts, receives feedback, distills from feedback-conditioned self-teacher; PGPO adds per-batch mutual-information multiplier ρ_k to gradient step
method.loss_formulation: L = D_KL(π_θ(·|x,y_{<t}) || stopgrad(π_θ(·|x,f,y_{<t})))
method.data_source: Science Q&A dataset (Chemistry, Physics, Biology, Materials Science)
key_components: information-modulated step-size multiplier
mutual information estimate between student predictions and feedback-conditioned teacher
physics-inspired viscosity analogy
bounded exponential multiplier with cap ρ_max

2606.03620.novelty: Introduces a per-batch adaptive step-size multiplier derived from mutual information between student predictions and feedback-conditioned self-teacher, grounded in viscous-fluid dynamics SDE analogy, to address credit assignment in SDPO

on_policy_mechanism.evidence_quote: In self-distilled policy optimization (SDPO), the student π_θ generates responses, receives feedback f_i, and distills from a self-teacher that retrospectively corrects mistakes

opd_classification.reasoning: Core contribution is a per-batch token/information weighting mechanism (adaptive step-size modulation) for on-policy self-distillation, fitting §6.1 (token/sample weighting for efficiency/stability).

key_findings: PGPO outperforms SDPO in 3 of 4 scientific domains with gains up to +4.51 points (Materials Science).
PGPO remains stable in settings where SDPO collapses late in training.
The physics-guided multiplier preserves order-1 weak SDE approximation guarantees with negligible overhead per iteration.
Sensitivity parameter α varies in effectiveness across domains; no single α is universally optimal.
2606.03620.ablations_summary: Sensitivity parameter α ablation shows α=1.0 best for Chemistry, α=1.5 best for Physics and Materials, but no α setting matches SDPO for Biology; α=0.5 generally underperforms.
limitations: Modulates step size at batch level only; finer per-token modulation not explored
Sensitive to choice of sensitivity parameter α
Biology domain shows slight decline with no α matching SDPO
Preliminary experiments on single dataset only
failure_modes: In Biology domain, PGPO underperforms SDPO across all α settings tested
Low α=0.5 causes significant degradation in Biology (52.00 vs 61.62)

theory.theoretical_claim: PGPO admits an order-1 weak SDE approximation with modulated drift
theory.proof_sketch: Since ρ is bounded and Lipschitz in I, the modified drift inherits Lipschitz and linear-growth conditions; result follows by applying Li et al. 2017 to the modified drift with unchanged diffusion coefficient.

2606.03620.relevance_to_opd: Directly extends on-policy self-distillation (SDPO) with adaptive step-size modulation, addressing credit assignment in the OPD training loop where the student generates its own rollouts and distills from a feedback-conditioned version of itself.

2606.04036.title: Self-Distilled Policy Gradient
2606.04036.summary: Combines full-vocabulary on-policy self-distillation with RLVR policy gradient and KL regularization

method.training_loop: For each step: sample rollouts from current policy without privileged context; compute binary verifier rewards and group-relative advantages; compute full-vocab reverse-KL OPD loss between student (no context) and teacher (privileged context) gated by positive advantage; add unnormalized KL regularization to reference policy; update θ.
method.loss_formulation: L_SDPG = L_out + β(k) L+_OPD + α L_K(π_θ, π_ref)
method.data_source: DAPO-Math-17k dataset with privileged solutions generated by Gemini 2.5 Pro
key_components: full-vocabulary reverse-KL on-policy self-distillation
positive-advantage gating
warmup-decay β schedule
unnormalized KL regularization to reference policy
REINFORCE-style outcome loss with group-relative advantage

2606.04036.novelty: Derives exact policy-gradient interpretation of reverse-KL full-vocabulary OPD, then combines gated self-distillation (same model with privileged context) with RLVR outcome rewards and unnormalized KL reference regularization, adding positive-advantage gating and warmup-decay schedule to stabilize training.

on_policy_mechanism.evidence_quote: Sample a group of G responses {y(i)}G i=1 ∼πθ(·|xj) // Rollout from the frozen unprivileged behavior policy ... Compute p=πθ(·|sj,i,t), q=SG[πθ(·|cj,sj,i,t)]

opd_classification.reasoning: Core contribution is on-policy self-distillation where the teacher is the same model conditioned on privileged information (PI from ground-truth answers), combined with RL outcome rewards; removing the distillation term loses the main contribution.

key_findings: SDPG-UFKL achieves 0.408 on AIME24 (best) vs 0.316 for GRPO and 0.395 for RLSD on Qwen3-4B.
SDPG-UFKL maintains substantially higher actor entropy throughout training, avoiding the entropy collapse observed in RLSD.
On Qwen3-1.7B, SDPG-UFKL achieves 0.212 best on AIME24 vs 0.115 for GRPO and 0.199 for RLSD.
Pure self-distillation baseline OPCD exhibits sharp degradation after step 250 on Qwen3-1.7B, confirming need for verifier coupling.
2606.04036.ablations_summary: Removing OPD term (β=0) loses early-training accuracy advantage on AIME24/25; removing KL regularization (α=0) achieves comparable accuracy but causes severely shortened response length and rising entropy, indicating policy instability.
limitations: Privileged OPD target may remain biased by information unavailable at inference due to irreducible conditional mutual-information gap
Training dataset with moderate difficulty needed to activate distillation signal via positive-advantage gating
failure_modes: Pure self-distillation without verifier can reinforce locally plausible tokens on globally wrong trajectories
OPCD (pure self-distillation) exhibits training collapse on smaller models after step 250

theory.theoretical_claim: Fixed-prefix reverse-KL OPD gradient equals detached-sampling policy-gradient surrogate with centered log-ratio advantage
theory.proof_sketch: Show student-side gradient of D_KL(p_t||q̄_t) equals E_{a~p̄_t}[A^dist_t(a) ∇logp_t(a)] where A^dist_t = SG[D̄_t - log(p̄_t(a)/q̄_t(a))] by adding valid baseline 1+D̄_t, using E[∇logp_t(a)]=0 at current iterate.

2606.04036.relevance_to_opd: Directly proposes an on-policy self-distillation framework where the student generates rollouts during training and receives dense full-vocabulary KL supervision from itself conditioned on privileged context, combined with sparse verifier rewards.

2606.04694.title: DuDi: Dual-Signal Distillation with Cross-Lingual Verbalizer
2606.04694.summary: Dual-signal multilingual distillation combining sequence-level and token-level signals with cross-lingual verbalizer for SEA SLMs

method.training_loop: Cold-start SFT → online training: student generates rollouts y'~π_θ(x) for sequence signal (SPIN) and ỹ~π_θ(p_z,x) for on-policy KD with cross-lingual verbalizer; teacher provides token-level logits on both off-policy (ground-truth) and on-policy (student-generated) sequences
method.loss_formulation: L_DuDi = α E[L_SPIN(x,y,y';π_θ,π_Ref)] + (1-λ) E[L_Off-KD(x,y;π_θ,π_θT)] + λ E[L_On-KD(x,ỹ,z;π_θ,π_θT)]
method.data_source: SEA-Instruct (28,000 samples, 4,000 per language across 7 SEA languages)
key_components: online sequence-level SPIN objective
off-policy token-level KD
on-policy token-level KD with student rollouts
cross-lingual verbalizer for teacher-student transfer

2606.04694.novelty: Unifies online self-play sequence signal with dual off-policy/on-policy token-level KD, plus a novel cross-lingual verbalizer that improves teacher-student logit overlap for multilingual settings, outperforming English-only or multilingual-only verbalizers

on_policy_mechanism.evidence_quote: the student generates its own responses ỹ ∼ π_θ(x), while the teacher provides token-level signals for guiding the student output logits to correct their self-generated mistakes.

opd_classification.reasoning: Core contribution is on-policy knowledge distillation with a cross-lingual verbalizer enhancing white-box teacher logit transfer to student on student-generated rollouts.

key_findings: DuDi achieves 10.1 average on SEA-HELM for Qwen2.5-0.5B, outperforming the strongest baseline DFT (9.7) by 0.4 points.
DuDi improves over GKD by 5.2%, 15.6%, and 7.5% on Qwen2.5-1.5B, Qwen3-0.6B-Base, and Llama3.2-1B respectively.
Removing off-policy KD causes the largest performance drop of 24.6%, while removing on-policy KD causes 6.6% drop.
Cross-lingual verbalizer achieves highest teacher-student overlap ratio throughout training compared to all other verbalizer variants.
Reverse KL substantially outperforms JSD (-23.8%) and forward KL (-37.8%) as KD objective.
2606.04694.ablations_summary: Off-policy KD is most critical (-24.6%), followed by on-policy KD (-6.6%), cross-lingual verbalizer (-5.0%), sequence signal (-4.7%), and English in verbalizer (-3.3%). All components are complementary.
limitations: Experiments limited to SEA languages; findings may not generalize to other language families or tasks beyond SEA-HELM.
Teacher model must share output vocabulary with student, constraining cross-family distillation options.
Limited gains on Burmese due to small teacher-student gap and weak teacher performance.
failure_modes: Burmese shows limited improvement due to smaller teacher-student gap and low teacher performance.
DFT as cold-start initialization degrades all subsequent distillation methods.
Multilingual verbalizer increases teacher-student mismatch, performing worst among verbalizer variants.
2606.04694.relevance_to_opd: DuDi is a direct on-policy distillation method combining student-generated rollouts with teacher logit supervision, extending GKD with cross-lingual verbalizer and sequence-level self-play signal for multilingual SLMs.

2606.04703.title: Rethinking Continual Experience Internalization for Self-Evolving LLM Agents
2606.04703.summary: Systematic study of stable multi-iteration experience internalization for self-evolving LLM agents

method.training_loop: Iterative loop: student generates trajectories → experience extracted → experience-aware teacher produces supervision (off-policy rejection-sampled or on-policy) → student trained via context-distillation → repeat
method.loss_formulation: L_off(θ) = E_{H~πT} Σ_t D_KL(p_t ∥ q_t); L_on(θ) = E_{H~πθ} Σ_t D_KL(q_t ∥ p_t)
method.data_source: 15K web-reasoning QA corpus from WebWalkerQA-silver, DeepDive, WebShaper, WebDancer, SailorFog-QA
key_components: principle-level experience granularity
step-wise experience injection
off-policy context-distillation with rejection sampling
iterative self-evolution loop

2606.04703.novelty: Identifies progressive capability collapse in multi-iteration on-policy context-distillation and proposes a stable recipe combining principle-level experience, step-wise injection, and off-policy distillation that sustains gains across self-evolution iterations

on_policy_mechanism.evidence_quote: In on-policy context-distillation, trajectories are generated by the student and the teacher supervises student-induced states with reverse KL

opd_classification.reasoning: Core contribution is a curriculum/recipe for stable multi-iteration context-distillation comparing on-policy vs off-policy regimes, experience granularity, and injection patterns—fitting stability/curriculum design for on-policy distillation.

key_findings: On-policy context-distillation suffers progressive capability collapse across iterations, falling below base model performance by iteration 3
Principle-level experience provides durable internalization signal (84% contain reusable strategies vs 3.7% for instance-level)
Step-wise injection achieves 31.2% vs 23.2% (global) on WebWalkerQA in single iteration with self-generated experience
Off-policy context-distillation with step-wise principle-level experience sustains gains across 3 iterations (16.6→33.1% on WebWalkerQA)
Global injection causes 63.82% premature-answer rate at iteration 3 vs 0% for step-wise injection
2606.04703.ablations_summary: Three dimensions ablated: experience granularity (instance vs principle), injection pattern (global vs step-wise), and internalization regime (on-policy vs off-policy). Each contributes to stability; combining all three yields sustained multi-iteration improvement.
limitations: Experiments limited to web-reasoning agent tasks; generalization to other domains untested
Only three dimensions studied; experience-pool size, selector quality, and filtering criteria not explored
failure_modes: Instance-level experience causes performance collapse below base model by iteration 3
Global injection leads to premature answering (63.82% rate)
On-policy context-distillation produces trajectory inflation (21.9 avg turns vs 4.5 for teacher)
2606.04703.relevance_to_opd: Directly studies on-policy context-distillation for LLM agents, showing its failure mode under iterative self-evolution and proposing off-policy distillation as a more stable alternative; provides empirical comparison of on-policy vs off-policy distillation regimes

2606.05122.title: Self-Evaluation Is Already There: Eliciting Latent Judge Calibration in Base LLMs with Minimal Data
2606.05122.summary: Eliciting latent self-evaluation ability from base LLMs via cyclic RL and masked judge distillation

method.training_loop: Alternate: (1) GRPO RL with reward combining quality + calibration on full response; (2) Masked SFT distilling judge scores into self-eval tokens only, on model's own rollouts. Repeat 15 cycles.
