method.loss_formulation: r = w_q * (1/3 * sum(j_a/9)) + w_c * (1 - MAE(s,j)/9)^gamma for RL; cross-entropy on self-eval score tokens only for distillation
method.data_source: 160 unique HelpSteer2-derived training prompts
key_components: Calibration-Coupled RL with GRPO
Masked Judge Distillation on self-eval tokens only
Stratified round-robin sampling over attribute-score bins
Nonlinear calibration exponent gamma

2606.05122.novelty: Combines on-policy RL with masked distillation of judge scores into self-evaluation tokens only, showing base LLMs already approximate external judge scores and can be elicited with ~160 examples (31x fewer than RL baseline)

on_policy_mechanism.evidence_quote: the distillation phase takes the rollouts collected during the first RL phase and trains on the judge's actual scores, with the loss restricted to the self-evaluation tokens, leaving the answer itself unchanged. The second phase thus amounts to on-policy distillation of the judge into the self-evaluation channel

opd_classification.reasoning: The core method is on-policy distillation of an external judge's scores into the model's self-evaluation tokens on the model's own rollouts, with RL augmenting the distillation cycle rather than being the sole contribution.

key_findings: Base Qwen3-4B already predicts external judge scores with calibration 0.50-0.70 before any targeted training.
SEE improves calibration by 0.25-0.66 MAE across benchmarks from only 160 unique examples (~31x fewer than RL baseline).
SEE reaches Adapted RLCR's final quality/calibration after ~0.8k sample-passes (~12x fewer).
Gains transfer to held-out judges (Claude Sonnet 4.6, Gemini 3.1 Flash-Lite) never seen during training.
Top-5 token accuracy reaches 0.878 on HelpSteer2 validation and 0.908 on AlpacaEval 2.0.
2606.05122.ablations_summary: Comparison of SEE vs Adapted RLCR (RL-only without distillation phase) shows the masked distillation phase is critical for calibration improvement. Per-attribute analysis shows improvement across all five attributes. Score-range analysis shows balanced coverage resampling helps extreme scores.
limitations: Evidence from a single base model (Qwen3-4B-Base) only
Cross-judge tests use LLM judges only, no human evaluation
Quality and calibration targets defined by LLM judge, inheriting its biases
Single data scale tested (160 examples, 15 cycles)
No multi-seed error bars or confidence intervals reported
failure_modes: Judge-independence verified only among LLM judges, not against human preference
Scaling behavior with more data, cycles, or larger models remains unknown
2606.05122.relevance_to_opd: SEE performs on-policy distillation of an external judge's multi-attribute scores into the student's self-evaluation tokens, using the student's own rollouts generated during training. The masked distillation phase is explicitly described as on-policy distillation of the judge.

2606.05152.title: Reinforcement Learning from Rich Feedback with Distributional DAgger
2606.05152.summary: Distributional DAgger variant for on-policy self-distillation with forward cross-entropy and future-aware credit assignment

method.training_loop: Sample rollouts from student policy, compute forward cross-entropy between feedback-conditioned teacher and student on visited states, compute future-credit term via REINFORCE, update with PPO-style trust region
method.data_source: SciKnowEval L3 (science), LiveCodeBench v6 (coding), CMU AIRe POPE-HARD + OmniMath (math)
key_components: forward cross-entropy objective
future-aware credit assignment via REINFORCE
feedback-conditioned self-teacher (EMA)
PPO-style trust-region update
top-K teacher token truncation

2606.05152.novelty: Proves f-divergence self-distillation (reverse-KL/JS) lacks monotonic policy improvement guarantee; proposes forward cross-entropy with full sequence-level gradients (future-credit term) that guarantees monotonic improvement and sublinear regret

on_policy_mechanism.evidence_quote: Sample rollout y_j ~ π_{θ_i}(·|x) and collect feedback f_j. Set state s_t ← (x, y_{j,<t}). Compute future credit C^{fut}_{j,t}

opd_classification.reasoning: Core contribution is a new forward cross-entropy divergence objective for on-policy self-distillation with monotonic improvement guarantees, fitting adaptive divergence/objective design

key_findings: DistIL achieves best avg@16 on science benchmarks with gains up to 9.6 points over next-best method at 5h on OLMo3
On hard math (AIME25), DistIL leads next-best by 3.8 points on Qwen3-4B and 1.4 points on Qwen3-8B
DistIL achieves Accuracy/Avg@16=0.656 and Score/Avg@16=0.482 on coding, outperforming SDPO (0.643, 0.467) and GRPO (0.600, 0.405)
GRPO exactly matches base model on hard math where pass rate is zero, confirming zero-advantage failure
Forward cross-entropy guarantees monotonic policy improvement (Proposition 4) while reverse-KL can decrease reward even with better teacher (Proposition 2)
2606.05152.ablations_summary: Future credit assignment is critical: removing it (CE baseline with local-only gradients) leads to higher variance and strictly worse performance. Top-100 teacher tokens outperforms Top-1 and Full distribution distillation.

theory.theoretical_claim: Forward cross-entropy guarantees monotonic policy improvement (Prop 4); sublinear O(n^{-1/4}) regret bound (Theorem 1); forward CE maximizes teacher-weighted lower bound on log-likelihood of success (Prop 5)

2606.10385.title: Beyond Absolute Imitation: Anchored Residual Guidance for Privileged On-Policy Distillation
2606.10385.summary: AR-OPD: anchor + oracle residual splits privileged signal to prevent hindsight leakage

method.training_loop: Student generates on-policy rollouts. Oracle privileged signal decomposed into: (1) locally-achievable anchor target (no hindsight required), (2) oracle foresight as controlled residual adjustment. L = L_anchor(rollout, anchor) + alpha * L_residual(rollout, oracle_foresight). Prevents student from learning locally-unsupported shortcuts.
method.loss_formulation: L_AR-OPD = L_imitation(student_rollout, anchor) + alpha * delta_guidance(oracle_foresight); anchor = locally achievable sub-target; oracle_foresight = residual oracle signal

Hindsight leakage reduction

2606.09091.summary: Global KL normalization to batch-relative advantages stabilizes OPD gradient magnitudes

method.training_loop: Standard on-policy KL distillation loop for MLLM. Compute per-token KL(student || teacher). 2606.10369.title: PADD: Path-Aligned Decompression Distillation for Non-Router Teacher to Guide MoE Student Learning
2606.10369.summary: Dense-to-MoE distillation via neuron clustering, online adaptive KD, path-refined GRPO, and reward-augmented load balancing

method.training_loop: Stage I: cluster teacher FFN neurons → init student experts + warmup with frozen routers. Stages II-IV (unified loop): forward=online adaptive distillation adjusting teacher temperature by student advantage; backward=PR-GRPO suppressing routing-shift gradients; update=reward-augmented load balancing bias.
method.loss_formulation: L_warmup = L_LM + α*L_KD + β*L_init; J_PR-GRPO(θ) = E[min(ρ̂·exp(-λΓ·I(A<0))·A, clip(...)·A)]
method.data_source: DeepScaleR math training dataset
key_components: neuron-cluster-based expert initialization
online adaptive distillation with advantage-temperature coupling
PR-GRPO path-refined policy optimization
reward-augmented load balancing

2606.10369.novelty: First unified framework for dense-to-MoE distillation that recovers implicit routing from router-less teachers via neuron clustering initialization, advantage-coupled adaptive temperature, routing-shift-aware gradient suppression (PR-GRPO), and reward-augmented expert bias, addressing router cold start, path rupture, capacity gap, and expert homogenization simultaneously.

on_policy_mechanism.evidence_quote: for group size G and input x, we sample G student responses y1,...,yG. Let r(x,yi) be the reward for yi, and r̄ and σr be the mean and standard deviation of group rewards. The student's within-group relative advantage is Ai,S = (r(x,yi) − r̄)/σr. Since the teacher has no explicit router, we adjust teacher log-probabilities based on Ai,S's assessment of the student path.

opd_classification.reasoning: The core contribution is an adaptive online distillation mechanism that dynamically adjusts teacher temperature based on student on-policy rollout performance (advantage-temperature coupling), making it an adaptive-objective on-policy distillation method.

key_findings: PADD achieves 80.2% average accuracy on Qwen family, surpassing the 7B teacher's 77.7% with only 3.3B active parameters.
PADD improves over MoE-Vanilla-GRPO by 8.8% and 8.4% on Qwen and DeepSeek families respectively.
PR-GRPO reduces router-shift by ~47% relative to Vanilla-GRPO, stabilizing MoE routing during RL training.
Stage I neuron clustering achieves NMI 0.030 vs 0.013 for Vanilla-GRPO, demonstrating effective expert specialization.
PADD best preserves general capabilities (52.0% vs 49.3% Vanilla-GRPO) under math-only training on Qwen family.
2606.10369.ablations_summary: Removing Stage I causes largest drop (-6.1% Qwen avg), followed by Stage II (-5.1%), Stage III (-2.6%), Stage IV (-1.5%). All stages are necessary; Stages I and II are most critical for knowledge transfer, Stage III stabilizes routing, Stage IV refines expert quality balance.
limitations: Only evaluated on mathematical reasoning domain with math-only training
Uses domain-specialized 7B teachers; scaling to larger teachers may require offline logit caching or progressive distillation
Complementary to sparse upcycling rather than a substitute; composing both pipelines requires aligned starting checkpoints
Stage IV shows minimal effect on DeepSeek family average
failure_modes: Without Stage I, router cold start causes random noise diffusion across experts on high-difficulty benchmarks (OlympiadBench drops 10.4 points)
Fixed-temperature distillation (without Stage II) fails to bridge capacity gap for long reasoning chains

compute_efficiency.teacher_inference_cost: 1× (teacher queried once per 8 student forward passes)

2606.10369.relevance_to_opd: PADD is an on-policy distillation method where the MoE student generates rollouts during training and receives adaptive teacher logit supervision along its own routing paths. The teacher temperature is dynamically adjusted based on the student's on-policy advantage, making this a clear instance of online on-policy knowledge distillation with architectural mismatch (dense→MoE).

2606.17199.title: PowerOPD: Stabilizing On-Policy Distillation with Bounded Power Transformation
2606.17199.summary: Bounded power-transformed rewards for on-policy distillation replacing unbounded log-ratio

method.training_loop: Student generates rollouts, compute token-level reward r_t = sg[pi_T(o_t|c_t)^alpha - pi_theta(o_t|c_t)^alpha], update student with policy gradient
method.loss_formulation: r^α_t = sg[π_T(o_t|c_t)^α − π_θ(o_t|c_t)^α], α > 0
method.data_source: DeepScaleR mathematical reasoning dataset
key_components: Box-Cox power transformation reward
bounded sign-consistent reward design
sampled-token policy gradient OPD

2606.17199.novelty: Replaces unbounded log-ratio OPD reward with Box-Cox power family reward (p^α - q^α) that is natively bounded in [-1,1] and sign-consistent, avoiding post-hoc stabilization failures

on_policy_mechanism.evidence_quote: It trains a student policy πθ to match a stronger teacher policy πT on trajectories generated by the student itself.

opd_classification.reasoning: Core contribution is a new bounded reward function (divergence/objective) for on-policy distillation replacing the unbounded log-ratio reward.

key_findings: PowerOPD achieves +6.37 Avg@8 and +5.71 Pass@8 over vanilla OPD in the best configuration (Qwen3-0.6B with Qwen3-4B teacher).
PowerOPD surpasses full-vocabulary OPD by up to +2.59 Avg@8 and +8.90 Pass@8 while reducing wall-clock time by 59.2% and peak GPU memory by 23.1%.
PowerOPD keeps gradient norms more than 3,000× smaller than vanilla OPD's initial spike.
Larger α generally improves accuracy, shortens responses, and stabilizes training dynamics without additional supervision.
PowerOPD achieves 10× sample efficiency over vanilla OPD on MATH-500 (same accuracy with 10× fewer steps).
2606.17199.ablations_summary: Sweep over α from 0.1 to 500 shows larger α improves accuracy and shortens responses; post-hoc methods (Clip, Tanh, Z-Score) partially help but cannot match natively bounded rewards; Z-Score can underperform vanilla OPD due to sign consistency violation.
limitations: Experiments conducted primarily on mathematical reasoning benchmarks and Qwen3-based teacher-student pairs
Not validated on code generation, general instruction following, or multilingual reasoning
failure_modes: Z-Score normalization can underperform vanilla OPD by flipping reward signs
Post-hoc stabilization methods fail to resolve early-position extreme rewards and delayed convergence

theory.theoretical_claim: Log-ratio reward is degenerate α→0 limit of Box-Cox family; any α>0 guarantees boundedness in [-1,1] and sign consistency by construction
theory.proof_sketch: Box-Cox h_α(x) = (x^α - 1)/α → log x as α→0; for α>0, p^α,q^α ∈ [0,1] so reward p^α - q^α ∈ [-1,1] (P1), and x^α strictly increasing implies sign consistency (P2)

2606.17199.relevance_to_opd: Directly addresses core OPD reward design by identifying unbounded log-ratio as root cause of training pathologies and proposing a natively bounded alternative reward family for on-policy distillation

2606.24143.novelty: First systematic study of staleness in async OPD showing forward KL is robust while reverse KL is vulnerable; proposes multi-sample MC to reduce variance while preserving correctability, and shows async RL surrogates (DecPPO, M2PO) do not help OPD

on_policy_mechanism.evidence_quote: On-policy distillation (OPD) trains a student on its own rollouts guided by teacher feedback and is becoming increasingly important for large language model (LLM) post-training.

opd_classification.reasoning: Core contribution is compute-efficiency via async pipeline and multi-sample MC estimator design for on-policy distillation under staleness, fitting §6.3 (compute efficiency) with secondary relevance to adaptive objectives (§4.1) and token weighting/estimator design (§6.1).

key_findings: Forward KL is robust to stale rollouts while reverse KL degrades faster under staleness
Recomputing A_θ at learner time without clipping is the most effective reverse-KL surrogate; advanced async RL methods (DecPPO, M2PO) do not improve over it
Multi-sample MC (m=4+) reduces one-sample variance while preserving MC correctability
AsyncOPD improves training throughput by 1.6× to 3.8× over strict synchronous training while maintaining comparable accuracy
MC64 at staleness 128 leaves only 11.2% of one-sample sequence-level variance
2606.24143.ablations_summary: Ablations cover: (1) KL direction (forward vs reverse) under staleness showing forward is more robust; (2) 2×2 advantage×clipping grid showing A_θ without clipping is best; (3) async RL surrogates (DecPPO, M2PO) showing no improvement; (4) sparse top-k vs MC with/without IS showing MC+IS is superior; (5) multi-sample MC (m=1,4,16,64) showing m≥4 improves large-staleness behavior
limitations: Only studies sparse and MC estimators, not dense full-vocabulary KL in async setting
Experiments limited to a single 8-GPU node
Scaling to larger multi-node clusters remains future work
failure_modes: Reverse KL with stale top-k support is support-mismatched and cannot be corrected by reweighting
One-sample MC suffers from high variance at large staleness

theory.theoretical_claim: Reverse-KL OPD admits exact old-to-current importance-sampling identity; multi-sample MC reduces variance by 1/m at fixed-prefix level
theory.proof_sketch: D_R(θ;s) = -E_{a~p_θ}[A_θ(a,s)] = -E_{a~p_old}[ρ_θ(a,s)A_θ(a,s)] by importance sampling identity, with score-function baseline cancellation

2606.24143.relevance_to_opd: Directly studies the systems and estimator design for on-policy distillation under asynchronous execution, analyzing how staleness affects KL-based OPD objectives and proposing practical solutions

2606.26091.title: On-Policy Self-Distillation with Sampled Demonstrations Reduces Output Diversity
2606.26091.summary: Shows on-policy self-distillation with sampled demonstrations reduces rollout diversity via PCMI bias

method.training_loop: Student generates rollouts, teacher (EMA of student) conditioned on sampled correct demonstration scores each rollout token-by-token, student minimizes reverse KL to teacher + KL to base
method.loss_formulation: L = (1/N) sum_{y in Y(x)} E_{ycorr~C(x)} sum_t KL(pi_theta(·|x,y_{<t}) || sg[pi_{theta_bar}(·|x,ycorr,y_{<t})])
method.data_source: Self-generated rollouts + sampled correct demonstrations (student or external)
key_components: PCMI-based theoretical analysis
graph path-finding controlled task
functional diversity (pass@k)
semantic diversity metric

2606.26091.novelty: Proves optimal SDSD policy tilts base distribution by expected pointwise conditional mutual information (PCMI) rather than reward, amplifying probability gaps among equally correct rollouts unlike standard RL

on_policy_mechanism.evidence_quote: For each question x, the student policy generates a group of N rollouts y_n ~ pi_theta(·|x), Y(x) = {y_1, ..., y_N}.

opd_classification.reasoning: Paper is an analysis/theoretical characterization of on-policy self-distillation showing it causes diversity collapse via PCMI bias, identifying failure modes of existing OPD methods.

key_findings: SDSD achieves competitive or better pass@1 but substantially lower pass@16 than GRPO (78.7 vs 83.6 on ScienceQA average with Qwen3-8B)
Optimal SDSD policy tilts base distribution by expected PCMI, amplifying probability gaps among equally correct rollouts
On Harder Graphs requiring diverse strategies, SDSD completely fails while GRPO succeeds
Diverse external demonstrations still lead to diversity collapse in SDSD models
Token-level entropy is not a sufficient metric of diversity—fails to distinguish semantic diversity differences
2606.26091.ablations_summary: K=3 teacher ensemble adds only 5.8% wall-clock time but does not fix diversity collapse; external diverse demonstrations also fail to restore diversity; GRPO+diversity reward recovers both modes while SDSD collapses regardless of KL regularization strength
limitations: Does not analyze settings where teacher is conditioned on richer privileged signals (runtime errors, environmental feedback)
Theoretical analysis assumes teacher frozen at base policy, whereas practice uses EMA teacher
Derivation assumes demonstrations sampled from base policy, not fully self-generated setup
Sequence-level derivation; token-level extension discussed but compounds autoregressively
failure_modes: SDSD fails completely on out-of-distribution settings requiring diverse strategies (Harder Graphs)
Pass@k curves flatten—generating more rollouts fails to solve new problems
Even with diverse external demonstrations, student diversity collapses

theory.theoretical_claim: Optimal SDSD policy tilts base distribution by expected PCMI score, amplifying probability gaps among equally correct rollouts unlike standard RL which preserves ratios
theory.proof_sketch: Lagrangian optimization of reverse KL to context-conditioned teacher + KL regularization to base yields exponential tilt by E[PCMI]; ratio of two correct sequences includes exp(PCMI gap) multiplicative factor absent in RL

2606.26091.relevance_to_opd: Directly analyzes on-policy self-distillation methods (SDPO, OPSD, OPCD) and identifies a fundamental diversity collapse mechanism caused by PCMI-based feedback bias in sampled-demonstration OPD

2606.27814.title: ATOD: Annealed Turn-aware On-policy Distillation for Multi-turn Autonomous Agents
2606.27814.summary: Hybrid annealed OPD-RL schedule with turn-level disagreement-uncertainty reweighting for multi-turn agents

method.training_loop: Student rolls out trajectories on-policy; compute GRPO advantages from env reward + OPD advantages from teacher logprobs with T-DUR turn weights; anneal κ(OPD) down and ρ(RL) up; update via clipped surrogate
method.loss_formulation: A_t = κ(s) * (logπ_T(a_t|s_t) - logπ_θ(a_t|s_t)) * w_{k(t)} + ρ(s) * A^GRPO_t
method.data_source: ALFWorld, WebShop, Search-QA environment interactions
key_components: Annealed OPD-RL coefficient schedule
Turn-level Disagreement-Uncertainty Reweighting (T-DUR)
Soft-OR fusion of disagreement and entropy proxies
Clipped surrogate actor update with hybrid advantage

2606.27814.novelty: Combines OPD and GRPO into a single token-level advantage with annealed coefficients transitioning from teacher-dominated to reward-dominated training, plus a turn-level soft-OR reweighting mechanism (T-DUR) that focuses distillation on high-utility agent decision turns

on_policy_mechanism.evidence_quote: OPD trains the student on trajectories sampled from the student itself while using an external teacher distribution to provide dense token-level supervision

opd_classification.reasoning: ATOD combines on-policy distillation with RL through an annealed schedule (RL-augmented OPD objective §4.3), with T-DUR providing turn-level token weighting (§6.1) and adaptive coefficient annealing (§4.2)

eval: Search-QA (NaturalQuestions, TriviaQA, PopQA, HotpotQA, 2WikiMultiHopQA, MuSiQue, Bamboogle)

key_findings: ATOD improves average success rate by 3.03 points over OPD and 23.62 points over GRPO across three student sizes
ATOD surpasses teacher models by 2.16 points on average across all benchmarks
For 0.6B student, ATOD lifts ALFWorld performance from 0.78% to 82.81% (over 100× improvement vs vanilla)
Removing annealing causes the largest performance drop (e.g., 0.6B drops from 82.8% to 75.8% on ALFWorld)
Turn-level T-DUR outperforms both token-level reweighting and uniform weighting across all model sizes
2606.27814.ablations_summary: Annealing schedule is most critical (largest drop without it, especially for weaker students). Turn-level T-DUR outperforms token-level reweighting and uniform weighting. Both components contribute independently to final performance.

theory.theoretical_claim: Entropy proxy h_k is an unbiased estimator of average token entropy with variance O(1/N_k) via martingale difference argument
theory.proof_sketch: X_t = -logπ_θ(a_t|s_t) has E[X_t|F_{t-1}] = H(π_θ(·|s_t)), so D_t = X_t - H_t is a martingale difference with uncorrelated cross-terms, giving Var(avg) = O(1/N_k)

2606.27814.relevance_to_opd: Directly extends on-policy distillation for multi-turn agents by combining OPD with RL via annealed coefficients and introducing turn-level reweighting to focus teacher logit supervision on high-utility decision points in agent trajectories

2606.28562.title: SEAD: Competence-Aware On-Policy Distillation via Entropy-Guided Supervision
2606.28562.summary: Entropy-guided token/temporal/prompt-level adaptive supervision for on-policy distillation

method.training_loop: For each step: select prompts via competence-gated curriculum, student generates rollouts, teacher scores with logits, partition tokens into Zone A/B/C by joint entropy, apply RKL on Zone B + annealed FKL on Zone C, skip Zone A
method.loss_formulation: L_SEAD = 1/|B∪C| * (Σ_{t∈B} L_RKL(t) + α(t_step)·λ·Σ_{t∈C} L_FKL(t))
method.data_source: DAPO-Math-17K (deduplicated)
key_components: sparse entropy-adaptive token zone partitioning
competence-driven FKL-to-RKL cosine annealing
competence-gated curriculum (easy-to-hard prompt ordering)

2606.28562.novelty: Unifies token-level zone selection (joint teacher-student entropy → skip/RKL/FKL), temporal divergence annealing, and prompt-level curriculum into a symbiotic OPD framework; first curriculum for OPD; shows super-additive component interactions

on_policy_mechanism.evidence_quote: Each OPD iteration: (1) samples rollouts x∼π_θold(·|q); (2) queries teacher logits on the rollout; (3) updates π_θ via a divergence loss.

opd_classification.reasoning: SEAD's core contribution is token-level selection (zone partitioning skipping ~50% tokens) combined with adaptive divergence and curriculum, which are efficiency/stability techniques for OPD

key_findings: SEAD achieves +4.8 avg accuracy over vanilla OPD across six math benchmarks on OLMo-3 (7B→32B)
Token Zones + KL Annealing yields 20× amplification over either component alone (+4.52 vs +0.32/+0.22)
~50% of tokens (Zone A) carry only 9.7% of total FKL loss, justifying sparse selection
Zone C tokens (10% of tokens) concentrate 3.19× their fair share of loss
Curriculum is the single strongest factor (+4.20 avg accuracy alone in ablation)
SEAD prevents entropy collapse: vanilla OPD entropy drops from 0.39→0.31 while SEAD maintains stable higher entropy
2606.28562.ablations_summary: 2^3 factorial ablation shows: Curriculum (C) alone +4.20; Token zones (T) alone +0.32; Annealing (A) alone +0.22; T+A +4.52 (super-additive 20× over A alone); T+A+C (full SEAD) +4.82. Components are symbiotically necessary with super-additive interactions.
limitations: Curriculum relies on static difficulty scores rather than adaptive re-estimation
Only evaluated on math domain; applicability to other domains (e.g., code) unverified
Efficacy on very long reasoning chains requires further investigation
failure_modes: Without curriculum, incoherent rollouts corrupt entropy landscape causing zone misclassification
Annealing without token zones provides negligible gain (+0.22)
Token zones alone can hurt hard benchmarks (AIME25 Δ=-1.7 for annealing-only without curriculum)

theory.theoretical_claim: Theorem 1: sparse gradient error O(sG√τ log|V|); Theorem 2: curriculum convergence speedup S²=(c/φ̄_U)² over uniform sampling
theory.proof_sketch: Zone A tokens have near-zero entropy for both teacher and student, so their gradient norms are bounded by O(G√τ); curriculum maintains ϕ(p_i)≥c on eligible prompts giving effective PL constant cμ vs ϕ̄_U·μ for uniform

2606.28562.relevance_to_opd: Directly proposes a novel OPD framework with three symbiotic components (token-level entropy zone partitioning, temporal divergence annealing, competence-gated curriculum) that address the unique challenge of supervision quality depending on student competence in on-policy distillation

2606.29502.title: UCOB: Learning to Utilize and Evolve Agentic Skills via Credit-Aware On-Policy Bidirectional Self-Distillation
2606.29502.affiliation_primary: Institute of Automation, Chinese Academy of Sciences
2606.29502.summary: Credit-aware bidirectional self-distillation between skill/no-skill context views for agentic RL

method.training_loop: Mixed skill/no-skill rollouts from same policy → group by anchor state → select higher-return view as local teacher → KL distill to opposite view + RL loss + reflection self-training
method.loss_formulation: L = L_RL + λ_CBSD * L_CBSD + λ_refl * L_refl + β_KL * L_KL
method.data_source: On-policy rollouts in ALFWorld, WebShop, Search-QA environments
key_components: Credit-aware bidirectional self-distillation (CBSD)
UCB-based dual-level skill retrieval
Anchor-state grouping for local credit
Top-K token support KL
Reflection self-training with utility-weighted advantage

2606.29502.novelty: Replaces fixed skill-to-no-skill teacher direction with bidirectional self-distillation where the higher-return context view (skill or no-skill) at each anchor state becomes the local teacher for the opposite view

on_policy_mechanism.evidence_quote: UCOB treats skill-conditioned and no-skill prompts as two on-policy context views of the same model, compares their return-to-go within the same task and anchor state, and uses the higher-return view as the local teacher.

opd_classification.reasoning: Self-distillation where student generates rollouts under two context views (same model), higher-return view provides logit-level KL supervision to the opposite view — pure self-distillation with adaptive direction selection and token-level gating.

eval: Search-QA (NQ, TriviaQA, PopQA, HotpotQA, 2Wiki, MuSiQue, Bamboogle)

key_findings: UCOB improves ALFWorld success by +23.5 points over Skill1 and +35.2 over SDAR on Qwen3-1.7B
UCOB improves WebShop success by +18.0 points over Skill1 and +21.1 over SDAR on Qwen3-1.7B
No-skill-to-skill routing occurs more often than skill-to-no-skill, confirming skill-conditioned view is not a reliable fixed teacher
Ablation shows removing CBSD or mixed rollouts causes the largest degradation, validating cross-context distillation
Self-trained reflection outperforms external GPT-5.4 reflection writer (89.1 vs 88.3 ALFWorld, 79.7 vs 72.7 WebShop)
2606.29502.ablations_summary: Removing CBSD or mixed rollouts causes largest degradation; anchor-state grouping, state skills, and reflection self-training each provide complementary gains; gap-gated and force-directed distillation are weaker than full bidirectional; top-K support stabilizes supervision; λ_CBSD=0.1 optimal; self-trained reflection beats fixed bank and external GPT-5.4
limitations: Search-QA gains are marginal (within 0.8 points of best), suggesting credit-aware bidirectional distillation is most beneficial in multi-turn agentic environments
Theoretical analysis is local one-update guarantee, not global convergence for the full nonstationary system
failure_modes: On Search-QA, UCOB does not uniformly dominate baselines
When skill-conditioned view is locally harmful, fixed-direction distillation degrades performance (motivating the bidirectional design)

theory.theoretical_claim: First-order local improvement: bidirectional distillation toward higher-return branch yields positive advantage surrogate improvement ηδ_x with trust-region bound
theory.proof_sketch: Performance-difference lemma applied to interpolated policy update at anchor state; bidirectionality avoids negative updates from fixed-direction when skill view is locally worse

2606.29502.relevance_to_opd: Directly extends on-policy self-distillation (OPSD) by making the teacher direction credit-aware and bidirectional rather than fixed from skill-conditioned to no-skill view; uses student-generated rollouts with KL loss between two views of the same model

2606.29476.title: CRAFT: Counterfactual Credit Assignment from Free Sibling Rollouts for Self-Distilled Agentic Reinforcement Learning
2606.29476.affiliation_primary: The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology
2606.29476.summary: Three-pillar counterfactual credit assignment for self-distilled agentic RL using GRPO sibling rollouts

method.training_loop: GRPO samples G rollouts per prompt; CTI importance-weights sibling advantages by teacher-student gap; adaptive controller schedules λ,µ; polarised KL routes rev/fwd by credit sign
method.loss_formulation: L_CRAFT(θ) = L_PG(θ) + µ(t) L_KL-pol(θ) + λ(t) L_CTI(θ)
method.data_source: ALFWorld, Search-QA, WebShop agentic environments with verifier rewards
key_components: Counterfactual Token Importance (CTI) estimator from sibling rollouts
Phase-aware adaptive controller (Pillar 2)
Direction-polarised KL penalty (Pillar 3)
Bit-exact reproducibility switches

2606.29476.novelty: Replaces the single retrospective gate in SDAR with a counterfactual signed per-token credit estimated via importance-weighted GRPO sibling rollouts at zero extra sampling cost, plus an asymmetric KL penalty routed by credit sign

on_policy_mechanism.evidence_quote: A second forward pass evaluates the same policy on the skill-augmented context s+ t — typically the prompt plus an oracle skill annotation, a verifier hint, or a retrieved successful trajectory — and yields the teacher log-prob logπ_T(y_t | s+_t). Because the teacher is just the student under a different context, it adds a single forward pass (no extra parameters, no extra optimiser state)

opd_classification.reasoning: [2026-08-12 boss ruling] RECLASSIFIED yes->no (score=7 review). CRAFT: counterfactual credit assignment for agentic RL; the OPD element is a credit-shaping variant on top of GRPO sibling rollouts. Excluded from V5 scope; removed from Awesome; PDF trashed.

key_findings: CRAFT-Full leads in every (env, model) cell of the main grid across 4 model scales and 3 environments
Pillar 1 (CTI) alone captures the bulk of gain: +1.9/+2.0/+1.5 over SDAR on ALFWorld/Search-QA/WebShop
Largest absolute gains on smallest model Qwen3-1.7B (+3.4 ALFWorld, +2.6 Search-QA, +5.5 WebShop), shrinking at larger scales
CRAFT vs Adaptive-CRINGE (isolating P1+P3) is consistently positive: +2.6 ALFWorld and +2.3 WebShop on Qwen3-1.7B
CRAFT-Full has smallest in-distribution to OOD gap (6.2 vs SDAR's 9.5 on ALFWorld)
2606.29476.ablations_summary: P1 alone captures bulk of gain; P2 adds small increment (≤0.4); P3 adds ~0.3-0.5% completeness; removing CTI (G_min=999) collapses to SDAR baseline; KL-direction swap drops below SDAR; temperature τ and β sweeps show robustness around defaults
limitations: Pillar 1 needs group rollouts (G≥2); non-group backbones via synthetic siblings are future work
Nine new hyperparameters
Pillar 3's standalone gain is small (completeness, not magnitude contribution)
All benchmarks are text-based agentic; multi-modal and cross-domain generalisation is future work
Pillar 3 negative branch is a forward-KL-inspired update rule, not an unbiased KL estimator
failure_modes: Small groups (G<G_min) fall back to single-rollout proxy, losing counterfactual signal
Weak teacher-student coverage (large importance ratio cap) makes variance bound loose
Within-group exchangeability assumption degrades for later tokens in trajectory

theory.theoretical_claim: CTI estimator is consistent with O(1/G) variance bound; controller has geometric convergence to fixed point
theory.proof_sketch: SNIS consistency via weak law of large numbers under coverage and group i.i.d. assumptions; delta-method expansion gives Var ≤ R²_max ρ̄²_t / (G-1)

2606.29476.relevance_to_opd: Self-distillation variant where the student generates on-policy rollouts via GRPO, and the same model conditioned on privileged context serves as teacher providing logit-level supervision; improves per-token credit assignment for the KL-based distillation loss

2606.29863.title: KbSD: Knowledge Boundary aware Self-Distillation for Behavioral Calibration in Agentic Search
2606.29863.summary: Quadrant-adaptive self-distillation with hint-augmented teacher for agentic search calibration

method.training_loop: For each query: estimate knowledge boundary quadrant, generate teacher rollouts with boundary hints, student generates own rollouts via GRPO, optimize joint RL + quadrant-adaptive KL distillation loss
method.loss_formulation: L(θ) = -E[1/G Σ min(ρ_i Â_i, clip(ρ_i,1-ε,1+ε)Â_i)] - βD_KL(π_θ∥π_ref) - γL_distill(q)
method.data_source: Synthesized multi-hop queries from HotpotQA and 2WikiMultiHopQA via fact injection and information fuzzing
key_components: hint-augmented self-distillation teacher
quadrant-adaptive KL objectives (reverse/forward/Pareto bidirectional)
knowledge boundary quantification
GRPO-based joint RL optimization

2606.29863.novelty: Information-asymmetric self-distillation where architecturally identical teacher receives boundary hints (parametric certainty, retrieval quality, target quadrant) with quadrant-adaptive divergence selection (reverse KL for concentrated integration, forward KL for diverse refusal, Pareto bidirectional for asymmetric quadrants), eliminating need for larger external teacher

on_policy_mechanism.evidence_quote: The second objective matches the teacher on student-sampled trajectories: L_rev(q) = E_{o∼π_θ} [Σ log π^T(o_t|o_{<t},q) / π_θ(o_t|o_{<t},q)]

opd_classification.reasoning: Proposes quadrant-adaptive divergence selection (reverse/forward/Pareto KL) as an adaptive distillation objective, with self-distillation from a hint-augmented copy of the same model on student-generated rollouts

key_findings: KbSD reduces average unreliability rate from 64.32% to 47.60% on Qwen2.5-3B and from 57.99% to 41.18% on Qwen2.5-7B compared to KbPO baseline
Removing distillation loss entirely degrades performance across all benchmarks, confirming dense process-level supervision is essential
Quadrant-adaptive KL outperforms fixed forward or reverse KL, particularly on benchmarks requiring diverse refusal (TriviaQA) or concentrated integration (2WikiMQA)
Improvement margin increases with model scale, suggesting larger models better leverage dense process-level supervision
2606.29863.ablations_summary: Removing L_distill entirely degrades avg unreliability from 47.60 to 61.92; Fixed-FKL yields 49.13 and Fixed-RKL yields 64.32, validating quadrant-adaptive divergence selection. Quadrant rebalancing reduces unreliability particularly on TriviaQA and NQ.
limitations: Residual challenge in Q4 (Internal quadrant) where agent still over-relies on retrieval despite accessible parametric answer
Extension to larger models and open-ended agentic settings left to future work
Tighter coupling between knowledge-boundary awareness and retrieval budgeting not addressed
failure_modes: Over-searching in Internal quadrant (Q4) when parametric answer is directly accessible
Excessive search iterations before convergence in cases with high prior knowledge
2606.29863.relevance_to_opd: Proposes on-policy self-distillation where student generates its own rollouts and a hint-augmented copy of the same model provides token-level KL supervision with quadrant-adaptive divergence direction selection, directly extending OPD to agentic search with heterogeneous knowledge states

2606.30044.title: Building Multi-Task Agentic LLMs via Two-Phase Distillation
2606.30044.summary: Two-phase distillation (off-policy then on-policy) for multi-task agentic LLMs

method.training_loop: Phase 1: collect teacher rollouts, SFT student (off-policy forward KL). Phase 2: sample from student, compute per-token reverse KL reward, update student via policy gradient (on-policy reverse KL).
method.loss_formulation: L = KL[π_θ(·|x) ∥ π_T(·|x)] = E_{y~π_θ}[Σ_i (log π_θ(y_i|xy_{1:i-1}) - log π_T(y_i|xy_{1:i-1}))]
method.data_source: Training prompts from τ2-bench (airline, telecom) and GEM (sudoku, mastermind); teacher rollouts from single-task RL experts
key_components: off-policy distillation (SFT on teacher rollouts)
on-policy distillation (reverse KL via policy gradient)
two-phase training recipe
multi-task teacher ensemble (one expert per task)

2606.30044.novelty: Identifies mode-covering failure of forward KL in multi-task distillation and proposes two-phase approach (off-policy initialization + on-policy refinement) that recovers single-task RL expert performance where either method alone fails

on_policy_mechanism.evidence_quote: On-policy distillation samples from the student model and optimizes the reverse KL divergence KL[π_θ ∥ π_T] between the student model and the teacher model. This requires sampling from the student model, which cannot be performed in advance.

opd_classification.reasoning: The paper proposes an adaptive two-phase distillation strategy combining off-policy (forward KL) and on-policy (reverse KL) objectives, addressing mode-covering limitations in multi-task settings.

key_findings: Two-phase distillation (Off.+On.) recovers single-task RL performance across all 4 tasks, with telecom pass^4 improving from 57.9% (off-policy only) to 69.4% on 8B models.
Off-policy distillation degrades in multi-task settings due to mode-covering: telecom pass^4 drops 9.9% vs single-task RL on 8B.
On-policy distillation alone fails without proper initialization, showing -9.5% pass^4 on telecom (8B) vs single-task RL.
The two-phase approach is robust to data mixture configurations in off-policy phase.
Filtering off-policy data to retain only mode-consistent tokens reduces telecom degradation from -9.9% to -0.8% pass^4.
2606.30044.ablations_summary: Key ablations: (1) Rollout from unified model vs individual experts validates mode-covering hypothesis; (2) Token-level filtered data reduces degradation from -9.9% to -0.8%; (3) Data mixture ratios show off-policy alone is sensitive but two-phase is robust; (4) Parameter merging fails significantly on agentic tasks; (5) Multi-task RL shows imbalanced optimization; (6) GKD without off-policy phase also degrades.
limitations: Evaluated on only 4 tasks across 2 domains (conversational agents and text games)
Requires training separate single-task RL experts first, adding computational overhead
On-policy phase requires teacher model inference during student rollout generation
failure_modes: On-policy distillation alone fails when student initialization is insufficient (SFT-only initialization)
Off-policy distillation fails in multi-task settings when aggregated expert data exceeds student capacity

theory.theoretical_claim: Toy example showing forward KL (off-policy) favors averaging policy U over correct copy policy C in multi-task settings, while reverse KL (on-policy) correctly favors C
theory.proof_sketch: In a two-task setting with limited student capacity, off-policy SFT loss of uniform policy U = log4 is optimal, while copy policy C has infinite SFT loss despite perfectly solving both tasks. On-policy reverse KL correctly assigns infinite loss to U and finite loss (log2) to C.

2606.30044.relevance_to_opd: Directly proposes and evaluates on-policy distillation (reverse KL with student rollouts and teacher logit supervision) as a refinement phase for multi-task agentic LLM training, analyzing when and why it outperforms off-policy distillation.

2606.30406.title: MOPD: Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation for Capability Integration in LLM Post-Training
2606.30406.summary: Multi-teacher on-policy distillation for integrating multiple RL domain experts into one LLM

method.training_loop: Student generates rollouts → each rollout dispatched to domain teacher for prefill → teacher returns per-token logprobs → student updated via per-token reverse KL loss
method.loss_formulation: L = E_{x,y~π_θ}[1/|y| Σ_t Σ_v π_θ(v) log(π_θ(v)/π_φ_d(v))]
method.data_source: Multi-domain prompts from Math (BigMath, ORZ), Instruction Following (IFBench-style), Software Engineering (R2E-Gym-Lite)
key_components: per-domain RL teachers from same SFT checkpoint
on-policy student rollouts
domain-routed teacher prefill
reverse KL per-token loss
top-k distillation variant
advantage clipping

2606.30406.novelty: Extends on-policy distillation to multiple domain-routed teachers for capability integration, with same-origin teacher stability and parallelizable pipeline, unlike single-teacher on-policy KD (MiniLLM/GKD)

on_policy_mechanism.evidence_quote: the student generates a trajectory for each prompt and records its per-token probability distribution along the trajectory; (3) each trajectory is dispatched to its corresponding domain teacher according to the task's domain, and then the teacher prefills on the trajectory to obtain its per-token probability distribution; (4) the student is updated by minimising the per-token reverse KL between the student and the domain teacher along the trajectory.

opd_classification.reasoning: MOPD performs on-policy distillation with multiple white-box domain teachers providing logit-level supervision on student-generated rollouts via reverse KL, a multi-teacher extension of on-policy KD.

key_findings: MOPD achieves normalised score 0.937 vs next-best Mix-RL at 0.882 (+5.5 points) on Qwen3-30B-A3B across 3 domains
MOPD closes 91-95% of student-teacher headroom uniformly on every domain with smallest per-domain range (0.044)
Same-origin teachers are critical: replacing with stronger but distributionally different Qwen3-235B-A22B causes training instability and collapse
Multi-round iteration improves normalised score from 0.937 to 0.986 in second round
MOPD is markedly more sample-efficient, reaching teacher-level plateau within 25-30K samples vs 150-180K for Mix-RL
2606.30406.ablations_summary: Policy-gradient vs top-k loss forms perform comparably (0.937 vs 0.909); same-origin teachers critical (external 235B teacher degrades to 0.600 or collapses to -1.19); multi-round evolution yields +0.049 normalised score improvement
limitations: Two regressions on MiMo-V2-Flash: IFBench (-2.2) and SWE-Bench Verified (-0.8)

2606.30345.title: DRIFT: Difficulty Routing Self-Distillation with Rhythm-Gated Exploration and Success Buffer Training
2606.30345.summary: Online self-evolution framework combining difficulty routing, rhythm-gated exploration, and success buffer for LLM self-distillation

method.training_loop: Student generates rollouts; routes negative samples to SDPO (self-distillation from success siblings) and positive samples to rhythm-gated GRPO; difficulty routing weights RL updates by problem pass rate; success buffer stores/replays correct trajectories
method.loss_formulation: L(θ) = E[1_{yi∈incorrect} L_SDPO(yi, fi) - γi * 1_{yi∈correct} J^rhythm_GRPO(yi)]
method.data_source: SciKnowEval reasoning subsets (Chemistry, Physics, Biology, Materials) and ToolAlpaca
key_components: Difficulty Routing
Rhythm-Gated Structured Exploration
Success Buffer
Two-Stage Curriculum Learning
Entropy-based teacher selection

2606.30345.novelty: Introduces problem-level difficulty routing using EMA pass rates to dynamically allocate self-distillation vs RL signals, combined with token-level rhythm gating that uses teacher-student entropy dynamics to concentrate exploration on structurally salient positions, plus a cross-batch success buffer for privileged supervision

on_policy_mechanism.evidence_quote: SDPO leverages the model itself to construct a teacher distribution under additional feedback conditions, thereby providing the student with a finer-grained learning signal. The student policy can be written as π_θ(· | x), whereas the self-teacher distribution is further conditioned on auxiliary feedback f, i.e., π_θ(· | x, f).

opd_classification.reasoning: DRIFT uses pure self-distillation (model's own successful siblings as teacher) with on-policy student rollouts and JSD loss, making it a self-distillation OPD method with adaptive difficulty routing and token-level weighting.

key_findings: DRIFT achieves 79.5% average accuracy across five benchmarks, outperforming GRPO by 9.5% and SDPO by 7.5%
On ToolUse, DRIFT reaches 79.2% accuracy, improving over GRPO by 13.5% and SDPO by 10.7%
Removing difficulty routing reduces average from 79.5% to 74.1%; removing success buffer reduces to 74.9%; removing warm-up reduces to 71.7%
DRIFT generalizes across model families (Qwen3, OLMo3) and scales (4B, 7B, 8B), with advantage amplifying as starting capability weakens
2606.30345.ablations_summary: All three major components contribute: difficulty routing (-5.4%), success buffer (-4.6%), warm-up stage (-7.8%). Complete system achieves best results on all five benchmarks, showing gains from joint effect rather than single component.
2606.30345.relevance_to_opd: DRIFT is a self-distillation OPD framework where the student generates its own rollouts, and JSD between student and privileged self-teacher (conditioned on success siblings) provides dense token-level distillation supervision on student-generated trajectories, combined with difficulty-aware routing and rhythm-gated exploration.

2606.30445.title: When Does Online Imitation Learning Help in LLM Post-Training? The Role of (Non-)Realizability Beyond Horizon
2606.30445.summary: Identifies non-realizability as key factor for online IL advantage over offline SFT in LLM post-training

method.training_loop: Theoretical analysis: prove offline IL has information-theoretic bottleneck under misspecification; propose Misspecification-Reward Alignment condition under which online IL (on-policy distillation with reverse-KL) succeeds
method.loss_formulation: J_on(π) = E_{x~D_x} E_{y~π(·|x)} [f(π^e(y|x))], with f(π^e(y|x)) = log(π^e(y|x)) for on-policy distillation
method.data_source: Countdown synthetic task, GSM8K, DeepScaleR, AIME benchmarks
key_components: non-realizability analysis
misspecification-reward alignment condition
information-theoretic lower bound for offline IL
structural condition for online IL effectiveness

2606.30445.novelty: Shows online IL advantage arises from non-realizability (misspecification) rather than error accumulation, proves information-theoretic lower bound for offline IL and structural condition for online IL even at horizon H=1

on_policy_mechanism.evidence_quote: the learner observes x_i ∼ D_x, executes a certain policy π_i to generate a response y_i ∼ π_i(·|x_i), and receives expert-provided information evaluated on this response... the expert reveals its conditional probability π^e(y_i | x_i) on that response

opd_classification.reasoning: [2026-08-12 boss ruling] RECLASSIFIED analysis->no (score=7 review). Online imitation-learning theory (non-realizability); analysis of online IL vs offline SFT rather than an OPD contribution. Excluded from V5 scope; removed from Awesome; PDF trashed.

key_findings: Under realizability, SFT fully recovers expert performance and on-policy distillation yields no further gains
Non-realizability is identified as a key factor driving online IL's advantage over offline IL

On-policy distillation from Skywork-7B improves student from 25.0% to 32.8% on AIME, while R1-Distill-7B only reaches 27.1%

limitations: Framework does not fully explain why on-policy distillation achieves better training efficiency than RLVR
Contextual bandit formulation (H=1) does not capture multi-step language generation structure
Finite policy class assumption may not hold for neural networks
Coverage coefficients may not be the finest characterization of base model requirements
failure_modes: Online IL fails when expert signal encodes preferences misaligned with reward that the student class can represent (Π_B example)
Offline IL fails when expert puts too little probability mass on responses the restricted student class can learn

theory.proof_sketch: Theorem 1: Constructs hard instance where expert puts 1-1/C_e_inf mass on action unavailable to student, requiring C_e_inf*log|Π|/N samples. Theorem 2: Decomposes expert signal into reward-aligned and residual terms, bounds residual contribution within ε-optimal set.

2606.30626.title: DOPD: Dual On-policy Distillation
2606.30626.summary: Advantage-aware dual OPD routing token supervision between privileged teacher and student policies

method.training_loop: Student rolls out on-policy; compute privilege advantage gap A from privileged teacher & student forward passes; route each token to one of four regimes (LH/LL/HT/HS) with different divergence objectives and strengths; update student.
method.loss_formulation: L_DOPD = I_LH * β_l * KL_reverse(Π_S||Π_T^priv) + I_LL * β_w * KL_reverse(Π_S||sg[Π_S^priv]) + I_HT * JS(Π_S||Π_T^priv) + I_HS * β_l * KL_reverse(Π_S||sg[Π_S^priv])
method.data_source: RaR-Science-20K, DAPO-Math-17K, Skywork-OR1-Coding-14K (LLM); ViRL39K (VLM); privileged info generated by GPT-5.4
key_components: privilege advantage gap
four token regimes with adaptive routing
dual supervision from privileged teacher and privileged student
adaptive divergence objectives (Top-K reverse KL vs full-vocab JS)
intensity coefficients β_w and β_l

2606.30626.novelty: Identifies 'privilege illusion' failure mode and proposes token-level advantage-aware routing that dynamically selects supervision source (teacher vs self), objective (JS vs reverse KL), strategy (full-vocab vs Top-K), and strength based on privilege advantage gap and relative probabilities.

on_policy_mechanism.evidence_quote: given the student policy, for particular inputs x, it samples the sequence of predicted trajectory y∼Π_S(⋅∣x). Then, the teacher policy, typically a stronger model, will offer token-level signals as optimization.

opd_classification.reasoning: DOPD proposes an adaptive divergence objective that routes token-level supervision dynamically based on advantage gap, combining features of adaptive distillation (§4.2) with token weighting (§6.1) and white-box teacher access (§5.1).

key_findings: DOPD outperforms Vanilla OPD by 7.5 points (LLM) and 6.0 points (VLM) averaged across eight benchmarks each.
DOPD recovers 89.8% of the teacher-student gap on LLM tasks and 69.2% on VLM tasks.
DOPD surpasses the teacher on four challenging benchmarks (AIME25, ZebraLogic, BFCLv3, LCBv5).
Across five model pairs of varying sizes, DOPD achieves 11.1-14.1 point gains, a 2-3× improvement over Vanilla OPD.
Ablating high-advantage tokens causes performance to drop to ~50% of Vanilla OPD gains, validating the privilege advantage gap mechanism.
2606.30626.ablations_summary: Removing privileged input drops performance most severely; teacher signals are the primary driver; student self-regularization is irreplaceable; advantage-aware routing adds 8+ points over equal distillation; β_w=0.3, β_l=0.6 are optimal intensity coefficients.
limitations: Method relies on availability and quality of privileged information, requiring annotation/generation costs.
Introduces extra computational overhead (one additional student forward pass) relative to Vanilla OPD.
Routing strategy relies on heuristic mechanisms rather than principled or learnable routing.
failure_modes: When privileged information directly provides final answers, performance degrades below no-privilege baseline due to shortcut learning.
Naive uniform distillation of privileged teacher causes entropy collapse and late-stage performance degradation (privilege illusion).
2606.30626.relevance_to_opd: Directly proposes a novel OPD method (DOPD) that introduces advantage-aware dual routing of token-level supervision between privileged teacher and privileged student policies, addressing privilege illusion in on-policy distillation.

2606.30923.title: Behavior Cloning is Not All You Need: The Optimality of On-Policy Distillation for Noisy Expert Feedback
2606.30923.summary: Proves online IL via OPD achieves horizon-free guarantees under noisy experts where offline BC fails exponentially

method.training_loop: Student rolls out greedy policy, queries noisy expert at visited states for augmented labels, updates via exponential weights on trajectory-level log-likelihood (NAIL) or gradient descent on augmented KL
method.loss_formulation: L = D_KL(P_{\hat{\pi},\pi^*_\eta} \| P_{\hat{\pi},\hat{\pi}_\eta}) \wedge D_KL(P_{\hat{\pi},\hat{\pi}_\eta} \| P_{\hat{\pi},\pi^*_\eta})
method.data_source: Student-generated rollouts with noisy expert feedback at visited states
key_components: greedy student rollouts
augmented trajectory KL divergence
noisy expert model
exponential weights aggregation
κ-domination condition

2606.30923.novelty: Shows sharp separation between offline and online IL under noisy experts: offline requires exponential-in-horizon samples while online (OPD) achieves polynomial/horizon-free guarantees; proposes NAIL algorithm with novel augmented trajectory KL loss

on_policy_mechanism.evidence_quote: In the online IL setting, a learner interacts with the environment in rounds. In each round t, the learner deploys a policy π_t and observes a trajectory τ(t) drawn from P^{π_t}. The learner can then query the (noisy) expert π⋆_η at each of the states visited in τ(t)

opd_classification.reasoning: This is a theoretical analysis paper proving optimality of OPD under noisy experts with novel loss formulation (augmented trajectory KL), fitting the theoretical analysis/decision framework category

key_findings: Offline BC requires exponential-in-horizon samples under noisy experts: n ≳ (1−η)^{−(H+2)} · log(|Π|)/ε
Online OPD (NAIL) achieves polynomial horizon dependence: n ≳ H²·log(|Π|)/ε²(1−η)²
For deterministic experts with unknown corruption, horizon-free guarantees are achievable: n ≳ log(|Π|)/ε(1−η(1+ρ))²
NAIL-F and NAIL-R achieve perfect accuracy on modular addition with η=0.2 while all baselines (BC, OPD-F, OPD-R) fail completely
On GSM-8K with noisy teacher (t=4), only NAIL variants surpass vanilla student baseline of 9.09%
2606.30923.ablations_summary: Student rollout temperature ablation shows greedy rollouts are crucial for high-noise settings; forward KL is more robust to temperature; interpolation between forward and reverse KL tested; horizon and noise level ablations confirm theoretical predictions
limitations: Results are in the finite policy class setting
Idealized corruption model may not capture real-world noise
Unknown corruption results only for deterministic experts
Linear-in-horizon gap between upper and lower bounds remains open
Experiments limited in scope and scale due to resource constraints
failure_modes: Standard OPD with sampled rollouts fails under high noise because student-sampled prefixes lead to uninformative teacher feedback
Offline BC fails when early corrupted tokens make entire trajectory suffix uninformative

theory.theoretical_claim: Offline IL requires exp(H) samples under noisy experts; online OPD achieves poly(H) or horizon-free guarantees; augmented trajectory Hellinger/KL controls regret
theory.proof_sketch: Backward induction peeling trajectory distributions step-by-step; κ-domination controls per-step error; mixability of trajectory-level log-loss + convexity of Hellinger for NAIL analysis; matching lower bounds via information-theoretic constructions

2606.30923.relevance_to_opd: Provides first theoretical foundation for why on-policy distillation outperforms offline SFT, proves optimality of OPD under noisy expert feedback, and proposes a novel augmented-trajectory KL objective (NAIL) as a principled OPD variant

2606.31984.summary: Generative Reasoning Re-Ranker combining mid-training, reasoning distillation, and RL for recommendation

method.data_source: Internal industrial recommendation logs (~70k user sessions from single day)

On-Policy Distillation (OPD) with reverse-KL anchor to teacher
DAPO RL with conditional verifiable rewards
Context compressor
Reasoning internalization via second RL pass

train: Internal Meta AI recommendation logs (70k sessions, single day)

A 1.7B OPD student distilled from 32B teacher recovers 82% of the teacher's gain at 5% of its size, yielding ~15× serving-ROI boost

Gains do not decay over 9 consecutive days despite 2-week model staleness
