On distant OOD languages (Norwegian, Khmer) where reward-only RL stalls at base ceiling, TR-RAG still improves evidence grounding
Removing char 3-gram reward causes largest ablation drop (-5.01 composite points)
2607.02966.ablations_summary: Full TR-RAG (77.81) > RL-only (75.62, +2.19 from teacher) > OPD-only (74.29, +3.52 from rewards). Removing char 3-gram reward causes -5.01, LLM-judge -1.90, language reward -0.15. Moderate β (0.002-0.02) is optimal; β=0.2 over-regularizes. Strong teacher helps most but weak teacher still beneficial.
limitations: Relies on stronger teachers and LLM-based judge during training (additional cost and potential evaluator bias)
Part of training data derived from translated benchmarks (translationese artifacts)
English-evidence only regime (not multilingual evidence)
Single random seed reported
Language-consistency reward simple; may need enrichment for low-resource languages
failure_modes: Over-large β (0.2) degrades performance due to over-regularization keeping student too close to frozen teacher
On extreme-script languages (Khmer) both methods remain capped at base model's 18% LC ceiling
Naive-RL can collapse Indonesian LC to 28.27% on Hotpot-ENKB5/Qwen-4B

theory.theoretical_claim: Pinsker-style bound: small token-mean KL to teacher bounds sequence-level reward deviation from teacher's expected reward
theory.proof_sketch: CorollaryB.6 uses Pinsker's inequality to show |E_πθ[r] - E_πT[r]| ≤ sqrt(0.5 KL(πθ||πT)), and token-mean KL bounds sequence-level KL via Eq.28

2607.02966.relevance_to_opd: Directly extends on-policy distillation (GKD/OPD) by combining the prefix-wise reverse-KL teacher anchor with sequence-level task rewards in a single objective, demonstrating the combination strictly dominates either alone on composite metrics for cross-lingual RAG

2607.04425.title: UI-MOPD: Multi-Platform On-Policy Distillation for Continual GUI Agent Learning
2607.04425.summary: Multi-teacher on-policy distillation with platform-conditioned routing for cross-platform GUI agents

method.training_loop: Stage1: SFT desktop/mobile teachers from Uni-GUI. Stage2: Student generates rollouts via GRPO, platform router selects teacher, compute reverse KL via K3 estimator, optimize clipped PG + β*MOPD loss.
method.loss_formulation: L(θ) = L_PG(θ) + β * L_MOPD(θ), where L_MOPD uses K3-estimated D_KL(π_θ || π_ref^(p)) with adaptive masking
method.data_source: Uni-GUI (~160K steps, ~11.5K trajectories from desktop/mobile environments)
key_components: platform-conditioned teacher routing
K3 KL estimator
adaptive KL masking
structured outcome reward
multi-teacher on-policy distillation

2607.04425.novelty: First application of multi-teacher on-policy distillation to GUI agents with platform-conditioned routing that selects platform-specific teachers per rollout environment, preventing behavioral convention mixing across heterogeneous platforms during continual learning.

on_policy_mechanism.evidence_quote: we let the student policy π sample rollouts online from its current policy and introduce teacher supervision only on the states actually visited by the student

opd_classification.reasoning: Uses white-box multi-teacher logit supervision on student-generated rollouts with reverse KL, combined with RL reward in an application domain (GUI agents).

key_findings: UI-MOPD achieves 38.2% on OSWorld and 12.0% on MobileWorld, corresponding to relative improvements of 12.7% and 55.8% over the base model.
Platform-specific SFT on OSWorld causes MobileWorld performance to drop to 0%, while UI-MOPD improves both platforms simultaneously.
UI-MOPD preserves GUI grounding ability (43.14% ScreenSpot-Pro vs 43.71% base) while Model Merge degrades to 37.13%.
UI-MOPD outperforms integration strategies including Mixed-SFT (35.0%/6.4%), Weight Averaging (36.5%/6.8%), and TIES Merging (36.8%/0%).
2607.04425.ablations_summary: Comparison of integration strategies (Mixed-SFT, Weight Averaging, TIES Merging) vs UI-MOPD shows platform-conditioned on-policy distillation is more effective. Single-platform SFT causes catastrophic forgetting on the other platform (MobileWorld drops to 0% after desktop SFT).
limitations: Evaluated on only two platforms (desktop and mobile)
Requires separate teacher training per platform
Teacher models are 4× larger than student
2607.04425.relevance_to_opd: Directly proposes multi-teacher on-policy distillation for GUI agents where the student generates rollouts online and platform-specific teachers provide reverse KL supervision on student-visited states, a direct instance of OPD extended to multi-teacher and multi-platform settings.

2607.04428.title: dOPSD: On-Policy Self-Distillation for Diffusion Language Models
2607.04428.summary: On-policy self-distillation for diffusion LLMs using trajectory-derived privileged information

method.training_loop: Student dLLM rolls out denoising trajectory; sample intermediate masked step as student state; teacher = same model scored at later more-decoded steps; distill averaged teacher into student via JSD; verify rollout correctness
method.loss_formulation: L = E_x E_{y~pi_theta} [1[y correct] * (1/|M_k|) sum_{i in M_k} JSD_beta(sg[p_bar_i] || pi_theta(.|x,s_k)_i)]
method.data_source: MixChain-Z-PRM12K (12K competition-style math problems with CoT solutions and verifiable answers)
key_components: trajectory-derived privileged information
teacher as averaged future denoising steps
rollout verification
token-level JSD objective
on-policy denoising trajectory

2607.04428.novelty: Sources the teacher's privileged information from the student's own denoising trajectory (later, more-decoded steps) rather than an external reference solution, resolving PI-free collapse and off-path noise issues specific to diffusion LLMs

on_policy_mechanism.evidence_quote: the student rolls out a completion while recording its decoding history; at an intermediate, heavily masked step it predicts the still-masked positions, and the same model, acting as the teacher, evaluates those same positions from later steps of that trajectory

opd_classification.reasoning: The teacher is the same model with privileged information (later trajectory states), making it a PI-based self-distillation method with a novel JSD objective specifically designed for diffusion LLMs

key_findings: dOPSD is the only method to improve the base model across all benchmarks on both Dream and LLaDA backbones
OPSD (full-solution) collapses, losing 14.2 GSM8K points on Dream (81.41→67.25), confirming PI-free hypothesis
Forward KL outperforms reverse KL on every task-backbone combination
Full teacher horizon (averaging all remaining trajectory steps) is best, with GSM8K 83.04 vs 78.14 at 200 steps
dOPSD without verification still improves over base model (MATH500: 38.97→40.94), showing trajectory-derived privilege works without answers
2607.04428.ablations_summary: Forward KL beats reverse KL; full teacher horizon is optimal vs truncated (0/50/100/200 steps); mask threshold τ=0.5 is best; rollout verification adds ~1.5 points average but method works without it
limitations: Requires correct rollouts for best performance (though works without verification)
Tested only on two diffusion LLM backbones
Training only on math domain
failure_modes: When teacher horizon is 0 (no peek-ahead), performance drops substantially below base model (GSM8K 70.44 vs 81.41)

theory.theoretical_claim: OPSD with instance-specific PI drives student toward weak PI-marginalized consensus (normalized geometric mean of per-PI teachers), explaining failure on dLLMs
theory.proof_sketch: Student cannot condition on y* at inference, so minimizing expected divergence over PI distribution D(·|x) converges to p*_S proportional to exp(E_{y*} log p_T(y|x,y*))

2607.04428.relevance_to_opd: Proposes a novel on-policy self-distillation method for diffusion LLMs where the teacher's privilege comes from the student's own denoising trajectory rather than external labels, with token-level JSD distillation on student-generated rollouts

2607.04763.title: Multi-Turn On-Policy Distillation with Prefix Replay
2607.04763.summary: Replayed-Prefix On-Policy Distillation (ReOPD) for multi-turn agentic tasks using offline teacher trajectories

method.training_loop: Replay teacher-forced prefix, student generates action at selected step, compute per-token KL against teacher on student's action tokens, weight steps by decay schedule κ^t, update student
method.loss_formulation: L(θ) = E_x Σ_t α_t E_{H_t~P_t} E_{A_t~π_θold} [w_t Σ_j D_KL(π_θ(·|x,H_t,a_t^{<j}) ∥ π_T(·|x,H_t,a_t^{<j}))]
method.data_source: Pre-collected teacher trajectories from teacher's GRPO RL training rollouts
key_components: teacher-forced prefix replay
student on-policy action at supervised step
step-decaying weight schedule κ^t
reliability-aware prefix distribution design
two-sided distribution shift analysis

2607.04763.novelty: Introduces replayed-prefix OPD that reuses offline teacher trajectories instead of live environment interaction, identifies the prefix trap (two-sided shift between student occupancy and teacher reliability), and proposes a step-decay schedule that emphasizes early low-shift positions

on_policy_mechanism.evidence_quote: student generates its action A_t = (a^1_t,...,a^{n_t}_t) ~ π_θold(·|x,h_t) autoregressively and is supervised, per generated token, by the teacher's conditional along that action, π_T(·|x,h_t,a_t^{<j})

opd_classification.reasoning: ReOPD proposes an adaptive reliability-aware step-decay schedule for weighting/sampling prefix positions in on-policy distillation, combining adaptive divergence weighting with curriculum-like step selection

key_findings: ReOPD improves math average from 55.1 to 57.2 over OPD with Qwen3-4B teacher, and from 51.0 to 53.7 with Qwen3-8B teacher
ReOPD is at least 4× faster per training step than OPD and uses zero tool calls during student training
ReOPD matches OPD on search tasks (40.5 vs 40.6) where teacher remains reliable on student histories
Step-decay schedule with κ=0.6 works across tasks without per-task tuning
Prefix source from teacher's own model is best, not a stronger generator - validating reliability view
2607.04763.ablations_summary: Chunk sampling shows early chunks best; decay κ sweep shows moderate decay (0.6) outperforms uniform (κ=1); prefix source ablation shows teacher's own prefixes beat stronger generators; RL-collected pool matches stationary teacher pool
limitations: Assumes access to pre-collected pool of teacher trajectories with recorded observations
Step-decay is coarse: captures depth not direct reliability measurement
Two-sided bound uses teacher support as surrogate for true teacher reliability
Pool coverage and quality bound what student can learn
failure_modes: When teacher-student gap is small, ReOPD merely matches OPD without improvement (search setting)
Later steps in trajectory have degraded supervision quality due to distribution shift

theory.theoretical_claim: Two-sided decomposition bounding gap between ideal interactive objective and replayed objective by student occupancy-mismatch TV term and teacher reliability term
theory.proof_sketch: Proposition 1 decomposes |R*(θ;θ_old) - L_ρ(θ;θ_old)| ≤ Σ_t α_t {2B·TV(d^t_θold, ρ_t) + E[ε^θ_{T,t}]} using bounded loss assumption and triangle inequality

2607.04763.relevance_to_opd: Directly proposes and studies on-policy distillation for multi-turn agentic settings, introducing reliability-aware prefix distribution design as an alternative to fully online OPD that uses teacher logit supervision on student-generated actions

2607.05394.title: Weak-to-Strong Generalization via Direct On-Policy Distillation
2607.05394.summary: Transfers weak model's RL-induced policy shift as implicit reward to stronger students on-policy

method.training_loop: Student generates rollouts; at each prefix, compute teacher/reference log-ratio as per-token reward on student top-k; Rao-Blackwellized policy gradient with adaptive KL anchor to student init
method.loss_formulation: J(θ) = E_x[E_{y~π_θ}[Δ_T(y|x)] - α D_KL(π_θ(·|x) ∥ π_S(·|x))]
method.data_source: Skywork-OR1-RL-Data math subset
key_components: policy-shift as implicit reward
top-k Rao-Blackwellized policy gradient
adaptive KL control
stop-gradient advantage weighting

2607.05394.novelty: Instead of imitating the weak teacher's final policy, Direct-OPD transfers only the RL-induced policy shift (log-ratio between post-RL and pre-RL checkpoints) as a dense implicit reward evaluated on student's own on-policy states, enabling weak-to-strong generalization where the student already exceeds the teacher

on_policy_mechanism.evidence_quote: On-policy distillation (OPD) supervises the student on trajectories it samples itself. Given a prompt x, the student draws yˆ ∼ π_θ(· | x), and at each visited prefix s_t = (x,yˆ_<t) we read off the student and teacher next-token distributions

opd_classification.reasoning: Direct-OPD uses student on-policy rollouts with teacher logit-level supervision (log-ratio of two teacher checkpoints evaluated on student states) in a KL-regularized policy gradient objective, combining RL-augmented distillation with a novel implicit reward from policy shifts

key_findings: Direct-OPD boosts Qwen3-1.7B from 48.3% to 62.4% on AIME 2024 in 4 hours on 8 A100 GPUs using a 1.5B teacher
Weak-to-strong transfer works even when student (R1-Distill-7B at 56.7%) already exceeds the post-RL teacher (JustRL-1.5B at 51.3%)
Running RL on 1.5B model then transferring with Direct-OPD outperforms running RL directly on 7B model at matched compute
Sequential composition of two independent policy shifts (JustRL + QuestA) accumulates gains: Qwen3-1.7B reaches 63.8% on AIME 2024
Short 2k-token training horizon generalizes to longer rollout behavior at test time
2607.05394.ablations_summary: Response length sweep (512/2k/4k) shows 2k optimal; KL coefficient sweep shows pair-dependent best values; adaptive KL balances mean reward toward zero; top-k overlap analysis shows transfer works without progressive imitation; teacher RL checkpoint selection (T300-T1500) shows later checkpoints give stronger transfer
limitations: Direct-OPD can fail when teacher/reference improvement is not meaningful on student-visited states
Best response length and KL strength remain teacher-student pair dependent
failure_modes: Vanilla OPD from weak teacher drags strong student down (R1-Distill-7B drops from 56.7 to ~50)
6k response length over-drives actor on unreliable late-prefix signal leading to worse validation (45.6 vs 48.8)

theory.theoretical_claim: Under KL-regularized RL, the policy-shift log-ratio Δ_T recovers the teacher's implicit reward up to a positive scale and per-prompt constant, so optimizing against Δ_T is equivalent to KL-regularized RL with the teacher's reward
theory.proof_sketch: From π* ∝ π_ref exp(r/β), log(π*/π_ref) = r/β - logZ(x), so Δ_T = (1/β)r_T - logZ_T, recovering reward up to scale and constant

2607.05394.relevance_to_opd: Proposes a novel on-policy distillation variant where the teacher signal is not the absolute logit distribution but the log-ratio between two teacher checkpoints (pre/post-RL), applied on student-generated rollouts as a dense implicit reward

2607.03572.title: Teacher Supervision over Representation Equivalence Classes: Why Distillation Transfers Capability Through the Output Function, Not the Features
2607.03572.affiliation_primary: Korea University of Technology and Education
2607.03572.summary: Theoretical framework showing capability transfers via output function (class invariant), not hidden features

method.training_loop: Corrupt teacher layers → train student with L_cka (relational) and/or L_logit (KL on output distributions) on probe set X → measure restoration
method.loss_formulation: L = L_logit + λ L_rel where L_logit = (1/|X|) Σ KL(p_τ(z_T(x)) ∥ p_τ(z_S(x)))
method.data_source: Generic text corpus (WikiText-103 for cross-width experiments)
key_components: representation equivalence class theory
joint quotient factorization
logit-KD as class-invariant objective
CKA-based relational matching
graft success prediction from subspace overlap

2607.03572.novelty: Reframes distillation as transferring the teacher's representation equivalence class rather than matching features; proves output function is the joint-class invariant that carries capability while hidden-state matching (even at CKA≈0.99) does not restore function

on_policy_mechanism.evidence_quote: L_logit = (1/|X|) Σ KL(p_τ(z_T(x)) ∥ p_τ(z_S(x))), with τ = 1 in our experiments

opd_classification.reasoning: [2026-08-12 three-condition audit] RECLASSIFIED analysis→no. Offline logit-KD theory on a fixed dataset: L_logit = KL(p_tau(z_T(x)) || p_tau(z_S(x))); rollout=no, freq=n/a, 0 mentions of "on-policy". Fails C1 and C3. Project rule: all three conditions (student rollouts in training, concurrent teacher supervision, per-step updates) must hold.

key_findings: CKA-only training restores representation geometry (CKA≈0.999) but leaves capability destroyed (PPL ratio ~3×10^6, top-1≈0)
Logit-only training restores capability (PPL ratio 1.02×, top-1 0.99) without aligning representation (CKA=0.894)
Feature-matching alone in cross-width distillation collapses model to PPL>10^6 even from pristine student
Restoration is confined to corpus-covered region: out-domain CKA drops to 0.53 without domain mixing
Untied models require explicit head training to fix output coordinate frame; tied models get this implicitly
2607.03572.ablations_summary: Three-way ablation (L_cka only vs L_logit only vs combined) shows capability driven entirely by logit term; feature term ranges from neutral (optimal W) to mildly harmful (learned W); cross-width surrogate with closed-form optimal alignment confirms feature-only collapse
limitations: Controlled studies fix architecture and share tokenizer embedding; cross-model and small-from-large transfer not established
Results are restoration studies, not production distillation systems
One-step output-function capability transfers but autoregressive trajectory capability is not guaranteed
Modest scale: single model pairs, few seeds, ≤2000 training steps for cross-width
Exact O(d) invariance approximate in transformers due to normalization layers
failure_modes: Teacher-forced/generation gap: top-1≈0.98 but greedy generation drifts with repetition loops
High-overlap grafts near output layers still fail due to amplification of small mismatches
Out-of-domain restoration fails without corpus coverage of that domain

theory.theoretical_claim: Output function factors through joint quotient (f = f̄ ∘ π_joint); absolute feature matching is ill-posed on representation equivalence classes; capability is a class invariant transferable only via output-function matching
theory.proof_sketch: Under Assumption 2.1 (absorbable reparametrization), joint action (h,θ)→(chQ,θ^{Q,c}) leaves network function unchanged; by universal property of quotient, f descends uniquely to joint quotient M/G as f̄ with f=f̄∘π_joint

2607.03572.relevance_to_opd: Provides theoretical foundation for why logit-level (output distribution) distillation transfers capability while feature-level matching does not, directly informing the design of on-policy distillation objectives that use KL divergence on output distributions

2607.04037.title: Reward-Gated On-Policy Distillation
2607.04037.summary: Reward-gated on-policy distillation filtering teacher logits by verifier-reward alignment

method.training_loop: Student samples trajectories on-policy, verifier assigns rewards, teacher provides token-level logits; gate keeps trajectories where reward sign agrees with teacher-student likelihood gap direction; reverse-KL loss on kept trajectories only
method.loss_formulation: L_RG-OPD = (sum_i g_i sum_t m_t^(i) KL(pi_theta(·|s_t^(i)) || pi_T(·|s_t^(i)))) / (sum_i g_i sum_t m_t^(i))
method.data_source: subset of UltraInteract
key_components: reward-teacher likelihood gate
top-K reverse-KL approximation with tail correction
GRPO advantage as gating signal

2607.04037.novelty: Introduces a binary gate that conditions on-policy distillation updates on directional agreement between verifier reward and teacher-student likelihood gap, filtering out misleading teacher signals on incorrect or teacher-disagreed trajectories

on_policy_mechanism.evidence_quote: At each iteration, for each prompt x, the student samples N trajectories from its own policy: {y(i)}N i=1 ∼ π_θ(·|x), and a verifier returns a scalar reward r_i for each trajectory.

opd_classification.reasoning: RG-OPD augments on-policy reverse-KL distillation with a reward-based trajectory gate, combining RL verifier signals with dense teacher logit supervision, fitting §4.3 (RL-augmented OPD objectives).

stabilization_tricks: top-K logit approximation with tail correction

key_findings: RG-OPD improves over vanilla reverse-KL distillation by 2.9 points average at 1K generation length and 2.8 points at 8K generation length.
At 8K generation length, RG-OPD improves over the untuned student by 8.2 points average.
RG-OPD outperforms TSD-KD by 4.9 points average at 1K generation length.
The gate becomes more selective over training, with kept token fraction decreasing from ~0.9 to ~0.7.
2607.04037.ablations_summary: Ablation on top-K truncation parameter shows k=30 yields best average (47.10); removing tail redistribution degrades performance; varying K shows diminishing returns beyond moderate values.
limitations: IFEval performance drops compared to TSD-KD, possibly due to TSD-KD's student-centric design preserving instruction-following behavior
Log-likelihood-based evaluation protocol is not natural for instruction-tuned models and RG-OPD does not consistently improve under it
failure_modes: On instruction-following (IFEval), RG-OPD scores below both the student baseline and TSD-KD
Under likelihood-based evaluation protocol, RG-OPD does not consistently outperform baselines
2607.04037.relevance_to_opd: Directly proposes a novel on-policy distillation method that gates teacher logit supervision based on verifier reward agreement, addressing failure modes of unconditional OPD.

2607.04751.title: Trust Region Policy Distillation
2607.04751.summary: Stabilizes on-policy distillation via proximal teacher interpolation and trust region iterations

method.training_loop: Student generates rollouts; compute TOP-D reward r̃_k=log(αρ_k+1-α); compute token-level advantages; perform multiple PPO-clip updates per batch with importance sampling
method.loss_formulation: J(θ) = (1/G) Σ_i Σ_t min[p_t^i * Â_t^i, clip(p_t^i, 1-ε, 1+ε) * Â_t^i] where r̃_k = log(α * π*(y_k|x,y<k)/π_θ(y_k|x,y<k) + 1-α)
method.data_source: DAPO-Math-17k dataset
key_components: External proximal teacher via probability interpolation
Internal trust region iterations with PPO-clip
Token-level advantage normalization
Length-normalized future return

2607.04751.novelty: Transforms unbounded OPD reward into bounded signal via probability-space interpolation (proximal teacher), enabling safe off-policy data reuse with formal variance bounds and monotonic improvement guarantees, unlike prior heuristic stabilization approaches

on_policy_mechanism.evidence_quote: Sample a batch of prompts X ⊂ D_x ... Perform rollout to sample G responses {y^i}^G_{i=1} ∼ π_{θ_old}(·|x) ... Compute TOP-D rewards r̃^i_k ← log(α π*(y^i_k|x,y^i_{<k}) / π_{θ_old}(y^i_k|x,y^i_{<k}) + 1 − α)

opd_classification.reasoning: TOP-D proposes an adaptive proximal teacher objective that bounds gradient variance (§4.1/4.2) and incorporates token-level advantage normalization (§6.1), with the core novelty being a new stabilized divergence objective with convergence guarantees.

key_findings: TOP-D achieves 25.84% absolute improvement over standard OPD on AIME24 (50.42% vs 24.58%) with Qwen3-8B-Base student
TOP-D surpasses DAPO (best RLVR baseline) by 17.5% absolute on AIME24
With smaller 1.7B student, standard OPD falls behind RLVR baselines while TOP-D maintains >10pp advantage over OPD
TOP-D introduces zero additional computational overhead over standard OPD
Method is robust to interpolation coefficient α ∈ {0.1, 0.2, 0.3} with marginal performance differences
2607.04751.ablations_summary: Removing proximal teacher (α=1.0) causes unstable training and significant performance degradation; disabling internal trust region iterations (w/o off-policy) drastically reduces sample efficiency; α sensitivity across {0.1, 0.2, 0.3} shows marginal differences demonstrating robustness
limitations: Validation limited to student models up to 8B parameters
Empirical evaluations constrained to 200-400 update steps without observing saturation
Not yet investigated scaling beyond 30B student models

theory.theoretical_claim: Bounded variance (Theorem 4.2), global convergence with asymptotic gap ε∞/α (Theorem 4.4), and monotonic improvement guarantee (Theorem 4.9)
theory.proof_sketch: Proximal teacher bounds token-level reward from below via log(αρ+1-α) ≥ log(1-α), yielding uniform gradient variance bound M²|V|max{(log(1-α))², C*α}; iterative convergence via contraction operator T with error accumulation bounded by geometric series; monotonic improvement via performance difference lemma adapted for variable-length generation

2607.04751.relevance_to_opd: Directly addresses instability of on-policy distillation by proposing a new bounded reward formulation (proximal teacher) that transforms unbounded KL-based OPD reward into a stable signal, with rigorous convergence guarantees and trust region data reuse

2605.29489.title: Access Sets Matter: Budgeting Expert Reads for Scalable Weight-Space Model Merging
2605.29489.summary: Budget-aware execution layer for LLM weight-space merging via expert access-set planning

method.training_loop: Catalog expert deltas → rank by norm/sketch scores → greedy select under I/O budget B → execute mask-aware merge operator Ψ_op on selected blocks → write merged checkpoint
method.data_source: Pre-existing fine-tuned checkpoints (Qwen3, Llama families)
key_components: expert access mask A
budget-aware greedy planner
mask-aware merge operator Ψ_op
DeltaIterator streaming executor
replayable manifest

2605.29489.novelty: Formulates LLM model merging as a budgeted expert access-set problem, decoupling which expert deltas are physically read from how they are combined, with provable budget soundness and omitted-update error bounds

on_policy_mechanism.evidence_quote: MergePipe exposes the hidden execution choice with an access mask... MergePipe does not introduce a new merge rule: it decides which deltas are physically materialized

opd_classification.reasoning: This is a systems/efficiency paper for weight-space model merging (I/O optimization), not a distillation method. No student rollouts, no teacher logit supervision, no KL loss.

key_findings: MergePipe achieves up to 11× speedups and order-of-magnitude expert-read I/O reduction across Qwen and Llama families
At 0.5 budget, relative ℓ2 deviation from full-read merge remains O(10^-3) with no monotonic downstream degradation
Planning overhead is only 1.04% of execution time; catalog storage is 3.79% of total I/O
For TIES at K=8 on Llama-3.1-8B, I/O drops from 79.5 GB to 3.46 GB with 91.7% wall-time reduction
2605.29489.ablations_summary: Budget sweeps from 10% to 100% show monotone realized expert-read I/O and accessed-block ratio; operator generality tested across AVG, TIES, DARE showing sparse methods benefit most
limitations: Assumes experts share a common weight coordinate system; does not address permutation or symmetry alignment
Budgeted merging is approximate; only full-budget recovers standard merge
Quality is empirical for nonlinear sparse operators like TIES and DARE
Benefits shrink for small expert sets, dense full-read regimes, or GPU-resident in-memory fusion
failure_modes: Gains naturally shrink for small expert sets or GPU-resident in-memory fusion scenarios
Selected-only renormalization breaks the additive omission bound

theory.theoretical_claim: Budget soundness, full-budget consistency, and additive omission bound: ‖M_full - M_A‖₂ ≤ Σ q_{t,b}(A)
theory.proof_sketch: For additive fixed-coefficient operators, omitted-update error equals sum of (1-A_{i,t,b})α_{i,t,b}Δ_{i,t,b}; triangle inequality over disjoint blocks yields the ℓ2 bound

2605.29489.relevance_to_opd: Not an OPD paper; it is a systems/efficiency paper for weight-space model merging. The paper explicitly acknowledges on-policy distillation as a complementary approach in its limitations section.

2607.05339.title: TREK: Distill to Explore, Reinforce to Refine
2607.05339.summary: Staged distillation-then-RL procedure using verified proposals to expand student exploration support before GRPO

method.training_loop: Mine hard prompts via low student pass rate → query proposal source → keep top-r verified student-proximal proposals → short forward-KL consolidation → return to on-policy GRPO refinement
method.loss_formulation: L = KL(q_prop(·|x) ∥ π_θ(·|x)) for consolidation, then L_GRPO for refinement
method.data_source: DAPO-Math-17K training pool; ALFWorld and ScienceWorld environments
key_components: prompt routing by unaided student pass rate
trimmed NLL reachability scoring
top-r student-proximal verified proposal selection
forward-KL consolidation phase
staged schedule with GRPO refinement

2607.05339.novelty: Uses distillation as exploration support expansion rather than imitation: identifies hard prompts where student lacks coverage, selects verified teacher proposals ranked by student proximity, consolidates via forward-KL before returning to GRPO; works with black-box teachers requiring only output trajectories

on_policy_mechanism.evidence_quote: Sample K unaided student rollouts and estimate p_S(x). if p_S(x) ≤ τ_low then Generate up to M proposal rollouts. Keep verifier-passing teacher trajectories.

opd_classification.reasoning: TREK uses verified teacher output trajectories (not logits) consolidated via teacher-forced NLL (SFT-like loss on selected proposals), then returns to GRPO; the forward-KL consolidation is effectively SFT on teacher text, not distributional logit-level supervision on student rollouts, failing C2 and C3 of the OPD iron law.

key_findings: TREK with DeepSeek-V4 proposals improves Qwen3-8B from 47.9 to 51.1 on AIME 2024 and from 36.9 to 40.3 on AIME 2025 (avg@16)
Self-context variant (no external teacher) still improves over direct GRPO, reaching 49.6/38.5 for Qwen3-8B on AIME 2024/2025
On agentic tasks, TREK raises ALFWorld success from 75.8 to 82.8 and ScienceWorld from 12.5 to 26.7
Forward-KL consolidation outperforms OPD-style supervision by 1.1–2.9 points across all scales
Gains concentrate on hardest task types: Heat&Place gains +19.1 points and Examine in Light gains +12.6 points
2607.05339.ablations_summary: OPD-style supervision vs forward-KL consolidation shows forward-KL is stronger for support expansion (1.1–2.9 point advantage). Per-task breakdown confirms gains concentrate on hard prompts. Self-context variant demonstrates method works without external teacher.
limitations: Quality of proposal filtering depends on verifier strength
Trimmed NLL reachability proxy does not capture fine-grained learnability and is sensitive to verbosity
Method adds teacher queries and verifier calls on top of ordinary GRPO
Verified-only rule is conservative; unverified trajectories may contain useful patterns but are unstable to consolidate at current student scales
failure_modes: Near-saturated benchmarks (e.g., MATH-500) show only modest gains due to limited headroom
Method stalls when proposal source also cannot produce verified solutions for hard prompts
2607.05339.relevance_to_opd: Directly compares against OPD-style supervision and argues forward-KL on verified teacher trajectories is superior for support expansion on hard prompts; positions itself as complementary to OPD methods that improve supervision on already-reachable behaviors

2607.05471.title: KAT-Coder-V2.5 Technical Report
2607.05471.summary: End-to-end agentic post-training framework for coding agents with multi-teacher on-policy distillation

method.training_loop: Train domain experts via PPO with harness randomization, then fuse via Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation: student generates trajectories, domain teacher provides token-level logits, optimize reverse KL
method.data_source: Repository environments from AutoBuilder + KwaiClawEnv synthesized tool-use trajectories
key_components: Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation (MOPD)
AutoBuilder environment construction
KwaiClawEnv tool-use trajectory synthesis
Asymmetric actor-critic PPO with hindsight-augmented value estimation
Harness randomization
Drift-aware dynamic truncation
Off-policy cold start
Harness-oriented reward framework

2607.05471.novelty: Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation (MOPD) that fuses five domain experts into a single student via reverse KL on student-generated trajectories with drift-aware truncation and off-policy cold start, avoiding see-saw degradation of weight-space merging

on_policy_mechanism.evidence_quote: the student first generates an on-policy trajectory y ∼ π_θ(· | x). The corresponding domain teacher π_T_d then provides token-level logit supervision on the same trajectory.

opd_classification.reasoning: MOPD is a white-box multi-teacher on-policy distillation method with reverse KL on student rollouts, with stabilization via drift-aware truncation (token weighting) and off-policy cold start

key_findings: KAT-Coder-V2.5 achieves 94.9 on PinchBench, the best agentic tool-use result surpassing Opus 4.8 (93.5)
KAT-Coder-V2.5 scores 65.2 on SWE-Bench Pro, ranking second only to Opus 4.8 (69.2)
Sandbox feedback error rate dropped from ~16% to below 2% after reliability hardening
MOPD fuses five domain experts without the see-saw effect of weight-space merging
AutoBuilder increased environment-construction success rate from 16.5% to 57.2%
2607.05471.ablations_summary: No formal ablation table is provided; the paper describes qualitative contributions of sandbox optimization (16%→<2% error), harness scaling for cross-harness generalization, drift-aware truncation for long-context stability, and off-policy cold start before MOPD
limitations: Extending verifiable environment construction to broader settings
Strengthening long-horizon credit assignment
Improving generalization on terminal and scientific tasks
failure_modes: Format/context-structure/control-flow overfitting when training on single harness
Teacher distribution becomes unreliable on long student-generated prefixes causing loss oscillation and entropy collapse
2607.05471.relevance_to_opd: Proposes Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation (MOPD) where the student generates agentic trajectories and multiple domain-expert teachers provide token-level logit supervision via reverse KL, with drift-aware truncation and off-policy cold start for long-context stability

2607.05804.title: TurnOPD: Making On-Policy Distillation Turn-Aware for Efficient Long-Horizon Agent Training
2607.05804.summary: Turn-level budgeting strategy for efficient on-policy distillation of long-horizon agents

method.training_loop: Student rolls out in environment, teacher provides reverse-KL supervision on student-visited prefixes; adaptive rollout-depth controller truncates rollouts, progressive turn-normalized loss shifts KL weighting from token-level to turn-balanced
method.loss_formulation: L = (1 - α) L_token + α L_round, where α increases linearly with training progress; base loss is reverse-KL: D_KL(π_θ(·|s_i) || π_T(·|s_i))
method.data_source: On-policy student rollouts in ALFWorld, WebShop, and Multi-Hop Search environments
key_components: adaptive rollout-depth budgeting via probe-based turn statistics
progressive turn-normalized loss budgeting with linear blend
survivor-weighted KL centroid
coverage-based lower bound

2607.05804.novelty: Introduces turn-level budgeting for agent OPD: adaptive rollout-depth controller that dynamically selects rollout length via survivor-weighted KL centroid and coverage thresholds, plus progressive turn-normalized loss that shifts from trajectory-level to turn-balanced KL allocation over training

on_policy_mechanism.evidence_quote: the student samples its own rollout τ ∼ π_θ(·|x) for a prompt x ∼ p_data, and a frozen teacher π_T provides token-level supervision on the student-visited prefixes

opd_classification.reasoning: The paper proposes a curriculum/scheduling strategy (adaptive rollout depth + progressive loss normalization) for on-policy distillation of agents, fitting efficiency/curriculum techniques for OPD.

key_findings: TurnOPD achieves 2.29× faster training on ALFWorld-1.7B while improving Same-Step Avg@4 from 83.0 to 86.3
On WebShop, TurnOPD improves both accuracy (82.80 vs 81.65) and wall time (1.24h vs 1.57h)
Adaptive depth alone cuts wall time from 4.42h to 1.96h but does not improve accuracy; linear KL blend improves accuracy to 85.1; combining both gives best tradeoff
Only 3.6–4.5% of KL loss is assigned to the deepest third of turns on ALFWorld under vanilla OPD
Qwen3-4B student exceeds teacher reference (92.21 vs 90.75) on ALFWorld with TurnOPD
2607.05804.ablations_summary: Adaptive depth provides efficiency (halves wall time) but not accuracy alone; linear KL blend provides accuracy improvement (+2.1 on ALFWorld-1.7B); combining both gives best accuracy-time tradeoff. Hard turn-level KL achieves 85.0 vs linear blend's 85.1. Coverage quantile p controls rollout depth conservativeness smoothly.
limitations: Evaluated on only three agent benchmarks with relatively structured environments
Requires periodic full-depth probe rollouts which add overhead
Coverage controller requires distinguishing successful from failed trajectories (though full-population CDF variant exists)
Method tested with only 100 optimizer steps
failure_modes: On Multi-Hop Search Same-Step setting, vanilla OPD retains small advantage over TurnOPD
Full-population CDF overestimates required depth due to failed trajectories stalling at max depth

theory.theoretical_claim: Contamination-compression bound: observed KL ≤ (1-λ(c)) × free-component KL, explaining why late-turn KL underestimates true policy disagreement
theory.proof_sketch: Uses joint convexity of KL divergence and log-sum inequality to show that context-forced mass λ compresses measured KL even when free-component disagreement persists

2607.05804.relevance_to_opd: Directly proposes and evaluates improvements to on-policy distillation for multi-turn agent tasks, with turn-level budgeting of both rollout depth and KL loss allocation as the core contribution

2607.06855.title: Geometric Self-Distillation for Reasoning Generalization
2607.06855.summary: Geometry-aware on-policy self-distillation using Hellinger loss and Fisher-Rao proximal drift control for OOD reasoning

method.training_loop: Student generates on-policy rollouts; privileged-context teacher (same model + solution trace) scores each position; Hellinger distillation loss + Fisher-Rao proximal penalty optimized via K-FAC natural gradient; checkpoint refreshed every K steps
method.loss_formulation: L(θ) = L_distil(θ) + λ L_prox(θ; θ_ckpt), where L_distil = E[D_H(p_θ, q)] and L_prox = E[d_FR²(π_θ, π_θ_ckpt)]
method.data_source: DAPO-Math-17k (competition mathematics with verifiable integer answers)
key_components: Hellinger divergence distillation loss with overlap-weighted gradient
Fisher-Rao proximal term to recent checkpoint
K-FAC natural gradient update
Privileged-context self-distillation (full solution trace as teacher context)

2607.06855.novelty: Replaces standard KL with Hellinger loss that attenuates teacher pull at low-overlap states via geometric-mean weighting, adds Fisher-Rao proximal penalty for cumulative drift control, and optimizes both in distribution geometry via natural gradient—all three in a unified information-geometric framework

on_policy_mechanism.evidence_quote: the student samples one on-policy rollout per problem from the question alone, and the teacher, the same model conditioned on a drawn solution, scores that trajectory at every position

opd_classification.reasoning: Proposes a new distillation objective (Hellinger + Fisher-Rao proximal) that modulates per-token teacher influence based on overlap geometry, fitting §4.1 (new fixed objective/divergence); also involves self-distillation (§5.3.2) and implicit token weighting via overlap (§6.1)

training_setup.compute_budget: ≈7 GPU-h per 8B training run on H200

key_findings: GEOSD improves average OOD accuracy by 5.7–8.6 points (avg@16) over the base model across three model families, while standard KL objectives degrade it
OOD gains hold consistently across five model scales (1.7B–32B), peaking at +8.6 at 8B and +6.1 at 32B
Standard forward KL matching concentrates probability mass at high-entropy states, resulting in false consensus (confident agreement on wrong answers), whereas GEOSD keeps alternatives in reach
GEOSD adds only 1.10× wall-clock overhead and 1.21× memory over standard OPSD
All three components (Hellinger loss, FR proximal, natural gradient) are load-bearing: removing any one surrenders a large part of the OOD gain
2607.06855.ablations_summary: Removing FR proximal (λ=0) causes largest OOD drop (-6.7 points) and highest drift; replacing Hellinger with JSD loses -4.4 OOD; replacing natural gradient with AdamW loses -3.8 OOD. All components are necessary for full performance.
limitations: Evaluated only on mathematical reasoning domain; transfer to code, scientific, or general multi-step reasoning is untested
Only full correct solution as privileged context studied; qualitatively different signals (hints, feedback) not evaluated
Teacher is always the current student; fixed reference, delayed copy, or EMA alternatives not evaluated
Supervision bounded by what base model can already produce (verified rollouts from π₀)
Encodes inductive bias that recent predictive behavior is worth preserving, which may hinder learning requiring large behavioral change
Moving anchor bounds rate of drift but not its endpoint over much longer training horizons
failure_modes: For weak base models, high-entropy states may reflect ignorance rather than healthy uncertainty, causing useful teacher signal to be attenuated
When correct continuation has negligible student mass initially, overlap weighting suppresses both harmful and useful teacher signal

theory.theoretical_claim: Near agreement all divergences coincide to leading order (Fisher quadratic); Hellinger gradient weights each token by geometric-mean overlap √(p_i q_i), attenuating unsupported teacher confidence; Fisher-Rao proximal in natural gradient yields checkpoint pullback
theory.proof_sketch: Second-order expansion of KL, Hellinger, Fisher-Rao around diagonal shows all equal ½Q(ε)+O(ε³); square-root embedding maps simplex to sphere where Fisher metric becomes round metric; natural gradient preconditioner converts FR proximal gradient into geometry-aware pullback (Appendix A)

2607.06855.relevance_to_opd: Directly proposes a new on-policy self-distillation objective (Hellinger + Fisher-Rao proximal) that addresses the OOD degradation problem in privileged-context OPSD by regulating both per-step teacher influence and cumulative predictive drift in distribution geometry

2607.07050.title: Behavior Leverage Imbalance in Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation
2607.07050.summary: Identifies behavior leverage imbalance in multi-teacher OPD and proposes SoftClamp calibration

method.training_loop: Student generates rollouts from current policy; two specialized teachers (tool-call, response) provide JSD supervision on student tokens; SoftClamp dynamically compresses extreme per-token JSD above threshold C=k*mean(d)
method.loss_formulation: L = JSD(p_t(·|x,y_{<i}) || p_s(·|x,y_{<i})) with d'_i = d_i * C/stopgrad(d_i) for d_i > C
method.data_source: APIGen-MT (15,419 tool-call + 15,420 response examples)
key_components: Multi-teacher on-policy distillation with JSD
SoftClamp per-token divergence calibration
Behavior leverage imbalance diagnosis
Format anchoring with supervised loss

2607.07050.novelty: Identifies that local token-level signals at mode-entry positions (e.g., <tool_call>) have disproportionate control over global generation mode in multi-teacher OPD, and proposes SoftClamp to dynamically compress extreme per-token JSD while preserving nonzero gradients

on_policy_mechanism.evidence_quote: In on-policy distillation, the student samples from its current policy and then learns from teacher distributions evaluated on the sampled trajectory.

opd_classification.reasoning: SoftClamp is a per-token divergence calibration/weighting method that compresses extreme token-level JSD signals in multi-teacher on-policy distillation, fitting §6.1 (token weighting).

key_findings: Vanilla GKD improves tool-call recall to 91.4% but raises over-calling to 13.7%, while SoftClamp reduces over-calling to 9.0% while matching 89.2% decision accuracy.
Aggregate token exposure and full-sequence JSD do not explain over-calling; tool/response JSD ratio is below 1.0 for all methods.
SoftClamp reduces multi-turn tool-call loops from 14.8% (Loop@3) to 10.1% and raises final-answer rate from 89.6% to 94.1%.
Response-side decision pressure (P(tool) on response samples) tracks final over-calling across GKD variants better than aggregate divergence metrics.
2607.07050.ablations_summary: Comparison of Vanilla GKD, Hard Clip (c=0.5), Global Reweight (α=0.3), and SoftClamp (k=3.0) shows progressive reduction in over-calling: 13.7% → 12.0% → 10.1% → 9.0%, with SoftClamp preserving gradients unlike Hard Clip.
limitations: Experiments focus on one base model and a two-teacher tool-call vs response setting
Reported numbers are point estimates without multi-seed studies
SoftClamp is a mitigation, not a theory-optimal solution; excessive compression could underfit useful specialization
Step-level evidence uses teacher-forced process metrics, not checkpoint-wise free-generation probes
BFCL multi-turn diagnostic is not official benchmark scoring
Supervised format anchor changes the pure OPD setting
failure_modes: When2Call out-of-domain: GKD variants retain high tool-call accuracy but perform worse on request-for-information and cannot-answer cases
Schema drift in pure OPD runs without format anchoring produces invalid tool-call strings
Excessive compression could underfit useful specialization signals from teachers
2607.07050.relevance_to_opd: Directly studies multi-teacher on-policy distillation, identifies behavior leverage imbalance as a failure mode, and proposes SoftClamp as a per-token JSD calibration method for GKD-based OPD in agentic tool-use settings.

2607.09375.title: Mach-Mind-4-Flash Technical Report
2607.09375.summary: 35B MoE model with 3B active params using multi-teacher on-policy distillation for expert fusion

method.training_loop: Train domain-specific RL experts in parallel, then fuse via MOPD: student generates rollouts, routed frozen teachers provide per-token reverse-KL supervision with clipped policy-gradient surrogate
method.data_source: Domain-specific synthesized data across reasoning, general, safety, tool-use, deep search, code agent, claw agent domains
key_components: Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation (MOPD)
routed reverse-KL objective
clipped policy-gradient surrogate for off-policy correction
dynamic multi-teacher scalable architecture
HMPO token efficiency
parallel RL expert training

2607.09375.novelty: Routed multi-teacher on-policy distillation (MOPD) that fuses multiple RL expert specialists into a single generalist via per-sample routing to domain teachers and token-level reverse-KL on student rollouts, eliminating see-saw degradation of mixed-reward RL

on_policy_mechanism.evidence_quote: each training sample is routed to the domain specialist that has already mastered it, and the student is supervised directly on its own rollouts through a token-level reverse-KL objective

opd_classification.reasoning: MOPD uses multiple frozen teacher models providing token-level reverse-KL supervision on student-generated rollouts with routed multi-teacher scheduling, fitting white-box multi-teacher OPD with a novel routed reverse-KL objective

key_findings: MOPD fuses 10+ specialist teachers into a single generalist without see-saw degradation, matching or exceeding individual expert performance
Mach-Mind-4-Flash (3B active) scores 92.70 on AIME'26, matching 120B-class models
Teacher-student same-size matching yields higher top-K overlap rate than substantially larger teachers
Adding code teacher improves non-code domains: AIME'25 +2.30, IFEval +2.14, Behavioral-SafetyBench +4.06
HMPO compresses reasoning chains by 19-46% with ≤0.7pp accuracy loss
Top-K overlap rate climbs monotonically from 0.73 to 0.84 during MOPD training
2607.09375.ablations_summary: Progressive teacher-composition study shows adding code teacher improves all domains (+0.85 to +4.06 across safety, math, IF benchmarks). Removing reasoning expert causes 2-4% drop on reasoning benchmarks. Same-size teacher outperforms larger teacher in overlap rate.
limitations: MOPD fusion introduces small but consistent gap on extremely long-horizon tasks like repository-level software engineering
HMPO currently targets single-turn reasoning; extending to multi-turn agentic trajectories remains open
Persistent multi-constraint web browsing and long-context comprehension remain weakest axes for compact models
failure_modes: Scaffold-specific behaviors are partially smoothed during distillation for long-horizon code agent tasks
Capabilities left unrepresented by teachers risk drifting during MOPD

theory.theoretical_claim: Single-sample k1 estimator is unbiased for reverse KL; clipped surrogate reduces to on-policy MOPD gradient when θ=θ_old
theory.proof_sketch: Appendix B derives k1 estimator unbiasedness for D_KL(π_θ||π_Tk), shows clipped surrogate collapses to Eq.3 when ρ_t≡1

2607.09375.relevance_to_opd: Directly proposes Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation (MOPD) as a core method: student generates rollouts, multiple frozen domain-expert teachers provide token-level reverse-KL supervision via routing, with clipped policy-gradient correction for asynchronous off-policy drift

2607.10805.title: Diagnosing and Mitigating Thinking Collapse in On-Policy Self-Distillation
2607.10805.summary: Diagnoses thinking collapse in reasoning OPSD and proposes AD-OPSD with adaptive pointwise divergence gating

method.training_loop: Student generates rollouts in thinking mode; teacher scores with ground-truth context; within top-p% student entropy sandbox, blend frozen base prior via sigmoid pointwise KL gate; outside sandbox, standard forward KL to teacher; optimize AD-OPSD loss
method.loss_formulation: L = sum_{yi in V_High-H} D_KL(pi_i*(·) || pi_theta(·)) + sum_{yj not in V_High-H} D_KL(pi_t(·) || pi_theta(·)), where pi_i* = U_i * pi_base + (1-U_i) * pi_t
method.data_source: OpenThoughts mathematical reasoning subset (up to 3K problems)
key_components: Entropy-based spatial sandbox localization (top-p% student entropy)
Asymmetrical pointwise divergence sigmoid gate (U_i)
Dual-perspective target interpolation between frozen base model and teacher
Active suppression region detection (logP_s > logP_t)

2607.10805.novelty: Identifies thinking collapse pathology in reasoning OPSD via entropy-based gradient masking and token-level discrepancy analysis; proposes asymmetrical pointwise KL divergence gate that dynamically blends frozen base prior with teacher target within localized high-entropy sandbox, replacing binary masking

on_policy_mechanism.evidence_quote: By distilling ground-truth-conditioned, on-policy target distributions of a teacher model into the student policy over its own sampled rollouts, OPSD avoids the exposure bias of off-policy imitation

opd_classification.reasoning: AD-OPSD proposes an adaptive gating mechanism (pointwise KL sigmoid gate) that dynamically modulates teacher influence per-token, fitting §4.2 (adaptive objective formulation)

key_findings: AD-OPSD improves over standard OPSD by up to +4.1% absolute average accuracy across diverse model scales and datasets
Standard OPSD collapses thinking density from 10.3 to 7.9 ET per 1k on Qwen3-1.7B; AD-OPSD recovers it to 8.4-8.6
Masking top 20% student entropy tokens recovers thinking density from 7.9 to 9.8 but fails to recover accuracy, motivating soft gating
Epistemic tokens are 95.35% concentrated in top 50% highest-entropy regions
Sigmoid pointwise KL gate outperforms alternatives by +3.9% on AIME 2025
AD-OPSD generalizes to NT/NT alignment, achieving +4.9% over standard OPSD under Thinking inference
2607.10805.ablations_summary: Sandbox percentile sweep shows optimal at 20-30%; gating function ablation shows sigmoid pointwise KL best (45.6% avg vs 43.6% next-best); static blending (SD-OPSD) effective but inferior to dynamic; context length study shows diminishing gains at longer horizons due to teacher-base convergence
limitations: Restricted to compact model scales (1.5B-4B) with LoRA due to compute constraints
Domain specialization limited to competition-level math; generalization to code, logic, multi-hop QA unexplored
Full-parameter fine-tuning and ultra-large models (32B, 70B) not evaluated
failure_modes: Performance gap diminishes at longer context horizons (2048 tokens) as teacher and base distributions converge
Over-expanding sandbox (100%) introduces correction dilution that weakens teacher corrective gradients
2607.10805.relevance_to_opd: Directly addresses a failure mode of on-policy self-distillation for reasoning LLMs and proposes an adaptive gating mechanism that modulates teacher logit supervision on student-generated rollouts

2607.13124.title: ShortOPD: Recovering Pruned LLMs with Short-to-Long On-Policy Distillation
2607.13124.summary: Short-to-long on-policy distillation recovers generation quality of structurally pruned LLMs

method.training_loop: Student generates on-policy rollouts with adaptive budget H_t; frozen pre-compression teacher scores same trajectories; student minimizes top-K JSD at every token; controller adjusts H based on repetition/truncation stats
method.data_source: 45,447 prompts: GSM8K train, MATH train, NVIDIA OpenCodeInstruct, MBPP, ShareGPT/Vicuna, UltraChat-200K
key_components: on-policy self-distillation from pre-compression teacher
generalized JSD with top-100+tail logits
repetition-gated short-to-long horizon controller
terminal periodic-loop detector
EMA-smoothed budget adaptation

2607.13124.novelty: Introduces a repetition-gated, truncation-aware short-to-long rollout budget controller for OPD that detects low-information repetitive suffixes in pruned model rollouts and adaptively shortens/lengthens the horizon, achieving equivalent quality with 71% fewer rollout tokens

on_policy_mechanism.evidence_quote: for each prompt x, the student samples on-policy rollouts y ∼ π_θ(· | x), the frozen teacher π_T is run on the same trajectories, and the student matches the teacher's next-token distribution at every response position

opd_classification.reasoning: The core novelty is a curriculum/scheduling mechanism (short-to-long budget control) that adapts rollout horizon during on-policy distillation training, fitting §6.2 (curriculum/scheduling for OPD efficiency)

key_findings: ShortOPD reaches 48.46 Avg (64.5% of teacher), nearly 9× the untrained pruned score of 5.71 and 18 points above the best off-policy baseline KD (30.52)
ShortOPD matches fixed H=8192 within 2 points while using 71% fewer rollout tokens (250M vs 869M) and 76% less wall-clock time (8.5h vs 35.9h)
Sparse-reward RLVR (PPO/GRPO) barely moves GSM8K accuracy (0.23/1.59) while ShortOPD on same prompts reaches 37.76
Recovery scales with epochs: 1→3 epochs improves Avg from 48.46 to 55.41 (73.7% of teacher)
Leave-one-domain-out shows domain-specific recovery: removing math drops GSM8K from 62.70 to 8.04
2607.13124.ablations_summary: On-policy vs off-policy: OPD beats KD by 18 Avg points. Dense vs sparse: OPD beats RLVR dramatically on GSM8K. Short-to-long vs fixed horizon: ShortOPD matches fixed-8192 within 2 points at 71% fewer tokens. Domain ablation: removing any domain sharply damages that domain's recovery.
limitations: Only tested with BI depth pruning at ~25% on Qwen3-4B; more pruning methods, model families, compression ratios, and larger models needed
Does not establish the boundary where a model has been compressed too aggressively for light post-compression recovery
failure_modes: Beyond ~35% compression the model enters incoherent regime where repetition-based detection no longer works
Recovery corpus must cover target capabilities; missing domains are not recovered

theory.theoretical_claim: Conditional OPD gradient vanishes linearly as student approaches teacher distribution under generalized JSD with top-K+tail aggregation and clipped importance weighting
theory.proof_sketch: At q=p, m=p so all log terms in JSD logit gradient are zero; first-order expansion shows gradient is O(δ) where δ=q-p; top-K+tail and clipping preserve the stationary point

2607.13124.relevance_to_opd: Directly proposes an on-policy distillation method where the pruned student generates rollouts and the pre-compression teacher provides dense logit-level JSD supervision at every token position, with a novel adaptive horizon controller

2607.13399.title: Demystifying On-Policy Distillation: Roles, Pathologies, and Regulations
2607.13399.affiliation_primary: The Chinese University of Hong Kong
2607.13399.summary: Systematic study of OPD as exploration catalyst, diagnosing pathologies and proposing signal regulations

method.training_loop: Student generates rollouts, teacher provides per-token log-ratio advantages, policy gradient with clipped importance ratio and regulated advantage (hard clip or log-scale compression)
method.loss_formulation: L_clip(θ) = -E[min(r_t * ã_t, clip(r_t, 1-ε, 1+ε) * ã_t)]
method.data_source: Nemotron-Cascade Math dataset
key_components: hard advantage clipping
soft log-scale compression
per-token advantage regulation
informativeness metric

2607.13399.novelty: Diagnoses two OPD pathologies (student-teacher mismatch and length exploitation) and proposes zero-overhead in-loop signal regulations (hard clipping and log-scale compression) that outperform naive OPD and larger teacher configurations

on_policy_mechanism.evidence_quote: OPD trains the student to minimize the reverse KL divergence from student to teacher: L_OPD(θ)=KL[π_θ∥π_T]=−E_{x,y∼π_θ}[log π_T(y|x)/π_θ(y|x)]

opd_classification.reasoning: This is an analysis/empirical study paper that diagnoses OPD pathologies and proposes lightweight signal regulation fixes, contributing to understanding failure modes and stabilization of OPD.

key_findings: OPD acts as exploration catalyst not ceiling breaker: pass@k convergence shows base model reaches OPD-trained levels at high k
Prompt diversity (n=1) consistently outperforms larger sampling depth (n=2, n=8) under fixed compute budget
Weaker teacher (Qwen3-1.7B-GRPO) outperforms stronger teacher (Qwen3-4B-GRPO) for base student due to distributional alignment
Log-scale compression with 1.7B-GRPO teacher achieves 30.4 avg score, surpassing naive OPD at 28.1 and GRPO baseline at 22.4
Regulated OPD with 4B teacher surpasses methods distilled from 30B teacher (UniOPD 30.7→32.5 on AIME25, GOPD 31.5→32.5)
2607.13399.ablations_summary: Compared hard clipping vs log-scale compression across teacher scales; log-scale better for matched teachers, hard clipping better for mismatched teachers; n=1 vs n=2 vs n=8 rollout configurations showing diversity wins; informativeness metric I predicts distillation trajectories
limitations: Hyperparameter heuristics for clipping bounds require empirical tuning based on teacher-student capacity gap
Study primarily focused on mathematical reasoning benchmarks with verifiable outcomes
Behavior of regulated OPD in open-ended text generation or knowledge-intensive QA tasks has not been fully verified
failure_modes: Student-teacher mismatch: stronger teacher (4B-GRPO) provides anti-correlated signals to base student
Length exploitation Mode A (Endless Exploration): student appends filler tokens to dilute negative advantages
Length exploitation Mode B (Abrupt Degeneration): student truncates responses prematurely for high prefix advantage
2607.13399.relevance_to_opd: Directly analyzes on-policy distillation, diagnosing its role as exploration catalyst, identifying two pathologies (student-teacher mismatch and length exploitation), and proposing signal regulation fixes that stabilize OPD training

2607.13639.title: OvisOCR2 Technical Report
2607.13639.summary: 0.8B end-to-end document parser via SFT, RL on 4B branch, on-policy distillation, and model fusion

method.training_loop: SFT both 0.8B and 4B → GRPO RL on 4B with multi-component reward → student 0.8B generates rollouts, teacher 4B scores top-k logits, reverse-KL loss → model fusion
method.loss_formulation: L_OPD(θ) = (1/|I|) Σ_{t∈I} D_KL(p̄_t ∥ q̄_t) where p̄_t is student top-k normalized, q̄_t is teacher top-k normalized
method.data_source: filtered real-document annotations + synthetic pages from HTML source
key_components: GRPO RL on 4B teacher branch
on-policy distillation with student top-k reverse KL
multi-component reward (text/formula/table)
model fusion via weighted parameter averaging
synthetic data pipeline with hard sample mining

contribution-guided token filtering
best-rollout selection
advantage flipping at localized tokens

The BPM target is exact at more than 99% of training positions where byte prefixes do not span multiple teacher tokens
Forward KL (β=0) performs best among three divergence variants on all three pairs
2607.22334.ablations_summary: Divergence choice (FKL > JSD > RKL) matters more than data changes; whitespace-row mask prevents code collapse; data-mixture and corpus-size perturbations shift avg@8 by at most 2 points; spanning corrections cover <1% of positions but are essential for stop-token transfer
limitations: Whitespace-row mask discards ~3.5% of aligned code rows, losing any signal they carry
Data quality bounds what experiments can show; whether remaining teacher-student gap survives higher-quality data is untested
Positions that reach no sync point are excluded from loss entirely
failure_modes: Whitespace collapse: byte-exact targets at all-whitespace positions transfer tokenizer segmentation patterns rather than predictive behavior, collapsing code pass rate
Late RKL collapse on most dissimilar pair (MiniMax-M2.7): pure mode-seeking with high tokenizer distance causes degeneration

theory.theoretical_claim: BPM target exactly recovers the teacher-induced byte-prefix marginal when relevant prefix does not span multiple teacher tokens (Proposition C.2); mass conservation proved via trie telescoping (Lemma C.1)
theory.proof_sketch: Each teacher token's mass telescopes along its byte-trie path; at the terminal node the full mass q(w) is credited exactly once to the deepest student-token ancestor, partitioning total mass across student tokens and residual

2607.22334.relevance_to_opd: Directly extends on-policy distillation to cross-tokenizer settings by constructing exact full-vocabulary distributional targets via byte-prefix marginalization, enabling OPD between any teacher-student pair regardless of tokenizer

2607.22629.title: Masked Distillation: Internalizing the Chain-of-Thought in Language Models
2607.22629.summary: Knowledge distillation framework that internalizes CoT reasoning into student parameters via masked on-policy reverse-KL

method.training_loop: Phase 1: collect teacher ITs via sampling. Phase 2: student generates rollouts conditioned on x only, teacher provides logits conditioned on x+ITs, minimize reverse-KL on student-sampled tokens.
method.loss_formulation: L_MD = D_KL( π_θ^S(·|x,y_{<t}) ∥ π^T(·|x,ITs,y_{<t}) ) computed on y'_t ~ π_θ^S
method.data_source: GSM8K (7.5K train) and Countdown (8K train)
key_components: masked distillation with α-suffix scaffolding
on-policy reverse-KL loss on student rollouts
teacher conditioned on its own ITs while student conditioned only on question
self-distillation and dual-model settings

2607.22629.novelty: Introduces masked distillation where teacher is conditioned on its own CoT trace (ITs) while student is conditioned only on input, with α-suffix scaffolding to interpolate between full internalization and full trace reproduction, using on-policy reverse-KL divergence

on_policy_mechanism.evidence_quote: On-policy KD: MinilLM[9], GKD[1], performs on-policy knowledge distillation by generating responses from the student model. L_GKD(θ):=E_{x∼X,y∼p^θ(·|x)} [D_KL(p_T(·|y_{<n},x) ∥ p^θ_S(·|y_{<n},x))]

opd_classification.reasoning: The method uses on-policy student rollouts with teacher logit supervision via reverse-KL divergence, with the novel contribution being masked conditioning (teacher sees CoT, student doesn't) and α-suffix scaffolding to control internalization degree.

key_findings: Full internalization (α=0) succeeds on GSM8K (76.0% vs 87.9% teacher) with 6.5× fewer tokens but fails on Countdown (41.7% below 56.2% base)
α=0.3 suffix scaffold on Countdown self-distillation raises accuracy from 41.7% to 86.2%, matching teacher (87.3%) at ~1.3× fewer tokens
On-policy reverse-KL significantly outperforms SFT: reverse-KL with 100 TTs achieves 67.25% vs SFT's 38.5% on Countdown
Under search-depth OOD shift, scaffold-trained variants (α=0.3-0.5) generalize better than non-masked (32.8% vs 25.7%)
2607.22629.ablations_summary: Compared teaching-token scaffolds vs suffix scaffolds (suffix wins), reverse-KL vs SFT (reverse-KL dramatically outperforms), varied α from 0 to 1.0 showing task-dependent optimal operating points
limitations: All variants use the same amount of training data and similar optimization steps, which may disadvantage masked variants
Amortization tradeoff between additional training cost and inference savings not studied
Only two domains tested (math and countdown)
failure_modes: Full internalization fails on Countdown where student has no prior pretraining exposure to the task format
Dual-model setting fails on hard OOD math (AIME-25: 0% for all variants) when teacher-student capacity gap is large
Search-depth shift causes accuracy collapse in dual-model Countdown setting
2607.22629.relevance_to_opd: Directly proposes on-policy knowledge distillation with reverse-KL where student generates rollouts and teacher provides logit supervision conditioned on additional context (CoT trace), extending GKD framework with masked conditioning

2607.23125.title: Self-Boosting Vision-Language Models with Noisy Student On-Policy Self-Distillation
2607.23125.affiliation_primary: The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology (Guangzhou)
2607.23125.summary: Self-distillation for VLMs using corrupted image inputs with clean-input predictions as teacher signal

method.training_loop: Sample mini-batch, generate on-policy response from corrupted image input, compute KL divergence between student (corrupted) and teacher (clean, stop-grad) distributions, update parameters
method.loss_formulation: L = E_{(q,x)~S, y~pi_theta(·|q,T(x))} D_KL(pi_theta(y|q,T(x)) || sg(pi_theta(y|q,x)))
method.data_source: Geometry3K training set (2.1K samples), MMK12 (15.6K), and multi-source collection (129K)
key_components: asymmetric input distributions via image corruption
self-distillation with stop-gradient teacher
on-policy rollout from corrupted inputs
reverse KL divergence loss
full vocabulary logit transfer

2607.23125.novelty: Introduces asymmetric input distributions (corrupted vs clean images) to enable self-supervised on-policy distillation without any external teacher model or ground-truth answers, where the same model serves as both teacher (clean input) and student (corrupted input)

on_policy_mechanism.evidence_quote:
Sample on-policy response y_i ~ pi_theta(·|q_i, T(x_i)), i=1,...,B
Compute the loss as Eq.(6)
L(θ) = E_{(q,x)~S, y~pi_theta(·|q,T(x))} D_KL(pi_theta(y|q,T(x)) || pi_theta(y|q,x))

opd_classification.reasoning: Pure self-distillation where the same model acts as both teacher and student with no external teacher, using on-policy rollouts and KL divergence loss on asymmetric inputs

key_findings: NOPD improves Qwen2.5-VL-7B by 20 points on Geometry3K validation set trained with only 2.1K samples
NOPD achieves 7.4 point gains on MathVista with Qwen2.5-VL-7B without any external supervision
NOPD matches or outperforms RLVR and on-policy distillation from external teachers on multiple benchmarks
NOPD achieves implicit reasoning compression, reducing tokens by 57.9% on MathVista while improving accuracy by 4.3%
NOPD improves three different models (Qwen2.5-VL-7B, Qwen3-VL-8B-Thinking, GLM-4.6V-Flash) on 10-12 out of 12 benchmarks
2607.23125.ablations_summary: Reverse KL outperforms forward KL and JSD; full vocabulary computation outperforms sampled token; synchronized teacher update beats fixed or EMA; all image corruption types help with combining all performing best; generation length of 2048 balances compute and performance
limitations: Method is only applicable to vision-language models because it relies on data augmentations for vision inputs

theory.theoretical_claim: NOPD gradient acts as contrastive policy gradient with log-ratio term as contrastive reward
theory.proof_sketch: Gradient derivation shows the loss gradient equals expectation over sampled tokens of log-ratio (corrupted/clean) times policy gradient, amplifying updates for tokens with large distribution discrepancy

2607.23125.relevance_to_opd: Directly extends on-policy distillation to the self-distillation setting where the same model serves as both teacher and student, eliminating the need for an external teacher by using asymmetric input distributions (clean vs corrupted images)

2607.23731.title: Outcome-Confounded Local Supervision in On-Policy Distillation
2607.23731.affiliation_primary: The Chinese University of Hong Kong, Shenzhen
2607.23731.summary: Diagnostic showing agreement-on-failure dominates OPD token mass due to outcome confounding

method.training_loop: Sample student rollouts, compute teacher likelihoods on student prefixes, cross pointwise divergence with trajectory outcome to form four-regime diagnostic
method.data_source: math_dapo discovery split (5,000 prompts)
key_components: outcome-resolved four-regime diagnostic
pointwise divergence estimator d_t
agreement-on-failure measurement
teacher-capability control (teacher-4/4)
three matched training probes (pure OPD, correct-only OPD, SPC)

2607.23731.novelty: Introduces outcome-resolved diagnostic crossing local teacher-student divergence with trajectory correctness, revealing agreement-on-failure dominates 67.84% of token mass and identifying a localization limitation of local divergence + outcome signals

on_policy_mechanism.evidence_quote: Given a prompt x, the student samples a response y = (y_1, ..., y_L). OPD then evaluates the teacher on each student-visited prefix s_t = (x, y_{<t}), producing π_T(·|s_t) without replacing the student's trajectory by a teacher solution.

opd_classification.reasoning: This is a diagnostic/analysis paper identifying a failure mode (agreement-on-failure) in OPD rather than proposing a new training method; it analyzes when local divergence signals are confounded by trajectory outcomes.

key_findings: Agreement-on-failure constitutes 67.84% of pooled response-token mass with Qwen3-8B student and Qwen3-32B teacher across eight seeds.
With Qwen2.5-7B/32B pair, agreement-on-failure remains at 67.68% of token mass, showing cross-pair generality.
Even on prompts the teacher solves in all four independent attempts, student accuracy rises to 86.91% but agreement-on-failure remains 14.76%.
Three training probes (pure OPD, correct-only OPD, SPC) do not consistently reduce agreement-on-failure.
89.15%-100% of wrong trajectories contain more than 80% low-divergence tokens across threshold reruns.
2607.23731.ablations_summary: Three training probes tested: pure OPD (76.17% val acc), correct-only OPD (75.20%), SPC (76.95%). SPC improves validation slightly but increases agreement-on-failure. Threshold sweep from 0.05 to 0.25 shows agreement-on-failure stable between 68.54% and 74.82%.
limitations: Primary evidence uses one mathematical-reasoning pipeline and a rule-based final-answer scorer.
1,024 rollouts from a larger prompt pool; seed variation is descriptive rather than population-level confidence interval.
Training comparison uses only two seeds and a small set of hand-designed probes.
Insufficiency argument is an indistinguishability boundary, not a formal impossibility theorem.
Have not empirically evaluated the three sources of localization information identified.
failure_modes: Local teacher-student agreement cannot distinguish tokens before and after a trajectory becomes unrecoverable.
Correct-only filtering discards information about where the student fails and provides no replacement target.
SPC contrast operates at sequence level without identifying where trajectories diverge.

theory.theoretical_claim: Indistinguishability argument: any token-wise intervention w_t = f(d_t, z(y)) cannot localize corrective targets inside failed trajectories because tokens with identical (d_t, z(y)) pairs may play different roles
theory.proof_sketch: Two tokens sharing the same observed pair (d_t, z(y)) must receive identical treatment under any such rule, even when one precedes the first reasoning error and the other lies after the trajectory is unrecoverable.

2607.23731.relevance_to_opd: Directly analyzes a fundamental failure mode of on-policy distillation: local teacher likelihoods on student-generated prefixes are confounded by trajectory outcome, identifying that agreement-on-failure dominates and simple interventions cannot resolve it without additional positional information.

2607.23740.title: Zing (知境) Technical Report: Social Mind for LLMs
2607.23740.summary: Framework for measuring, internalizing, and grounding social intelligence in LLMs

method.training_loop: Stage 1: SFT on CoT traces + GRPO with process/verifiable rewards; Stage 2: capability-oriented SFT + on-policy distillation (OPD) + mixed-reward GRPO
method.data_source: FLARE data flywheel: capability-diagnosis-driven synthesis from SoMBench taxonomy
key_components: FLARE data flywheel
capability diagnosis
staged training
on-policy distillation
rubric-based GRPO
multi-teacher capability routing

2607.23740.novelty: Diagnosis-driven staged training recipe combining capability-gap-targeted data synthesis, on-policy distillation, and rubric-based RL for social intelligence internalization

on_policy_mechanism.evidence_quote: Joint OPD and mixed-reward GRPO then refine the remaining unstable capabilities by combining teacher-guided process regularization with outcome and rubric rewards

opd_classification.reasoning: [2026-08-12 boss ruling] RECLASSIFIED yes->no. Application/system paper excluded from OPD scope. Zing social-intelligence technical report; OPD appears as one stage of a staged training recipe, not an OPD method contribution. Removed from Awesome list; PDF trashed.

key_findings: Best model (claude-opus-4-8) reaches only 72.08% on SoMBench, showing substantial remaining headroom
Zing-27B-Stage2 achieves the best average score among all compared models across five social-cognition benchmarks
Zing-32B-Stage2 shows competitive performance against DeepSeek-V4-Pro
None of 17 secondary dimensions reaches the 90% near-ceiling band on SoMBench

limitations: Social intelligence evaluation remains incomplete
Best model still misses ~28% of benchmark

Weak emotion-cause binding
Surface commonsense shortcuts instead of context-sensitive reasoning
