2607.24720.title: The Physics of Multi-Turn Long-Horizon Planning: From Pre-training to Post-training via Single- and Multi-Teacher On-Policy Agentic Distillation
2607.24720.affiliation_primary: Institute of Automation, Chinese Academy of Sciences
2607.24720.summary: Systematic study of long-horizon planning across pre-training, OPD, and multi-teacher OPD stages

method.training_loop: Student generates multi-turn rollouts in environment, teacher provides token-level logit supervision via reverse KL on student trajectories, cascaded multi-teacher OPD trains sequentially
method.loss_formulation: L = E_{tau~pi_theta} [ sum_k sum_t D_KL(p_{k,t} || q_{k,t}) ]
method.data_source: Synthetic controllable planning gym with hierarchical skill graphs across 3 domains
key_components: On-policy agentic distillation (OPD)
Multi-teacher on-policy distillation (MOPD)
Top-k OPD
Full-vocabulary OPD
PG-style OPD
GKD-style OPD
Controllable planning gym

2607.24720.novelty: Unified study distinguishing planning patterns (low mutual information) from planning knowledge (high mutual information) to identify applicability boundaries of GRPO vs OPD, plus multi-teacher cascaded OPD analysis showing shared planning patterns enable cross-environment generalization

on_policy_mechanism.evidence_quote: On-Policy Agentic Distillation optimizes the student policy π_θ directly on its self-explored interactive trajectories. Formally, we define a K-turn trajectory τ = (g, s_0, Ŷ_1, s_1, ..., Ŷ_K, s_K) ∼ π_θ

opd_classification.reasoning: The paper's core contribution is a systematic analysis of on-policy distillation (OPD) for multi-turn agentic planning, studying its applicability regions vs GRPO and extending to multi-teacher OPD, making it an analysis paper centered on OPD mechanisms.

train: Controllable Planning Gym (Fantasy Alchemy, Livestock Farming, Electronic Assembly)
eval: Controllable Planning Gym test set (Short/Middle/Long horizons)

key_findings: OPD has a broader effective region than GRPO under low-quality pre-training data and long planning horizons, achieving +18.42 avg improvement vs GRPO's +7.39 in 4Opt:8Sub setting
Internalized world models improve long-horizon generalization by +45.8% avg@8 on long-horizon tasks compared to direct answering
Mismatched procedural knowledge between teacher and student causes ID performance collapse (-36.09 points on FA Middle) even when teacher achieves 100% accuracy
Multi-teacher OPD enables cross-environment generalization when planning patterns are shared and compatible, transferring abilities to unseen domains
Suboptimal trajectories in pre-training cause catastrophic collapse on long-horizon tasks due to compounding errors
Just 5% long-horizon trajectories in pre-training boosts long-horizon pass@8 from 0% to 11.46%
2607.24720.ablations_summary: Key ablations compare GRPO vs OPD across 3 applicability regions (unnecessary/effective/unsupported), analyze impact of pre-training data quality (4Opt vs 4Opt:4Sub vs 4Opt:8Sub), planning horizon (short/middle/long), knowledge alignment (matched vs mismatched recipes), and multi-teacher patterns (shared/partial/conflict)
limitations: Uses synthetic controllable environments rather than real-world agentic tasks
Model sizes not specified, likely small-scale given from-scratch pre-training
Counterfactual synthesis rules used for scalability may not fully represent real-world complexity
Only cascaded MOPD studied, not mixture-based multi-teacher approaches
failure_modes: OPD fails when teacher and student have mismatched procedural knowledge (different valid paths for same goal)
GRPO fails in long-horizon + low-quality pre-training settings due to sparse credit assignment and vanishing gradients
Multi-teacher OPD causes catastrophic forgetting when environments have completely conflicting planning patterns
OPD reduces entropy and limits capability upper bound compared to GRPO's pass@k ceiling

theory.theoretical_claim: Mutual information framework: planning patterns have low I(T;P) enabling RL generalization, while planning knowledge has high I(T;K) requiring SFT injection
theory.proof_sketch: Defines I(T;P) < I(T;K) based on reusability of patterns vs task-specificity of knowledge, uses SVD cosine similarity to demonstrate gradient direction consistency of OPD vs GRPO

2607.24720.relevance_to_opd: Directly studies on-policy distillation for multi-turn agentic planning, comparing OPD variants (PG-style, GKD-style, Top-k, Full-vocabulary) with GRPO, identifying applicability boundaries, and extending to multi-teacher cascaded OPD (MOPD)

2607.24653.title: Kimi K3: Open Frontier Intelligence
2607.24653.summary: 2.8T MoE model with KDA, AttnRes, and multi-teacher on-policy distillation for unified post-training

method.training_loop: SFT cold-start → domain/effort-specialized RL (9 experts) → Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation (MOPD) consolidating experts into unified model via per-token log-ratio reward in RL framework
method.loss_formulation: r_opd(y_t | e, x, y_{<t}) = clip(sg(log(pi_teacher(y_t|x,y_{<t}) / pi_theta(y_t|e,x,y_{<t}))), -R_max, R_max)
method.data_source: Curated web text, code, math, knowledge, vision corpora + RL task synthesis with knowledge-graph-guided retrieval
key_components: Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation (MOPD)
Domain-specialized RL experts at multiple reasoning efforts
Partial rollout scheme for long-horizon tasks
KDA + AttnRes + Stable LatentMoE architecture

2607.24653.novelty: Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation using per-token log-ratio as dense reward in RL framework to consolidate 9 domain/effort-specialized teacher experts into one unified model, integrated with partial rollout for million-token agentic trajectories

on_policy_mechanism.evidence_quote: Given an input query x and the prefix response y<t, the per-token OPD reward evaluated on yt between the teacher π(d,e)_teacher and the student πθ is defined as: r_opd(yt | e, x, y<t) = clip(sg(log(π(d,e)_teacher(yt|x,y<t) / πθ(yt|e,x,y<t))), -Rmax, Rmax)

opd_classification.reasoning: MOPD uses student-generated rollouts with per-token teacher log-probability ratio as dense reward signal integrated into RL, combining on-policy generation with teacher distributional supervision — fits RL-augmented OPD (§4.3) and multi-teacher scenarios (§5.1)

teacher.name: Kimi K3 domain/effort RL expert (9 experts)

key_findings: Kimi K3 achieves approximately 2.5× improvement in overall scaling efficiency over Kimi K2
Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation consolidates 9 domain/effort expert models into a single unified model
Scaling RL FLOPs consistently improves capabilities across knowledge, reasoning, vision, general agent, and coding tasks
KimiK3 scores 67.5% on DeepSWE, 88.3% on Terminal-Bench 2.1, 81.2% on FrontierSWE, and 91.2% on BrowseComp
Total of 51,219,741 sandboxes across 1,505,678 images were created during training and evaluation
2607.24653.ablations_summary: Architecture ablations show KDA lower-bounded decay eliminates diagonal-tile bottleneck; MoonViT-V2 from-scratch training matches SigLIP-initialized baseline with better stability; SiTU-GLU controls activation explosion while preserving SwiGLU local response; Quantile Balancing achieves perfect expert load balance; cosine decay consistently outperforms WSD under respective optimal hyperparameters
limitations: Overall performance still trails the most powerful proprietary models (Claude Fable 5 and GPT-5.6 Sol)
Gap remains on research-level tasks like HLE-Full and CritPt

theory.theoretical_claim: Balanced assignment with at most E/R redundant experts per rank is always feasible and essentially tight
theory.proof_sketch: Proved that MoonEP perfect balance always exists with at most E/R redundant experts per rank via integer linear programming analysis

2607.24653.relevance_to_opd: Introduces Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation (MOPD) that consolidates domain-specialized RL expert policies into a unified model using per-token log-ratio between teacher and student as dense reward signal during student rollouts, directly instantiating on-policy distillation at frontier scale

2607.24771.title: RoCo-ACE: Rollout-Conditioned Online Distillation for Retention-Aware Knowledge Injection
2607.24771.summary: Rollout-conditioned contrastive online distillation for knowledge injection with retention

method.training_loop: Student generates rollout, EMA teacher scores rollout with reference-free and reference-conditioned views, RoCo reweights distillation by likelihood contrast, ACE adds sparse CE on omitted anchors
method.loss_formulation: L = λ_RoCo * L_RoCo + λ_ACE * L_ACE, where L_RoCo = weighted-avg D_KL(q_ref || p_θ) and L_ACE = weighted CE on anchor tokens
method.data_source: EVOKE (entity/news updates), MLLM-CL VP and Sci benchmarks
key_components: same-rollout reference-free/reference-conditioned likelihood contrast (RoCo)
sparse anchored cross-entropy for omitted facts (ACE)
EMA teacher synchronized from student
span-aware weight smoothing

2607.24771.novelty: Uses same-rollout likelihood contrast between reference-free and reference-conditioned teacher views to selectively reweight on-policy distillation tokens, plus sparse anchor correction for omitted facts, improving injection-retention trade-off over uniform online distillation

on_policy_mechanism.evidence_quote: the student samples an on-policy rollout y = (y_{i,1},...,y_{i,T_i}) ∼ p_θ(· | x_i, I_i). This rollout exposes a supervision split for factual updating

opd_classification.reasoning: The method uses adaptive token-level reweighting of KL distillation loss on student-generated rollouts via reference-conditioned likelihood contrast, fitting §4.2 (adaptive objective). Token weighting aspect also relates to §6.1.

key_findings: RoCo-ACE achieves 27.6 EVOKE Inj. Acc. (+11.2 over base, +6.7 over SDFT) while keeping Ret. Avg. at 56.5 (only -0.7 from base model's 57.2)
Compared with KORE (strongest non-ours injection), RoCo-ACE improves EVOKE Inj. Acc. by 2.4 and Ret. Avg. by 9.5 points
Same-rollout likelihood contrast (RoCo) improves EVOKE from 20.9 to 23.7 over uniform SDFT, adding ACE further reaches 27.6
Method generalizes to Qwen3-VL-30B (31.2 vs 21.6 base) and InternVL3.5-8B (20.9 vs 11.1 base)
2607.24771.ablations_summary: RoCo contrast reweighting contributes +2.8 EVOKE over uniform SDFT; ACE adds +3.9 on top; full-reference SFT controls hurt retention more than ACE; fixed teacher loses 2.0 injection points vs EMA; mismatched reference drops to 18.5 proving semantic alignment is needed
limitations: Designed for settings with authoritative natural-language references; weaker for label-only or very short answers
Does not use region-level or OCR-level evidence annotations for visual grounding
Retention evaluated empirically; no formal guarantees over all non-updated capabilities
Depends on reference quality; noisy or biased references can amplify wrong signals
failure_modes: When target entity is completely absent from rollout, RoCo alone cannot directly teach it (requires ACE)
Noisy or stylistically biased authoritative references can lead RoCo contrast to amplify wrong signal
Very short or implicit-evidence references provide weak anchor signal for ACE
2607.24771.relevance_to_opd: Directly proposes a novel on-policy distillation objective that uses student-generated rollouts with adaptive token-level KL reweighting based on reference-conditioned likelihood contrast from an EMA self-teacher, advancing granularity of OPD supervision for knowledge injection

2607.26057.title: Pass the Baton: Trajectory-Relayed On-Policy Distillation
2607.26057.summary: Relay-OPD detects teacher-student reasoning divergence to trigger brief teacher takeovers during on-policy distillation

method.training_loop: Student rolls out trajectory; at handoff triggers (teacher wants reflection, student doesn't), teacher generates brief leg; student resumes; distill on relay trajectory with clipped reverse-KL advantage
method.loss_formulation: L = -E[1/N sum_t min(ρ_t A^Relay_t, clip(ρ_t, 1-ε, 1+ε) A^Relay_t)] where A^Relay_t = log π_T(z_t|h_t) - log π_θ̄(z_t|h_t)
method.data_source: English subset of DAPO-Math-17K
key_components: handoff trigger based on teacher-student continuation asymmetry
relay trajectory construction with teacher legs
relay budget (M,L) limiting interventions
unified speculative decoding engine
reverse-KL single-sample objective on relay tokens

2607.26057.novelty: Identifies teacher-student continuation asymmetry on failed prefixes as a label-free handoff trigger and introduces budgeted relay trajectories that interleave brief teacher legs into student rollouts, concentrating correction at early failure points while preserving on-policy properties

on_policy_mechanism.evidence_quote: At each training iteration, standard OPD first generates an on-policy trajectory using the old student policy: y = (y_1,...,y_N) ~ π_θ̄(·|x). ... The teacher then supplies dense token-level guidance on the prefixes the student actually visits.

opd_classification.reasoning: Relay-OPD is an adaptive on-policy distillation method that introduces state-driven teacher intervention during student rollouts, modifying the trajectory construction with a budgeted curriculum of teacher legs.

key_findings: Relay-OPD outperforms standard OPD by +5.73% and FastOPD by +1.49% average accuracy for the 1.7B student across 8 math benchmarks
Training trajectory length is reduced by over 50% compared to standard OPD (2296 vs 4658 tokens for 1.7B)
Teacher token ratio starts at ~13% and drops to 2-3% after about 20 training steps as the student improves
Replacing only the single reflection token at triggers (0.35% teacher tokens) already lifts accuracy from 27.73 to 34.96 (+7.23%)
Relay-OPD reduces inference response length by 14-28% compared to FastOPD while improving accuracy
2607.26057.ablations_summary: Teacher leg adds +2.77% over trigger-stop alone; relay token objective (46.96) outperforms student draft token (44.56) and teacher FKL (44.08); optimal budget is M=2, L=3; handoff K=5 beats K=1 (44.27) and K=10 (43.14); all K values beat standard OPD (K=|V|, 41.23)
limitations: Evaluation limited to mathematical reasoning with Qwen3 teacher-student pairs
Reflection-token set may need adjustment for different model families
Benefits expected to diminish as teacher-student capability gap narrows
Relay budget tuned on 1.7B student and reused for 0.6B without re-tuning
failure_modes: When teacher-student gap is too small, continuation asymmetry signal weakens
Overly long or frequent teacher takeovers (high M or L) push trajectory too far from student policy, degrading performance
2607.26057.relevance_to_opd: Directly extends on-policy distillation by addressing prefix failure through state-driven teacher intervention during student rollouts, maintaining on-policy properties while providing corrective teacher logit supervision at critical failure points

2607.26246.title: Weak-to-Strong On-Policy Distillation
2607.26246.summary: On-policy distillation from weak models via contrastive logit directions anchored on student base

method.training_loop: Student generates on-policy rollouts; proxy teacher logits = softmax(z_base + α(z+ - z-)); student minimizes per-token reverse KL(πS || πT,α) on own rollouts for 100 steps
method.loss_formulation: L = E_{x~D, y~πS(·|x)} [ Σ_t KL( πS(·|s_t) || πT,α(·|s_t) ) ] where πT,α(·|s_t) = softmax(z_base(s_t) + α(z+(s_t) - z-(s_t)))
method.data_source: DeepMath-103K (level-6 subset) for math, Eurus-RL-Code for code
key_components: contrastive logit direction from positive/negative weak model pair
proxy teacher synthesis via logit arithmetic anchored on student base
per-token reverse KL on student rollouts
three contrast pair instantiations: pre-RL/post-RL, smaller/larger, correct/wrong hints
multi-teacher composition via additive logit directions

2607.26246.novelty: Constructs a proxy teacher by adding the logit difference of a weak positive-negative model pair to the student's own base model, enabling on-policy distillation from models weaker than the student without distribution mismatch or capability ceiling

on_policy_mechanism.evidence_quote: The student πS, initialized from the same base model, generates on-policy rollouts and minimizes the per-token reverse KL toward this proxy teacher.

opd_classification.reasoning: White-box logit-level proxy teacher constructed from weak models; student generates own rollouts and minimizes reverse KL against teacher logits, fitting the OPD paradigm with a novel teacher construction from weaker sources.

teacher.name: Proxy Teacher (Qwen3-4B w/ correct hints + Qwen3-4B w/ wrong hints + Qwen3-8B base)

key_findings: W2S-OPD outperforms OPD by 11.4% relative on math reasoning in the single-teacher pre-RL/post-RL setting (avg 51.8 vs 46.5)

All experiments use Qwen3 family models with shared vocabulary
Limited to math and code domains in evaluation

When capability gap in contrast pair is small, improvement is reduced

top-K KL divergence with tail bucket
safety teacher from aligned model

template-independent refusal prior distillation

stagnation detection flag

2607.29209.title: SAF-OPD: Stable Advantage Fusion for On-Policy Distillation
2607.29209.summary: Stable four-stage fusion of RLVR and OPD advantages via magnitude and temporal control

method.training_loop: GRPO samples student rollouts, teacher scores each token for OPD advantage, SAF applies sparsify→tanh-compress→KL-triggered-warmup→anneal to OPD advantage before fusing with GRPO advantage for policy gradient update
method.loss_formulation: A_total_{i,t} = A^GRPO_i + opd_coef(s) * scale(s) * A^{OPD,tanh}_{i,t}
method.data_source: 57K DeepMath (difficulty>=6) for math, 25K Eurus-RL-Code for code
key_components: top-k% sparsification of OPD advantage
bounded tanh compression
KL-triggered warm-up
linear annealing of OPD coefficient

2607.29209.novelty: Identifies magnitude and temporal mismatches when naively fusing GRPO and OPD advantages, and proposes a four-stage switchable pipeline (sparsify-then-compress for magnitude, warm-up-then-anneal for temporal) that controls the OPD advantage before fusion, unlike prior fixed-coefficient or coarse response-level gating approaches

on_policy_mechanism.evidence_quote: Student responses are sampled on policy, and the teacher scores those same responses token by token rather than generating separate trajectories.

opd_classification.reasoning: The paper fuses OPD with RL (GRPO) via a controlled advantage fusion mechanism, making it an RL-augmented OPD method; it also contributes token-level sparsification (§6.1) and temporal scheduling (§6.2).

key_findings: SAF improves aggregate score over fixed-coefficient GRPO+OPD by 0.51–2.70% across all six model–domain settings

2607.29209.ablations_summary: Magnitude control alone (top-k + tanh) matches fixed fusion (44.35% vs 44.38%); adding warmup without annealing yields 44.07%; annealing alone gives 45.23%; full SAF with δ=0.2 achieves 45.89%; δ=0.3 drops to 44.51%

Single teacher (Qwen3-30B-A3B) used; untested with other teachers
Hyperparameter sensitivity across untested domains not explored

For Qwen3-1.7B code, OPD-only outperforms SAF (51.77% vs 51.39%)

2607.29320.title: MAGA: Multi-Platform Self-Fusion of GUI Agents via Structured Action Distillation
2607.29320.summary: Structured action distillation for unifying domain-specific GUI agents via conditional signal re-allocation

method.training_loop: Student generates rollouts on offline GUI inputs; routed domain-specific teacher scores student tokens with type-hinted prompt; token weights assigned by action correctness rules; update student with weighted reverse-KL advantage
method.loss_formulation: L_Maga(θ) = -E_{d,x,y} [1/|y| Σ_t w_t * sg[log π_Td(y_t|P_T(x,z*),y_{<t}) - log π_θ(y_t|P_S(x),y_{<t})] * log π_θ(y_t|x,y_{<t})]
method.data_source: 343k proprietary industrial examples (200k web, 93k MobileWorld, 50k OSWorld)
key_components: student-side conditional training signal re-allocation
teacher-side type hint
routed domain-specific teacher scoring
action structure-aware token weighting

2607.29320.novelty: Introduces action-grammar-aware token weighting for on-policy distillation in GUI agents: removes fully correct trajectories, amplifies action span when type is correct, masks parameters when type is wrong; adds training-only teacher hint with ground-truth action type

on_policy_mechanism.evidence_quote: For a student π_θ generating tokens y = (y_1,...,y_{|y|}) with prefix y_{<t}, calculating the exact reverse KL divergence against T_d requires summing over the full vocabulary. For efficiency, we approximate this using only the single sampled token y_t

opd_classification.reasoning: [2026-08-12 boss ruling] RECLASSIFIED yes->no (score=7 review). MAGA: GUI-agent multi-platform fusion; action-grammar token weighting is domain-specific rather than a general OPD method. Excluded from V5 scope; removed from Awesome; PDF trashed.

Multi-step tasks remain challenging because training uses only single-step supervision

2607.29494.title: Adaptive FastOPD: Progress-Aware Rollout Horizon Expansion for Efficient On-Policy Distillation
2607.29494.affiliation_primary: University of Science and Technology of China
2607.29494.summary: Progress-aware rollout horizon expansion strategy for efficient on-policy distillation

method.training_loop: Start with short rollout horizon H0; student generates rollouts; monitor 4 teacher-student signals in boundary region; expand horizon only when progress plateaus and utilization gate satisfied; repeat until Hmax
method.loss_formulation: L_OPD(θ) = (1/Σμ) Σ_{i,j} μ_{i,j} Σ_{v∈S_{i,j}} ℓ_clip(ρ_{i,j,v}(θ), A_{i,j,v})
method.data_source: DAPO-Math-17K
key_components: progress-aware horizon expansion
four complementary OPD signals (top-k overlap, shared probability mass, shared-greedy penalty, unshared-token penalty)
normalized badness scores with EMA smoothing
length-utilization gate (horizon-hit rate and boundary-reach rate)
stage-relative baseline

2607.29494.novelty: Replaces fixed-interval or absolute-threshold rollout expansion with stage-relative progress detection using multi-signal aggregation and utilization gating, reducing sensitivity to hyperparameters across models and training stages

on_policy_mechanism.evidence_quote: OPD samples sequences from the current student and uses the teacher's token-level distributions on student-generated prefixes as supervision

opd_classification.reasoning: The paper proposes an adaptive curriculum for rollout horizon expansion in OPD, which is an efficiency/stability technique related to curriculum scheduling (§6.2) with elements of compute efficiency (§6.3).

key_findings: Adaptive FastOPD achieves highest average score (56.1) on DeepSeek pair while reducing training time by 49.1% relative to OPD 15K

limitations: Remaining dependence on adaptation parameters (Nbase, β, Kpat, τ_hit, τ_reach)
Evaluated only on mathematical reasoning tasks
Only tested with two teacher-student pairs

2608.00485.title: SERL-SQL: Selective Hindsight Distillation for Text-to-SQL Reinforcement Agentic Learning
2608.00485.summary: Execution-hindsight teacher reweights GRPO advantages on SQL tokens for Text-to-SQL agents

method.training_loop: Sample on-policy SQL trajectories from student, teacher re-scores with execution hindsight, compute teacher-student log-prob gap, convert to bounded masked weights on SQL/action tokens, reweight GRPO advantages, update student policy

method.data_source: BIRD training set
key_components: selective action mask on SQL/tool-action tokens
execution-hindsight teacher re-scoring
sign-aware bounded reweighting
hindsight decay coefficient
schema grounding agent
hierarchical reward verifier

2608.00485.novelty: Uses execution feedback (runtime errors, empty results, etc.) as privileged teacher context to compute teacher-student log-prob gaps, converted into bounded sign-aware reweighting factors applied selectively to SQL/tool-action tokens within GRPO, rather than uniform trajectory-level credit assignment

on_policy_mechanism.evidence_quote: A teacher policy π_T periodically synchronized with the student and treated as a stop-gradient model. For a student-generated token y_t,i, the teacher evaluates the same token with execution hindsight

2608.00782.title: Distill Where You Fail: Recovering Learning Signals of Negative RL-Groups from Adaptive Teacher Guidance
2608.00782.summary: Selective on-policy distillation on negative zero-variance GRPO prompts with token selection and auxiliary SFT

method.training_loop: GRPO rollouts → identify negative zero-variance prompts → apply teacher-weighted OPD on selected tokens + SFT on teacher trajectories for those prompts; standard GRPO otherwise

method.data_source: DeepMath (57K math samples, difficulty≥6) and Eurus-RL-Code (25K code samples)
key_components: sample selection on negative zero-variance prompts
teacher confidence advantage weighting
Soft-OR token selection (entropy + divergence)
auxiliary SFT on teacher-generated correct trajectories

on_policy_mechanism.evidence_quote: The main idea of OPD is to let the student generate its own trajectories, and then minimize the reverse KL divergence between the student and the teacher on those student-generated trajectories

2608.01263.title: Distill What the Student Can See: Fisher-Projected On-Policy Distillation for Vision-Language Models
2608.01263.summary: Fisher-projected on-policy distillation projects teacher corrections onto student's visual tangent space

method.training_loop: Student generates on-policy rollouts; compute teacher & student logits on student prefixes; estimate visual tangent space via perturbation probes; Fisher-project teacher correction; optimize reverse KL to projected target
method.loss_formulation: L = (1/|T_y|) sum_{t in T_y} KL(p_{theta,t} || q^R_t) where q^R = softmax(stopgrad(l_theta) + g^R)
method.data_source: Geo3K geometry problem dataset
key_components: Fisher-projected capacity-aware target
continuous visual perturbation probes for tangent space estimation
on-policy student rollouts
reverse KL loss with projected target

2608.01263.novelty: Projects the teacher-student log-probability gap onto the student's local visual response tangent space under the Fisher metric, filtering out unrealizable corrections that require teacher-only visual capacity

on_policy_mechanism.evidence_quote: The student generates an on-policy trajectory, after which the student and teacher distributions are evaluated on the same student-visited prefixes.

opd_classification.reasoning: FP-OPD introduces a novel capacity-aware target via Fisher projection that modifies what distributional signal the student receives, making it a new adaptive objective/target for on-policy distillation.

stabilization_tricks: ridge regularization for Fisher Gram matrix

Replacing Fisher metric with Euclidean projection drops average from 51.27 to 42.48 (-8.79 points)
FP-OPD improves all seven benchmarks in 8B-to-2B setting and five of seven in 32B-to-8B setting

Only evaluated on Qwen3-VL family

theory.theoretical_claim: Local expansion of reverse KL induces Fisher inner product as the natural geometry for projection
theory.proof_sketch: KL(p || softmax(log p + δ)) = 0.5 <δ,δ>_p + o(||δ||^2), justifying Fisher metric for projection

2608.01303.title: AlphaG-OPD: Reliability-Gated Sibling Counterfactuals for On-Policy Distillation in Symbolic Alpha Factor Discovery
2608.01303.summary: Structural on-policy distillation for GFlowNet symbolic alpha factor discovery via paired counterfactuals

method.loss_formulation: L = L_ETB + λ * L_OPD, where L_OPD = (1/|B|) Σ D_KL(π*(·|s) ∥ P_F^θ(·|s, A_s))
method.data_source: CSI300/500/1000 and S&P500 stock market data (2010-2024 China, 2010-2020 US)

reliability-gated paired counterfactual teacher (Component II)
bounded credit consolidation with replay and gradient balancing (Component III)

2608.01303.novelty: First structural OPD for GFlowNet-based symbolic search: creates a self-generated local teacher from matched sibling counterfactuals under shared suffixes with empirical reliability gating (agreement + LCB), without external teacher model

on_policy_mechanism.evidence_quote: The evolving student policy provides the states, and a teacher supplies a local action target at those same states. This reduces the state-distribution mismatch of static distillation and turns feedback on the student's current behavior into a direct probability update

opd_classification.reasoning: The method constructs a self-generated teacher (no external model) from paired counterfactual evaluations at states visited by the student's own policy, with reliability gating and KL-bounded targets — pure self-distillation with on-policy rollouts.

2608.01589.summary: Replaces complete solution in OPSD teacher context with structured problem-space guidance

method.training_loop: Offline extract problem-space guidance from verified solutions; student samples on-policy trajectory from question; teacher scores student prefixes conditioned on guidance; update student with clipped-KL loss

On-policy student rollouts
Clipped-KL token-level distillation from privileged teacher

2608.01597.title: HindSearch: Trajectory-Level Hindsight Critique for Search-Augmented Reinforcement Learning
2608.01597.summary: Hindsight critique on failed search rollouts provides auxiliary OPD signal for GRPO

hint-conditioned frozen teacher for OPD
search-action token masking
clamp on teacher-student logprob gap

2608.01735.title: DAPD: Dual-Anchored Policy Distillation
2608.01735.summary: Dual-anchored policy distillation addressing privilege illusion in on-policy self-distillation via matched-information paths

method.training_loop: Sample on-policy rollout y from student; compute None/Cross/Self distributions on both y and y*; evaluate Entangled Distillation, Inference Anchor, Privileged Anchor in both directions; combine losses and update LoRA
method.loss_formulation: L_DAPD = λ * L^{y→y*}_{DPA} + (1-λ) * L^{y*→y}_{DPA}, where L^{s→s̄}_{DPA} = L^{s̄}_{infer} + L^s_{ent} + L^s_{priv}
method.data_source: OpenThoughts data (math, code, science domains)
key_components: Dual-Path Anchoring (DPA)
Dual-Source Anchoring (DSA)
Self-conditioned bridge distribution
Inference Anchor
Privileged Anchor
Component-clipped forward KL

2608.01735.novelty: Identifies information asymmetry as root cause of privilege illusion in OPSD and introduces matched-information anchoring via a self-conditioned bridge distribution with dual-path (unconditioned + privileged) and dual-source (reference-to-rollout + rollout-to-reference) alignment, unlike prior methods that filter/reweight the privileged signal

on_policy_mechanism.evidence_quote: the student samples a rollout y ∼ p_θ(· | x). OPSD then evaluates the same policy at each prefix y_<t under two information conditions: (1) None distribution p_None,θ,t = p_θ(· | x, y_<t), which predicts without privileged information, and (2) Cross distribution p_Cross,θ,t = p_θ(· | x, y_<t, y∗), which predicts while conditioning on the reference y∗

opd_classification.reasoning: DAPD proposes a new distillation objective (component-clipped forward KL with dual-path and dual-source anchoring) for on-policy self-distillation where the student generates rollouts and the same model under privileged conditioning provides logit-level supervision.

key_findings: DAPD improves over OPSD by +2.00 points average on Qwen3-4B across six benchmarks
Gains persist across scales: +2.69 at 4B, +2.41 at 8B, +2.78 at 32B over OPSD
DAPD reduces late-stage wrong claims by 73% relative to OPSD at training steps 250-300
Dual-rollout reference-free variant still improves over OPSD by +2.41 points at 4B and 8B
Optimal reference-guidance weight λ decreases from 0.5 at 1.7B to 0.2 at larger scales
2608.01735.ablations_summary: Both DPA paths (unconditioned + privileged) are needed for each guidance source; combining reference and rollout guidance (DSA) outperforms either alone (65.28 vs 63.89/65.09); scale-dependent sensitivity shows smaller models prefer stronger reference guidance while larger models prefer rollout guidance; component-clipped forward KL outperforms reverse KL and unclipped variants
limitations: Multiple anchored distributions increase training-time computation with no inference-time cost
Weights may need recalibration across scales or architectures
Verified-rollout extension requires an automatic correctness signal unavailable for open-ended tasks
failure_modes: At 1.7B scale, gains are smaller (+1.94) as rollouts are noisier and less informative
Without component clipping, performance degrades (62.50 vs 65.28)

theory.theoretical_claim: Paired-prefix None-distribution alignment bound showing joint optimization of Inference Anchor and Entangled Distillation tightens upper bound on TV distance between reference-side and rollout-side None distributions
theory.proof_sketch: Triangle inequality decomposes TV(None_ref, None_roll) into three terms controlled by Inference Anchor, bridge consistency, and Entangled Distillation; Pinsker's inequality and Jensen convert KL losses to TV bounds; Lemma 1 lifts token-level to sequence-level via autoregressive hybrid distributions; shared-parameter transfer shows Inference Anchor gradient reduces Cross-to-None CE in expectation

2608.01837.title: PCSD: Persistent Consistency for Self-Distillation in Agentic Reinforcement Learning
2608.01837.summary: Token-level weighting for on-policy self-distillation based on persistent local teacher support signals

method.training_loop: Student rolls out trajectories via GRPO; frozen skill-augmented teacher scores student tokens; PCSD computes adaptive exponential-decay aggregation + trend modulation + sigmoid gating to derive token-level distillation weights; joint optimization of GRPO + weighted distillation loss

key_components: adaptive exponential-decay aggregation window
trend-aware modulation
sigmoid continuous gating
on-policy self-distillation with privileged teacher

2608.01837.novelty: Derives token-level distillation weights from local persistence of teacher-favoring signals via adaptive window aggregation, exponential decay, and one-sided trend modulation, replacing isolated pointwise or uniform step-level weighting

on_policy_mechanism.evidence_quote: The student collects on-policy trajectories via multi-turn interaction, while a frozen, skill-augmented teacher scores the student-generated tokens.

opd_classification.reasoning: Core contribution is a novel token-level weighting scheme for on-policy self-distillation that adaptively weights distillation based on local persistence of teacher signals, fitting §6.1 (token weighting) with adaptive elements (§4.2) and privileged-information teacher (§5.3.1).

20-28% of valid tokens have w_{k,i} > 0.5, indicating concentrated selective distillation rather than uniform weighting

limitations: Uses fixed hyperparameters for local aggregation and gating without adapting to evolving trajectory statistics
Keeps privileged teacher frozen, preventing co-evolution with student
High-variance regions may still partially smooth abrupt meaningful changes

2608.01953.title: Look Ahead Before You Distill: Future Trajectory Validation of Teacher Guidance for Agentic On-Policy Distillation
2608.01953.summary: Future trajectory validation of teacher bridges for agentic on-policy distillation

method.training_loop: B2F curriculum shortens teacher prefix; at high-disagreement turn, execute teacher bridge, roll out student continuation, validate via teacher-preferred token ratio gain, optimize accepted bridges with PPO loss
method.loss_formulation: L_FTB = L_B2F + λ_br * L_bridge, where L_bridge = -E[g(τ)/M_br * Σ sg[A_i^br] log π_θ(x_i^br|c_i^br)]

teacher bridge execution in environment

teacher-preferred token ratio gate
B2F temporal curriculum

2608.02087.title: Instruction-Conditioned Exploration with Asymmetric Reinforcement Learning and Self-Distillation
2608.02087.summary: ICE + Asymmetric-RL/SD: instruction-conditioned exploration with self-distillation for LLM RL

Guarantee covers teacher-verified targets not inference-time actions
Transfer from base LLaDA yields much narrower speed range than TAD-S-initialized model
failure_modes: MBPP task shows accuracy regression (-1.20 points) under OPTD
Adaptive compression at large horizons trades 1.05-1.53 accuracy points for TPF gains
Only 10.1% of states have full 8× compression available

theory.theoretical_claim: Lemma 1: fallback consistency guarantee - verified action S(x) is jointly outcome-preserving under frozen teacher with at most n counterfactual checks
theory.proof_sketch: C_0=∅ is always consistent (ordinary first teacher release), so m* is well-defined; descending exhaustive scan finds longest prefix preserving teacher rollout outcome in at most n checks

2608.02942.relevance_to_opd: Directly proposes on-policy distillation for diffusion LLMs where the student generates its own partial states during training and receives frozen-teacher distributional supervision (KL anchor) on those states, addressing state-distribution mismatch inherent in off-policy few-step distillation

2608.02948.title: Rubrics as Privileged Information for Open-Ended Generation
2608.02948.summary: Extends on-policy self-distillation to open-ended generation using rubrics as soft privileged information

method.training_loop: Student generates on-policy rollout; EMA teacher conditioned on rubric PI scores rollout; minimize per-token reverse KL between student and rubric-conditioned teacher distributions with clipping
method.data_source: HealthBench (2000 training prompts with physician-created rubrics), RubricHub Science (1000 prompts)
key_components: rubrics as soft privileged information for teacher conditioning
on-policy self-distillation with EMA teacher
per-token KL clipping
reverse KL for mode-seeking behavior

2608.02948.novelty: Extends OPSD from verifiable domains (hard PI like ground-truth answers) to open-ended generation using soft PI (rubrics), showing rubric conditioning provides 1.7x stronger per-token KL signal than reference completions on student rollouts

on_policy_mechanism.evidence_quote: Given a prompt x, rubric r, and the student's on-policy roll-out ŷ∼ π_S(·|x), the teacher's response is additionally conditioned on the rubric: π_T(· | x,r,ŷ_{<t}), whereas the student has no rubric access

opd_classification.reasoning: Self-distillation where same model acts as both teacher (with rubric PI) and student (without PI), using on-policy rollouts and per-token KL divergence loss - pure self-distillation with privileged information

key_findings: RuPI beats RaR GRPO by up to +0.10 absolute score on HealthBench while using 8× fewer on-policy generations per training prompt
Rubric conditioning produces 1.7× more per-token KL than reference conditioning on student rollouts
Soft rubric PI outperforms hard reference PI by +0.034 to +0.079 absolute score under matched recipe and KL direction across three models
On-policy rollouts are critical: off-policy (λ=0) collapses the rubric advantage and fails to improve over base
On RubricHub Science/ResearchQA, RuPI outperforms both reference-PI distillation and RaR RL (66.6% vs 64.2% and 57.6%)
2608.02948.ablations_summary: Key ablations: on-policy fraction (λ=0 vs 0.5 vs 1 shows monotonic improvement with on-policy fraction); forward vs reverse KL (comparable in-domain but reverse KL better preserves OOD capabilities); per-token KL clipping (removing clip changes score by ≤0.014); SFT baselines (neither reference-SFT nor RCG-SFT recovers RuPI's gain, confirming on-policy dense-KL mechanism is essential)
limitations: Evaluated on only two open-ended domains (medical and scientific Q&A)
LoRA hyperparameters, EMA decay, and KL clip threshold inherited from prior work without sensitivity sweep
Cross-domain suite limited to 4 tasks; contamination-resistant benchmarks would strengthen OOD claim
Assumes rubric and reference answer are both high-quality and aligned with evaluation criteria
Low-quality or misaligned rubrics may transfer harmful guidance
failure_modes: Off-policy distillation (λ=0) eliminates the rubric advantage and fails to improve over base
Forward KL degrades instruction-following (IFEval) on Qwen models
When rubrics are low-quality, synthetically generated, or misaligned with downstream task, the ordering rubric PI > reference PI need not hold
2608.02948.relevance_to_opd: Directly extends on-policy self-distillation (OPSD) to open-ended generation by using rubrics as soft privileged information; student generates on-policy rollouts, teacher (EMA of student conditioned on rubric) provides dense per-token KL supervision on those rollouts

2608.03092.title: SMOPD: Multi-Reward Reinforcement Learning via Specialize-and-Merge Online Policy Distillation
2608.03092.summary: Two-stage multi-reward RL: specialize teachers per reward, merge via on-policy distillation

method.training_loop: Stage1: Train reward-specialized teachers with skewed GDPO priority weights. Stage2: Student generates rollouts, teachers provide top-κ logits on student prefixes, student minimizes forward KL to teacher mixture + balanced GDPO anchor loss.
method.loss_formulation: L = L_GDPO(π_θ; w_equal) + λ · Σ_t KL(p_T_mix(·|s_t) || p_θ(·|s_t))
method.data_source: RLLA-4K train split (ToolRL) for complementary rewards; Alpaca prompt-only for conflicting rewards
key_components: reward-priority teacher specialization
union top-κ teacher mixture distribution
forward KL on-policy distillation loss
balanced GDPO sequence-level anchor

2608.03092.novelty: Resolves dense-vs-sparse reward signal imbalance in multi-reward RL by training separate reward-prioritized teachers then merging them via token-level on-policy distillation with a uniform teacher mixture and task anchor, unlike prior work that balances rewards within a single policy.

on_policy_mechanism.evidence_quote: Unlike offline distillation, the student generates its own responses (on-policy), and teachers provide top-𝜅 log-probabilities on the student's sequences—following the on-policy distillation paradigm

opd_classification.reasoning: The method uses multiple white-box teachers providing logit-level supervision on student-generated rollouts via forward KL, combining RL anchor with token-level OPD in a multi-reward setting.

key_findings: On Qwen2.5-1.5B complementary rewards, SMOPD achieves +48% composite gain over GDPO baseline (2.740 vs 1.849) with format compliance jumping from 8.8% to 97.5%.
The merged SMOPD student surpasses both individual teachers on safe alignment across three backbones.
Top-16 teacher probability mass preserves ~0.994 of teacher distribution, making larger κ unnecessary.
Forward KL outperforms reverse KL by 0.082 Overall on 7B safe alignment due to mode-covering behavior preserving diverse teacher capabilities.
Uniform teacher mixing outperforms adaptive confidence-failure gates across most settings.
2608.03092.ablations_summary: Task anchor adds +0.095 Overall beyond pure OPD (5.544→5.639 on 7B). Forward KL is stable across κ∈{16,32,64} (spread 0.007). Reverse KL underperforms forward KL by 0.082. Uniform mixing beats adaptive sequence/token gates. Moderate priority profiles (0.7/0.3) work as well as aggressive (0.9/0.1).
limitations: Teachers are same size as student (no larger teacher benefit explored)
Anchor uses GDPO which could be improved with better advantage estimators like GD2PO
Evaluated only on up to 7B scale
failure_modes: On Llama-3.2-3B where teacher specialization is most challenging, both teachers degrade substantially and SMOPD only approaches but does not surpass the strongest scalarized baseline GD2PO

theory.theoretical_claim: Pure OPD is capped at teacher mixture (gradient vanishes at p_θ=q), while the anchor's policy gradient survives at this ceiling, enabling the student to exceed teachers.
theory.proof_sketch: Forward KL gradient equals zero when student matches mixture; policy gradient from GDPO anchor remains nonzero unless mixture already locally maximizes task reward; for sparse rewards, OPD activates the anchor by raising success rate above zero.

2608.03092.relevance_to_opd: Directly proposes a multi-teacher on-policy distillation method where the student generates rollouts, frozen reward-specialized teachers provide top-κ logit distributions on student sequences, and the student minimizes forward KL to the teacher mixture—a core OPD contribution for multi-reward balancing.

2608.03610.title: Language-Specialized Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation for Multilingual LLM-Based ASR
2608.03610.summary: Multi-teacher on-policy distillation with language routing for multilingual LLM-based ASR

method.training_loop: Train language-specialized teachers via DAPO RL; student generates on-policy rollouts; route to top-K teachers per language; compute weighted reverse-KL token-level loss; update student
method.loss_formulation: L_MOPD(θ) = E_{x~D} [Σ_{k=1}^K λ_k L_k(x;θ)], L_k = E_{τ~π_θ} [1/|τ| Σ_t D_KL(π_θ(·|s_t) ∥ π^T_{ϕ_{ℓ(x),k}}(·|s_t))]
method.data_source: 50k multilingual utterances from WenetSpeech, KeSpeech, WenetSpeech-Yue, LibriSpeech
key_components: DAPO-based language-specialized teacher training
language-routed top-K teacher selection
weighted multi-teacher token-level reverse-KL aggregation
static vs dynamic acoustic prefix configurations

2608.03610.novelty: First application of multi-teacher on-policy distillation to ASR, introducing language routing, acoustic-prefix configurations (static/dynamic), and weighted multi-teacher aggregation that enables student to surpass all teachers

on_policy_mechanism.evidence_quote: the student generates an on-policy trajectory τ ∼ π_θ(· | x). Let s_t = (x, τ_{<t}) denote the decoding state at step t. The distillation loss from the k-th ranked teacher is defined as L_k(x;θ) = E_{τ∼π_θ} [1/|τ| Σ_t D_KL(π_θ(·|s_t) ∥ π^T_{ϕ_{ℓ(x),k}}(·|s_t))]

opd_classification.reasoning: [2026-08-12 boss ruling] RECLASSIFIED yes->no (score=8 review). Multilingual ASR application; contribution is language routing plus acoustic-prefix configurations for ASR rather than a general OPD advance. Excluded from V5 scope; removed from Awesome; PDF trashed.

stabilization_tricks: asymmetric clipping in DAPO teacher training

key_findings: LS-MOPD with 3 teachers achieves 4.45% average error rate in offline setting, outperforming the best-teacher oracle (4.59%) and all open-source baselines
Static acoustic prefix yields better gradient alignment and distillation performance despite slightly weaker teachers compared to dynamic prefix
Multi-teacher aggregation consistently outperforms single-teacher distillation, with student surpassing all individual teachers on most benchmarks
In streaming setting, LS-MOPD with 3 teachers reduces average error from 5.74% to 5.18%, a 9.8% relative improvement
2608.03610.ablations_summary: Key ablations compare static vs dynamic acoustic prefix (static wins on gradient alignment and final performance), number of teachers (1/2/3, with diminishing but positive gains from additional teachers), and teacher aggregation weights (0.6/0.2/0.2 for 3 teachers)
limitations: Evaluation covers only a single model backbone and limited set of target languages
Dynamic acoustic-prefix configuration remains preliminary and does not fully exploit its potential
Broader validation across model architectures and languages is still warranted
failure_modes: Dynamic acoustic prefix can cause teacher-student conditioning mismatch, reducing distillation effectiveness
In streaming with dynamic prefix, adding more teachers does not always improve performance on all subsets
2608.03610.relevance_to_opd: Directly extends on-policy distillation to multilingual ASR with language-routed multi-teacher supervision on student-generated rollouts using reverse-KL loss, demonstrating student can surpass all teachers

2608.04408.title: Not Every Divergence Should Be Suppressed: Counterfactual Recoverability in On-Policy Distillation
2608.04408.summary: Counterfactual recoverability labels guide selective supervision in on-policy distillation

method.training_loop: Student generates rollouts; error states replayed with budget-matched teacher continuation & rollback branches; 3-way oracle label (recoverable/irreversible/ambiguous) controls retain/rollback/SOD training action
method.loss_formulation: L_OPD(s) = -log π_θ(a*_T(s) | s) where a*_T = argmax_{a∈A(s)} P_T(a|s,A)
method.data_source: 30 AIME2024 training-manifest tasks in sequential agent environment
key_components: counterfactual recoverability labels
budget-matched continuation/rollback branches
three-way oracle controller
candidate-conditioned distillation backbone
shared admissible action set

2608.04408.novelty: Introduces counterfactual recoverability as a decision variable for OPD, replacing divergence-only heuristics with budget-matched replay branches that reveal whether an error state warrants continuation or rollback, achieving AUC 1.000 vs 0.392 for divergence alone

on_policy_mechanism.evidence_quote: each training update first produces a student trajectory and records eligible error states. The online labeler then checks that the state has a remaining budget, runs matched branches, and records the label

opd_classification.reasoning: The paper proposes a selective supervision mechanism that determines per-state whether to retain, rollback, or default to SOD based on counterfactual recoverability labels, which is a token/state weighting strategy built on top of on-policy distillation.

key_findings: Recoverability proxy achieves AUC of 1.000 vs 0.392 for divergence alone on 99 non-ambiguous AIME states
Mean continuation-minus-rollback effect is +0.185 for recoverable states and -1.000 for irreversible-but-avoidable states
Oracle reaches 0.578 success on held-out AIME2025 vs 0.517 for SOD reproduction (best baseline)
Retaining teacher-correctable prefixes provides the largest individual contribution in ablations
101 of 200 states are ambiguous, bounding the oracle's applicability
2608.04408.ablations_summary: Full oracle achieves 0.583 on held-out 60-task; removing rollback drops to 0.550, removing retain drops to 0.483, removing both (label only) drops to 0.450, showing retention is the largest single contribution
limitations: Oracle uses approximately 3× the teacher tokens of E0 controls
101 of 200 states are ambiguous with insufficient branch evidence
Results from one teacher, fixed manifests, and only 3 seeds
Not a deployable system; requires a state-only estimator for online use
Training costs are unmatched across methods
failure_modes: Ambiguous states (50.5% of diagnostic population) lack enough evidence for strong intervention
Divergence-only diagnostic achieves below no-skill AUC (0.392) in this setting
2608.04408.relevance_to_opd: Directly advances OPD by proposing counterfactual recoverability as a decision variable for selective supervision on student-generated trajectories, replacing divergence-only heuristics with outcome-grounded branch diagnostics

2608.04419.title: SPOT: Sparse Probing and Outcome Calibration for On-Policy Distillation
2608.04419.affiliation_primary: The Chinese University of Hong Kong, Shenzhen
2608.04419.summary: Outcome-calibrated targets for OPD via sparse probing and verifier-scored student continuations

method.training_loop: For each prompt: roll out student trajectory, score positions by teacher entropy×top-k mass×S-T gap, probe top-M positions with student continuations scored by verifier, construct KL-regularized outcome-calibrated targets, update with OPD + branch loss
method.loss_formulation: L = (1/T) \sum_t L^{OPD}_t + (\beta / max(1,|B^+|)) \sum_{t \in B^+} L^{Branch}_t
method.data_source: MATH (7,500 examples) and DAPO-Math-14k (14,116 examples)
key_components: position acquisition score (entropy × top-k mass × S-T gap)
sparse probing with verifier-scored student continuations
outcome-calibrated targets via KL-regularized reward tilting
B+ gating (retain only positions with positive-reward candidates)

2608.04419.novelty: Introduces a two-decision framework (where to probe and what to distill) for OPD: uses multiplicative position scoring to allocate probing budget, then constructs closed-form KL-regularized targets by tilting teacher prior with verifier-scored student continuation values, unlike EOPD which uses only entropy threshold and uncalibrated teacher prior

on_policy_mechanism.evidence_quote: Rollout x ∼ π_θold(·|q) Query the teacher π_T(·|c_t) at every prefix c_t = (q, x_{<t}) Score every valid position by its position-level acquisition score

opd_classification.reasoning: SPOT augments OPD with RL-style verifier signals to calibrate the teacher distribution target, combining token-level KL distillation with outcome-based reward tilting, fitting §4.3 (RL-augmented objective).

key_findings: SPOT achieves the best macro Pass@8 at all three evaluated student scales, improving over OPD by 4.55–5.28 points and over EOPD by 2.49–3.19 points.
Relative to standard OPD, SPOT improves macro Avg@8 by 0.47–1.48 points across all student scales.
Verifier-guided calibration improves macro Avg@8/Pass@8 by 3.21/7.38 points over uncalibrated branch distillation (Qwen3-1.7B).
SPOT generalizes to Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct, raising macro Pass@8 from 29.65 (OPD) to 34.05.
Branch-distillation weight β=0.1 is optimal; the Full multiplicative acquisition score (H×C×G) outperforms all partial variants.
2608.04419.ablations_summary: Full acquisition score (H×C×G) achieves 21.51/41.60 macro Avg@8/Pass@8 vs best partial variant HC-Mass at 20.47/37.91. Verifier guidance adds +3.21/+7.38 over uncalibrated targets. β=0.1 outperforms β∈{0.05,0.5,1.0} on competition benchmarks.

theory.theoretical_claim: Closed-form KL-regularized target with monotone value-prior tradeoff and diminishing returns of KL budget
theory.proof_sketch: Gibbs variational identity shows unique optimizer is exponential tilt of teacher prior; trust-region equivalence via KKT; monotonicity via log-partition derivatives; Pinsker gives improvement-deviation bounds

2608.04419.relevance_to_opd: Directly proposes a novel OPD method that improves where and what to distill by combining sparse position selection with verifier-calibrated teacher targets on student-generated trajectories

2608.04794.title: Privileged, but Biased: How PI-Conditioned Teachers Break Self-Distillation
2608.04794.summary: Shows PI-conditioned self-distillation fails as sole objective on hard reasoning tasks

method.training_loop: Student generates rollouts; PI-conditioned self-teacher (same model + reference solution) provides per-token JSD targets on student rollouts; student minimizes dense per-token divergence (Eq.1)
method.data_source: MMLU-Pro, DAPO-Math-17k, CodeForces, BFCL multi-turn
key_components: PI Bias Score
per-token JSD loss
EMA teacher
per-token clipping
correctness-blindness analysis
token-type loss attribution

2608.04794.novelty: Demonstrates that PI-conditioned self-distillation (SDPO/OPSD) as sole objective fails on difficult tasks via a measured causal chain: PI bias → loss blind to correctness → effort on uninformative tokens → exploration penalized → flattened student; introduces PI Bias Score metric

on_policy_mechanism.evidence_quote: the self-teacher is the same model additionally conditioned on the PI r: p_T(· | x,y_{<t}) = π_{θ'}(· | x,r,y_{<t}), where θ' is the student's own parameters or a slow copy that tracks them

opd_classification.reasoning: Paper is an analysis/critique of on-policy self-distillation methods (SDPO, OPSD), documenting failure modes rather than proposing a new OPD method; fits failure-mode analysis sections

key_findings: SD as sole objective degrades think-mode accuracy by up to 3.51 points average on agentic tasks and 7.0 on individual benchmarks
PI Bias Score reaches 0.52 on in-context solution vs ≤0.02 on different correct solution, showing teacher encodes one trajectory not correctness
Per-token loss overlaps at ~3.5×10−4 for correct and incorrect rollouts, confirming loss is blind to correctness
Stopwords, uncertainty markers, punctuation and whitespace absorb 55.4% of per-token loss
Off-path KL within correct rollouts is ~0.31 vs ~0.08 on-path (4× factor), penalizing exploration
Results hold under both SDPO and OPSD recipes, across model scales (8B, 32B), reasoning modes, and PI forms
2608.04794.ablations_summary: Three PI forms (whole solution, hints, skills) tested: whole solution has high PI bias but maintains near-base performance; hints/skills reduce bias but weaken signal, losing 5.1 and 3.5 points respectively. Response-length tertiles, difficulty splits, and model scale (8B vs 32B) all show consistent failure pattern.
limitations: Study is observational, characterizing the objective rather than proposing a remedy
Evaluates only one model family (Qwen3) at two scales
Results average four rollouts; some per-domain differences are small relative to run-to-run variation
Hints and skills are model-generated, so weak-PI results may partly reflect their construction
Does not test SD combined with reward terms
failure_modes: PI-conditioned teacher encodes one specific trajectory rather than correctness in general
Loss cannot distinguish correct from incorrect rollouts
Dense loss concentrates on uninformative tokens (stopwords, punctuation)
Exploration/deliberation tokens are penalized most within correct rollouts
Student flattens rather than sharpens, producing earlier-committing but not more accurate policy
2608.04794.relevance_to_opd: Directly analyzes on-policy self-distillation (SDPO, OPSD) where student generates rollouts and a PI-conditioned self-teacher provides dense per-token KL supervision; documents systematic failure modes of this OPD paradigm on hard tasks

2608.05131.title: OPD-V: Visual On-Policy Self-Distillation with Modality Balance
2608.05131.summary: Visual on-policy self-distillation using modality balance as privileged information via dual teachers

method.training_loop: Student generates rollouts from Original Image; Positive Teacher (Zoom-In Image) and Negative Teacher (Mask Image) score same tokens; positive Modality-Balance Logits Margin defines trust region; JSD distillation within region
method.loss_formulation: L = E[1/(sum r_t) * sum_{t in R_MB} r_t * delta_t^MB * D_JS(q_t^+, p_{theta,t})]
method.data_source: 6.2K visual reasoning samples from Vision-OPD
key_components: Positive Teacher with Zoom-In Image
Negative Teacher with Mask Image
Modality-Balance Logits Margin
Modality-Balance Trust Region
Jensen-Shannon distillation
EMA teacher update
Top-K distillation

2608.05131.novelty: Introduces Modality Balance as privileged information for OPSD by constructing dual teachers (Zoom-In and Mask Image) whose logit margin defines a trust region for selective self-distillation, addressing modality imbalance in MLLMs

on_policy_mechanism.evidence_quote: The trainable MLLM p receives only the Original Image and textual query, and samples the on-policy trajectory y =(y ,...,y )∼p (·|I,x).

opd_classification.reasoning: Self-distillation where the student generates rollouts, a detached copy (same model with EMA) provides logit-level supervision on student-visited states, using JSD loss; the novelty is modality-balance-based token selection, which is a form of token weighting within pure self-distillation.

key_findings: OPD-V raises Qwen3.5-4B average from 64.30% to 80.01%, a 15.71 percentage-point gain across 6 benchmarks.
OPD-V with 4B parameters outperforms 397B Qwen3.5 (77.44%) and 1T Kimi-K2.6 (72.81%) in average accuracy.
OPD-V reduces wall-clock step latency by 31.8% on 4B and 24.7% on 9B compared to standard OPSD.
Response length is reduced by 74.5% compared to OPSD (141 vs 554 tokens at final training steps).
Combining Positive and Negative Teachers yields 80.01% vs 74.62% (Positive only) and 71.98% (Negative only).
2608.05131.ablations_summary: Positive Teacher alone reaches 74.62%, Negative Teacher alone 71.98%, combined yields 80.01%. Zoom-In Image outperforms Repeat Image (80.01% vs 75.95%). Mask Image outperforms Blur (74.31%), Prune (73.74%), and No Image (72.17%).

compute_efficiency.teacher_inference_cost: 2× (two teacher forward passes but offset by shorter rollouts)
compute_efficiency.speedup_vs_baseline: 1.32× (31.8% less step time vs OPSD on 4B)

2608.05131.relevance_to_opd: Directly extends on-policy self-distillation (OPSD) for multimodal LLMs by introducing modality-balance-aware token selection through dual teacher logit margins, applying JSD distillation only on student-generated tokens within a trust region.

2608.04788.title: Agentic Reinforcement Learning with Observation-Calibrated Self-Distillation
2608.04788.summary: Calibrated self-distillation contrasting Full and Observation-Ablated replay views for agentic RL

method.training_loop: GRPO rollout → NLL-guided step selection → Full & Observation-Ablated replay scoring → observation residual q modulates token-level GRPO advantage → PPO-clip update
method.loss_formulation: L = E[min(r*A_OCSD, clip(r,1-ε,1+ε)*A_OCSD) - β_KL * D_KL(π_θ ∥ π_ref)]
method.data_source: ALFWorld, WebShop, Search-QA environment interactions
key_components: Observation-Calibrated residual from Full vs Observation-Ablated replay views
NLL-guided step selection
Sign-preserving advantage modulation with tanh-bounded residual
GRPO trajectory-level advantage preserved

2608.04788.novelty: Identifies confounding in agentic privileged replay scoring where scaffold changes conflate with observation information; proposes contrasting structurally matched Full and Observation-Ablated replay views to derive a calibrated observation residual that modulates token-level GRPO updates

on_policy_mechanism.evidence_quote: OCSD generates on-policy outputs under the original interaction context and re-scores the same tokens after rollout using replay evidence E_i,k. We denote the original-context and replay-conditioned token distributions by π_S and π_T, referred to as the student and teacher views, respectively.

opd_classification.reasoning: Self-distillation where the same model acts as both student (original context) and teacher (privileged replay view), with on-policy rollouts scored under two replay views to derive a KL-like log-probability residual that modulates RL updates.
opd_classification.overridden_by: boss ruling 2026-08-09: boundary case rejected — OCSD: same-model privileged replay rescore -> advantage modulation, no distill loss (fails C3), same pattern as SERL-SQL

eval: Search-QA (NQ, HotpotQA, TriviaQA, PopQA, 2Wiki, MuSiQue, Bamboogle)

key_findings: OCSD outperforms GRPO by 8.9, 12.2, and 14.0 points on ALFWorld across Qwen3-1.7B, 4B, and 8B respectively
Standalone OPSD performs substantially worse than GRPO, while OCSD's calibrated residual better aligns with local environment feedback
Observation residual AUROC for distinguishing valid/invalid actions is 0.707 vs 0.654 for Full support
OCSD overhead is only 1.40% relative to the shared GRPO pipeline (7.64 seconds per iteration)
Swapping realized observations with donors reduces AUROC from 0.803 to 0.542, confirming observation-action correspondence drives the residual
2608.04788.ablations_summary: Removing Observation-Ablated Teacher still improves over GRPO; random step selection helps but less than NLL-guided; applying to all steps hurts; removing sign alignment reduces to GRPO level
limitations: Two-observation replay horizon may not generalize to all environments
Method relies on deterministic environment feedback for labeling
Tested only on Qwen3 family models
failure_modes: Applying residual calibration to all steps (w/o step selection) degrades below GRPO on ALFWorld
Standalone OPSD collapses to near-zero performance on Search-QA
2608.04788.relevance_to_opd: Proposes an on-policy self-distillation method where the same model generates rollouts and then re-scores them under privileged replay views, deriving a calibrated log-probability residual (analogous to KL divergence) to modulate token-level RL updates

2608.06756.title: Capek 0.5: An Execution-Centric Vision-Language Model for Embodied Intelligence
2608.06756.summary: Unified embodied VLM consolidating 4 capability specialists via TIES merging + routed MOPD

method.training_loop: Train 4 GRPO specialists (Spatial, Temporal, Guidance, State) from shared backbone; merge with TIES; refine with routed multi-teacher on-policy distillation (MOPD) on student rollouts
method.loss_formulation: L_MOPD(θ) = E[1/|y| Σ_t D_KL(π_θ(·|h_t) ∥ q_r(·|h_t))]
method.data_source: Curated multi-source embodied data: SenseNova-SI-8M, VSI-590K, CLEVRER, NExT-QA, PixMo, DROID, BEHAVIOR-1K, etc.
key_components: execution-centric capability taxonomy
GRPO specialist training with verifiable rewards
TIES weight-space merging
routed multi-teacher on-policy distillation (MOPD)

2608.06756.novelty: Execution-centric taxonomy grouping embodied capabilities by functional role, with specialist-to-unified consolidation via TIES initialization followed by routed MOPD where each sample is distilled from its responsible specialist on student-generated prefixes

on_policy_mechanism.evidence_quote: for an input x, the student first samples a response y∼π_θ(·|x), and the routed teacher q_r is then evaluated on the resulting student-generated prefixes h_t=(x,y_{<t}), where r indexes the capability route selected for the sample.

opd_classification.reasoning: The paper's consolidation stage (MOPD) has student generate rollouts (C1), frozen specialist teachers provide log-probability supervision on student tokens (C2), and the loss is reverse KL divergence (C3). The multi-teacher routing and TIES initialization are novel contributions to on-policy distillation for multi-capability integration.

key_findings: Capek 0.5-35B-A3B improves 28 of 34 matched benchmark rows over its Qwen3.6 initialization
TIES+MOPD consolidation achieves the best overall trade-off across all four capability domains
On EmbodiedBench EB-HAB, Capek 0.5 achieves 63.0% success rate vs 46.0% for the backbone (+17.0pp)
Long-horizon task success increases by 26.0pp on EB-HAB and 6.0pp on EB-ALF
The 2B track improves 30 of 34 rows, validating the recipe transfers across capacity regimes
2608.06756.ablations_summary: Controlled consolidation study compares Mix-RL, TIES-only, MOPD-only, and TIES+MOPD: TIES preserves spatial/temporal well; MOPD excels on action/state tasks; TIES+MOPD achieves best on 3 of 8 signature benchmarks and second-best on remaining 5
limitations: Currently limited to perception and reasoning; does not directly output low-level robot controls
Evaluation restricted to simulated environments; no physical robot deployment
State Verification data constructed solely from BEHAVIOR-1K trajectories

2608.06802.title: Simple-OPD: Demystifying Warm-up for On-policy Distillation

method.training_loop: Step1: Warm up student with LoRA SFT on teacher-generated CoT rollouts until near saturation. Step2: Standard on-policy distillation with reverse KL on student rollouts.
method.loss_formulation: L_OPD(θ) = E_{x~D_x, ŷ~π_θ(·|x)} [1/L Σ_t D_KL(π_θ(·|c_t) ∥ π_T(·|c_t))]
method.data_source: DAPO-Math-17K prompts with teacher-generated CoT responses for warm-up
key_components: LoRA warm-up on teacher CoT
near-saturation training duration
low LoRA rank for OOD preservation
standard reverse KL OPD

opd_classification.reasoning: 老大裁决 2026-08-12: 剔除。贡献是 off-policy warm-up 的消融性质研究（错误 CoT rollout 仍可用作初始化），OPD 目标本身未改动；增益约 1 点，属预处理配方而非 OPD 方法推进。已从 v5 正文与 awesome 移除。

2608.07068.title: MemOPD: On-Policy Distillation through Memory State Alignment for Long-Horizon Agents
2608.07068.summary: Memory-aligned on-policy distillation reconstructing invocation states for long-horizon agents

method.training_loop: Frozen student snapshot rolls out compact-memory agent interactions; reconstruct each invocation's exact state; pack calls; frozen teacher scores student actions under aligned states; PPO + reverse-KL OPD loss updates student
method.loss_formulation: L_actor = L_PPO - αH + λL_OPD, where L_OPD = (1/Σm^T_j) Σ_j m^T_j Σ_{v∈V} p_{θ,j}(v) log(p_{θ,j}(v)/p_{T,j}(v))
method.data_source: Multi-objective QA from HotpotQA and Natural Questions with local Wikipedia corpus; SFT trajectories from gpt-oss-120b
key_components: memory state alignment
rollout context equivalence (RCE)
exact call reconstruction and packing
sampled action domain masking
combined PPO + reverse-KL OPD objective

2608.07068.novelty: Identifies and resolves state mismatch when context rewriting in compact-memory agents causes teacher to score actions under unvisited states; proposes reconstruction that restores exact invocation states (positions, visibility, prediction locations) before applying OPD, verified by RCE criterion

on_policy_mechanism.evidence_quote: The frozen behavior policy π_old then samples complete student interactions, and PPO optimizes the student using the final task reward... The frozen teacher then adds dense supervision without generating the trajectory or replacing the task reward.

key_findings: MemOPD-3B improves F1 over PPO by up to 416.2% on Q16 long-horizon retrieval
Memory state alignment improves F1 by 7.0% over persistent-history teacher scoring in matched control

RCE is preserved across five different context update strategies within numerical tolerance

2608.07371.title: Trajectory-Relative Hindsight Distillation for Agentic Reinforcement Learning
2608.07371.summary: Trajectory-relative hindsight distillation allocating turn-level supervision via normalized profile

method.training_loop: GRPO rollouts → freeze scoring snapshot → compute hindsight-conditioned log-prob gaps per token → aggregate into trajectory-normalized turn weights → joint loss with clipped dense hindsight + GRPO outcome
method.loss_formulation: L(θ) = L_out(θ) + clip_{b_g}(λ_g L_dense), where L_dense = -(1/M) Σ m_{τ,k,t} w_{τ,k} Δ^θ_{τ,k,t} log π_θ(y_{τ,k,t}|h_{τ,k,t})
method.data_source: Online rollouts from WebShop and ALFWorld environments
key_components: turn-aligned outcome view
hindsight-conditioned policy gap
trajectory-relative turn normalization with mean-one profile
joint GRPO + dense hindsight objective with relative clamp

2608.07371.novelty: Introduces trajectory-relative turn allocation that normalizes hindsight gap magnitudes across turns to a mean-one profile, redistributing dense supervision while preserving signed token-level revision direction, unlike prior methods that lack calibrated cross-turn allocation

on_policy_mechanism.evidence_quote: Freeze the pre-update snapshot π_old and use it as the scoring snapshot π_T while collecting groups of completed on-policy trajectories {(τ_i, R_i)}.

opd_classification.reasoning: TRIAL uses on-policy self-distillation: the student generates rollouts, a frozen snapshot of the same model (hindsight-conditioned) provides logit-level supervision via KL-like log-probability gaps on student-generated tokens, satisfying all three OPD conditions with self as teacher.

key_findings: TRIAL improves WebShop success from 56.4% to 75.2% and task score from 78.7% to 85.7% with Qwen3-1.7B

2608.07371.ablations_summary: Controlled profile study: Uniform (unit weights) adds 6.4pts WebShop success over GRPO but no consistent gains elsewhere; Permuted (shuffled turn assignments) varies by environment; TRIAL's source-aligned profile adds 12.4pts success and 7.9pts score over Uniform on WebShop and 8.6/11.2pts on ALFWorld Seen/Unseen

Assumes completed trajectory exposes serializable post-action evidence alignable with decisions
Requires hindsight-conditioned forward pass increasing training cost over GRPO
Results reported with a single seed; cross-seed variance unmeasured

Continuous action spaces not evaluated
2608.07371.relevance_to_opd: TRIAL is an on-policy self-distillation method for multi-turn agents: the student generates rollouts, a frozen hindsight-conditioned copy of itself provides token-level log-probability supervision, and trajectory-relative normalization allocates this dense signal across turns

2608.07935.title: Adaptive Supervised Anchoring for On-Policy Self-Distillation
2608.07935.summary: Context-separated anchoring for on-policy self-distillation with adaptive weighting

method.training_loop: Student generates rollout yˆ; distillation branch computes JSD(teacher||student) on rollout prefix; anchoring branch computes CE on canonical prefix y*; adaptive weight w=1-sim(yˆ,y*) scales anchor; joint update of shared LoRA params
method.loss_formulation: L_SDS = (1/|yˆ|) Σ D(p_T(·|x_PI,yˆ_{<t}) || p_S(·|x,yˆ_{<t})) + α·w_anchor·(−1/|y*|) Σ log p_S(y*_t|x,y*_{<t})
method.data_source: ToolAlpaca (SDFT-processed) and SimpleMath datasets
key_components: context-separated anchoring
adaptive anchoring weight from rollout-target similarity
rollout-conditioned self-distillation with privileged teacher
generalized Jensen-Shannon divergence

2608.07935.novelty: Identifies rollout-conditioned signal degradation in OPSD and proposes context separation where anchoring CE is computed on canonical prefixes while distillation uses student rollout prefixes, with an adaptive weight derived from token-level rollout-target alignment

on_policy_mechanism.evidence_quote: At each step the student generates an on-policy rollout yˆ ∼ p_S(·|x). Both policies evaluate this rollout: at position t they produce next-token distributions p^t_T = p_T(·|x_PI, yˆ_{<t}) and p^t_S = p_S(·|x, yˆ_{<t}) over the same student-generated prefix.

opd_classification.reasoning: The paper proposes an adaptive objective that modulates anchoring weight based on rollout-target alignment, fitting adaptive divergence/objective formulation (§4.2), with elements of token weighting (§6.1) and privileged information teacher (§5.3.1).

stabilization_tricks: LoRA on all attention and MLP modules

key_findings: SDS achieves 62.43% SimpleMath accuracy on Qwen3-4B vs 23.23% for OPSD and 56.43% for SFT
SDS retains 93.2% of base AIME24 Avg@8 while SFT retains only 52.6%
Teacher target-token accuracy drops from 80.4% under canonical prefixes to 6.5% under student rollouts (rollout-conditioned signal degradation)
Naive OPSD+CE collapses AIME24 to 3.33% due to target-context mismatch, while SDS achieves 67.98%
Adaptive anchoring weight stabilizes at nonzero level providing continuous coordination without hard stage switching
2608.07935.ablations_summary: Context isolation is critical (naive OPSD+CE collapses to 3.33% AIME vs 67.98% for SDS); fixed anchoring weights cannot simultaneously achieve task performance and retention; two-stage SFT→OPSD underperforms SDS on both axes; alignment metric choice shows SDS is stable across graded metrics but binary exact match is less effective
limitations: Evaluation confined to single model family (Qwen3) and two adaptation tasks
Controlled prefix corruption is only a tractable proxy for natural context degradation
Generalization across model families and broader task settings unverified
failure_modes: When α is too high, excessive anchoring suppresses on-policy exploration needed for OPSD
Fixed weight variants cannot simultaneously achieve strong task and retention performance
2608.07935.relevance_to_opd: Directly improves on-policy self-distillation by identifying rollout-conditioned signal degradation and proposing context-separated supervision with adaptive anchoring, combining on-policy distillation with canonical-context SFT in a principled unified framework

2608.08146.title: Long SKILL Compliance as Logical Reasoning: Closure-Grounded Detection with Scaling-Guided On-Policy Distillation
2608.08146.summary: Graph-based compliance detection with scaling-guided on-policy distillation for long SKILL documents

method.training_loop: Student generates rollouts from current policy; frozen teacher scores each token on student prefix; k1 reverse-KL estimator used as detached advantage in policy gradient update
method.loss_formulation: L = policy gradient with detached advantages from k1 = log π_θ(a_t|x_<t) - log π_T(a_t|x_<t)
method.data_source: Three anonymized enterprise datasets (Fulfillment, AfterSales, MerchantSupport) with scaling-guided sample selection

Two-level retrieval with dependency closure
Complexity-aware empirical scaling model
Scaling-guided sample prioritization for OPD

on_policy_mechanism.evidence_quote: For each training prompt, the student samples one response from its current policy. At each response token a_t, the frozen teacher scores the same token conditioned on the student-generated prefix x_<t.

key_findings: SkillCDG improves Qwen3.5-4B F1 by up to 12.8 percentage points over RawSkill baseline
