2608.08176.title: Matching Supervision to the Student's Learning Capacity: A Unified Framework for On-Policy Self-Distillation
2608.08176.summary: Unified framework jointly optimizing token weighting and PI strength in on-policy self-distillation via single dual variable

method.training_loop: Student generates rollout; teacher (same model + PI) scores tokens; compute per-token divergence/difficulty; soft weights via sigmoid(g-λd)/τ; update λ by dual ascent on load-ε; update β by primal residual ε-load; train on weighted KL loss
method.loss_formulation: L = ∑_t w_t D_KL(p^β_T ∥ p_S)_t / ∑_t w_t, where w_t = σ((g_t - λd_t)/τ)
method.data_source: OpenThoughts mathematical reasoning subset (up to 30K chain-of-thought augmented problem-solution pairs)
key_components: soft token weighting via sigmoid on net value
PI strength adaptation via primal residual update
single dual variable λ governing both axes
Learnability Frontier formulation

2608.08176.novelty: Formalizes token selection and PI control as coupled axes sharing a learning-capacity budget, solved by a single Lagrangian dual variable that simultaneously sets token-selection threshold and PI adjustment direction

on_policy_mechanism.evidence_quote: Student rollout: yˆ∼p S (·|x) Teacher scoring: pβ T (·|x,yˆ <t ) at PI strength β Per-token divergence: g t ←D KL (pβ T ∥p S ) t

opd_classification.reasoning: The paper jointly optimizes token weighting (§6.1) and PI-level adaptation (§5.3.1) with an adaptive capacity budget, making token weighting the primary novel mechanism within an OPSD framework.

key_findings: USD raises the 9-cell overall mean from 56.4 to 58.7 (+2.3 points) over vanilla OPSD across three Qwen3 scales
Each axis (token selection, PI adaptation) is individually beneficial but the joint variant is uniformly best across all scales
USD outperforms GRPO at every scale (+4.7, +2.0, +1.5 per-scale average at 1.7B, 4B, 8B) with far smaller sampling budget
Sensitivity analysis shows performance peaks at ε=0.3, confirming a genuine capacity-matching trade-off
2608.08176.ablations_summary: Token selection alone yields +1.8 avg at 1.7B; PI adaptation alone yields +0.9 at 1.7B; combining both gives +2.5. Relative contribution of each axis varies by scale. Capacity budget ε peaks at 0.3; both tighter and looser budgets degrade performance.
failure_modes: Overly tight capacity budget over-filters and starves student of learnable signal
Overly loose budget leaves constraint rarely active, reverting to near-uniform weighting

theory.theoretical_claim: Under monotonicity assumption, the primal residual update β←β+η_β(ε−load(β)) converges monotonically to the optimal PI strength β⋆ that satisfies the KKT condition
theory.proof_sketch: Feasibility via injectivity of load function gives unique root; G strictly increasing on feasible set implies optimum at constraint boundary; residual has sign of β⋆−β ensuring monotone convergence

2608.08176.relevance_to_opd: Directly proposes a novel on-policy self-distillation method that jointly optimizes token-level weighting and privileged information control through a unified Lagrangian framework, advancing the OPD paradigm with capacity-matched supervision

2608.08726.title: PAST: Privileged Adaptation from Complete Student Trajectories for On-Policy Self-Distillation
2608.08726.affiliation_primary: The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology (Guangzhou)
2608.08726.summary: Adapts privileged teacher from complete student trajectories before on-policy self-distillation

method.training_loop: Each cycle: freeze student, sample rollouts, verify outcomes, adapt teacher (preserve correct via full-vocab KL, redirect failed via GRPO+proximity), distill adapted teacher on student prefixes via forward-KL
method.loss_formulation: L = (m_+ L_+ + m_- L_-) / (m_+ + m_-) for teacher; L_S = E[1/T sum D_KL(q_U(·|H_t) || π(·|H_t))] for student
method.data_source: Mathematical reasoning problems (AIME 2024, AIME 2025, HMMT 2025 training tasks)
key_components: correct-trajectory preservation via full-vocabulary KL matching
failed-trajectory adaptation via GRPO with student-proximity regularization
causal student distillation on original prefixes
adaptive failed-branch sampling

2608.08726.novelty: Uses complete student trajectories (including outcome) as additional privileged information for the OPSD teacher, with separate adaptation objectives for correct (preserve student distribution) and failed (verifier-seeking + proximity) branches, then distills back to prefix-only student

on_policy_mechanism.evidence_quote: At cycle k, the frozen student p_k generates Y ~ p_k(· | X) without privileged information. PAST gives the teacher the same task-side privilege Z as Vanilla OPSD and adds the complete student response Y.

opd_classification.reasoning: Self-distillation where student generates rollouts, a privileged copy of the same model (adapted teacher) provides full-vocabulary logit supervision on student prefixes via forward-KL; the teacher is adapted per-cycle making it an adaptive self-distillation method.

key_findings: PAST improves Avg@12 macro average over Vanilla OPSD by 5.617 points (95% CI [2.592, 8.333])
Joint correct-and-failed training leads every task, reaching 48.426 macro versus 45.864 for failed-only and 44.908 for correct-only
Factorial study shows trajectory access alone adds 0.555 points and adaptation alone adds 0.092 points, but combined they add 5.617 points
Adaptive sampling uses 17.6% fewer teacher samples while reaching slightly higher macro average (47.284 vs 46.728)
Trajectory removal and shuffling perturbations confirm the adapted teacher uses matching hindsight context
2608.08726.ablations_summary: 2×2 factorial separates trajectory access from teacher adaptation showing complementary roles; branch ablation shows joint correct+failed training best; objective ablation shows full-vocabulary KL and generalized JSD similar quality; adaptive sampling reduces cost without quality loss; trajectory perturbation confirms matching context use
limitations: Main evidence uses only a 1.7B student; one-seed 4B extension gives mixed task-level results
Verifier checks final answers only, not intermediate reasoning steps
Failed branch uses success masking, adaptive group sizes, one retry, and all-failure skipping whose finite-sample estimator is not proven unbiased
Theory covers population objectives and causal projection rather than finite-sample estimator properties
failure_modes: On Qwen3-4B, PAST lowers AIME24 score compared to Vanilla OPSD while improving other tasks
Trajectory access alone without adaptation can lower at least one task (HMMT25 drops from 31.574 to 29.444)

compute_efficiency.memory_footprint: 62.971 GB peak (vs 53.837 GB for Vanilla OPSD)

theory.theoretical_claim: Forward-KL distillation projects trajectory-conditioned teacher to conditional arithmetic mean; perfect privileged teacher need not transfer; value-aligned causal transfer condition for local improvement
theory.proof_sketch: Decomposition of E[D_KL(q_U||π)] into privileged variation I(A;U|H) and causal shift D_KL(q||π); construction showing teacher with probability-one success but zero student update; value margin condition for positive transfer via conservative interpolation

2608.08726.relevance_to_opd: Directly extends on-policy self-distillation (OPSD) by using complete student trajectories as additional privileged information for the teacher, with formal analysis of what survives causal projection to a prefix-only student

2608.08764.title: Learning from Consensus and Disagreement: Unsupervised On-Policy Self-Distillation with Minority-Trajectory Contrast
2608.08764.summary: Unsupervised on-policy self-distillation using consensus as privileged context and minority calibration

method.training_loop: Sample s rollouts per prompt, group by answer, select consensus trajectory as privileged context for frozen self-teacher, align teacher logits with fresh student rollout via forward KL, penalize minority trajectories via KTO-style reference-anchored loss
method.loss_formulation: L = L_con(x) + λ L_dis(x), where L_con = (1/|M_r|) Σ min{D_α(q+_t, p_θ,t), τ} and L_dis = E[softplus(β ℓ⁻_t(θ)) - log2]
method.data_source: OpenThoughts (problem prompts only, no solutions used)
key_components: consensus-conditioned self-teaching
reference-anchored disagreement calibration
KTO-style minority trajectory penalty
on-policy rollout regeneration
answer-level self-consistency grouping

2608.08764.novelty: Replaces external supervision in privileged on-policy self-distillation with agreement-derived context from unlabeled rollouts and adds a KTO-style disagreement calibration branch to prevent false-consensus amplification

on_policy_mechanism.evidence_quote: the student independently samples a training trajectory r ∼ P_θ(·|x). Separating these roles is important: the evidence trajectories decide what information the teacher receives, whereas the fresh trajectory determines the prefixes on which teacher and student distributions are aligned.

opd_classification.reasoning: Self-distillation where the frozen self-teacher (same model with privileged consensus context) provides logit-level supervision on student-generated on-policy rollouts, making it a pure self-distillation OPD method with a novel unsupervised privilege construction.

key_findings: CODA-Full improves Qwen3-1.7B base by 6.38 points average accuracy without any external supervision, exceeding supervised OPSD by 0.31 points.
On Qwen3-4B, CODA-Full reaches 54.57% average, only 0.25 points behind supervised OPSD (54.82%).
Disagreement calibration improves consensus-only from 34.37% to 36.12% average on 1.7B, preventing late-stage training collapse.
Shortest modal trajectory selector yields best results (+0.86 over random), showing concise privileged context is more effective than verbose.
2608.08764.ablations_summary: Key ablations: (1) Consensus Only vs Full shows disagreement calibration adds +1.75 avg on 1.7B; (2) Oracle filtering does not consistently improve over unfiltered consensus; (3) Trajectory selector comparison shows shortest > random > longest; (4) Consensus sample size s=10 balances accuracy and compute vs s=5 and s=20.

Disagreement calibration does not fully match oracle filter stability
Heuristic negative supervision introduces minor trade-offs on some benchmarks

Consensus-only distillation suffers severe late-stage training collapse
Penalizing minority trajectories may inadvertently suppress correct answers under biased policy
2608.08764.relevance_to_opd: Directly proposes a novel on-policy self-distillation method where the student generates fresh rollouts and a frozen self-teacher (conditioned on consensus-derived privileged context) provides token-level KL supervision on those student trajectories, with a complementary disagreement regularizer.

2608.08960.title: Reading is not Reasoning: Bridging the Agentic Policy Gap in Vision–Text Compression
2608.08960.summary: Cross-modal self-distillation from text-history to visual-history agent policy

method.training_loop: Stage 1: Offline SFT on rendered visual histories from successful text-policy trajectories. Stage 2: GRPO RL with online forward-KL distillation from frozen text-history teacher on student-visited states.
method.loss_formulation: L(θ) = L_GRPO(θ) + λ L_on(θ), where L_on is capped forward KL from teacher text-history policy to student visual-history policy on student rollouts
method.data_source: SearchQA (NQ + HotpotQA training splits) and ALFWorld
key_components: offline trajectory self-distillation
online policy self-distillation via forward KL
GRPO reinforcement learning
cross-modal paired contexts (text vs rendered image history)

2608.08960.novelty: Introduces cross-modal on-policy self-distillation where the same model's text-history policy provides dense logit supervision on states visited by the visual-history policy during RL, addressing a diagnosed agentic policy gap rather than OCR quality.

on_policy_mechanism.evidence_quote: On states induced by the visual-history policy's own actions, a frozen text-history policy receives the paired textual history and provides full-vocabulary supervision on the student-generated response prefixes.

opd_classification.reasoning: Self-distillation where the same model's stronger text-history policy (teacher) provides logit-level forward-KL supervision on student visual-history policy rollouts during RL training; the teacher is the model itself under a different modality context.

key_findings: CAPS improves over AgentOCR by 5.0% (3B) and 3.4% (7B) on SearchQA average EM while reducing peak memory-context cost by up to 83.4%.
On ALFWorld H=50, CAPS gains 15.6% (3B) and 14.5% (7B) over AgentOCR and surpasses its own text-history teacher by 2.8-3.1 points.
Offline and online distillation are complementary: combining them yields 39.2 vs 37.4 (offline-only) and 37.1 (online-only) for 3B SearchQA.

2608.08960.relevance_to_opd: Directly implements on-policy distillation: the visual-history student generates rollouts during GRPO training, and a frozen text-history teacher (same model, different modality input) provides full-vocabulary forward-KL supervision on student-generated response prefixes at student-visited states.

2608.09119.title: Motif 3: Technical Report
2608.09119.summary: 314B MoE LLM with GDLA attention and multi-teacher on-policy distillation post-training

method.training_loop: Pretrain 314B MoE → general SFT → train 7 specialist teachers via GRPO/SFT → MOPD: student generates on-policy rollouts, each routed to domain teacher for token-level log-prob supervision
method.loss_formulation: L_MOPD = -E_t[w̃_t * sg(log(π_T(y_t|x,y<t) / π_old(y_t|x,y<t))) * log π_θ(y_t|x,y<t)]
method.data_source: Multi-domain prompts spanning agentic, math, code, science, chat, professional work, long-context
key_components: Multi-teacher On-Policy Distillation (MOPD)
ICE-POP importance weight filtering
Seven specialist teachers (6 GRPO + 1 SFT)
GDLA attention
Expert-Specific PolyNorm
Modified manifold-constrained hyper-connections

2608.09119.novelty: Multi-teacher on-policy distillation consolidating 7 domain-specialist teachers into one student using per-token log-prob supervision with ICE-POP importance filtering, without environment rewards or KL regularization

on_policy_mechanism.evidence_quote: We generate on-policy trajectories with the student, route each example to its domain specialist, and disable environment grading so that verifier rewards do not enter the optimization objective.

opd_classification.reasoning: MOPD generates student rollouts (C1), obtains teacher log-prob supervision on those rollouts (C2), and uses a log-probability-based distillation loss (C3 - policy gradient weighted by teacher advantage signal). Though not pure KL, it is distributional teacher supervision on student-generated text.

key_findings: Motif 3 achieves 35.3 on τ3-Banking, the highest among compared models including DeepSeek-v4-Pro (30.1)
Motif 3 achieves 51.5 on ITBench-AA public subset, highest among compared models
GDLA reaches a loss of 3.2 with 9.2% fewer training tokens than MLA in controlled experiments
MOPD consolidates 7 specialist teachers into a single model competitive across all evaluated domains
2608.09119.ablations_summary: Controlled 10B-param experiments compare GDLA vs GDA vs MLA (GDLA lowest loss), Expert-Specific PolyNorm vs SwiGLU (higher effective rank with PolyNorm), and decaying router noise vs baseline (faster load balancing with noise)
limitations: Training and evaluation do not cover the full diversity of real-world tasks, domains, languages, interaction patterns, and deployment conditions
Primarily a text model, limiting applicability to tasks requiring direct understanding of visual inputs
Long-horizon applications require reliable state tracking, planning, recovery over substantially longer trajectories than evaluated
failure_modes: Performance on SciCode and CritPt remains below strongest models, suggesting room for improvement in scientific coding and specialized scientific reasoning
AA-Omniscience accuracy (30.1) remains below best-performing models
2608.09119.relevance_to_opd: Directly implements multi-teacher on-policy distillation (MOPD) as the final post-training stage, where student generates its own rollouts and receives per-token log-probability supervision from domain-specialist teachers, consolidating multiple RL-trained experts into a single model

2608.09228.title: Privileged Solutions or Context-Induced Teacher Behavior? Dissecting On-Policy Self-Distillation
2608.09228.affiliation_primary: Mohamed bin Zayed University of Artificial Intelligence
2608.09228.summary: Shows OPSD gains persist when teacher sees unrelated problem solutions, not paired target solutions

method.training_loop: Student generates on-policy rollout on target problem A; frozen self-teacher scores rollout conditioned on different problem B's solution; Forward-KL update on student
method.data_source: OpenThoughts Math 30k (siyanzhao/Openthoughts_math_30k_opsd)
key_components: on-policy student rollout
frozen self-teacher with mismatched context
Forward-KL with clipping
LoRA adapter

2608.09228.novelty: Introduces OP2SD which replaces paired target solution with unrelated problem-solution pair in teacher context, demonstrating OPSD gains arise from context-induced teacher behavior rather than privileged answer transfer

on_policy_mechanism.evidence_quote: the current student first samples a complete response to the target problem: ŷ_i ~ p_θ(·|x_i). Second, to compute the OPSD loss, the same output is replayed under both the student and the teacher.

opd_classification.reasoning: This is an analysis paper dissecting when/why on-policy self-distillation works, investigating failure modes and the role of teacher context, rather than proposing a new OPD method.

key_findings: OP2SD achieves highest Avg@12 in 8 of 9 model-benchmark groups, showing paired target solutions are unnecessary for OPSD-like gains
For Qwen3-8B, OP2SD outperforms OPSD by 10.83, 10.69, and 9.38 points on AIME2024, AIME2025, and HMMT2025
A single fixed mathematical worked example preserves gains (diversity is unnecessary), but trivial or physics contexts fail
Cross-subject physics context reduces accuracy below base model, indicating mathematical solution context is important
Locally corrupted solutions perform comparably to correct ones, suggesting exact correctness is not required
2608.09228.ablations_summary: Key ablations: (1) Fixed single example vs varying examples - diversity unnecessary; (2) Locally corrupted vs correct solution - correctness unnecessary; (3) Verbose vs concise solution - conciseness helps; (4) Physics vs math context - math context necessary; (5) Trivial 1+1 example - fails; (6) Target-only and Answer-only controls - fail in matched mode setting; (7) Domain matching - coarse domain matching unnecessary
limitations: All tasks are mathematical; generalization to other domains untested
Only Qwen3-1.7B, 4B, 8B models evaluated
Each condition has only one training run; no training-run variance captured
Deterioration observed under longer OP2SD training without understanding the mechanism
Does not identify the causal mechanism for why mathematical context works
failure_modes: Physics context causes non-terminating repetitive trajectories and substantially reduces accuracy below base
Trivial mathematical context (1+1) fails completely with Avg@12 of only 5.21/5.28/2.29
Extended training (400 updates) degrades performance similar to OPSD
Verbose correct solution reduces accuracy compared to concise version
2608.09228.relevance_to_opd: Directly analyzes on-policy self-distillation by disentangling privileged information from context-induced teacher behavior, showing that the target-specific solution is not necessary for OPSD gains and that teacher context effects are a major contributor

2608.09263.title: Privileged Likelihood Is Not Automatically Value: Three Checks for Token Credit in On-Policy Self-Distillation
2608.09263.summary: Formal framework showing privileged likelihood scores need three checks before serving as token credit in on-policy self-distillation

method.training_loop: Sample rollouts from gpt-oss-20b, external LLM writes hindsight feedback, frozen model copy scores token likelihoods under positive/negative contexts, combine with outcome coefficient for policy gradient update
method.data_source: AIME 2025 competition math problems
key_components: three-check framework (Q1: score tracks success, Q2: feedback construction, Q3: training loss behavior)
cross-fitting to remove own-rollout dependence
privileged likelihood token scores from frozen model copy
formal affine equivalence conditions for token value

2608.09263.novelty: Formal separation of three necessary checks (outcome alignment, feedback independence, gradient direction) for privileged self-distillation token scores, with proofs showing conditional mutual information is constant w.r.t. student and scalar weight preservation does not preserve parameter gradients

on_policy_mechanism.evidence_quote: A frozen or earlier copy of the rollout model then turns those texts into token likelihood differences. Thus the external LLM writes the feedback, while the model copy supplies the score used for training.

opd_classification.reasoning: This is primarily a theoretical/empirical analysis paper examining failure modes of on-policy self-distillation, establishing formal conditions under which privileged likelihood scores can serve as token credit, rather than proposing a new OPD method.

key_findings: Implemented additive token score achieves AUC=0.505 (near chance) for correctness discrimination, and 0.474 after length adjustment (slightly favoring incorrect traces)
Outcome-only control achieves 64.2% avg@4 accuracy vs 24.2-33.9% for five token-score variants on AIME 2025
One-sided teacher-policy residual is negative for both correct (-0.0334) and incorrect (-0.0502) rollouts across all 18 logged updates
Cross-fitting removes self-dependence but does not validate the score: held-out feedback AUCs remain near chance
57-71% of absolute token-score weight falls in the highest-entropy token decile
2608.09263.ablations_summary: Five token-score variants compared: three additive (entropy-gated, source-clipped, both) and two KL-regularized (full KL, projected KL). All trail outcome-only control. Additive variants drift toward higher token entropy and reference-policy KL; KL-regularized variants stay near outcome-only range but gain no accuracy.
limitations: Single seed, single benchmark (AIME 2025), unequal run lengths
Feedback from external LLM judge - results may not extend to self-generated feedback
Positive/negative templates violated matched-template requirement in audited runs
Frozen-target analysis does not account for moving teachers, shared parameters, optimizer memory
Outcome-only run was still improving when stopped - not an empirical ceiling
failure_modes: Token likelihood score assigns large positive credit to irrelevant high-entropy tokens
Own-rollout feedback creates self-dependence where rollout selects its own scoring context
Policy-weighted baseline can reverse raw score sign producing wrong update direction
Additive token scores move model toward higher entropy and KL divergence without accuracy gains

theory.theoretical_claim: Token likelihood difference equals action value iff d(s,v) = α(s) + β(s)Q^π_U(s,v) with β>0; conditional MI in forward-KL decomposition is constant w.r.t. student; positive mean-one token weights do not preserve expected parameter gradient
theory.proof_sketch: Proposition 1: affine equivalence via zero-sum tangent space orthogonality; Proposition 2: forward-KL projection identity showing MI is irreducible constant; Proposition 5: two-coordinate counterexample showing scalar invariants don't determine vector gradient

2608.09263.relevance_to_opd: Directly analyzes failure modes of on-policy self-distillation with privileged information, establishing formal conditions that must be verified before treating token likelihood scores as valid credit signals in OPD systems

2608.09447.title: WDL-OPD: Weak-Driven On-Policy Distillation via Mixture-Constrained Co-Training
2608.09447.summary: Mixture-constrained co-training of anchor+auxiliary policies matched to frozen teacher via reverse KL on geometric mixture

method.training_loop: Anchor generates rollouts; compute top-k support from anchor logits; form geometric mixture of anchor+auxiliary log-probs; minimize reverse KL(mixture||teacher) updating both policies
method.loss_formulation: L = D_KL(q_M(·|s_t) || q_T(·|s_t)) where q_M = normalize(q_A^λ · q_U^{1-λ})
method.data_source: execution- or answer-verified math prompts (104,935) and code prompts (20,247)
key_components: geometric mixture of anchor and auxiliary distributions
anchor-only rollout generation
shared top-k support
reverse KL to frozen teacher
co-training both policies with shared loss

2608.09447.novelty: Replaces frozen auxiliary/proxy contrast (as in OPD2, W2S-OPD) with a jointly trainable auxiliary policy that shares the mixture KL loss, creating branch-level degrees of freedom for co-adaptation

on_policy_mechanism.evidence_quote: generate y ∼ π A (· | x) for each x ∈ B ▷ no gradient through sampling... L ← L+ (cid:80) v∈Kt eℓM(v)[ℓ M (v)−ℓ T (v)]... backpropagate L/N to π A and π U

opd_classification.reasoning: Proposes a new divergence objective (reverse KL on geometric mixture of two trainable policies matched to teacher) for on-policy distillation, which is a novel loss formulation.

key_findings: WDL-OPD raises MATH500 accuracy from 0.630 to 0.685 at 4B and from 0.521 to 0.585 at 1.7B
Seven single-policy OPD configurations in code exhibit entropy growth or trajectory degradation while co-training avoids those failures
The initially weaker auxiliary branch crosses the anchor by step 40 and becomes the best final artifact at 4B scale
Frozen-auxiliary limit recovers an anchor-plus-contrast proxy target equivalent to OPD2/W2S-OPD forms
2608.09447.ablations_summary: The paper does not include systematic ablations (acknowledged as limitation); discusses frozen-auxiliary limit theoretically as equivalent to proxy-target methods, and identifies the controlled baseline matrix needed for future work
limitations: 1.7B math curriculum differs between single- and two-policy stages
Code comparisons use different starting checkpoints
Training two policies costs more than standard OPD; FLOP-matched control is missing
OPD2, W2S-OPD, Simple-OPD, SPOT not run in same harness
All experiments use Qwen3 family only; may not transfer to other model families or open-ended generation
failure_modes: 4B code checkpoint develops repetition around steps 100-109 after peak
MBPP+ score decreases with WDL-OPD at 4B scale
Anchor branch is non-monotonic, falling before recovering in 4B math

theory.theoretical_claim: Frozen-auxiliary limit recovers extrapolated target z*_A = z_T + (1-λ)/λ (z_T - z_U) + c'1, relating to OPD2/W2S-OPD proxy targets
theory.proof_sketch: Equality of softmax distributions implies logit equality up to constant; solving λz_A + (1-λ)z_U = z_T + c1 for z_A gives the extrapolated form

2608.09447.relevance_to_opd: Directly proposes a novel OPD method: co-trains two policies via reverse KL between their geometric mixture and a frozen teacher on anchor-generated rollouts, extending single-policy OPD with branch-level degrees of freedom

2608.09555.title: Bidirectional Context Self-Distillation for Reinforcement Learning of Skill-Based LLM Agents
2608.09555.summary: Bidirectional context self-distillation rescales GRPO advantage for skill-based LLM agents

method.training_loop: Sample rollouts under base skill context C0, re-score tokens under augmented (Meta-Skill) and pruned contexts using same policy, compute bidirectional log-prob gaps, rescale GRPO advantage, update with clipped objective
method.loss_formulation: L_BCSD(θ) = -E[min(ρ_{i,t}(θ) A^{BCSD}_{i,t}, clip(ρ_{i,t}(θ),1-ε,1+ε) A^{BCSD}_{i,t})] + β L_KL
method.data_source: On-policy rollouts from ALFWorld and WebShop environments
key_components: Meta-Skill extraction from successful/failed trajectories
Bidirectional context views (augmented + pruned)
Gap-weighted advantage rescaling
Linear decay of rescaling coefficient λ_n
Meta-Skill periodic refresh

2608.09555.novelty: Unlike prior OPSD methods using a single privileged context teacher, BCSD constructs two complementary context views (augmented Meta-Skill and pruned general skill) and uses their token-level log-prob gaps to rescale RL advantage rather than as a separate distillation loss

on_policy_mechanism.evidence_quote: For each trajectory τ_i sampled under C_0, we keep the realized response sequence y fixed and use the same policy to re-score its tokens under C_1 and C_2. This yields two token-level log-probability gaps

opd_classification.reasoning: Self-distillation where the same policy acts as teacher under different contexts on student-generated rollouts, with token-level KL-like log-prob gaps used to rescale RL advantage — a pure self-distillation method combined with RL for agents.

key_findings: BCSD achieves 83.6% success rate on ALFWorld with Qwen2.5-7B, outperforming the best baseline by 3.1 points
With Qwen2.5-3B, BCSD surpasses strongest baselines by 5.4 points on ALFWorld and 9.4 points on WebShop success rate
Token-level agreement between augmented and pruned views stays near 50%, confirming complementary rather than redundant signals
Removing Meta-Skill view causes the largest degradation (82.0→71.1 on ALFWorld), confirming its importance
BCSD shows greater sensitivity to removing task-specific skills than Skill_GRPO*, indicating better skill utilization rather than memorization
2608.09555.ablations_summary: Removing Meta-Skill teacher causes largest drop (-10.9 ALFWorld, -16.4 WebShop); removing Pruned-Skill also hurts (-7.0, -9.4); constant λ degrades both benchmarks; disabling Meta-Skill refresh hurts especially on WebShop (-16.4); α=0.9 outperforms 0.5 and 0.1 settings; λ_0=0.1 optimal among tested values
limitations: Method relies on external LLM for Meta-Skill extraction and pruning
Evaluated only on two agent benchmarks (ALFWorld and WebShop)
Requires periodic Meta-Skill refresh adding extraction overhead
failure_modes: Large λ_0 (0.5) overemphasizes context-dependent teacher signals and hurts performance
Constant λ without decay keeps policy dependent on privileged signals even after improvement
Equal weighting (α=0.5) causes conflicting signals and unstable training
2608.09555.relevance_to_opd: Directly extends on-policy self-distillation (OPSD) to skill-based LLM agents by using bidirectional context views of the same policy as complementary self-teachers, with token-level log-prob gaps rescaling GRPO advantage on student rollouts

2608.09745.title: SR-OPSD: Self-Referenced On-Policy Self-Distillation
2608.09745.affiliation_primary: Shanghai University of Finance and Economics
2608.09745.summary: Reference-anchored Rényi projection for on-policy self-distillation in LLMs

method.training_loop: Sample rollouts from student policy; construct geometric target from EMA self-teacher and frozen reference; minimize forward Rényi divergence from target to student at each token position; update self-teacher via EMA
method.loss_formulation: L = sum_t D_rho(pi*_alpha(·|h^sf_t, h^ref_t) || pi_theta(·|h_t))
method.data_source: SciKnowEval, challenging math problems (738), LiveCodeBench v6
key_components: Normalized geometric target interpolation between self-teacher and reference policy
Rényi divergence projection
EMA self-teacher with privileged context
Frozen reference policy anchoring

2608.09745.novelty: Separates target placement (geometric interpolation coefficient alpha) from projection geometry (Rényi order rho) in on-policy self-distillation, showing that reference anchoring only helps when combined with appropriate Rényi projection rather than standard KL/JSD

on_policy_mechanism.evidence_quote: At each outer iteration, OPSD first samples a batch from the rollout policy π_θold and then treats the resulting contexts as fixed while updating the student.

opd_classification.reasoning: Proposes a new divergence objective (Rényi) with adaptive reference-anchored target for on-policy self-distillation, where the teacher is a self-teacher (EMA of student with privileged context).

eval: SciKnowEval (Chemistry, Physics, Biology, Materials, Tool use)

key_findings: SR-OPSD achieves 75.2 five-domain average Avg@16 at 15h on Qwen3-8B vs 72.4 for SDPO and 69.2 for GRPO
On AIME25, SR-OPSD improves Pass@64 by 6.7 points over GRPO (80.0 vs 73.3)
On LiveCodeBench v6 with Qwen3-8B, SR-OPSD reaches 50.1 vs 48.8 for SDPO and 41.2 for GRPO
Self-reference alone degrades performance under JSD/FKL (-2.2 and -2.8 points) but improves with Rényi projection (+1.7 over best non-Rényi variant)
SR-OPSD stabilizes policy entropy dynamics compared to RKL-based SDPO which shows entropy collapse
2608.09745.ablations_summary: Self-reference without Rényi projection hurts performance (-2.2 for JSD, -2.8 for FKL). Rényi order ρ improves monotonically from 0.50 (79.9) to 0.95 (81.1). Complete SR-OPSD (self-reference + Rényi) outperforms best non-Rényi variant by 1.9 points.
limitations: Theoretical characterization concerns token-level optimization at fixed rollout contexts and does not establish global convergence
Context-distribution shift remains an additional source of error not fully controlled
Target-interpolation coefficient, Rényi order, and teacher update rate are fixed and selected empirically
Not evaluated under noisy feedback or at larger model scales
failure_modes: At smallest scale (Qwen3-0.6B), SR-OPSD trails GRPO and SDPO by 0.5 and 0.7 points due to untuned hyperparameters
On Biology domain, SR-OPSD trails SDPO by 3.5 points for Qwen3-8B

theory.theoretical_claim: Token-level variational characterization showing SR-OPSD objective equals forward Rényi projection from geometric target to student plus constant
theory.proof_sketch: Proposition 3.2 shows J_{α,ρ} = -D_ρ(π*_α || π_θ) - ρ/(ρ-1) log Z_α via algebraic manipulation of Rényi divergence definition, establishing equivalence between maximizing J and minimizing forward Rényi projection at fixed contexts

2608.09745.relevance_to_opd: Directly proposes a new on-policy self-distillation method that uses student-generated rollouts and Rényi divergence between a geometric self-teacher/reference target and the student policy, advancing the OPD objective design space

2608.09826.title: Distill Skills into Weights, Not Prompts: Abstract Skills as Privileged Signals for On-Policy Self-Distillation
2608.09826.summary: On-policy self-distillation using skill-conditioned teacher context with annealed tilted cross-entropy

method.training_loop: Student generates rollouts from question-only context; same-weight teacher scores rollouts with skill card context under stop-gradient; annealed tilted cross-entropy + GRPO loss on student prefixes; gate filters problems by sampled teacher advantage
method.loss_formulation: L(θ) = λ_R L_R(θ) + λ_D E_x[g_K(x) E_{ŷ~p_S} (1/|ŷ|) Σ_n L_n^(τ)] where L_n^(τ) = -(1/τ) log Σ_v q_n(v) p_n(v)^τ
method.data_source: DAPO-Math-17k and mathematics split of OpenThoughts
key_components: shared-parameter self-distillation with skill-conditioned teacher
annealed tilted (Rényi-type) cross-entropy objective
empirical usefulness gate
explicit-answer-filtered skill cards

2608.09826.novelty: Introduces skill-conditioned privileged context (not full solution) as teacher signal in shared-parameter on-policy self-distillation, with annealed Rényi-type cross-entropy that bounds logit gradients and converges to forward-KL, targeting zero-variance GRPO groups where reward signal vanishes

on_policy_mechanism.evidence_quote: All trajectories ŷ are sampled from the student. For each position, define p_n := p_S(· | x, ŷ_{<n}) and q_n := sg[p_T(· | x, s, ŷ_{<n})], where sg denotes stop-gradient.

opd_classification.reasoning: Self-distillation where student generates rollouts, same-weight teacher provides logit supervision under privileged context, with an adaptive annealed divergence objective

key_findings: SKALD improves overall avg@8 over GRPO by +2.46, +4.85, and +12.01 at 0.6B, 1.7B, and 4B respectively
Zero-variance-only distillation recovers 84.7% of the full gain at 1.7B, confirming the mechanism targets uninformative GRPO groups
SKALD remains +4.06 above FLOP-matched GRPO and exceeds contextual skill exposure by +3.77 at 1.7B
Zero-variance groups account for 63.0–68.0% of training groups across scales
Risk-neutral training diverges in 2/3 1.7B and 3/3 4B seeds whereas all tilted runs converge
2608.09826.ablations_summary: Ordered ablation at 1.7B: skill abstraction +0.55, annealed tilting +0.88, usefulness gate +0.43. At 4B: +1.65, +3.73, +2.33. Shuffled skill still gives +3.31 over GRPO. Removing skill from teacher reduces from 50.37 to 48.01.
limitations: Three sizes from one model family do not establish a general scaling law
The fixed gate is an empirical filter with 14.6% sign reversals by training end
Shared-parameter teacher may cease to satisfy design desiderata as training evolves
Controls narrow but cannot logically eliminate conditional-leakage concerns
Requires offline Qwen3-14B for skill extraction and screening
failure_modes: 14.6% of initially positive gate cases reverse sign by training end (false positives)
Risk-neutral (τ=0) training diverges in majority of seeds at 1.7B and all seeds at 4B
Mixed-variance-only distillation yields only +0.79, showing limited benefit on non-zero-variance groups

theory.theoretical_claim: Tilted objective has logit-gradient coordinates bounded in [-1,1], stationary solution is escort distribution p* ∝ q^{1/(1-τ)}, and τ→0 recovers teacher cross-entropy (forward-KL student gradient)
theory.proof_sketch: Lemma 1 shows gradient ∇_{z_n} L^(τ) = p_n - r_n^(τ) with effective target r_τ(v) ∝ q_n(v)p_n(v)^τ; minimizer over simplex is p* ∝ q^{1/(1-τ)}; limit τ→0 gives r=q recovering H(q,p)

2608.09826.relevance_to_opd: Directly proposes on-policy self-distillation where student generates rollouts and same-weight teacher provides token-level logit supervision under privileged skill context, with a novel annealed cross-entropy objective targeting zero-variance RL groups

2608.09836.title: Mismatch Matters: On-Policy Distillation Beyond Token Agreement
2608.09836.summary: TIDE corrects OPD failures via bounded Hellinger suppression of student-excess tokens and analytic teacher top-K recovery of student-deficit tokens

method.training_loop: Student generates rollouts; compute per-token excess (bounded Hellinger) and deficit (forward KL on teacher top-K) scores; quantile-gate selects severe positions; apply branch-specific losses jointly
method.loss_formulation: L_TIDE = L_exc + λ L_def, where L_exc uses sg[2(exp(a_t/2)-1)] log q_θ(o_t|s_t) on excess-gated positions, L_def = -Σ p̄(v) log q_θ(v|s_t) on deficit-gated positions
method.data_source: DAPO-Math-17K
key_components: quantile-gated token selection
Hellinger-shaped bounded suppression for student-excess
analytic teacher top-K recovery for student-deficit
independent dual-branch mismatch correction

2608.09836.novelty: Identifies degenerate agreement failure mode in OPD where repetitive student prefixes create artificially low KL; proposes treating excess and deficit mismatch directions independently with bounded Hellinger shaping (proper divergence geometry) and analytic top-K teacher injection bypassing sampling

on_policy_mechanism.evidence_quote: Sample a prompt batch x ∼ D and generate o ∼ q_θ(·|x) ... Construct s_t = (x, o_{<t}) and compute a_t ← log p(o_t|s_t) − log q_θ(o_t|s_t)

opd_classification.reasoning: TIDE introduces a novel divergence-based objective (Hellinger-shaped excess + forward-KL deficit) that replaces the standard reverse-KL in OPD, fitting §4.1 (new objective/divergence), with token-level selection fitting §6.1

key_findings: Under strong mismatch (Qwen3-8B→Qwen3-1.7B-Base), TIDE raises Avg@8 from 6.9% (OPD) to 20.3%, a 13.4 point improvement
TIDE reduces average response length from 22,395 to 7,294 tokens (3.1× reduction) and missing-boxed rate from 65.5% to 5.4% under strong mismatch
Under weak mismatch (JustRL-1.5B→R1-Distill-1.5B), TIDE achieves 46.7% Avg@8, improving over OPD by 1.0 points
Deficit-only intervention raises Avg@8 from 6.87 to 18.32, showing student-deficit tokens carry substantial learning value despite 95.5% having <1% sampling probability
Supervising the 20% most mismatched positions more than doubles Avg@8 (14.58) compared to matched-only supervision (7.18)
2608.09836.ablations_summary: Selection alone raises Avg@8 from 6.87 to 14.58; Hellinger excess branch reaches 18.57; deficit branch reaches 18.32; full TIDE achieves 20.34. The two branches move length in opposite directions (excess longer, deficit shorter), and their combination gives shortest responses. λ sensitivity shows stable accuracy across [0.25, 1.0] but generation quality degrades at low λ. Gate keep-rate ρ∈[0.1,0.5] varies Avg@8 by only 1.55 points.
limitations: Limited to two teacher-student pairs and mathematical reasoning; dialogue, code, and multilingual settings remain open
Fixed-state operator-level theory gives no global convergence guarantee
Adaptive keep-rate schedules not explored
Assumes a locally reliable teacher
failure_modes: Degenerate agreement: student exploits repetitive loops to achieve near-perfect token agreement with teacher despite globally flawed responses
Standard OPD collapses to base student performance (6.9% Avg@8) under strong teacher-student mismatch

theory.theoretical_claim: Hellinger shaping provides bounded, locally faithful correction aligned with squared Hellinger divergence (Proposition 1); deficit score decomposes into within-support KL + coverage gap (Proposition 2)
theory.proof_sketch: Proposition 1: h(a)=2(exp(a/2)-1) is bounded in (-2,0) for a<0, locally linear, and E_q[-h(a(v))∇logq]=4∇H²(p,q). Proposition 2: d_t = D_KL(p̄||q^K) + (-log Q_t) via substitution q(v)=Q_t·q^K(v).

2608.09836.relevance_to_opd: Directly proposes a novel on-policy distillation method (TIDE) that addresses fundamental failure modes of standard OPD by replacing the reverse-KL objective with branch-specific corrections for student-excess (bounded Hellinger) and student-deficit (analytic teacher top-K) tokens, with student generating its own rollouts and teacher providing logit-level supervision.

2608.18183.title: Accelerating Visual On-Policy Distillation with Batched Speculative Jacobi Rollouts
2608.18183.summary: HB-SJD: batched speculative Jacobi decoding to speed up student rollouts in visual OPD

method.training_loop: for step: freeze student; generate image-token suffix from real prefix via batched SJD (per-image progress, Full/Compact exec); teacher scores suffix; biKL update
method.loss_formulation: L_{OPD} = E_{\tilde{x}\sim p^k_{mix,\theta}}[\frac{1}{T-k}\sum_{t=k+1}^{T} D_{biKL}(p_{S,\theta}(\cdot|\tilde{x}_{<t}), p_T(\cdot|\tilde{x}_{<t}))],\ D_{biKL}(p,q)=\frac{1}{2}KL(p\|q)+\frac{1}{2}KL(q\|p)
method.data_source: ImageNet real prefixes + student-generated image-token suffixes
key_components: Speculative Jacobi Decoding as draft-model-free rollout engine
Independent per-image decoding progress with batched verification
Hybrid Full/Compact execution with hardware-calibrated threshold γ
Greedy and probabilistic SJD verification
History-offset draft initialization exploiting spatial locality

2608.18183.novelty: First to use speculative Jacobi decoding as a batched rollout backend for on-policy distillation of visual AR models; extends single-sequence SJD to large-batch training with independent per-image progress and hybrid execution, leaving teacher and objective unchanged.

on_policy_mechanism.evidence_quote: In visual on-policy distillation, part of the sequence is generated by the current student rather than from real data or the teacher. Given a real prefix xreal, the student generates the suffix

opd_classification.reasoning: The underlying training is on-policy KL distillation (GKD/VarKD), but the output modality is image tokens (LlamaGen image generation), which is out of scope for text-output OPD; contribution is a rollout-efficiency system, not a new distillation objective.

eval: ImageNet (50K samples: FID, IS, Precision, Recall)

key_findings: HB-SJD gives 1.48×/1.56× rollout speedups for GKD and 1.58×/1.65× for VarKD on LlamaGen-B/L with greedy verification, FID within ~0.02 of AR baselines.
Independent per-image progress is essential: batch-synchronous SJD is slower than cached AR (4239 vs 3982 ms), while independent progress reaches 3275 ms (1.216×).
Hybrid Full/Compact execution reduces mean latency from 3292 ms to 2784 ms (1.182× over Full) and P95 from 4714 to 3969 ms.
Speedup grows with longer student suffixes: 1.392× at prefix ratio 0.75 up to 1.699× at 0.20.
Speedup is stable across training stages (1.530×, 1.500×, 1.483× at 2K/12K/22K steps) and batch sizes 8–64 (1.298×–1.486×).
Greedy verification is faster (1.613×) than probabilistic SJD verification (1.500×) due to lower rejection rate and no full-vocab resampling.
2608.18183.ablations_summary: Independent progress vs sync batch (+~30% latency reduction), hybrid execution (+18% over Full), Jacobi window W=8 optimal for latency though W=16 used, insensitive to history offset H and threshold γ, greedy beats probabilistic verification.
limitations: Synchronous vs independent comparison also differs in proposal construction, so ablation is system-level rather than isolating scheduling.
Larger Jacobi windows increase commit rate but not end-to-end efficiency (latency non-monotonic in W).
Probabilistic verification incurs higher cost from full-vocabulary probability computation and resampling.
failure_modes: Batch-synchronous SJD is slower than cached AR rollout (0.939×) due to shared-window waiting.
Compact execution alone can be suboptimal when many images are active due to KV-cache row indexing overhead.
2608.18183.relevance_to_opd: Directly targets the rollout bottleneck of on-policy distillation (GKD/VarKD-style biKL on student-generated suffixes) but in the visual AR image-generation domain; the drop-in speculative rollout backend idea is transferable to text OPD efficiency.

2608.19408.title: Beyond Imitation: Filtering On-Policy Distillation by Reasoning Progress
2608.19408.affiliation_primary: The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology (Guangzhou)
2608.19408.summary: R2-OPD masks OPD reverse-KL on spans whose progress ranking conflicts with KL

method.training_loop: for batch: student samples y~π_S; compute student top-16 support reverse-KL vs teacher; segment y by discourse markers; MC rollouts (N=8) estimate solve prob → process rewards; merge sign-consistent spans; rank PR vs avg KL; mask top-q% conflicting segments; update student on masked, renormalized KL
method.loss_formulation: L_{R2\text{-}OPD} = \mathbb{E}_{x_i, y_i\sim\pi_S(\cdot|x_i)}\Big[\frac{1}{Z_i}\sum_{t=1}^{T_i} M_t^{(i)}\,\ell_t^{KL,S,(i)}\Big],\ \ell_t^{KL,S}=\sum_{v\in S_t} w_{t,v}\log\frac{\pi_S(v|h_t)}{\pi_T(v|h_t)},\ Z_i=\sum_t M_t^{(i)}
method.data_source: deduplicated DAPO-Math-17K prompts with verifier-compatible ground-truth answers; student-generated on-policy responses
key_components: support-restricted (student top-16) reverse-KL OPD objective
Monte Carlo process reward via answer-eliciting on-policy continuations (N_eval=8, 300 tokens)
discourse-marker-based reasoning segmentation with S_min=3 sentences
sign-consistent segment merging (telescoping sum, Lemma 1)
segment-level KL averaging (variance reduction, Proposition 2)
within-response rank-conflict detection between process reward and avg KL
masking of top-q% (q=30) inconsistent segments with loss renormalization
conservative fallback: PR-unavailable responses keep full supervision

2608.19408.novelty: Unlike prior OPD calibration that uses token entropy (E-OPD), teacher–student divergence (TIP-OPD), sequence position (IW-OPD), or trajectory-level correctness (Uni-OPD), R2-OPD introduces a teacher-independent, segment-level reasoning-progress signal (verifier-based MC process rewards) used only as a reliability test: it masks distillation supervision where progress and KL rankings disagree, rather than adding process reward as an objective, and provides sign-consistent merging with theoretical noise-cancellation guarantees.

on_policy_mechanism.evidence_quote: the student generates responses on-policy, the teacher supplies token-level distributional supervision on the resulting student contexts, and the student is updated using the reverse-KL objective.

opd_classification.reasoning: Core contribution is a token/segment-level masking (weighting) scheme applied to standard reverse-KL OPD on student rollouts, with the mask derived from external verifier-based process rewards.

stabilization_tricks: loss renormalization by unmasked token count
conservative fallback retaining supervision when PR unavailable

key_findings: R2-OPD reaches 35.06 avg@4 and 51.83 pass@4 on DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-1.5B, beating standard OPD by 2.51 and 4.46 points.
R2-OPD exceeds the strongest recent variant Uni-OPD by 4.28 avg@4 and 5.17 pass@4, though Uni-OPD remains better on OlympiadBench (53.16 vs 46.86).
On Qwen3-1.7B with e3-1.7B teacher, R2-OPD lifts aggregate pass@4 from 45.70 (OPD) to 48.19 with higher pass@4 on all three benchmarks.
Sign-consistent merging raises PR–KL rank agreement from ~0.20–0.27 to 0.55–0.73 and improves AIME24/AIME25 avg@4 by 15.00/14.16 points.
Masking ratio q=30 is optimal; q=50 collapses AIME24/AIME25 to 19.17/12.15.
About a third of student responses contain correct reasoning but are truncated by overthinking, motivating process-level rather than outcome-only filtering.
2608.19408.ablations_summary: Masking ratio: q=10 underfilters (lower AIME), q=30 best, q=50 removes useful teacher guidance (AIME24 19.17, AIME25 12.15); OlympiadBench is insensitive. Removing sign-consistent merging drops AIME24 to 17.5 and AIME25 to 11.67 (−15.0/−14.16) with a 0.96 gain on Olympiad, and PR–KL rank agreement falls to near/below random.
limitations: Process-reward estimation adds cost and Monte Carlo variance (authors plan to reduce it)
Generalization to larger models and other domains not examined
Benefit varies across benchmarks; Uni-OPD stronger on OlympiadBench and merging slightly hurts there
Only 1.5B/1.7B models and math domain evaluated
failure_modes: Overly aggressive masking (q=50) sharply degrades AIME accuracy
Without sign-consistent merging, noisy fine-grained PR/KL comparisons make filtering harmful on AIME
Responses lacking ground-truth string or too few segments cannot be filtered and fall back to plain OPD
Little to no gain over OPD on OlympiadBench avg@4 (46.86 vs 46.86)

theory.theoretical_claim: Lemma 1: aggregated process reward over a merged run telescopes to endpoint solve-probability estimates, cancelling internal boundary MC errors; Proposition 2: segment-averaged KL κ_j is unbiased with Var ≤ σ²(1+ρ)/(L_j(1−ρ)) = O(1/L_j) under geometrically decaying token correlations
theory.proof_sketch: Telescoping sum of finite differences Sˆ_m − Sˆ_{m−1} leaves only endpoints; variance bound sums covariances with |Cov| ≤ σ²ρ^{|t−s|} and applies the geometric series.

2608.19408.relevance_to_opd: Directly an OPD method: it keeps the standard reverse-KL on-policy distillation loop and proposes a segment-level, process-reward-based reliability filter to mask teacher supervision that conflicts with reasoning progress, addressing the teacher-similarity-as-proxy failure mode of reasoning-oriented OPD.

2608.19098.title: Open-MOPD: Diagnosing and Fixing Capability Imbalance in Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation
2608.19098.summary: Diagnoses and fixes cross-domain budget imbalance in multi-teacher OPD

method.training_loop: for step: student samples rollouts; route by domain label to RL teacher; cache teacher logprobs on student top-k; compute weighted dense reward; K PPO inner updates with student-term refresh
method.loss_formulation: r_t = \sum_{v\in S_t} \mathrm{sg}[\log\pi_{\phi_{d(x)}}(v|x,y_{<t}) - \log\pi_\theta(v|x,y_{<t})]\cdot \mathrm{softmax}_{u\in S_t}[\log\pi_\theta(u|x,y_{<t})](v), S_t=\mathrm{TopK}_{16}(\pi_\theta); PPO advantage = w_d r_t^{(k)}, w_d = w^{share}_d\cdot\mathrm{Clamp}((m_d/m_{ref})^\alpha,0.05,20)/\sum_j \tilde w_j s^{tok}_j
method.data_source: Union of DAPO-Math-17k, DeepScaler-24k (LCB-decontaminated), Nemotron-IF-RL-46k prompts; student rollouts on these prompts
key_components: oracle-routed multi-teacher OPD benchmark on SmolLM3-3B
token-share balancing (w_share = g*/s_tok)
gap-following dynamic budget allocation ((m_d/m_ref)^alpha, clamped)
student reward refresh across K inner PPO updates with cached teacher logprobs
top-k=16 dense reward in PPO advantage slot

2608.19098.novelty: First controlled, fully open M-OPD testbed with oracle routing; shows teacher conflict is not the bottleneck (mean disagreement 0.126 nat) but token-budget misallocation is (IF = 20.3% prompts, 0.99% gradient tokens); introduces three targeted mechanisms raising recovery from 35.6% to 83.4%.

on_policy_mechanism.evidence_quote: The teacher evaluates student rollouts via a single prefill pass to generate the teacher distribution.

opd_classification.reasoning: Core contribution is per-domain token weighting and dynamic budget allocation (plus staleness fix) inside a white-box multi-teacher OPD loop where the student generates rollouts and teachers supply top-k log-prob differences as dense reward.

training_setup.compute_budget: 1×8 A100-80GB node for OPD stage; 600 steps; ~1298s per outer step at K=4
stabilization_tricks: reward refresh of student-dependent term across inner updates
token-share balancing to equalize loss share

key_findings: Naive M-OPD recovers only 35.6% of the SFT→RouteRL improvement (28.05 vs RouteRL 32.35), while Open-MOPD recovers 83.4% (31.24).
IF falls 6.16 points below its RouteOPD reference under naive M-OPD, 3.3× the math gap (1.89), and plateaus earliest.
Teacher disagreement is small (mean 0.126 nat, <0.27 nat throughout; only 0.62% tokens >1 nat) and conflict masking/consensus targets reduce total score by 0.52–0.83 points.
IF accounts for 20.3% of prompts but only 0.99% of gradient tokens because mean response length is ~409 vs ~10,500 tokens for math/code.
Token-share balancing alone yields +1.17, gap-following +0.72 more (K=1); reward refresh adds +0.81 at K=4 with no measurable runtime cost (27.3s vs 27.8s dense reward computation).
Inverse reward normalization (α=-0.5) creates a feedback loop that collapses training at step 74.
Integration gap reduced from 3.50 points to 0.31 points relative to RouteOPD.
2608.19098.ablations_summary: Cumulative ladder (Table 4): Naive M-OPD 28.05 → +share 29.22 (+1.17) → +gap 29.94 (+1.89) at K=1; at K=4: naive 29.28, +share+gap 30.43, +refresh (full Open-MOPD) 31.24 (+3.19). Conflict-mask/consensus interventions all hurt; negative-α gap weighting collapses training.
limitations: Single student model/base (SmolLM3-3B) studied; results stated for 'one student model'.
Oracle routing by ground-truth domain labels; routing ambiguity not addressed.
Only three domains (math, code, IF) considered.
Reward refresh only repairs the student-dependent term; sampled states still come from rollout time.
failure_modes: Naive M-OPD: concise IF domain starves of gradient tokens and stagnates/degrades mid-training.
Inverse reward normalization (α<0) diverges and crashes training at step 74.
Removing or averaging high-conflict tokens degrades performance.
Too-small base (Qwen3-1.7B) yields 69–80% truncation, making mechanism attribution impossible.
2608.19098.relevance_to_opd: Directly extends single-teacher OPD to multi-teacher capability integration; provides an open reproducible M-OPD recipe and diagnoses token-budget imbalance, convergence-rate drift, and reward staleness as key OPD failure modes with targeted fixes.
comparable_papers: MOPD: Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation for Capability Integration (Ma et al. 2026)
AsyncOPD: How Stale Can On-Policy Distillation Be? (Kang et al. 2026)
Rethinking On-Policy Distillation of LLMs (Li et al. 2026)

2609.27869.title: Learning What to Activate: Combinatorial Capability Allocation for Long-Horizon Multimodal Agents
2609.27869.summary: On-policy preference-distilled capability-subset allocator for multimodal agents

method.training_loop: for 5 outer iters: student rolls out trajectories → GPT-5.5 pairwise prefs on visited (s,S) → fit BT utility v_φ → induce teacher Bernoulli policy → KL distill on mixed prefixes + trajectory PG
method.loss_formulation: L_p(\phi) = -E[w(y\log\sigma(\Delta v_\phi)+(1-y)\log\sigma(-\Delta v_\phi))];\; L_D(\theta)=E_{s_t\sim d^{\pi_\theta}}\sum_i E_{S_{t,<i}\sim q_{\eta,i}}[D_{KL}(\pi_T(z_{t,i}|s_t,S_{t,<i})\|\pi_\theta(z_{t,i}|s_t,S_{t,<i}))];\; \theta^\star=\arg\min[L_{PG}(\theta)+\alpha L_D(\theta)]
method.data_source: Student rollouts on OSWorld, VisualWebArena, GAIA, MMMU-Pro with K=8 capability library; GPT-5.5 pairwise preference labels on student-visited states and partial subsets
key_components: conditional pairwise capability utility (Bradley–Terry with null anchor)
autoregressive include-or-skip capability-subset policy
dual-level on-policy distillation (state-level rollout + annealed teacher–student prefix mixture)
trajectory-level policy gradient on task success − activation cost − switching cost

2609.27869.novelty: Formulates capability allocation as subset-valued decision with coupled values, recovers a teacher subset policy from sparse conditional pairwise preferences (not action labels), and extends on-policy distillation to correct both state-level and prefix-level (partial subset) mismatch via annealed mixture rollouts.

on_policy_mechanism.evidence_quote: On states visited by the student policy, the stronger teacher compares the marginal net values of candidate capabilities

opd_classification.reasoning: Student is a lightweight non-LLM allocator outputting binary capability subsets (actions, not text) and the teacher signal is GPT-5.5 pairwise preference labels converted through a Bradley–Terry utility model, not LLM logit/distributional supervision, so C2 and modality scope fail despite the on-policy KL structure.

stabilization_tricks: annealed teacher–student prefix mixture η from 1 to 0 over first half of training
batch-mean return baseline with within-batch advantage standardization
separate AdamW optimizers/schedules for utility model and policy

key_findings: With Kimi-K2.6 executor, CoCA reaches 43.3 OSWorld success vs 36.8 for best baseline NaviAgent, at cost 0.31 vs 0.51.
CoCA reduces switching cost to 0.83 on OSWorld vs 1.71 for NaviAgent and raises teacher-agreement rate to 0.84.
On GAIA efficiency, CoCA uses 6.5 LLM calls and 18.6k tokens per task vs 8.1 calls / 24.3k for NaviAgent, activating 2.9 capabilities per stage.
Removing trajectory RL raises switching cost from 0.83 to 1.58 on OSWorld while only mildly affecting success (43.3→40.1).
Removing stage-level on-policy rollout drops OSWorld success from 43.3 to 38.4, the largest single-component drop.
2609.27869.ablations_summary: All five components help: set-conditioned utility (w/o: 39.6 OSWorld), set-level on-policy prefix mixing (41.2), stage-level on-policy rollout (38.4), trajectory RL (40.1, SwC 1.58), null anchor (41.5, PPA 0.74) vs full CoCA 43.3.
limitations: Additional training cost from iterative on-policy teacher-guided preference collection and trajectory-level optimization (train cost 7.4 vs 0–5.8 for baselines)
Return bound (Theorem 3) may scale with horizon through the teacher advantage bound rather than giving a linear-horizon guarantee
Preference fitting alone is insufficient when the comparison graph is poorly conditioned (small γ_c)
failure_modes: Overly aggressive cost regularization (large λ) or switching constraints (large μ) limit effective capability selection
Without null anchor, utility shift ambiguity miscalibrates include/skip decisions
Without on-policy prefix mixing, student trained on mismatched partial subsets makes suboptimal later selections

theory.theoretical_claim: Utility estimation error bounds teacher-policy TV (Thm 1); prefix-level KL on student prefixes bounds subset TV via hybrid argument (Thm 2); student–teacher return gap ≤ 2T·Ā_T·min{1, Σ_i sqrt(C_e C_{s,i} ε_i/2)} with state/prefix density-ratio terms (Thm 3)
theory.proof_sketch: Strong convexity of anchored BT risk bounds utility error; hybrid-sequence telescoping plus Pinsker and Jensen convert per-position KL to subset TV; performance-difference identity plus bounded advantage converts TV to return gap.

2609.27869.relevance_to_opd: Applies on-policy distillation ideas (student-visited states, DAgger-style annealed teacher–student mixture, per-decision KL to a teacher distribution) to a non-LLM capability-subset allocator with a preference-derived teacher; conceptually related to OPD for agents but does not distill LLM token distributions.

2608.21500.title: SecOPD: Mitigating Adaptive Prompt Injections by On-Policy Distillation
2608.21500.summary: On-policy distillation from clean-input self-teacher for prompt-injection defense

method.training_loop: for iter: build clean p_c and attacked p_a; sample z~π_θ(·|p_a); per-token A_t=sg[logπ_ref(z_t|p_c,z<t)−logπ_θ(z_t|p_a,z<t)]; policy update with A_t
method.loss_formulation: L(\theta) = -\sum_{t=1}^{T} A_t \log \pi_\theta(z_t | p_a, z_{<t}),\quad A_t = \mathrm{sg}[\log \pi_{\text{teacher}}(z_t | p_c, z_{<t}) - \log \pi_\theta(z_t | p_a, z_{<t})] \;(\text{sampled reverse KL})
method.data_source: 19K dataset constructed from Cleaned-Alpaca (samples with non-empty input) with simulated injections sampled from an injection pool
key_components: paired clean/attacked input construction
student rollout on attacked input
frozen initialization model as teacher scoring rollout tokens under clean input
token-level reverse-KL advantages (cross-context token scoring)
LoRA student adapter training via Tinker

2608.21500.novelty: Adapts on-policy distillation to prompt-injection defense by instantiating a privileged teacher (the frozen initialization model given the injection-free clean input) that scores the student's attacked-input rollout token by token, replacing sequence-level DPO/GRPO signals used by Meta-SecAlign and GRPO defenses.

on_policy_mechanism.evidence_quote: TheLLMfirstgeneratesarolloutfromanattackedinputcontaininga trusteduserpromptanduntrustedexternaldata. ThesamerollouttokensarethenscoredbytheinitializationLLM giventhecorrespondingcleaninput

opd_classification.reasoning: Student generates on-policy rollouts on attacked inputs while the frozen initialization model, given privileged clean input, provides per-token log-prob (reverse-KL) supervision — a privileged-information self-teacher OPD applied to a new security domain.

stabilization_tricks: LoRA rank 128 adapter (only student adapter updated)

key_findings: SecOPD reduces SEP PISmith adaptive ASR on Qwen3.6-27B to 9.0% vs 94.0% for Meta-SecAlign (DPO) and 61.2% for GRPO, an order-of-magnitude improvement.
SecOPD achieves lowest static SEP ASR (1.3%) and basic adaptive ASR (0.2%), vs 28.9%/5.5% for Meta-SecAlign.
Security generalizes to unseen agentic tool-calling: AgentDojo ASR 4.7% vs 5.5% Meta-SecAlign and 26.7% undefended (GRPO gets 0.7% but utility drops to 82.5%).
Average utility across seven benchmarks is 88.1%, matching the undefended model, whereas GRPO drops to 83.1%.
Manual audit of 46 Minerva-Math regressions found only 4 genuine reasoning errors; most are answer-organization/extraction failures.
2608.21500.ablations_summary: No formal component ablation; comparison against sequence-level baselines (Meta-SecAlign DPO, GRPO with Gemini judge reward + KL to undefended model) isolates the effect of token-level clean-input feedback; case study shows SecOPD omits injected sentence while DPO/GRPO models append it.
limitations: Only targets indirect prompt injection with benign user prompt; not applicable to jailbreaks or direct prompt injections
Assumes system provides a clear trusted/untrusted input separation signal
Reasoning traces contain no acknowledgement of injections, which may hinder downstream reasoning-trace-based detection defenses
Future stronger adaptive attacks may break the model; authors do not claim to solve prompt injection
failure_modes: PISmith adaptive attacker still succeeds on 9.0% of SEP examples
On AgentDojo Slack, SecOPD ASR remains 24.8% and AdvUtility drops to 50.5%
Some Minerva-Math responses switch to unrelated problems or terminate early before a final answer
2608.21500.relevance_to_opd: Direct application of on-policy distillation (Thinking Machines style token-level reverse-KL advantages) where the teacher is the same frozen model given privileged clean context; demonstrates OPD as a credit-assignment-superior alternative to DPO/GRPO for security fine-tuning and links OPD to context distillation.

2608.21229.title: Beyond Attention Masks: Instruction Anchoring for Efficient In-Context Diffusion Generation
2608.21229.affiliation_primary: Harbin Institute of Technology / Kling AI Research
2608.21229.summary: AnchorCache: static text anchors for exact reference K/V caching in diffusion DiTs

method.training_loop: Stage1: teacher-forced velocity MSE at data interpolants (30k steps). Stage2: roll out student sampler, query frozen full-attention teacher at student-visited states, MSE on velocities (500 steps).
method.loss_formulation: L_{TF}=E_{x_0,x_1,c,t}\|v_\theta(x_t,c,t)-v_{full}(x_t,c,t)\|_2^2;\; L_{OPD}=E_{z_1,c,t}\|v_\theta(\bar z_t,c,t)-v_{full}(\bar z_t,c,t)\|_2^2,\;\bar z_t=sg(z_t^\theta)
method.data_source: OmniEdit + OrionEdit (image editing), Emilia-Dataset (TTS), OpenVE-3M (video editing)
key_components: static text anchors (ST) conditioning reference branch
exact reference K/V reuse across denoising steps
teacher-forced velocity distillation (Stage 1)
on-policy refinement at student-visited states with stop-gradient (Stage 2)
full-trajectory query sampling with Nq=4

2608.21229.novelty: First use of on-policy distillation for architectural recovery in diffusion models; resolves cacheability–conditioning trade-off via parameter-free static instruction anchors rather than attention-mask design or extra conditioning modules.

on_policy_mechanism.evidence_quote: Stage 2: on-policy refinement. We roll out the current student from z ∼ N(0,I) and collect

opd_classification.reasoning: Output is image/speech/video (non-LLM diffusion) and the supervision is MSE on velocity fields, not a KL/distributional divergence, so it fails the modality scope and C3 despite genuine student rollouts.

training_setup.compute_budget: unspecified (Stage1 30k steps + Stage2 500 steps, global batch 8, bf16, DeepSpeed ZeRO-2)
stabilization_tricks: Stage1 teacher-forced initialization before on-policy stage

key_findings: AnchorCache achieves 6.40× DiT speedup on Qwen-Image-Edit (40 steps, 8 references) while OmniContext Overall rises from 7.680 (isolated cache) to 8.185 vs 8.119 for full attention.
Continued teacher-forced training saturates at 8.015±0.015 Overall (30k–33k steps), while on-policy refinement reaches 8.057 after 250 updates and 8.185 after 500.
Static anchors improve Stage-1 OmniContext Overall from 7.529 (isolated) to 8.019; Stage 2 further improves to 8.185.
Full-trajectory query sampling with Nq=4 gives +0.166; low-noise-only queries degrade performance (−0.131 at Nq=4).
Guidance-aware OPD variants (IBM, PDM with γ=4) underperform unguided OPD by ~0.16 Overall.
Combining with SageAttention2 increases speedup to 7.99× with Overall dropping to 8.062.
Across speech (OmniVoice) and video (MiniMax-H3), AnchorCache matches full-attention quality with 1.50× and 1.80× speedups.
2608.21229.ablations_summary: Static text anchors account for the largest quality gain over the isolated cache at both recovery stages; Stage 2 on-policy refinement provides complementary gains beyond saturated teacher-forcing; full-trajectory query sampling is essential, and low-noise-concentrated queries hurt; guided-rollout branch-aware losses do not help.
limitations: Guided vs unguided rollout effect not isolated from branch-aware supervision (no guided-rollout positive-only control).
Compute analysis describes structural scaling, not exact wall-clock latency.
Table 8 cross-system comparison is not a controlled leaderboard.
Staged schedule motivated empirically, not shown mathematically necessary.
failure_modes: Concentrating OPD queries in low-noise region degrades performance (−0.083 / −0.131).
Guidance-aware OPD variants (IBM, PDM) reduce Overall by ~0.16.
Isolated cache without anchors degrades subject consistency and identity fidelity.
Combining with SageAttention2 causes larger quality drop (0.123) than on the full-attention base.

theory.theoretical_claim: Softmax analysis: required logit margin for a relevant reference token grows as log N with number of competing reference tokens; compute-scaling analysis showing identical per-step cost to isolated cache
theory.proof_sketch: Requiring attention mass p+≥ρ on the relevant token gives a − b_eff ≥ log N + log(ρ/(1−ρ)), so instruction-agnostic references push discrimination burden onto the dynamic query; AnchorCache conditions keys k_R(r,c) to share this burden.

2608.21229.relevance_to_opd: Transfers the on-policy distillation principle (student-visited states, frozen teacher queried there) from LLMs to diffusion architectural recovery; demonstrates teacher-forced saturation vs on-policy recovery, but uses velocity MSE on non-text outputs, so it is an adjacent cross-domain application rather than OPD proper.

2608.20831.title: STAR-OPD: Structured Aspect-Cascade-Aware On-Policy Reward Distillation for ABSA Quadruple Extraction
2608.20831.summary: Reward-weighted on-policy reverse-KL distillation for ABSA quadruple extraction

method.training_loop: for iter: sample batch (difficulty-aware + replay); student samples ŷ~π_S(·|x); compute set-structured rewards R (Hungarian-matched); batch-normalize → weight α; L = α·rKL(π_S‖π_T) + β·KL(π_S‖π_ref); update
method.loss_formulation: L = L_{rKL} + \beta L_{ref},\quad L_{rKL} = \mathbb{E}_{\hat{y}\sim\pi_S}\big[\alpha(x,\hat{y})\log\frac{\pi_S(\hat{y}|x)}{\pi_T(\hat{y}|x)}\big],\quad L_{ref} = \mathbb{E}_{\hat{y}\sim\pi_S}\big[\log\frac{\pi_S(\hat{y}|x)}{\pi_{ref}(\hat{y}|x)}\big],\quad \alpha = w(R(x,\hat{y})),\; R=\sum_k \lambda_k(x)R_k
method.data_source: E-ABSA20K training split with filtered pseudo-labels from a CoT fine-tuned Qwen3-32B teacher (70% retained); SemEval-2014 Restaurant/Laptop
key_components: student rollouts (on-policy)
reverse-KL distillation from teacher on student rollouts
cascade-aware set-structured rewards (base, binding, hallucination, category, format) after Hungarian matching
batch-normalized reward-to-weight transform (clipped exp, τ_w=2.0, α∈[0.2,3.0])
reference-policy KL regularizer (β=0.1)
input-adaptive reward weighting for product-part cases
difficulty-aware sampling, low-reward replay buffer, curriculum
teacher scoring over aspect taxonomy for category reward

2608.20831.novelty: Instantiates generic on-policy distillation (MiniLLM/GKD/G-OPD) for structured extraction by weighting reverse-KL updates with task-specific, order-invariant tuple-level rewards targeting target–aspect binding and target hallucination, rather than proposing a new generic OPD principle.

on_policy_mechanism.evidence_quote: on generic on-policy distillation by training on student rollouts and applying structured aspect-

opd_classification.reasoning: Student samples its own rollouts, teacher provides reverse-KL logit supervision on those rollouts, and the KL loss is reward-weighted by task-specific structural rewards, i.e., an RL/reward-augmented OPD objective applied to a new structured-extraction domain.

training_setup.compute_budget: 4×A100 80G × ~24h for on-policy student distillation (+ 4×A100 × ~14h teacher fine-tuning)
stabilization_tricks: curriculum on hard-sample exposure (0.3→0.7 over first 30% steps)

key_findings: STAR-OPD (Qwen3-4B) outperforms SeqKD, GKD, MiniLLM and G-OPD on all four E-ABSA20K domains, e.g., 0.739 vs 0.711 (G-OPD) on WomenBags and 0.771 vs 0.741 on Furniture, significant vs MiniLLM (p<0.05).
Target hallucination rate drops from 9.75% (SeqKD) to 7.22%, approaching the teacher's 6.67%.
Removing on-policy training causes the largest ablation drop (0.747→0.702, −0.045); removing rewards (plain on-policy rKL) drops to 0.716 (−0.031).
Among reward terms, removing R_bind hurts most (−0.018); collapsed scalar reward −0.013; greedy instead of Hungarian matching −0.012.
Gains on SemEval-2014 over generic OPD baselines are small (0.732 vs 0.728 Restaurant) and not consistently significant.
Largest gains on E-ABSA20K-Hard product-part subset (0.665 vs 0.644 G-OPD, teacher 0.687).
Distilled 4B student is 2.18× faster and 1.7B is 7.31× faster than the 32B teacher at inference.
2608.20831.ablations_summary: On-policy exposure contributes most (−0.045 when removed), reward shaping −0.031; binding reward is the most important reward term (−0.018), followed by hallucination (−0.010), category (−0.009), format (−0.012), adaptive weighting (−0.010); decomposed rewards beat a collapsed scalar reward (−0.013); Hungarian matching beats greedy (−0.012).
limitations: Analysis centered on ABSA quadruple extraction in e-commerce reviews; generality to other structured extraction unverified
Rewards operate at structured outcome level after generation, not token/process level, limiting early intervention
Depends on teacher quality and pseudo-label filtering pipeline; hard-subset analyses are diagnostic, not basis for broad statistical claims
Rule-based rewards raise shortcut/reward-hacking concerns, only informally checked via training dynamics
failure_modes: Small gains and inconsistent significance on simpler, low-tuple-density data (SemEval-2014)
Plain on-policy exposure without structural rewards is insufficient (0.716 vs 0.747)
Hallucination reward can be gamed by empty predictions without the |Q̂|>0 indicator guard
2608.20831.relevance_to_opd: Direct OPD paper: reverse-KL on student rollouts from a 32B teacher (MiniLLM-style), extended with task-specific structural reward weighting of rollouts and a reference KL, showing on-policy exposure is the largest contributor for structured extraction distillation.

2608.21811.title: Hints, Critics, and Teachers: Prior Injection for Sparse-Reward RL in Vision–Language Math Reasoning
2608.21811.summary: Controlled 11-arm comparison of text/distribution/value priors for sparse-reward VLM math RL

method.training_loop: for 500 steps: sample 256 prompts×4 rollouts from student (vLLM); compute advantage per arm (GRPO reward / −reverse-KL to 7B teacher / hint prefix / critic GAE); update via verl
method.loss_formulation: opd arm: A_t = -KL(\pi_\theta \| \pi_T) per token (k1 estimator), no reward; saf arm: L = L_{GRPO} + \lambda(t)\,\mathrm{clamp}(\mathrm{KL\ term}, \pm 2), \lambda(t): 1 \to 0 cosine
method.data_source: 20,830 hard visual-math problems filtered from MathV360K (base solves ≤1/8 rollouts)
key_components: GRPO baseline (n=4 groups)
hint-guided exploration (UFT-style reference-solution prefix, cosine-annealed 95%→5%)
pure on-policy distillation from Qwen2-VL-7B (advantage = −reverse KL, k1)
ReOPD teacher-trajectory prefix replay (κ=0.6)
srpo: distillation gated to failed rollouts
saf: annealed, clamped global teacher-KL added to GRPO
VAPO critic with clipped-MSE vs HL-Gauss categorical value loss
blind LLM judge (DeepSeek) with McNemar exact tests

2608.21811.novelty: First side-by-side comparison of hint, on-policy-distillation, and value-critic priors on one VLM under identical budget; shows pure OPD from a weak teacher inherits its ceiling while annealed hybrid OPD+GRPO helps; discovers that a long-used held-out slice anti-correlates (ρ=−0.74) with cross-domain transfer.

on_policy_mechanism.evidence_quote: opd is pure on-policy distillation from a Qwen2-VL-7B teacher in the Thinking Machines recipe [6]: the per-token advantage is the negative reverse KL to the teacher (k1 estimator), with no task reward.

opd_classification.reasoning: Paper does not propose a new OPD objective but empirically analyzes OPD variants (pure, replay, gated, annealed) against other priors, documenting the teacher-ceiling failure mode and the success of annealed hybrid OPD+GRPO.

training_setup.compute_budget: one 8×A800 node per arm × 11 arms, 500 steps each (distillation arms split node 4/4 student/teacher)

key_findings: Six delivered-prior arms occupy DynaMath 30.6–32.9% vs 27.0–29.1% for GRPO and four undelivered-prior arms, with no overlap.
Pure on-policy distillation (opd, reopd) converges to GRPO-level performance because the 7B teacher itself scores only 27.9% on the pool; reverse-KL imitation cannot exceed the teacher.

saf (GRPO + clamped, cosine-annealed teacher-KL) beats GRPO by +8.6 pp on sparse-800 and posts the best DynaMath-hard score (18.3%), while failure-gated persistent distillation (srpo) lands at GRPO level.
Hint arms beat GRPO by +10.4 to +11.4 pp on sparse-800 (p<1e-4); UFT's auxiliary hint-token NLL contributes nothing (51.4/52.0/52.4 n.s.).
Swapping clipped-MSE for HL-Gauss critic loss moves sparse-800 from 39.2 to 53.6 (+14.4 pp) and DynaMath from 27.0 to 31.9.
old-319 held-out slice anti-correlates with DynaMath transfer (ρ=−0.74, p=0.011) while sparse-800 predicts it (ρ=+0.89, p<0.001); three earlier conclusions retracted.
Stacking hint and distillation priors (hintsaf) buys nothing (49.4 on sparse-800, n.s. vs parents) since both solve the same early all-wrong-group bottleneck.
2608.21811.ablations_summary: hintonly vs uft001/uft002 isolates exploration vs auxiliary NLL (no difference); vapo vs vapohl isolates critic loss (+14.4 pp); opd vs reopd isolates prefix replay (n.s.); srpo vs saf isolates gated-persistent vs global-annealed distillation (saf +8.6 pp over GRPO, srpo ≈ GRPO); hintsaf tests prior composition (redundant).
limitations: Single training seed (42); seed std ≈2.4–2.7 pp, so within-group orderings should not be ranked
Pooled in-domain metric is a size-weighted summary, not an unbiased in-domain accuracy
old-319 retained only for comparability; not a generalization measure
sparse-800 shares distribution/template families with training (~3 pp template-duplicate inflation)
Predictivity of sparse-800 for transfer is an observation, not a rule
DynaMath-hard (n=104) is underpowered (best arm p=0.09)
Distillation arms never see ground-truth answers while reward arms do (supervision asymmetry)
Judge run-to-run variance ≈±0.5 pp
failure_modes: Pure OPD from a weak teacher (27.9% on pool) caps student at teacher ceiling, matching plain GRPO
Distillation gated to failed rollouts and never decayed (srpo) yields no gain over GRPO
Prefix replay (reopd) adds nothing in single-turn setting
Clipped-MSE critic starts at explained variance −755 and never recovers
Near-chance multiple-choice held-out slice ranks methods backwards
2608.21811.relevance_to_opd: Directly benchmarks on-policy distillation (Thinking Machines recipe, ReOPD replay, gated and annealed hybrids with GRPO) on a 2B VLM against hint and critic priors, providing empirical evidence for the teacher-ceiling limitation of pure OPD and for annealed OPD+RL hybrids as the robust variant.

2608.22364.title: WAM-OPD: On-Policy Distillation for World Action Models
