2608.22364.summary: On-policy teacher labeling of student robot histories for video-first WAMs

method.training_loop: Student Flash-WAM collects env trajectories; frozen LingBot-VA teacher labels histories with (z_T,a_T); student predicts z_S then a_S from sg(z_S); pseudo-Huber+FM losses update rank-8 JointLoRA for 3 epochs
method.loss_formulation: L(\theta) = \lambda_z \rho_\delta(z_S - z_T) + \lambda_a \rho_\delta(a_S - a_T) + \lambda_{FM} \| v^{act}_\theta(x^a_{\sigma=1},1,c) - (\epsilon_a - a_T) \|_2^2, \quad (\lambda_z,\lambda_a,\lambda_{FM})=(1,1,0.2)
method.data_source: Eight student-generated RoboTwin 2.0 trajectories per task (160 teacher-labeled macro-step contexts) plus four calibration trajectories
key_components: student-induced environment history collection
frozen LingBot-VA teacher labeling video+action targets
deployment-consistent action branch conditioned on stop-gradient student video plan
pseudo-Huber endpoint regression on video and action
action flow-matching auxiliary at high-noise boundary
rank-8 JointLoRA over 30 shared Transformer blocks

2608.22364.novelty: First application of on-policy (student-occupancy) distillation to video-first world action models; identifies the teacher-plan/student-plan conditioning mismatch and trains the action branch under the student's own video plan, versus VLA-OPD's token reverse-KL and Flow-OPD/DiffusionOPD's generative-path matching.

on_policy_mechanism.evidence_quote: acts in the environment and therefore determines the history distribution. A frozen teacher

opd_classification.reasoning: Robotics domain: outputs are video latents and robot action chunks (not text), and the loss is pseudo-Huber endpoint regression rather than a KL/distributional divergence, so it fails the modality scope and C3.

training_setup.compute_budget: unspecified (120 optimizer steps, batch size 4, 3 epochs per task)
stabilization_tricks: LoRA rank-8 with frozen base weights
checkpoint screening on disjoint calibration split

train: RoboTwin 2.0 student-collected trajectories (HANDOVER MIC, PUT OBJECT CABINET)

key_findings: WAM-OPD raises exact-paired held-out success on HANDOVER MIC from 0.0% to 58.3% (+58.3pp).
On PUT OBJECT CABINET success rises from 16.7% to 33.3% (+16.7pp) with the same recipe.
Only 8 student trajectories, 160 teacher-labeled contexts, and 120 optimizer steps of rank-8 LoRA were needed per task.
Gains are task-dependent; evaluation uses 6 scene seeds × 2 noise banks (12 paired units) per task.
2608.22364.ablations_summary: No ablations conducted; action-only vs joint update, fixed-package vs refreshed OPD, and cross-task retention are listed as planned (TBD).
limitations: Only two clean simulation tasks and a small held-out set; no multi-task average or real-robot transfer
Fixed trajectory package is on-policy only for the released collector and becomes stale after updates
Teacher action target is conditioned on teacher video plan, so teacher-plan/student-plan mismatch persists
Shared JointLoRA gradient interaction between video and action not measured
No compute-matched comparison to SFT, RL, action-only distillation, or full pathwise flow supervision
Contact diagnostics from restored snapshots unreliable; only official latched eval_success claimed
failure_modes: Dropping the microphone can move the episode outside useful teacher support
Smaller gains on PUT OBJECT CABINET suggest benefit depends on task and evaluation distribution
2608.22364.relevance_to_opd: Extends the on-policy distillation principle (student-induced occupancy, dense frozen-teacher supervision, cites GKD/VLA-OPD/Flow-OPD) to robotics world action models, but outputs are video/actions and the objective is pseudo-Huber regression rather than KL, placing it outside LLM OPD scope.

2608.22278.title: DreamMimic: Learning Visuomotor Whole-Body Loco-Manipulation via World Model
2608.22278.summary: World-model-assisted DAgger+RL distillation of privileged teacher into visual humanoid policy

method.training_loop: for each episode: sample teacher/student-driven envs by ratio ρ (PCG via reward EMAs); collect rollouts; update RSSM world model; update student with action-MSE + multi-step latent consistency + PPO
method.data_source: Simulated humanoid rollouts (Isaac Gym) on OMOMO and BEHAVE HOI reference trajectories processed via InterAct pipeline
key_components: Dreamer-style RSSM world model for predictive representation
auxiliary prediction heads (reward, privileged state, contact, object state)
action-conditioned multi-step latent consistency loss (H=3)
Performance-Conditioned Guidance (PCG) adaptive teacher-rollout ratio
InterMimic-style reference-buffer curriculum
DAgger + auxiliary PPO regularization

2608.22278.novelty: Repurposes a Dreamer-style RSSM not for planning but as a frozen action-conditioned metric for multi-step teacher-student latent alignment, plus reward-based adaptive teacher/student environment allocation (PCG) replacing iteration-based teacher annealing.

on_policy_mechanism.evidence_quote: use PPO regularization as an auxiliary stabilizer on student-

opd_classification.reasoning: Robotics domain with action outputs (out of scope) and teacher supervision is MSE on mean actions/latents rather than a KL/distributional loss over text.

stabilization_tricks: PPO introduced after warm-up as low-weight regularizer
frozen world model for latent consistency

key_findings: DreamMimic reaches 92.2% success on OMOMO vs 72.6% for ResNet-18 DAgger+RL and 0% for RL-only visual baselines.
Removing multi-step latent distillation drops OMOMO success from 92.2% to 70.6%.
Adding object-state prediction reduces object tracking error from 12.7 to 10.0 cm; full model reaches 8.8 cm.
PCG matches naive annealing in success (72.7%) on BEHAVE but improves robot tracking error from 15.2 to 10.2 cm and duration from 275.21 to 289.53 steps.
Depth+segmentation input gives 92.2% success vs 86.3% (seg-only) and 88.2% (depth-only/RGB).
2608.22278.ablations_summary: Multi-step latent supervision is the largest contributor (92.2→70.6 without); auxiliary heads as policy inputs (84.3 when losses only), deterministic recurrent state (74.5 with stochastic only), action conditioning (90.2 without), and PCG vs naive annealing (better tracking error/duration) each contribute.
limitations: Evaluation confined to simulation with ground-truth rendered depth and segmentation; no real-robot experiments
Failures under severe occlusion or visually ambiguous contacts
G1 upper-body hand contacts lack precision, policy pushes heavy objects rather than lifting
Cross-embodiment and cross-simulator results are qualitative only
failure_modes: severe occlusion / ambiguous contacts leading to policy errors
loss of contact with object leading to falls
imprecise fine-grained hand-object interaction after retargeting
2608.22278.relevance_to_opd: Robotics teacher-student distillation with DAgger-style on-policy student rollouts and adaptive teacher/student rollout mixing (PCG); conceptually adjacent to on-policy distillation scheduling but uses action-MSE/latent-MSE, not logit KL, and outputs are motor actions, so out of OPD scope.

2608.24987.title: D3-MOPD: Dynamic Domain ScheDuling for Efficient Multi-Teacher Distillation
2608.24987.summary: Reverse-KL-driven online domain-mixture scheduler for multi-teacher OPD

method.training_loop: for step: sample stratified batch by p_k; student rolls out; domain teacher prefills on rollouts; reverse-KL loss update; every n=10 steps off-process watcher maps per-domain KL gap×velocity → new p_k via softmax+floor
method.loss_formulation: J_{MOPD}(\theta)=\sum_{k=1}^{K} p_k \, \mathbb{E}_{x\sim D_k, y\sim\pi_\theta(\cdot|x)}\big[ D_{KL}(\pi_\theta(\cdot|x,y)\,\|\,\pi_{T_k}(\cdot|x,y)) \big], \quad p_k(t)=\epsilon+(1-K\epsilon)\frac{\exp(\tilde s_k(t)/T)}{\sum_j \exp(\tilde s_j(t)/T)}, \quad s_k=\widetilde{KL}_k \cdot v_k
method.data_source: ~4k prompts per domain: DAPO-Math-17K (Math), CodeI/O (Code), filtered Nemotron-Cascade 2 (IF), Fission-GRPO training set (Tool-use)
key_components: per-domain reverse-KL on student rollouts (vanilla MOPD)
off-process asynchronous watcher (no training-loop change)
remaining-gap signal (KL normalized by initial KL)
descent-velocity signal averaged over R=3 windows
composite gap×velocity signal with max-normalization
softmax with temperature T=0.5 and per-domain floor ε=0.10
stratified data source with batch-level jitter η=0.30
optional velocity floor and rehearsal-domain skip extensions

2608.24987.novelty: First to treat the per-domain data ratio in multi-teacher OPD as an online variable, reusing the already-computed per-domain reverse-KL (gap × descent velocity) to reallocate rollout budget across asynchronously converging domains with zero training overhead; prior MOPD work (Ma et al., Nemotron-Cascade 2, Chen et al.) keeps the mixture fixed.

on_policy_mechanism.evidence_quote: The trainer follows vanilla MOPD: at each rollout step, the student generates responses from prompts

opd_classification.reasoning: Core method is an adaptive data-mixture/curriculum scheduler over domains for on-policy reverse-KL distillation from multiple white-box teachers, improving efficiency (3× fewer rollout steps).

training_setup.compute_budget: 7 GPU nodes (4 trainer, 2 SGLang rollout, 1 teacher node shared by 4 teachers) × 256 rollout steps; GPU type/hours unspecified
training_setup.rl_algorithm: pure-KD (per-token reverse-KL on slime, CISPO clipped importance weighting, clip 0.2)
stabilization_tricks: R=3 window averaging of descent velocity
per-domain mixture floor ε=0.10 against forgetting

key_findings: D3-MOPD closes 97% of the average student-to-teacher gap vs 63% for vanilla MOPD (per-benchmark peaks) on Qwen3.6-35B-A3B.
D3-MOPD surpasses the vanilla peak average (61.4 at step 143) by step 47 (62.1), ~3× fewer rollout steps; peak average 62.3 at step 95.
D3-MOPD exceeds specialist teachers on HMMT (+0.9), IFEval (+0.4), and OJBench C++ (+1.2).
Per-domain reverse-KL plateaus at very different steps (Code ~48, Math ~96, IF ~144) and benchmark peak order matches this r-KL convergence order.
Watcher adds no sync overhead: throughput 520 vs 531 tokens/GPU/s (2.1% difference attributed to sequence-length shift).
On Qwen3.5-4B student, D3-MOPD reaches normalized 1.01 vs 0.86 for vanilla and peaks 40 steps earlier (119 vs 159).
At a single best-average checkpoint, normalized score is 0.73 (D3) vs 0.48 (vanilla).
2608.24987.ablations_summary: Composite signal beats single signals (w/o velocity 61.41, w/o gap 61.46 vs 62.34 avg); removing jitter drops peak avg by 0.71 (61.63), mostly on code; R=1 vs R=3 velocity smoothing 62.17 vs 62.34; velocity floor φ=0.2 helps IF (+0.8 IFBench) with similar average; rehearsal skip prevents self-teacher domain from inflating allocation.
limitations: Distillation primarily closes existing gaps; student generally stays below the domain-expert teachers' maximum
Hard-clipped velocity can starve a domain whose KL briefly rebounds (needs velocity floor extension)
Self-teacher (rehearsal) domains inflate normalized gap due to near-zero initial KL (needs rehearsal skip)
Exponential-decay theory is a simplifying assumption, not a necessary condition
Evaluated only with same-backbone teachers on 4 domains; scaling-with-K benefit is argued, not demonstrated
failure_modes: Code benchmarks converge and begin degrading after ~80 steps under fixed mixture (domain over-optimization)
Velocity-only (w/o gap) scheduler oscillates early and peaks latest (step 255)
KL rebound in IF (steps 60–150) drives its allocation to the floor despite large remaining gap when φ=0
Frozen-student teacher domain receives 0.40–0.52 share without rehearsal skip

compute_efficiency.speedup_vs_baseline: 3.0× (rollout steps to reach vanilla peak); 25% fewer steps on 4B

theory.theoretical_claim: Under an exponential KL-decay model with uniform allocation and λ_k BW/K ≪ 1, the composite signal s_k = normalized-gap × velocity ≈ (BW/K)|∂KL̃_k/∂n_k|, so argmax s_k greedily maximizes reduction in average normalized gap (Proposition 1)
theory.proof_sketch: KL̃_k = e^{-λ_k n_k}; marginal reduction λ_k KL̃_k; single-window relative change δ = e^{-λ_k BW/K} − 1 gives v_k = 1 − e^{-λ_k BW/K} ≈ λ_k BW/K; product yields (BW/K) λ_k KL̃_k.

2608.24987.relevance_to_opd: Directly extends multi-teacher on-policy distillation (MOPD) with an adaptive curriculum over domains driven by the reverse-KL signal, improving both peak quality and sample efficiency of OPD without changing the loss.

2608.24696.title: On-policy Distillation with Verifiable Reward
2608.24696.summary: ReLU-gates sampled-token OPD reward by verifier correctness, unifying OPD and RLVR

method.training_loop: for batch: student samples rollouts; verifier labels R∈{+1,-1}; teacher scores sampled tokens; reward = R·ReLU(R·log(π_T/π_θ)); policy-gradient update (REINFORCE or GRPO advantage)
method.loss_formulation: L_{OPDVR}(\theta) = -\sum_{t=1}^{|o|} R_{OPDVR}(o_t)\log\pi_\theta(o_t|q,o_{<t}),\quad R_{OPDVR}(o_t)=\max(0,\log\frac{\pi_T(o_t|q,o_{<t})}{\pi_\theta(o_t|q,o_{<t})})\cdot(+1) \text{ if correct},\ \max(0,\log\frac{\pi_\theta}{\pi_T})\cdot(-1) \text{ if incorrect};\ \text{GRPD: } R=\mathrm{sign}(\hat A_{i,t})\cdot\mathrm{ReLU}(\mathrm{sign}(\hat A_{i,t})\log\frac{\pi_T}{\pi_\theta})
method.data_source: DeepMath filtered subset (57k, difficulty ≥6) and DAPO-Math-17k math prompts with verifiable answers
key_components: sampled-token reverse-KL OPD reinterpreted as implicit token-level reward log(π_T/π_θ)
verifier-conditioned ReLU gate enforcing non-negative rewards on correct trajectories and non-positive on incorrect
conditional token mask removing verifier-conflicting tokens (~50% of tokens)
GRPD: replacing binary verifier sign with GRPO group-relative advantage sign
no extra hyperparameters vs. weighted OPD+RLVR combinations

2608.24696.novelty: Unlike prior OPD+RLVR combinations that weight two losses (OPD+GRPO), switch by advantage sign (Distilled RL), or scale conflicting tokens (SG-OPD), OPDVR shows a single hyperparameter-free ReLU gate on the sampled-token log-ratio converts OPD into a proper RLVR method, and proves the gated update is never anti-aligned with the verifier gradient and can exceed the teacher.

on_policy_mechanism.evidence_quote: The most widely adopted variant is sampled-token OPD. It uses a single Monte Carlo sample

opd_classification.reasoning: Core contribution is a new RL-augmented OPD objective where the verifier reward gates the sampled-token reverse-KL log-ratio on student rollouts, with the teacher's distributional signal remaining the central loss.

teacher.name: Qwen3-4B-RL (Qwen3-4B-nonthinking trained with GRPO on DeepMath)

training_setup.rl_algorithm: REINFORCE-style policy gradient with gated OPD reward; GRPO variant (GRPD)

benchmarks.name: Average (6 benchmarks, GRPD same-arch on DAPO-Math-17k)

key_findings: OPDVR reaches 49.1 avg in same-arch setting vs 47.8 for sampled-token OPD and 47.9 for ExOPD, and surpasses the teacher on AIME24 (36.9 vs 36.0).
In cross-arch setting (Qwen3-1.7B-Base←Qwen3-4B-Base-RL) OPDVR gets 22.8 avg vs 21.7 for the best baseline Top-64 OPD.
GRPD (GRPO-advantage variant) achieves 49.4 avg, beating GRPO (44.8), OPD (48.4), and Distilled RL (48.7), with +6.5 AIME24 and +10.9 AIME25 over GRPO.
Inverse-gated ablation drops to 44.6 avg (below vanilla OPD 47.8), confirming the gate direction matters (OPDVR +1.3, inverse −3.2 vs OPD).
Roughly half of sampled tokens (≈0.48–0.50 for 4B, ≈0.40–0.44 for 1.7B) are zero-gated consistently throughout training.
Theory shows OPDVR's update is never anti-aligned with the verifier gradient and equals OPD minus a verifier-conflicting component.
2608.24696.ablations_summary: Inverse-gated variant (keeping exactly the tokens OPDVR masks) performs worse than vanilla OPD on all six benchmarks (44.6 vs 47.8 avg), while OPDVR improves to 49.1; still, even inverse-gated improves over the initial student (42.0), showing the teacher signal remains useful even with misaligned signs.
limitations: No explicit limitations section; experiments confined to math reasoning with Qwen3 models up to 4B
Requires a verifier (ground-truth answers) so applicability is limited to verifiable domains
failure_modes: In the cross-architecture setting the student only closes ~40% of the teacher gap (22.8 vs 30.9)
OPDVR underperforms ExOPD on MATH500 (84.7 vs 86.6) and Minerva (33.2 vs 35.9) in the same-arch setting
Entropy and response-length dynamics are dictated by the teacher-student pair (4B response length inflates >4×), not controlled by the objective

theory.theoretical_claim: Verifier alignment: ⟨Δ_OPDVR,Δ_RLVR⟩ ≥ 0 always while OPD can be anti-aligned; OPD = OPDVR + conflict term with non-positive verifier projection; in a two-token toy problem OPDVR strictly outperforms both OPD and a suboptimal teacher
theory.proof_sketch: Write OPDVR token update as R·ReLU(R·r_t)·u_t; its inner product with the RLVR direction R·u_t equals ReLU(R r_t)||u_t||² ≥ 0, whereas OPD gives r_t R ||u_t||², negative when signs disagree; decomposing OPD as OPDVR plus r_t·1(r_t R<0)u_t isolates the harmful component; in a binary-token example with student q0 > teacher p, both gated updates vanish so the student stays at q0 and J=2q0−1 > 2p−1.

2608.24696.relevance_to_opd: Directly extends sampled-token on-policy distillation by reinterpreting its log-ratio as an implicit RL reward and gating it with verifiable correctness, providing a hyperparameter-free bridge between OPD and RLVR (REINFORCE/GRPO) and a theoretical account of when OPD conflicts with task reward.

2608.25936.title: One Symptom, Three Levers: A Critical Review of On-Policy Self-Distillation
2608.25936.summary: Critical review of OPSD organizing collapse via token weighting, PI choice, teacher dynamics

method.training_loop: Review of OPSD loop: student samples rollout ŷ~p_S(·|x); frozen self-teacher scores each token given PI y*; forward-KL(p_T||p_S) per token, clipped, averaged; update student only
method.loss_formulation: L_{OPSD}(\theta) = \frac{1}{|B|}\sum_{(x,y^\star)\in B}\frac{1}{|\hat y|}\sum_{n=1}^{|\hat y|}\sum_{v\in V}\min\left(p_T(v)\log\frac{p_T(v)}{p_S(v)},\tau\right),\; p_T=p_\theta(\cdot|x,y^\star,\hat y_{<n}),\; p_S=p_\theta(\cdot|x,\hat y_{<n})
method.data_source: No new experiments; synthesizes reviewed OPSD literature on mathematical reasoning (annotated math solutions in cited works)
key_components: Lever A: signal geometry (forward vs reverse KL, token weighting/selective density)
Lever B: nature of privileged information (answer, solution, partial trace, plan, rubric, critique, feedback)
Lever C: loop stability (frozen vs EMA vs gated-refresh teacher; decay of PI exposure)
Collapse as symptom measured via pass@k not entropy
PMI mechanism explaining PI-induced suppression of deliberation tokens

2608.25936.novelty: First critical review restricting to OPSD on math reasoning that unifies collapse phenomena under a three-lever framework, imports the learning-using-privileged-information and robotics 'reconstructibility' criterion, proposes a risk-ordered PI taxonomy, and separates settled from disputed results; no new method or experiments.

on_policy_mechanism.evidence_quote: On-policy distillation trains a language model on its own generations while a teacher scores them token by token. It combines the dense supervision of imitation learning with the on-policy sampling of reinforcement learning.

opd_classification.reasoning: Review paper with no new experiments that analyzes OPSD failure modes (collapse, PI leakage, forgetting) and organizes the field into a decision framework of three levers.

benchmarks.metric: accuracy (best-over-checkpoints, Qwen3-1.7B OPSD, from founding paper)

benchmarks.name: C-Eval
benchmarks.metric: accuracy (DOPD, final-answer PI vs no-PI vs step-wise hints)

key_findings: Privileged information helps only when the student can reconstruct it at test time; the reference solution/final answer is the least transferable choice, degrading thinking models by up to −17% (avg@16).
Collapse is not visible in mean score or entropy: on Qwen3-8B self-distillation raised pass@1 from 71.9 to 73.4 while pass@16 fell from 83.6 to 78.5.

Uniform token weighting is suboptimal; distilling only on positively aligned tokens (~half) is estimated to improve the signal 10–15×, and entropy-aware forward-KL on high-entropy tokens costs ~4.5% overhead.
OPSD step costs about twice a GRPO step (20.6s vs 11.2s on Qwen3-8B, 8×H100) but converges in fewer steps with a single 1,024-token rollout instead of 8×16k.
Intermediate-abstraction PI (step-aligned critique +5.27 over solution-conditioned OPSD, +16.11 over GRPO avg@12; step-wise hints 71.3 vs 63.0 on C-Eval) outperforms the oracle answer.

A frozen teacher imposes a performance ceiling while a lock-step teacher collapses the loop; EMA, gated refresh, trust-region teachers and PI decay (ATESD +0.95 to +2.33 avg@12) are proposed remedies.
2608.25936.ablations_summary: No ablations performed; the review synthesizes cited comparisons: forward vs reverse KL (reverse KL raises pass@1 but collapses pass@k), PI type comparisons (answer < solution < partial trace < hints/critique/feedback), and teacher update rules (frozen vs EMA vs gated refresh), noting no systematic cross-PI or cross-update-rule comparison exists.
limitations: Restricted to mathematical reasoning; multimodal and agentic branches excluded
Nearly all cited works are preprints less than six months old
Most evidence is on a single model family (Qwen) at sizes of a few billion parameters
No new experiments; PI risk taxonomy is only partially supported by literature and may contain errors
Reasoning benchmarks are fragile (variance, contamination, Qwen-specific effects)
failure_modes: Diversity collapse: pass@1 up while pass@k down, worse out of domain
PI leakage/shortcuts: student learns to rely on information unavailable at test time
Suppression of deliberation/epistemic tokens when teacher is conditioned on the answer, harming thinking models
Rich-get-richer: sampled demonstrations as PI amplify dominant modes and kill rare correct strategies
Catastrophic forgetting in continual learning: dense self-distillation forgets more than sparse RL
State-oblivious collapse when teacher is refreshed at fixed intervals onto a drifting student

theory.theoretical_claim: Conceptual: OPSD token signal is a PMI between token and privileged context; collapse governed by three levers; forgetting ordering SFT > dense self-distillation > sparse RL (conjecture)
theory.proof_sketch: Derives forward-KL gradient ∝ p_S(v) − p_T(v) w.r.t. logits; frames OPSD as learning-using-privileged-information (Vapnik) and imports stop-gradient/EMA/asymmetry rules from SSL (SimSiam, BYOL, Mean Teacher); no formal theorems.

2608.25936.relevance_to_opd: Directly surveys the on-policy self-distillation branch of OPD, formalizing the OPSD loop, cataloguing failure modes (collapse, PI leakage, forgetting) and remedies (token weighting, PI choice, teacher dynamics), and providing an evaluation grid (pass@k, controls) for OPD research.

2608.25643.title: A Token-Level Analysis of Sampled-Token Reverse-KL On-Policy Distillation
2608.25643.summary: Gradient-norm analysis of K2 reverse-KL OPD; SuRe surprise-aware token reweighting

method.training_loop: for step: sample student rollouts; per token compute Δlogp=logπ_T−logπ_S, L_t=½Δlogp²; w_t=1+α(1−sg(π_S)); L=mean(w_t L_t); update θ
method.loss_formulation: L_{RKL-rw} = \frac{1}{|T|}\sum_{t\in T} w_t \cdot \frac{1}{2}(\log\pi_T(y_t|c_t)-\log\pi_S(y_t|c_t))^2,\; w_t = 1+\alpha(1-\mathrm{sg}(\pi_S(y_t|c_t)))
method.data_source: DeepMath 57K hard split (difficulty ≥ 6), prompts only; responses sampled on-policy from student
key_components: per-token K2 estimator of reverse KL on student rollouts
exact ℓ1 gradient-norm identity: 2|Δlogp_t|(1−π_S(y_t|c_t))
token-level gradient allocation diagnostics (deciles, top-k% coverage vs entropy/JSD)
SuRe detached bounded weight w_t∈[1,1+α]
orientation/mean-normalized/shuffled controls

2608.25643.novelty: First closed-form characterization of how the sampled-token K2 reverse-KL OPD loss allocates logit-gradient norm across tokens (factorizing into teacher–student gap × (1−π_S)), plus empirical evidence that low-student-probability tokens dominate the update budget; SuRe differs from entropy-based token selection/masking by using a smooth, detached, threshold-free student-probability weight requiring no extra model or forward pass.

on_policy_mechanism.evidence_quote: We optimize the K2 estimator of reverse KL at each tokenonstudentrollouts.

opd_classification.reasoning: Core method is a per-token reweighting (SuRe) of a reverse-KL OPD loss on student rollouts with a frozen Qwen3-8B teacher, motivated by a theoretical gradient-norm analysis of token allocation.

key_findings: The ℓ1 norm of the per-token K2 reverse-KL logit gradient factorizes exactly as 2|Δlogp_t|(1−π_S(y_t|c_t)).
Ranking tokens by |Δlogp_t| captures 54.1%/74.6% of summed gradient norm in the top 5%/10% tokens vs 28.4%/47.3% for JSD and 23.7%/42.4% for entropy.
Only 8.5% of OPD-rollout tokens and 7.1% of Base-rollout tokens have |Δ_OPD−Base|>1 after training, i.e., checkpoint shift is localized.
SuRe (α=1.0) improves vanilla OPD on AMC23 by +3.7pp avg@8 and +7.5pp pass@8 at 1.7B and +5.0pp pass@8 at 4B; AIME24 pass@8 at 1.7B rises 16.67→23.33.
Vanilla OPD beats offline KD and SeqKD on every math benchmark; KD/SeqKD sometimes fall below Base.
SuRe matches or exceeds GRPO on avg@k on all four math benchmarks (e.g., MATH-500 67.65 vs 65.80) but trails on AIME25 pass@8.
OOD (CRUX, IFEval, MMLU-Pro) results are broadly comparable between OPD and SuRe; both slightly below Base on 1.7B MMLU-Pro.
Second seed (43) reproduces MATH-500 avg@4 gain: 66.40 (OPD) vs 67.50 (SuRe).
2608.25643.ablations_summary: α sweep {0.2,0.5,1.0,2.0}: pass@k on AMC23 rises monotonically to α=1.0 at small k, α=2.0 weakens gains (non-monotonic). Orientation controls: High-reweight (weighting confident tokens) underperforms SuRe; Random-reweight/exact-shuffled still exceed vanilla OPD so gain is not fully attributable to exact surprise alignment. Mean-normalized SuRe preserves gain (MATH-500 avg@4 69.20 vs 66.55), so a larger mean weight is not necessary; rank-reversed 67.00; uplift-only 68.40.
limitations: Only sampled-token reverse-KL OPD studied; full-vocabulary distillation and JSD objectives not investigated
Experiments limited to math reasoning with relatively short reasoning traces
Limited model/OPD configurations; no larger-scale students due to compute budget
Controls do not statistically separate exact surprise alignment from generic non-uniform weighting
failure_modes: Both AIME25 metrics decrease with SuRe at 4B scale (17.08→14.17 avg@8, 40.00→36.67 pass@8)
Larger amplification (α=2.0) weakens small-k gains and approaches vanilla OPD
Slight MMLU-Pro degradation below Base for both OPD and SuRe on 1.7B
Probability-only weight amplifies all low-π_S tokens regardless of sign of teacher–student gap

theory.theoretical_claim: Lemma 1: ℓ1 norm of per-token K2 reverse-KL logit gradient equals 2|Δlogp_t|(1−π_S(y_t|c_t)); K2 logit gradient is unbiased for reverse-KL gradient under current-student sampling at fixed context
theory.proof_sketch: Chain rule through softmax Jacobian ∇_z logπ_S(y_t)=e_{y_t}−π_S gives ∇_z L_t = −Δlogp_t(e_{y_t}−π_S); summing absolute coordinates over the sampled token and competitors each yields |Δlogp_t|(1−π_S), giving the factor 2.

2608.25643.relevance_to_opd: Directly analyzes the standard sampled-token reverse-KL (K2) OPD loss used in Qwen3/Thinking-Machines-style pipelines, showing gradient concentration on student-surprised tokens and proposing a token-weighting variant (SuRe) as an efficiency/allocation technique for OPD.

2608.27409.title: Consolidating RLVR Capabilities Across Domains: A Deep Dive into Fusion Paradigms
2608.27409.summary: Controlled comparison of Merge, Mix RL, and multi-teacher OPD for fusing RLVR experts

method.training_loop: Train 5 per-domain RLVR experts (GRPO); fuse via (a) task-vector Merge, (b) Mix RL GRPO on pooled data, (c) MOPD: student samples rollouts, domain expert supplies token logprobs, minimize reverse KL
method.loss_formulation: L(\theta)=\mathbb{E}_{q,o\sim\pi_\theta}\left[\sum_{t=1}^{|o|} D_{KL}(\pi_\theta(\cdot|s_t)\,\|\,\pi_{\theta_i}(\cdot|s_t))\right]
method.data_source: Polaris (math, 38,131 hard), OpenScienceReasoning-2 (50,000), CodeContests+Open-R1 (19,169), WildChat-1M+Open-Instruct (16,575), Workplace Assistant agent (10,229); mixed corpus of 87,699
key_components: Per-domain GRPO experts (full-parameter and LoRA r=32)
Task Arithmetic merge (λ=0.6) plus TIES/DARE/SCE/Average variants
Mix RL single GRPO run on mixed corpus (25/22/22/19/12%)
Multi-teacher on-policy distillation with sampled-token reverse KL (log-ratio estimator)
Task-vector cosine geometry analysis at layer 16
pass@k coverage and held-out capability retention analysis

2608.27409.novelty: First unified comparison of Merge, Mix RL and MOPD on shared experts/data across 4B and 8B Qwen3 backbones, explaining domain-level differences via behavioral transfer and task-vector geometry, and quantifying MOPD's teacher-bounded ceiling and cost trade-offs; no new distillation objective is proposed.

on_policy_mechanism.evidence_quote: keeps both, supervising a student on its own rollouts with logits from the expert corresponding to

opd_classification.reasoning: The paper contributes no new OPD objective but provides a controlled empirical analysis and decision guideline for when multi-teacher OPD is preferable to merging or mixed RL, including its teacher-bounded failure mode and compute costs.

training_setup.compute_budget: 32×H20 GPUs; MOPD fusion stage 741 GPU-h (4B) / 899 GPU-h (8B); per-domain RL 5,220 / 4,670 GPU-h; Mix RL 3,042 / 3,138 GPU-h
stabilization_tricks: Sampled-token reverse-KL estimator via log-probability ratio
lower LoRA learning rate for math domain

key_findings: Average performance of the three fusion paradigms differs by at most 1.4 points on either backbone, but the gap reaches 8.6 points on a single benchmark.

MOPD stays close to its teachers on all domains (avg 63.3 vs 63.9 on 4B; 53.2 vs 53.8 on 8B) but never surpasses them on average, whereas Merge and Mix RL trail IF experts by 4.9-9.2 points on IFBench.
MOPD converges fastest: at least 70% of its total gain is reached by step 100 of 300, and it stays above per-domain RL at matched data exposure.
MOPD's fusion stage costs 741/899 GPU-h (<0.2× per-domain RL) but end-to-end cost is 1.14×/1.19× because it presupposes trained experts; Mix RL costs 0.58×/0.67×; Merge is ≈0.

Math, science and code reinforce each other (layer-16 task-vector cosine 21.7e-3 on 4B, 50.7e-3 on 8B for math-science) while IF and agent are near-orthogonal (|cos| ≤ 2.3e-3); IF expert lowers BFCLv3 by 9.8 points on 4B.
At pass@32 on AIME 2025/26 none of the fusion paradigms is distinguishable from the base model, indicating reweighting rather than expanded coverage.
No paradigm scores below the base model on held-out SimpleQA-Verified or AA-LCR.
2608.27409.ablations_summary: Merging method sweep (Average, TA, TIES, DARE-TA, SCE, Concat, SVD) shows TA/DARE-TA best (4B avg 63.7/63.8; 8B 53.7/54.2), Average and SCE much worse on 8B; λ sweep for TA shows accuracy rises with λ but response length grows 2,042→7,334 tokens with thinking-mode leakage up to ~66%, motivating λ=0.6; LoRA experts track full-parameter within 1.4 points and LoRA merges are ~1 point lower.
limitations: Only the standard reverse-KL form of MOPD is studied; variants that extrapolate beyond the teacher (reward extrapolation, policy shift) are left to future work.
Unclear whether such variants lift the teacher ceiling under multi-domain fusion where the student must reconcile multiple teachers.
LoRA adapters' routing/transfer advantages at serving time are not exploited in the fusion comparison.
Costs reported for full-parameter runs only; Qwen3-8B results reported in non-thinking mode only.
failure_modes: MOPD is bounded by its teachers: no signal encourages surpassing them, so gains flatten while per-domain RL continues to improve.
MOPD provides no expansion in solution coverage because teachers derive from the same base model and have no new solution support to import.
Mix RL underperforms on domains with no positive transfer (IF trails experts by 9.2 at 4B, 4.9 at 8B) because progress tracks the domain's share of prompts.
Merge retains only ~60% of the IF expert's IFBench gain due to near-orthogonal task vectors; large merge scaling λ causes thinking-mode leakage.

compute_efficiency.speedup_vs_baseline: MOPD fusion stage <0.2× per-domain RL GPU-h (741 vs 5,220 on 4B), but 1.14-1.19× end-to-end including expert training

2608.27409.relevance_to_opd: Provides a controlled empirical characterization of multi-teacher on-policy distillation versus model merging and mixed-domain RLVR, quantifying MOPD's fast convergence, teacher-bounded ceiling, cost structure, and lack of coverage expansion, offering decision guidance for when to use OPD for consolidating domain experts.

2608.26872.title: Self-OPD: On-Policy Distillation for Flow Matching Models without Teacher
2608.26872.affiliation_primary: Tsinghua University / Zhejiang University / Alibaba Group
2608.26872.summary: Teacher-free reward-driven step-wise self-distillation for flow matching image models

method.training_loop: For each on-policy timestep: branch prediction into K SDE candidates, ODE-rollout to images, score with rewards vs ODE self-reference, compute advantages, pull-push regress velocity
method.loss_formulation: L^{(j)} = \frac{(1+\eta^2/2)^2|\Delta t_j|}{2\sigma_{t_j}^2}\frac{1}{K}\sum_{k=1}^K |A_k|[r_k\|v_\theta - v_+^{(k)}\|^2 - (1-r_k)d_k\|v_\theta - v_-^{(k)}\|^2],\quad L_{total}=\sum_j \alpha_j L^{(j)}
method.data_source: Student's own SDE-branched rollouts on OCR/GenEval/aesthetic prompts scored by reward models (OCR accuracy, GenEval, PickScore, HPSv2)
key_components: SDE branching exploration (K=8)
deterministic ODE self-reference baseline
all-branch pull-push advantage-weighted regression
direction-aware attenuation d_k
SDE-variance (per-step KL) normalization
reward-level fusion for multi-objective alignment
timestep weighting alpha_j

2608.26872.novelty: Replaces teacher-provided velocity targets in Flow-OPD/DiffusionOPD with reward-ranked self-explored SDE branches and a self-reference ODE baseline, adds signed pull-push with direction gating, and fuses multiple objectives at the reward level rather than the velocity-field level, removing task-specific teacher training.

on_policy_mechanism.evidence_quote: At each timestep, Self-OPD branches the deterministic next-state prediction into K stochastic SDE candidates, rolls them out with the ODE sampler, and compares their rewards against a deterministic self-reference baseline to obtain normalized advantages.

opd_classification.reasoning: Output modality is images (flow matching T2I, out of scope) and there is no separate teacher providing distributional supervision—supervision comes from scalar reward models on self-generated branches, so C2 fails.

training_setup.compute_budget: unspecified GPUs; ~62h (OCR) / ~90h (GenEval) wall-clock from scratch, ~44-48h with warm-start

key_findings: Mixed-reward Self-OPD achieves GenEval strict 0.9521, OCR 0.9597, and same-test-image PickScore 23.87 / HPSv2 0.3214, beating teacher-based DiffusionOPD (22.72 / 0.2676) without any teacher.
Single-reward Self-OPD outperforms Flow-GRPO and GRPO-Guard on every task with identical base model and rewards (e.g., OCR 0.9745 vs 0.9253/0.9348).
Self-OPD reaches DiffusionOPD-level OCR (0.946) in ~62h from scratch vs DiffusionOPD's 97h total; warm-start reaches it in ~48h (roughly 2× faster).
Best-of-K regression barely surpasses baseline and is unstable; all-branch pull-push plus |Δt|-aligned KL normalization stabilizes and accelerates training.
Unbounded direction gate d_k∈[0,2] causes sharp collapse to GenEval 0.768; bounded [0,1] gate trains monotonically.
DiffusionOPD's PickScore drops by Δ=1.23 when moving from aesthetic to task prompts, while Self-OPD shifts only Δ=0.48.
2608.26872.ablations_summary: All-branch advantage weighting beats Best-of-K; |Δt|-aligned KL normalization further speeds convergence; bounding d_k to [0,1] prevents collapse; early-timestep weighting speeds convergence while a TIS variant that oversamples early steps degrades below base.
limitations: Relies on reward models (OCR, GenEval, PickScore, HPSv2) and uses PickScore/HPSv2 as guards against reward hacking
Timestep importance sampling variant degrades performance below base model
failure_modes: Best-of-K target regression yields unstable, non-monotonic training
Unbounded repulsion coefficient causes performance collapse
Oversampling early timesteps (TIS) drops below base model

theory.theoretical_claim: Per-step reverse-KL gradient between reward-tilted target and Gaussian SDE kernel equals precision-scaled mean displacement; Self-OPD loss is a Monte-Carlo estimate of this gradient; reward-level fusion equals a single joint tilt by composite advantage
theory.proof_sketch: Reverse KL decomposes into E_q*[log q*] (independent of student mean) minus E_q*[log q_θ]; gradient of Gaussian log-density w.r.t. mean is Σ^{-1}(x−μ), so ∇D_KL = Σ^{-1}E_q*[μ_θ − x] with Σ = σ²|Δt|I; product of per-objective tilts collapses into exp(Σλ_m A_m/τ) since normalizers are constant.

2608.26872.relevance_to_opd: Borrows the OPD framing (per-step supervision on student's own trajectory, per-step KL normalization from Flow-OPD/DiffusionOPD) but replaces teacher velocity targets with reward-ranked self-exploration in an image-generation domain; conceptually related to teacher-free/self-distillation and reward-as-teacher variants but not LLM OPD.

2608.26735.title: Preserving General Capabilities During Domain Specialization with Uncertainty-Calibrated MOPD
2608.26735.summary: Token/trajectory filtering for multi-teacher OPD to restore general skills

method.training_loop: for prompt q: sample anchor (T=1) + m explore (T=1.5,top-p .9) rollouts; route to domain/general teacher; keep explore traj if pos-adv density ≥ anchor; Bernoulli-mask tokens by CLL endorsement; reverse-KL MOPD update
method.loss_formulation: L_{MOPD}(\pi_S) = -\mathbb{E}_{q,d,y\sim\mu_S}\left[\frac{1}{T}\sum_{t=1}^{T} \hat{A}_t^{MOPD} \log \pi_S(y_t|q,y_{<t})\right],\; \hat{A}_t^{MOPD}=\mathrm{clip}\left(\log\frac{\pi_{T(d)}(y_t|q,y_{<t})}{\pi_S(y_t|q,y_{<t})},c_{min},c_{max}\right); tokens retained w.p. w_{cll}(A_t,x)=\mathbb{1}[A_t>0]s_{cll}(x)+\mathbb{1}[A_t<0](1-s_{cll}(x)),\; s_{cll}(x)=\exp(\min(\log p_T(x)+H[p_T],0)); trajectories retained iff r(y^e)\ge r(y^a)
method.data_source: Prompt-only mixtures: 10k CoSER role-play prompts + 10k Nemotron Post-Training v1 general prompts (chat/code/math/STEM); medical: 9,926 prompts from MedMCQA, MedReason, Medical-R1-Distill-Data, m23k + same 10k general prompts; responses generated on-policy by student
key_components: Dual-temperature candidate sampling (anchor T=1.0 + exploration T=1.5, top-p 0.9)
Positive-advantage-density trajectory filtering against prompt-specific anchor
Centered log-likelihood (CLL) entropy-calibrated teacher-endorsement score
Direction–endorsement consistency Bernoulli token masking
Prompt-level deterministic routing to domain vs general teacher
Clipped reverse-KL token advantage (MOPD surrogate)

2608.26735.novelty: Unlike vanilla MOPD and Counteraction-Aware MOPD (sample selection for gradient conflict), this work argues the advantage sign alone is an unreliable update direction and introduces a teacher-internal, entropy-centered endorsement score (CLL) to probabilistically gate token updates, plus higher-temperature exploration with anchor-relative positive-density trajectory filtering to expose larger positive teacher–student gaps; it replaces hard top-k or fixed-threshold token selection with a continuous entropy-adaptive rule.

on_policy_mechanism.evidence_quote: is supervised on its own sampled trajectories by domain and general teachers

opd_classification.reasoning: Core contribution is selective token-level masking (CLL keep-probability) and trajectory-level filtering of student-rollout tokens under white-box multi-teacher reverse-KL distillation, i.e., a token-weighting/stability technique within OPD.

training_setup.compute_budget: 4 nodes × 8 NVIDIA H800 GPUs (duration unspecified); 468 outer updates role-playing, 231 medical
stabilization_tricks: frozen domain teacher copy of student init

key_findings: Uncertainty-calibrated MOPD raises the general-capability average over vanilla MOPD by +2.40 points (50.70→53.10) in role-playing and +5.32 points (49.06→54.38) in medical adaptation, i.e., 4.73% and 10.84% relative gains.
In role-playing it also improves the vertical average by +3.78 over vanilla MOPD (41.22→45.00), while in medical it stays near the best recovery baseline (60.65 vs 60.95).
Under a matched rollout budget of 8 responses/prompt, vanilla MOPD reaches 52.23/43.38 (general/vertical) vs ours 53.10/45.00, so gains are not from more sampling alone.
CLL masking alone improves vanilla MOPD from 50.70→51.01 general and 41.22→43.36 role-playing; adding dual-temperature sampling gives 52.83; adding density filtering gives 53.10/45.00.
Positive-density filtering raises the kept-trajectory positive-token fraction from 0.5026 to 0.5939 and mean positive advantage from 0.0705 to 0.1375 versus dropped trajectories.
Continuous entropy-centered CLL beats hard top-k endorsement (k=1: 50.76/41.32; k=3: 50.74/42.31) with 51.01/43.36.
Exploration temperature 1.5 gives the best role-playing average (42.66) among 1.2/1.5/1.8/2.0; higher temperatures are less stable.
2608.26735.ablations_summary: CLL sample masking > vanilla MOPD (+0.31 gen, +2.14 vertical); dual-temperature sampling adds +1.82 gen; positive-density filtering adds +0.27 gen and +1.76 vertical; sample masking beats multiplicative weighting on vertical/GPQA (43.36 vs 42.92; 62.63 vs 59.09); positive-density filtering beats likelihood filtering (51.69 vs 50.45 gen with ≥ rule); rollout-budget control confirms gains are not from 8× sampling alone.
limitations: Theoretical properties are local (filter enrichment and entropy-adaptive consistency), explicitly not a global convergence guarantee for neural policy optimization.
Experiments only cover homogeneous, same-scale Qwen3 teacher–student setups (4B and 8B); no cross-scale or cross-family teachers.
Medical vertical average slightly drops below the best recovery baseline (60.65 vs 60.95) and below SFT (60.96).
failure_modes: Higher exploration temperatures (1.8, 2.0) become less stable overall and can overwhelm the filter with noisy trajectories.
Vanilla MOPD suppresses teacher-endorsed tokens when the student is slightly more confident (negative advantage despite shared top-1), which motivates the method.
Hard top-k endorsement is over-strict on diffuse and over-permissive on concentrated teacher distributions.
CLL weighting (instead of masking) continues applying reduced updates on unreliable tokens and underperforms on GPQA (59.09 vs 62.63).

theory.theoretical_claim: Positive-density filter lower-bounds retained trajectories' mean positive-advantage density by the anchor score; CLL keep-probability equals min(p_T(x)/exp(-H[p_T]),1) for reinforcement and its complement for suppression, giving entropy-adaptive direction–endorsement consistency
theory.proof_sketch: Each retained exploration response satisfies r(y)≥r(y^a) by construction, so the average over the kept set (with or without anchor) is ≥ r(y^a). Rewriting s_cll = exp(min(log p_T + H, 0)) = min(p_T/b_T, 1) with b_T = exp(-H) shows endorsement compares token probability to an entropy-induced typical scale and is non-decreasing in teacher entropy for fixed p_T below that scale.

2608.26735.relevance_to_opd: Directly extends white-box multi-teacher on-policy distillation (MiMo/Nemotron-Cascade/DeepSeek-V4 style MOPD) with novel token-level gating and rollout-selection mechanisms for the domain-specialization/capability-recovery setting; diagnoses a failure mode of sign-based reverse-KL token advantages and provides a teacher-entropy-calibrated fix comparable to selective/entropy-aware OPD variants.

2608.26658.title: PailitaoGR: Latent Think-with-Images for Generative Image Retrieval
2608.26658.summary: On-policy JSD distillation from crop/OCR privileged teachers into full-image generative retriever

method.training_loop: for batch: student (full image) samples SID ŝ~p_θ(·|H^I); Crop/OCR teachers scored on student prefix ŝ_<t; L=CE+λ_opd·JSD(top-100)+ROT attn+entropy+gated selective aux loss
method.loss_formulation: L_item = L_CE + \lambda_{opd} L_{OPD} + \lambda_{rot} L_{rot} + \lambda_{ent} L_{ent},\quad L_{OPD} = \mathbb{E}_{\hat{s}\sim p_\theta(\cdot|H^I)}\left[\frac{1}{|\hat{s}|}\sum_{t} JSD(\tilde{p}^C_t, \tilde{q}^I_t)\right];\; L_t = L_{base} + \lambda_{gate}(w^{help}_t w^{cap}_t L_{open} + (1-w^{help}_t) L_{close})
method.data_source: Pailitao (Taobao) online image-search logs with behavioral SIDs (clicks, purchases, add-to-cart, favorites), 7 product categories
key_components: Target Enhancer (target token scoring + token-level residual modulation)
On-policy distillation from Crop Teacher on student-generated SID prefixes (JSD / forward-KL over teacher top-100)
Granularity-aware ROT attention loss and coarse-to-fine entropy attention loss
Auxiliary Enhancer conditioned on Target Anchor
Selective (in-capacity incremental) contrastive distillation from OCR Teacher gated by teacher utility and student accessibility

2608.26658.novelty: First industrial generative image retriever operating on original uncropped query images; instead of explicit crop/OCR tool calls, it internalizes them via on-policy distillation from privileged-input teachers (Crop Teacher, OCR Teacher) evaluated on the student's own SID rollouts, plus a novel gated transfer that only distills the OCR Teacher's gain over the Crop Teacher when the evidence is both useful (teacher utility) and accessible to the student; student surpasses both teachers.

on_policy_mechanism.evidence_quote: Ateachdecodingstep𝑡,boththeCropTeacherandthestudentare thenqueriedusingthesamestudent-generatedprefixsˆ<𝑡:

opd_classification.reasoning: Student samples its own SID trajectories (C1), separately trained Crop/OCR teachers with privileged inputs (GT crop region, pre-extracted OCR) provide token-level distributions on those prefixes (C2), and the loss is JSD/forward-KL (C3); the teacher is a privileged-information teacher and ablation shows OPD is the largest contributor.

teacher.name: OCR Teacher (Qwen3.5-0.8B, crop + OCR text input)

stabilization_tricks: JSD / forward KL rather than reverse KL
soft sigmoid gates on teacher utility and student accessibility for auxiliary transfer
residual token modulation preserving original visual features
joint CE ground-truth supervision alongside distillation

train: Pailitao online image-search logs (1,159,746 query images, 7 categories)
eval: Pailitao temporally-disjoint test set (8,647 query images, click & purchase behaviors)

key_findings: PailitaoGR outperforms the directly SFT-trained full-image baseline by an average of 13.8% across ten metrics and the second-best existing method by 12.16%.
The full-image student surpasses the Crop Teacher and OCR Teacher by 4.76% and 2.76% on average despite teachers using crop / crop+OCR inputs at train and test time.
Ablation: removing OPD drops CLICK H@10 from 76.51 to 73.05 (largest drop), removing ROT to 73.47, removing entropy to 75.64.
Gains are largest for small search targets: for ROT ratio 0–5%, CLICK H@1 improves +18.52 (18.01→36.53) vs +8.46 for ROT ≥40%.

Adding the utility criterion to indiscriminate auxiliary transfer improves the four metrics by ~2.0 pp on average; accessibility criterion adds further consistent gains (CLICK H@10 77.04→78.71→79.19).
Improvements are larger on queries containing OCR (+13.44 CLICK H@1 over SFT) while remaining competitive on queries without OCR (+12.08).
2608.26658.ablations_summary: Target-focused perception (OPD+ROT+entropy) lifts SFT baseline CLICK H@10 63.24→76.53; adding selective auxiliary utilization →79.19. Within target-focused objectives OPD contributes most, ROT second, entropy least. For auxiliary transfer, utility gating (+~2 pp) and accessibility gating add successive gains over indiscriminate transfer.
limitations: No explicit limitations section; evaluation restricted to a single e-commerce platform (Pailitao) and seven product categories.
Requires ground-truth target bounding boxes and pre-extracted OCR to build teachers during training.
failure_modes: Indiscriminate transfer of OCR-teacher capability underperforms gated transfer (77.04 vs 79.19 CLICK H@10), i.e., forced imitation of irrelevant/inaccessible auxiliary information hurts.
Standard teacher-forced distillation suffers train–inference mismatch on erroneous prefixes, motivating on-policy prefixes.
Gains shrink as the search target occupies a larger fraction of the image (ROT ≥40%: +8.46 vs +18.52 H@1).
2608.26658.relevance_to_opd: A clean applied instance of on-policy distillation with privileged-information teachers: the student generates SID rollouts from the full image, and same-size teachers with cleaner inputs (crop, crop+OCR) supply per-token distributions on those prefixes via JSD/top-K forward KL; adds a selective gating rule (teacher utility × student accessibility) for deciding when to distill, and shows the student can exceed its PI teachers.

2608.27960.title: When Teacher Guidance Misleads: Reward-Aligned On-Policy Distillation
2608.27960.summary: RA-OPD filters student rollouts whose trajectory-level distillation return conflicts with verifier reward

method.training_loop: for iter: sample 1 rollout/prompt from student; teacher scores tokens r_t=logπ_T−logπ_θ; G=mean r_t; R=Verify; mask m=1[(2R−1)G≥0]; minimize masked k1 OPD PG loss
method.loss_formulation: L_{RA-OPD}(\theta) = -\frac{1}{Z}\sum_{i=1}^{B} m_i \sum_{t=1}^{|\tau_i|} sg[r^{OPD}_{i,t}] \log p_{\theta,i,t}(o_{i,t}),\; r^{OPD}_{i,t}=\log\pi_T(o_{i,t}|s_{i,t})-\log\pi_\theta(o_{i,t}|s_{i,t}),\; m_i=1[(2R_i-1)G_i\ge 0],\; Z=\sum_i m_i|\tau_i|
method.data_source: DAPO-Math-17K (math), Eurus-2-RL-Data-Code-25K (code); student on-policy rollouts
key_components: trajectory-level distillation return G (mean token log-ratio)
binary outcome verifier reward R
reward-alignment mask m=1[(2R-1)G>=0]
sampled-token k1 reverse-KL policy-gradient OPD objective
single rollout per prompt, no extra teacher evals

2608.27960.novelty: Unlike Uni-OPD's relative margin consistency across a rollout group (needing multiple rollouts and reward diversity), RA-OPD applies an absolute per-trajectory check comparing the sign of the trajectory-level distillation return with the verified outcome reward, dropping correct-negative and incorrect-positive trajectories at zero additional rollout/teacher cost.

on_policy_mechanism.evidence_quote: ForstandardOPDandRA-OPD,thestudentsamplesoneon-policyresponsepertrainingpromptthroughvLLM,afterwhichtheteacherscoresthesampledtrajectoryandthestudentisupdatedwiththesampled-tokenk1OPDobjective.

opd_classification.reasoning: Core contribution is a trajectory-level masking/weighting of the standard reverse-KL OPD signal using verifier rewards to remove misaligned teacher guidance, i.e. a reliability/weighting technique on top of white-box OPD.

training_setup.compute_budget: unspecified GPUs; ~4.48h total for RA-OPD over plotted interval (vs 4.38h OPD, 14.41h Uni-OPD)
stabilization_tricks: zero gradient when all trajectories filtered

key_findings: RA-OPD reaches 45.88 avg@k on Qwen3-4B-Base (+5.20 over standard OPD, +3.52 over ExOPD) and 49.43 on Qwen3-8B-Base (+5.09 over OPD, +2.48 over ExOPD).
On DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-7B with Skywork-OR1-Math-7B teacher, RA-OPD gets 69.34 avg@k (+4.91 over OPD, +2.79 over Uni-OPD) and 83.48 pass@k.
On code, RA-OPD averages 58.97 avg@4, +3.93 over OPD and +2.87 over ExOPD.
Training time is 4.48h vs 4.38h OPD and 14.41h Uni-OPD (Uni-OPD ≈3.22× RA-OPD).
Reward-misaligned trajectories are prevalent: 48.63% (Qwen3) and 68.23% (DeepSeek) dropped on average; P(G<0) averages 94.25% and 92.46%.
Early in training nearly all correct trajectories are filtered and nearly all incorrect kept; this shifts as the student improves.
Actor entropy is nearly unchanged (0.183 vs 0.177 on Qwen3-8B; 0.424 vs 0.422 on DeepSeek).
2608.27960.ablations_summary: On Qwen3-8B-Base: masking only correct-negative (RA-C) gives 45.31 avg@k, only incorrect-positive (RA-I) 45.83, both (RA-OPD) 49.43 vs OPD 44.34; training only on the two conflict types (RA-Inv) yields 43.41, above base (26.30) but below OPD, indicating misaligned trajectories carry noisy but nonzero signal.
limitations: Requires a verifiable outcome reward (binary verifier), so only applies to verifiable tasks such as math and code
Filters a large fraction (48–68%) of trajectories, discarding potentially useful token-level signal
Evaluated only with sampled-token k1 OPD, on Qwen3 and DeepSeek-R1 families at 4B–8B scale
failure_modes: When Z=0 (all trajectories in a batch filtered) the distillation gradient is zero and no update occurs
Early training filters nearly all correct trajectories because teacher assigns lower probability than student to most trajectories (G<0 ~94%)
2608.27960.relevance_to_opd: Directly an OPD method: standard reverse-KL sampled-token OPD on student rollouts with a verifier-based trajectory-level reliability filter on teacher guidance; addresses the misaligned-teacher-guidance reliability problem in OPD.

2608.27857.title: SpikeOPD: Stable On-Policy Distillation for Autoregressive Spiking Language Models
2608.27857.affiliation_primary: The Chinese University of Hong Kong, Shenzhen / A*STAR
2608.27857.summary: Stable on-policy KD from ANN teacher to spiking LM via reference anchoring + spike reg

method.training_loop: Sample 480-tok FineWeb prompts; active SNN generates K=32 tokens (T=1.0), detach; frozen OPT teacher, active SNN, frozen ref SNN score same prefixes; L=KL(pT||qθ)+0.75·KL(qθ||qref)+0.3·L_spk; update θ only
method.loss_formulation: L_{total} = \frac{1}{K}\sum_t KL(p_T(\cdot|s_t)\|q_\theta(\cdot|s_t)) + \beta_{ref}\frac{1}{K}\sum_t KL(q_\theta(\cdot|s_t)\|q_{ref}(\cdot|s_t)) + \lambda_{spk}\frac{1}{|S_{spk}|}\sum_{l}([r_{min}-r_l]_+^2+[r_l-r_{max}]_+^2+\rho(r_l-r_l^{ref})^2)
method.data_source: FineWeb prompts (480 tokens) with student self-generated 32-token continuations; Stage-1 SpAD KD on FineWeb-Edu 10BT
key_components: full-vocabulary forward-KL teacher correction on self-generated prefixes
matched-prefix policy anchoring KL(q_theta||q_ref) to frozen initial KD checkpoint on same prefixes
layerwise spike-rate regularization on layers {3,6,9,12} with interval and reference-rate penalties
paired-prefix diagnostics for output-policy mismatch and spiking-dynamics drift
matched-seed stress test for rollout-feedback collapse

2608.27857.novelty: First on-policy distillation for autoregressive spiking LMs; identifies prefix-source mismatch manifesting as spiking-dynamics drift and delayed rollout-feedback collapse of vanilla full-KL OPD, and fixes it with a coupled reference-KL anchor on the same self-generated prefixes plus SNN-specific layerwise firing-rate regularization.

on_policy_mechanism.evidence_quote: Figure4:OverviewofSpikeOPD.Onthesamedetachedself-generatedprefixes,teachercorrectiontransferstheANNdistribution,

opd_classification.reasoning: Student SNN generates rollouts each update, frozen OPT ANN teacher provides full-vocab KL on those rollouts (passes C1-C3); core contribution is applying/stabilizing OPD in a new domain (spiking LMs) with a diagnosed collapse failure mode.

key_findings: SpikeOPD improves the eight-task average over KD SNNs by 0.8, 1.7, and 2.9 points at 0.125B, 0.35B, and 1.3B with firing rates (0.17-0.19) and analytical OPs/energy unchanged or slightly lower.
Vanilla full-KL OPD collapses into repetition in all 10 matched seeds (avg onset 168.5 updates; Adj. 39.1%), while SpikeOPD stays non-collapsed in 0/10 runs (Adj. 0.1%, Dist.-4 99.2%).
Small-LR and gradient clipping only delay collapse (onset 527 and 327 updates) rather than preventing it.
Removing matched-prefix reference KL causes the largest ablation drop (35.5% to 31.7%); removing teacher KL or spike regularization also degrades accuracy.
Existing OPD variants (EOPD, Lightning OPD, OPRD) either degenerate (EOPD Adj. 24.77%) or fail to improve accuracy (34.0-34.6% vs KD 34.7%) under the same 0.125B checkpoint and 500-update budget.
Paired-prefix diagnostics show KD teacher-KL Self-Corpus gap grows to ~0.9 while SpikeOPD stays smaller; hidden-state and membrane gaps fall from 0.102/3.46 (KD) to 0.095/2.67.
Rollout length K=32 and layer interval ΔL=3 are intermediate optima; K=128 (34.8%) and ΔL=12 (34.6%) both underperform.
2608.27857.ablations_summary: All three terms needed: w/o reference KL drops avg from 35.5% to 31.7% (largest), w/o teacher OPD term leaves mismatch uncorrected, w/o spike regularization reduces accuracy; rollout length K and spike-layer interval ΔL both show intermediate optima; gains hold across 1k/2k/4k SpAD initializations (+0.6-0.8).
limitations: Operation and energy numbers are analytical estimates under the BiSpikCLM protocol, not hardware latency or power measurements.
Internal-dynamics trajectory diagnostics are reported for the 125M model only and cannot be compared across scales.
Most controlled ablations and sensitivity settings are single-seed runs.
Theoretical results are local (snapshot/semi-gradient objective, logit convexity, finite-horizon bounds) and make no global convergence or stability claims.
Absolute performance still depends on offline checkpoint maturity; SpikeOPD complements rather than replaces offline SpAD.
failure_modes: Teacher-only full-KL OPD (Vanilla OPD) exhibits delayed rollout-feedback collapse into repetitive text in all 10 seeds.
Excessively long rollouts (K=128) accumulate feedback from the evolving policy and reduce accuracy.
Dense spike constraints (ΔL=1) suppress useful adaptation while sparse constraints (ΔL=12) leave internal drift under-controlled.
Removing the matched-prefix reference anchor leads to unstable adaptation and a 3.8-point accuracy loss.

theory.theoretical_claim: Full-vocabulary forward KL is exact per prefix and an unbiased MC estimate of the snapshot objective; per-prefix KL is convex in logits (Hessian diag(q)-qq^T ⪰ 0); spike-regularization gradient and finite-horizon surrogate temporal gradient are bounded
theory.proof_sketch: Exactness follows from explicit full-vocab sums; unbiasedness from linearity of expectation with detached rollouts; PSD curvature from variance identity a^T(diag(q)-qq^T)a = Var_q(a); gradient bounds via triangle inequality and surrogate slope bound, submultiplicativity of Jacobian norms over T_s=4 steps

2608.27857.relevance_to_opd: Directly extends GKD-style on-policy distillation (student rollouts + full forward KL from frozen teacher) to ANN-to-SNN migration, documents a rollout-feedback collapse failure mode of teacher-only OPD, and introduces a reference-policy anchor evaluated on the same self-generated prefixes as a stabilizer, benchmarking against EOPD, Lightning OPD, and OPRD.

2608.29846.title: Influence-Directed Distillation: Solving the Diversity Bottleneck in Sampled-Token On-Policy Distillation
2608.29846.summary: Entropy-influence gated advantage shrinkage fixes pass@k collapse in sampled-token OPD

method.training_loop: for step: student samples rollouts; query teacher log-prob of sampled tokens only; A_y=log q(y)-log p(y); compute I_H(y)=A_y*D_y from student logits; if I_H<0 scale A_y by w_y=|q-p|/(q+p); update with -sg(Ã_y) log p_θ(y|h)
method.loss_formulation: \ell^{IDA-OPD}_y = -\mathrm{sg}(\tilde{A}_y)\log p_\theta(y|h),\quad \tilde{A}_y = A_y \text{ if } I_H(y)\ge 0;\ w_y A_y \text{ if } I_H(y)<0,\quad A_y=\log p_T(y|h)-\log p_\theta(y|h),\ w_y=\frac{|q_y-p_y|}{q_y+p_y},\ I_H(y)=A_y D_y
method.data_source: DeepMath103K filtered to difficulty level 6 (math); code subset filtered from Yang et al. 2026 RLCode data
key_components: First-Order Local Entropy Influence I_H(y)=A_y·D_y (Theorem 1)
sign-of-I_H gate selecting entropy-contracting updates
divergence-adaptive shrinkage weight w_y=|q_y-p_y|/(q_y+p_y)
sampled-token reverse-KL OPD estimator (single teacher log-prob per token)

2608.29846.novelty: Unlike EOPD/AOPD which reintroduce top-K/full teacher distributions via forward KL to restore diversity, IDA-OPD uses only the teacher's sampled-token log-prob plus a student-side first-order entropy proxy to selectively shrink low-discrepancy entropy-contracting updates, and identifies that entropy drain concentrates at low teacher-student discrepancy rather than high-divergence tokens.

on_policy_mechanism.evidence_quote: Let V denote the vocabulary and let h be a decoding prefix visited by a student rollout, with student and teacher next-token distributions

opd_classification.reasoning: Core method is a token-level advantage reweighting/gating scheme for sampled-token reverse-KL OPD aimed at preserving entropy/diversity, backed by a first-order theoretical diagnostic.

stabilization_tricks: sign-preserving advantage shrinkage (never flips teacher correction direction)
I_H gate leaves entropy-expanding updates intact

train: code subset from Yang et al. 2026 RLCode data

key_findings: IDA-OPD improves pass@16 over vanilla OPD by +8.3 (HMMT Feb), +4.6 (AIME24), +4.3 (AIME25) in the 4B setting and +7.2/+4.2/+6.0 in the 8B setting.
IDA-OPD matches or exceeds the teacher's pass@16 on several benchmarks (83.3 vs 80.0 on 4B AIME24; 76.7 vs 73.3 on 8B AIME25).
Cumulative entropy loss peaks at near-zero teacher-student discrepancy (δ≈0), driven by a massive volume of highly aligned tokens, not high-divergence tokens.
The first-order influence I_H(y)=A_y·D_y tightly tracks measured one-step entropy change while advantage A_y alone does not (two-sided fan).
On code, IDA-OPD gains +2.1/+0.9 on MBPP+ and +1.3/+1.0 on LiveCodeBench (pass@1/pass@16) over OPD.
OPD puts ~74% of tokens in the lowest entropy bin (0.0–0.1) vs teacher ~57%; IDA-OPD stays at ~55%.
IDA-OPD matches or exceeds teacher-informed AOPD/EOPD pass@16 while transferring only O(L) scalars instead of O(L_sel·K) top-K distributions.
2608.29846.ablations_summary: Removing the I_H gate (uniform shrinkage) drops pass@1 56.7→53.8 on AIME24; hard-masking contracting updates preserves pass@16 (82.0) but inflicts largest pass@1 drop (52.1); replacing I_H gate with sign(A_y) gate protects diversity worst (pass@16 76.8/65.2); linear shrinkage c_y=w_y beats constant, sqrt, and square mappings on all columns.
limitations: Theorem 1 assumes idealized logit-space single-step updates; real training uses shared weights and AdamW (validated only empirically)
Evaluated only on same-family, same-size Qwen3 teacher→student pairs where teacher is an RL-trained variant of the student
failure_modes: Hard masking of all entropy-contracting updates over-protects entropy and sacrifices pass@1
Convex (square) shrinkage over-suppresses moderate-divergence corrections, giving lowest pass@1
Constant shrinkage leaves low-divergence entropy drain uncurbed while weakening high-divergence corrections

theory.theoretical_claim: Theorem 1: under a local logit-space gradient step on the sampled-token OPD loss, ΔH = η·A_y·D_y + O(η²), where D_y depends only on the student distribution; Proposition 1: w_y A_y = O(A_y²) as A_y→0 and w_y A_y → A_y as |A_y|→∞
theory.proof_sketch: A single sampled-token OPD update perturbs logits along Δz_k = ηA_y(I[k=y]-p_k); propagating through the softmax Jacobian gives Δp_i with A_y factoring out; expanding ΔH = -Σ log p_i Δp_i to first order yields ηA_y D_y.

2608.29846.relevance_to_opd: Directly addresses diversity/entropy collapse in sampled-token (single-sample reverse-KL) on-policy distillation with a token-level adaptive advantage reweighting that needs no full-vocabulary teacher logits; competes with EOPD, AOPD, REOPOLD, TIP.

2608.31046.title: Does On-Policy Distillation Really Distill? From Noisy Teacher to Self-Improvement
2608.31046.summary: Shows OPD gains come from suppressing low-logp tokens; proposes teacher-free OPSA

method.training_loop: for each step: student samples 1 rollout/prompt (batch 64); select lowest-20%-logp tokens; assign entropy-scaled negative advantage A_i=-1/2-(H_i-H_min)/(2(H_max-H_min)); policy-gradient update; no teacher/reward
method.loss_formulation: L_{OPSA} = -E[ \frac{1}{|S_{lowest20}|} \sum_{i \in S_{lowest20}} A_i^{dyn} \log \pi_\theta(y_i|x;y_{<i}) ], \quad A_i^{dyn} = -\frac{1}{2} - \frac{H_i - H_{min}}{2(H_{max}-H_{min})}
method.data_source: DAPO-17k questions only (no labels); Open-R1 Codeforces for code experiments
key_components: OPD noise analysis (advantage sign vs verifiable reward)
low-logp token selection (bottom 20%)
fixed vs entropy-adaptive negative advantages
supervision-free token-level policy gradient (OPSA)
multi-domain OPSA (MD-OPSA)

2608.31046.novelty: First quantitative demonstration that OPD teacher advantages are ~30-50% noisy yet students are insensitive; shows fixed negative advantage on low-logp tokens matches OPD, motivating a fully teacher-, reward-, and hint-free on-policy method (OPSA) that outperforms OPD, OPSD, GRPO and TTRL.

on_policy_mechanism.evidence_quote: On-Policy Distillation (OPD) (Agarwal et al., 2024; Gu et al., 2024) addresses this limitation by using a strong teacher to provide token-level advantages through reverse Kullback-Leibler (KL) optimization on student-sampled trajectories

opd_classification.reasoning: The paper is an empirical dissection of OPD's mechanism (noisy teacher supervision, which tokens/signals matter) and its proposed OPSA removes the teacher entirely (fails C2), so it is an analysis-of-OPD paper rather than a new OPD method.

training_setup.compute_budget: 8×H100 (or H200) GPUs; ~500 training steps at 46.3 s/step for Qwen3-1.7B
training_setup.rl_algorithm: token-level policy gradient with self-assigned negative advantages (slime framework; no GRPO/PPO/teacher)
stabilization_tricks: restrict updates to lowest-20% logp tokens
negative-only advantages (positive fixed advantage caused collapse)
entropy-adaptive advantage magnitude normalized per rollout

key_findings: OPD teacher advantages on \boxed{} answer tokens disagree with verifiable rewards 30.6% (4B), 34.7% (30B-A3B) and 50.6% (235B-A22B) of the time; the 235B teacher assigns negative advantages to 97.8% of correct answers.
Training OPD only on noisy trajectories, only on clean trajectories, or on all trajectories converges to comparable AIME24 Avg@4.

29.2% of OPD token advantages are exactly zero and 51.7% have |A|<1e-4, concentrated on high-logp student tokens; training only on top-20/40% logp tokens (even with random advantages) yields no improvement.
Restricting OPD to the lowest-20% logp tokens matches full OPD; replacing all advantages with a fixed -0.5 matches OPD, while fixed +0.2 collapses within 40 steps.
Entropy-adaptive negative advantages (δ=1) reach 50.0% Avg@4 on AIME24 vs 35.13% for standard OPD.
OPSA on Qwen3-1.7B: AIME24 Avg@32 13.44→48.85 (+263%), beating GRPO (33.96), OPD (32.08), OPSD (33.33), TTRL (19.90); average Avg@32 beats best baseline by 11.04 points.
OPSA trains at 46.3 s/step vs 61.2 s for OPD and 186.2 s for GRPO on Qwen3-1.7B.
MD-OPSA (mixed math+code data) matches or exceeds single-domain OPSA without domain-specific teachers.
2608.31046.ablations_summary: Token fraction: bottom 10% over-sharpens and underperforms; 20/30/40% all exceed 45 Avg@4. Sign of entropy correlation: δ=1 best, δ=-1 unstable and slightly worse than δ=0. Masking reflective fork tokens eliminates length/accuracy gains. Token-budget-matched inference ('wait' appending) does not close the gap for GRPO/OPD. Inference-time temperature/min-p tuning cannot reproduce OPSA gains.
limitations: Experiments limited to models ≤9B; scaling to larger or MoE models unclear
OPSA redistributes existing probability mass, so gains may be limited for heavily post-trained, very low-entropy models
Modest improvements in thinking-mode Pass@k suggest it may not expand the exploration frontier
Mechanism of OPD with K1 estimator requires further theoretical analysis
failure_modes: Fixed positive advantages cause policy collapse (response length→0, gradient norm explodes)
Training only on bottom-10% logp tokens over-sharpens and causes entropy collapse
Negative correlation of advantage magnitude with entropy (δ=-1) becomes unstable at steps 350-450
Masking fork tokens causes response length collapse at ~300 steps
Large teachers (235B-A22B) give near-uniformly negative, correctness-insensitive advantages on student rollouts

compute_efficiency.teacher_inference_cost: none for OPSA (teacher-free); 1× teacher forward per step in OPD analysis
compute_efficiency.speedup_vs_baseline: 1.3× vs OPD (46.3 vs 61.2 s/step), 4.0× vs GRPO (186.2 s/step)

theory.theoretical_claim: Logit-level gradient analysis of the OPD loss: gradient vanishes when |A_t| is small or when the sampled-token probability approaches one, explaining why high-logp tokens contribute nothing
theory.proof_sketch: ∂L/∂z_v ∝ A_t(1-π_s(v)) for the sampled token and -A_t π_s(v) for unsampled tokens, so both regimes yield negligible updates

2608.31046.relevance_to_opd: Directly interrogates whether OPD (reverse-KL K1 advantages on student rollouts) actually transfers teacher knowledge; shows teacher supervision is noisy and largely replaceable by teacher-free negative advantages on low-logp tokens, challenging the core OPD mechanism and offering OPSA as a supervision-free alternative.

2609.02817.title: Cliff: Learning Process Rewards from the First Mistake
2609.02817.summary: GRPO reward shaping: LLM teacher finds first mistake, splits advantage

method.training_loop: sample N student rollouts per query → verifier reward → teacher solves & judges each rollout, locates Pitfall Step p(a) → prefix/suffix token advantages → GRPO update
method.loss_formulation: A_{i,j} = A_cor - b if R=1; \lambda A_cor - b if R=0, j<p(a_i); A_inc - b if R=0, j\ge p(a_i); plugged into GRPO clipped objective (\beta=0)
method.data_source: DAPO-math-17k-processed (math), DeepCoder (coding); SFT warmup on OpenThoughts
key_components: Pitfall Step identification by LLM teacher judge
teacher reference solution verified by automatic verifier (fallback to GRPO if wrong)
token-level advantage split into correct prefix / incorrect suffix
zero-mean recentering offset b
λ=0 to avoid length hacking
p(a)=0 hard cap for overlength rollouts

2609.02817.novelty: Instead of PRMs or OPD logit matching, uses an off-the-shelf LLM judge to split each incorrect rollout at its first mistake and assign separate GRPO advantages to prefix and suffix; model-agnostic and tokenizer-agnostic, with theoretical analysis of length hacking.

on_policy_mechanism.evidence_quote: Specifically, we utilize a teacher model to judge student rollouts and locate the first mistake in the student’s reasoning.

opd_classification.reasoning: Student generates rollouts (C1) but teacher provides only a textual judgment converted to token-level advantages (reward signal, not logits) and the loss is a GRPO policy-gradient objective, failing C2 and C3; OPD appears only as a baseline.

training_setup.compute_budget: 4×H100 80GB or B200 192GB GPUs, 200 training steps (hours unspecified)
stabilization_tricks: skip teacher judging for zero-variance groups
fallback to GRPO when teacher reference solution fails verifier

key_findings: Cliff outperforms on-policy distillation by ~15% and vanilla GRPO by ~7% averaged across 12 scenarios (2 students × 3 teachers × 2 domains).
On Qwen3-4B math, Cliff with SOTA teacher reaches 65.66 avg vs 61.68 for GRPO and 58.17 for OPD (Qwen3-32B teacher).
OPD baseline underperforms GRPO in most settings (e.g., Phi-4-mini + Gemma OPD math avg 44.40 vs GRPO 49.88).
'GRPO with Teacher' (teacher only judges correctness) yields marginal gains (62.37 vs 61.68), so gain comes from prefix/suffix credit assignment not merely using an LLM judge.
Teacher judges reach >90% judgment accuracy and ~3-sentence average pitfall distance from humans when given a verified reference solution.
Removing the ground-truth filter costs ~2% for Qwen3-32B/Gemma3-27B teachers but almost nothing for the SOTA teacher (64.90 vs 65.66).
λ=1.0 causes length hacking (avg len 1959 vs 1506) and worse accuracy (63.98 vs 65.66); λ=0 is best.
2609.02817.ablations_summary: GRPO-with-teacher ablation shows the credit assignment (not the teacher judge alone) drives gains; λ ablation shows λ=0 best and λ=1.0 induces length hacking; removing GT filter hurts weaker teachers by ~2%; judge quality ablation shows incorrect reference solutions degrade judgment accuracy (e.g., Qwen3-32B 91→60).
limitations: Teacher pitfall-step localization does not always match humans (inherent ambiguity in locating first mistake)
Requires an LLM teacher capable of identifying the first mistake; weaker teachers need ground-truth verification of reference solutions
Single-turn coding only due to resource limitations
Binary rewards assumed; non-binary rewards require thresholding
failure_modes: Weaker teachers (Qwen3-32B, Gemma3-27B) degrade ~2% when reference solutions are not verified against ground truth
Large λ (e.g., 1.0) induces length hacking with longer but meaningless rollouts
Without hard cap p(a)=0 for overlength rollouts, teacher may reward unfinished but not-yet-wrong long prefixes
Teacher may misidentify pitfall step (Case 3: flags a correct but insufficient claim)

compute_efficiency.teacher_inference_cost: 1× (teacher solves each query once and judges each student rollout; skipped for zero-variance groups)

theory.theoretical_claim: Length-mass analysis: GRPO lengthens iff correct rollouts are longer than incorrect ones; Cliff lengthening condition ρ > 1 - s̄(1+λ(1-µ)/µ); λ=0 eliminates length hacking, λ < L_cor/L_max sufficient for correct rollouts to outrank incorrect ones
theory.proof_sketch: Define length mass Φ as sum of (non-EOS minus EOS) token advantages; using zero-mean recentering, Φ=2Nb for Cliff; expand b via Eq. 5 to derive sign condition in terms of ρ, µ, s̄, λ; show larger λ increases lengthening pressure and derive conditions C1/C2 excluding hacking.

2609.02817.relevance_to_opd: Directly positions itself as an alternative to OPD for fine-grained supervision in RLVR, claiming OPD requires same-family tokenizers/reasoning patterns; uses OPD (k1 estimator and cross-tokenizer OPD) as a baseline and reports Cliff beats it by ~15%, making it a useful comparison point on OPD failure modes but not itself an OPD method.

2609.02401.title: CA-OPD: Confidence-Aware On-Policy Distillation for Structured Visual Prediction
2609.02401.summary: Confidence-gated interleaved OPD with intervention-aligned CE/KL supervision

method.training_loop: Per token: student samples ŷ_t; if teacher NLL(ŷ_t)>τ_s replace with teacher argmax + CE loss, else keep + top-k forward-KL; cosine-relax τ_s over training
method.loss_formulation: L_{CA-OPD} = \frac{1}{\sum_t m_t}\sum_{t=1}^{L} m_t\big[\lambda_{CE} r_t(-\log\pi_S(y_t|s_t;\theta)) + \lambda_{KL}(1-r_t)\sum_{v\in V^{(k)}_{T,t}}\pi_T(v|s_t)(\log\pi_T(v|s_t)-\log\pi_S(v|s_t;\theta))\big],\; r_t=\mathbb{I}[-\log\pi_T(\hat y_t|s_t)>\tau_{nll,s}]
method.data_source: 15,100 distillation examples (11,184 GUI grounding + 3,916 OCR); SFT init on 40K OCR + 6K RefCOCO examples
key_components: teacher-NLL confidence gate on student proposals
teacher argmax write-back into mixed prefix (discrete, no gradient)
intervention-aligned supervision: CE at replaced positions, top-k forward KL at retained positions
cosine strict-to-relaxed threshold schedule (α 0.50→0.25 after 0.1 hold)
multi-teacher domain routing (grounding vs OCR teacher)
chunked 32-token rollouts with restart from first replaced position

2609.02401.novelty: Versus SKD, replaces rank-based acceptance with exact teacher probability (NLL threshold), anneals the threshold strict-to-relaxed to progressively hand rollout control to the student, and uses the same intervention decision to select the per-token loss (CE at teacher-corrected tokens, distributional KL at retained tokens), unifying state visitation and supervision.

on_policy_mechanism.evidence_quote: the teacher evaluates the student’s proposed token. Highly supported proposals are retained and

opd_classification.reasoning: Core contribution is a curriculum over rollout construction (confidence-gated teacher intervention with annealed strict-to-relaxed schedule) with an adaptive per-token CE/KL objective, applied to multimodal GUI/OCR distillation.

training_setup.compute_budget: 8×A800 (4 student GPUs FSDP + 4 teacher replicas), 471 optimizer steps at ~59.3 s/step
stabilization_tricks: top-k (k=64) truncated forward KL clamped at zero
cosine-annealed NLL threshold with 0.1 warm-up hold

key_findings: CA-OPD (annealed α 0.50→0.25) beats standard OPD on all six target benchmarks, e.g. ScreenSpot-Pro 40.82→45.92 (+5.10) and CC-OCR 63.93→67.32 (+3.39).
Relative to the raw Qwen3.5-0.8B baseline, gains are +9.08 (SS-v2), +9.50 (SS-Pro), +6.72 (OCRv2-EN), +9.77 (OCRv2-ZH).
CA-OPD outperforms OfflineKD and SKD on every target benchmark while keeping RefCOCO/MMBench retention within 0.43 points of all baselines.
Random intervention at a comparable write-back rate (3.87%) gives 40.20 SS-Pro vs 45.92 for confidence gating (5.40%), and confidence gating without prefix write-back gives only 40.92.
Increasing SKD replacement rate from 0.16% to 3.41% raises SS-Pro to 44.00, still 1.92 below CA-OPD; CA-OPD performance is non-monotonic in replacement rate.
Reversed schedule (44.36), fixed threshold (44.58), sampled write-back (43.61) and KL at replaced positions (45.26) all underperform the full method (45.92) on SS-Pro.
CA-OPD-triggered proposals have median teacher rank 3 with 100% (grounding) / 88% (OCR) inside teacher top-25, so rank-based gating would retain them.
Annealed gating reduces cross-run std vs OPD on SS-Pro/CC-OCR/OmniDoc from 1.46/0.96/1.13 to 0.72/0.51/0.33.
On SS-Pro examples already solved by SFT-init, OPD drops 96.03→90.18 while CA-OPD retains 93.83.
Gains transfer to Qwen3-VL-8B→2B without task SFT (SS-Pro 46.40 OPD → 48.36 CA-OPD).
2609.02401.ablations_summary: Both selective (confidence-based) placement and actual prefix write-back are required; random placement or gating without write-back ≈ OPD. Annealed strict-to-relaxed cosine schedule > fixed > reversed; argmax correction > sampled; CE at replaced positions > KL at replaced positions. Intervention budget alone does not explain gains.
limitations: Assumes teacher probabilities are sufficiently calibrated to identify unreliable student transitions; domain shift may require retuning the confidence floor.
Validated only with shared teacher–student tokenizers; mismatched tokenizers and open-ended generation untested.
Mixed-prefix rollout queries the teacher at every visited state, costing ~1.5× the wall-clock of ungated OPD.
Gating reduces but does not eliminate erosion of mastered behavior (93.83 vs SFT-init 96.03 on all-correct SS-Pro examples).
failure_modes: Random teacher intervention placement at matched budget yields no gain over OPD (40.20 vs 40.82 SS-Pro).
Reversed (relaxed-to-strict) schedule degrades performance (44.36 SS-Pro).
Sampled rather than argmax teacher write-back degrades performance (43.61 SS-Pro).
