Ungated OPD is unstable across runs and degrades already-mastered examples.
OmniDocBench shows essentially no gain over SFT-init (70.43 vs 70.49).
2609.02401.relevance_to_opd: Directly extends interleaved on-policy distillation (GKD/SKD lineage): student generates rollouts, teacher logits gate and correct unreliable tokens, and per-token supervision switches between CE and top-k forward KL; demonstrates OPD for structured VLM outputs (GUI coordinates, OCR text) with multi-teacher routing.

2609.04172.title: Rethinking On-Policy Distillation of Large Language Models II: One Training Example
2609.04172.summary: One-shot OPD: a single query recovers most of full-data OPD gain; OPD is data-overfed, algorithm-starved

method.training_loop: for step t: sample 64 rollouts from student on 1 (or n) fixed query; teacher scores every visited prefix; per-token advantage log π_T − log π_θ (or student top-k); AdamW update
method.loss_formulation: L_{OPD}(\theta) = \mathbb{E}_{x\sim D, y\sim\pi_\theta}\left[\sum_{i=1}^{L} KL(\pi_\theta(\cdot|s_i) \| \pi_T(\cdot|s_i))\right], \; A_i = \log\pi_T(y_i|s_i) - \log\pi_\theta(y_i|s_i)
method.data_source: single query (or 4/16-shot semantic-cluster representatives) drawn from DAPO-Math-17K, Open-R1 Codeforces, UltraData-SFT-2605 subset, xLAM-function-calling-60K; also content-light templates and WildChat
key_components: one-shot on-policy distillation
state coverage metric (teacher-hidden-state K-means clusters)
absorption rate / teacher-student distance metrics
semantic-cluster query selection (BGE-M3)
multi-teacher OPD (MOPD) with 16 queries per domain
content-light template and off-domain WildChat inputs

2609.04172.novelty: First study of the role of training data in OPD (prior work is algorithm-side only): shows a single query suffices for hundreds of steps of improvement, introduces state coverage and absorption rate as diagnostics, and shows 16 semantically diverse queries match full-data OPD and MOPD, while content-free templates and off-domain WildChat prompts nearly match real queries.

on_policy_mechanism.evidence_quote: On-policy distillation (OPD) samples trajectories from the student and aligns the student to the

opd_classification.reasoning: Analysis paper on standard white-box OPD (student rollouts + per-token teacher KL) that dissects data efficiency and alignment dynamics rather than proposing a new objective.

stabilization_tricks: student top-k (k=16) advantage estimator for math runs

benchmarks.name: Math average, one-shot OPD step 1000 (vs full-data 72.1)

key_findings: One-shot OPD on math reaches 68.5 vs 69.8 for full-data OPD at step 300, recovering 69% of the teacher–student gap and 87% of full-data OPD's gain; at step 1000 it recovers 72%.
The one-shot effect holds across R1-Distill-1.5B, Llama-3B-It, OLMo-7B-It-DPO (77.1→85.5, 28.2→40.2, 70.8→82.4) and across code (73%), IF (66%), and agentic tool use (64% gap recovery).
A single query's rollouts cover 71.5% of the state clusters full-data OPD visits (65.9% within 100 steps); 16 semantically diverse queries reach 98.9% and match full-data validation accuracy.

The absorption rate (fraction of teacher–student distance closed per update) falls similarly for 1, 4, 16, and 17k queries (78–84% of step-30 distance removed by step 300), so slow alignment is a property of OPD not the data.
16 diverse queries per domain match full-data MOPD (52.9 vs 52.8, 101% of full-data gain).
Content-light templates and off-domain WildChat queries approach the real-query baseline (59.1→69.8) using a third to a half of the rollout tokens.
One-shot OPD's validation gain over 1000 steps is more than twice that of one-shot RLVR on the same query.
2609.04172.ablations_summary: Off-policy fixed-trajectory ablation shows accuracy rises monotonically with distinct trajectories (1→64) and a fixed state set still trains for ~200 steps; 16 queries from 16 clusters beat 16 from one cluster (70.9 vs 69.9, coverage 98.9% vs 76.8%); query scheduling order barely matters; learning rate rescales the step axis without changing the slowdown shape; gain is insensitive to query difficulty, response-length cap, and temperature; coverage ordering is stable across K, reference set, and state positions.
limitations: State coverage is a semantic-level proxy measured against a reference space built from full-data rollouts and weights every cluster equally regardless of visit frequency or remaining teacher signal.
What sets the absorption rate remains open.
MOPD experiments use only three domains with one teacher each; extension to more teachers/domains, larger students, agentic tool use, and long contexts is untested.
failure_modes: A scaffold that closes the think block immediately (<think>\n</think>\n) collapses into short meta-level replies that cannot be trained on.
WildChat off-domain queries cost about one point in mathematics relative to real queries.
Absorption rate keeps falling, so hundreds of steps are needed even on a fixed state set.
2609.04172.relevance_to_opd: Directly analyzes standard OPD (GKD-style per-token KL on student rollouts) from the data side, showing data is over-supplied and the optimizer's absorption rate is the bottleneck; provides state-coverage diagnostics and guidance for query selection and step-efficient OPD.

2609.04108.title: Sequential Beats Joint: On the Interplay between On-Policy Distillation and RLVR
2609.04108.summary: Two-stage OPD-then-RL beats pure OPD, RLVR, and all joint OPD+RL fusions

method.training_loop: Stage 1 (steps ≤ S=60): sample student rollouts, per-token reverse-KL advantage d_t = log π_T − log π_θ from frozen teacher, PPO-clip update; Stage 2: switch to pure GRPO with verifiable reward.
method.loss_formulation: L_{OPD}(\theta)=KL(\pi_\theta\|\pi_T)=\mathbb{E}_{y\sim\pi_\theta}[\log\frac{\pi_\theta(y|x)}{\pi_T(y|x)}]=-\mathbb{E}\sum_t d_t^{(i)},\; d_t^{(i)}=\log\pi_T(y_t|h_t)-\log\pi_\theta(y_t|h_t);\; A_t^{alg}=d_t^{(i)} \text{ if step}\le S,\; \hat A^{(i)} \text{ (GRPO) otherwise}
method.data_source: Reasoning Gym procedural generators (K&K, Zebra, Countdown; 20K instances each) and DeepMath-103K
key_components: unified token-level policy-gradient view of OPD-RLVR hybrids
hard switch from OPD (reverse-KL) to GRPO at step S
frozen external teacher Qwen3-8B
EOS-position masking of teacher signal
switch-point selection by OPD validation score

2609.04108.novelty: Rather than a new fusion rule, shows that sequentially applying OPD then RLVR outperforms all weighted-additive and teacher-modulated joint methods, and explains it via pass@k expansion/sharpening, teacher-ceiling dynamics, KL decomposition, and parameter sign-conflict analysis; also shows OPD is a better cold start than SFT.

on_policy_mechanism.evidence_quote: by supervising the student on its own rollouts with token-level teacher signals which has been widely adopted in recent industry post-training pipelines

opd_classification.reasoning: Core contribution is how to combine on-policy reverse-KL distillation with RLVR (sequential vs joint), with student rollouts, teacher token-level log-prob supervision, and KL loss all central; plus mechanistic analysis and a practical switching recipe.

stabilization_tricks: EOS-position masking of teacher signal due to tokenizer EOS mismatch

key_findings: OPD-then-RL reaches 80.6 avg pass@1 on logic reasoning vs 53.9 (OPD), 49.4 (GRPO), leading joint combination methods by 11.7–26.7 points.
On math, OPD-then-RL attains 31.8 avg pass@1 (vs 31.0 OPD, 28.4 GRPO), significantly ahead of 6 of 9 competing methods and tied with the 3 strongest.
OPD lifts the whole pass@k curve (largest gain at large k) while RL narrows the pass@128−pass@1 gap; OPD-then-RL dominates all baselines across k.
Pure OPD and all joint methods plateau below the teacher's 56.6 pass@1 on K&K, while OPD-then-RL averages 20+ points above the teacher.
During the RL stage KL(p_S‖p_T) rises only because student entropy falls faster than cross-entropy; shared top-K mass with the teacher keeps increasing, so sharpening stays within teacher support.
Sign-conflict rate with OPD updates is 3.38%/3.89% (K&K/Countdown) for OPD-then-RL vs 20.36%/17.00% for pure RL and 15.02%/13.71% for KDRL.
Replacing KDRL's sign-conflicting parameters with OPD values monotonically raises pass@k while lowering pass@1; random replacement does not.
OPD validation score at the switch point largely determines post-RL accuracy; step 60 adopted as default.
OPD cold start beats SFT cold start by 4.9 pass@1 (30.3 vs 25.4) before RL, and after GRPO gains +7.2 avg pass@32 (51.3→58.5) while SFT-then-RL degrades pass@32.
With Qwen3-0.6B-Base, OPD-then-RL reaches 70.4 avg logic pass@1 vs 45.0 (GRPO) and 48.9 (OPD); ordering reproduces with OLMo-3.1-32B→OLMo-3-7B.
2609.04108.ablations_summary: Switch-point ablation (step 20/60/100) shows later switch helps when OPD still improving, converges when OPD saturated; KDRL β ablation (1/0.2/0.02/0.002) shows weighted-additive methods highly β-sensitive; KDRL-annealing (soft switch) underperforms hard switch (68.9 vs 80.6 logic pass@1); OPD vs SFT cold start favors OPD; sign-conflict parameter replacement identifies pass@1/pass@k trade-off subspace.
limitations: Only external stronger frozen teacher studied; task-specific, multi-teacher, and on-policy self-distillation settings left to future work
Frozen off-the-shelf teacher; teacher-first RLVR-then-distill allocation not compared under equal compute
Only reverse-KL OPD objective used; forward KL, JSD, full-distribution variants unexplored
failure_modes: Joint OPD+RL methods interfere and lag pure OPD pass@1 on math where the teacher is strong
Weighted-additive methods erode pass@32 (avg −2.0 on logic) and are highly sensitive to β
Pure OPD and joint methods are ceilinged by teacher performance
Switching to RL before OPD saturates caps achievable accuracy
2609.04108.relevance_to_opd: Directly studies how OPD (reverse-KL on student rollouts from Qwen3-8B) should be combined with RLVR, unifying KDRL/SRPO/HDPO/TRRD/RLSD under a token-level advantage view and showing sequential OPD-then-RL dominates; provides mechanistic evidence that OPD expands coverage and RL sharpens within teacher support.

2609.03699.title: Predictive Zonotope Reduction: Precise Runtime Monitoring under Uncertainty
2609.03699.affiliation_primary: CISPA Helmholtz Center for Information Security
2609.03699.summary: MPC-based zonotope reducer selection distilled into neural ranking policy for runtime monitors

method.training_loop: Run MPC-F (beam search over reducer sequences) on 128 sampled traces as teacher; train 2x32 MLP ranking policy on teacher rankings; DAgger-augment 3 policies into ensemble + MPC guard
method.loss_formulation: L(Z,\hat{Z}) = \sum_{i=1}^{d} (\sum_j |g_{j,i}| - \sum_j |\hat{g}_{j,i}|)^2 (Squared Hull Error, MPC cost); student trained with pairwise ranking loss
method.data_source: 128 randomly sampled MuJoCo 5-DoF robot arm traces with ISO 5725 sensor noise, labeled by MPC-F teacher; 6 extra DAgger traces per ensemble member
key_components: Predictive Zonotope Reduction as optimal control problem
beam-search MPC (H=5, W=4) with causal input prediction
pairwise ranking-loss policy distillation
DAgger-augmented 3-policy ensemble (Vote3)
short-horizon MPC guard for non-unanimous votes (Vote3-Guarded)
RLola implementation on Raspberry Pi 5

2609.03699.novelty: Treats zonotope order-reduction method selection as a sequential control problem (vs. fixed reducer throughout the run) and distills the MPC selector into a fast neural ranking policy for embedded real-time monitors

on_policy_mechanism.evidence_quote: To improve robustness to covariate shifts, we combine multiple neural policies with DAgger [10] augmentations into an ensemble.

opd_classification.reasoning: Non-LLM domain: distills an MPC controller into a small MLP that outputs discrete reducer selections for robotics runtime monitoring (no text output, no logit-level distributional KL from an LM teacher).

training_setup.compute_budget: Raspberry Pi 5 (16GB) evaluation; 1,400 monitoring runs; training compute unspecified
stabilization_tricks: pairwise ranking loss instead of classification

train: 128 randomly sampled 5-DoF MuJoCo robot arm traces labeled by MPC-F
6 additional DAgger-sampled traces per ensemble policy
eval: 20 held-out random-waypoint MuJoCo robot arm traces at 10Hz with geofence spec, bounds b in {40,80,120,150,200,250,500}

benchmarks.name: Median Squared Hull Error L at b=150, G15

key_findings: At b=150 the best fixed reducer (Combastel) has FPR 29.68% versus 1.76%–5.08% for dynamic PZR selectors.
MPC-Greedy (H=1) alone reduces median loss from 6.4e-4 to 2.6e-7 and FPR from 29.68% to 1.96%; MPC-L (H=5) reaches 1.6e-7 loss and 1.78% FPR, beating Greedy in 107 of 140 cells.
Dynamic controllers select Scott ~85% of the time despite its poor standalone performance (FPR 39.70%), relying on Girard/PCA to condition matrices.
Distilled G15 policy retains MPC-scale loss (1.9e-7) with much lower latency; Fig. 6 indicates roughly 34–39× latency reduction versus control policies on Raspberry Pi 5.
Over 69,120 selections, 94.02% of ensemble votes were unanimous; the guard activated on 5.98% and changed the method in 2.65%.
False-negative rate is 0 across all methods over ~700,000 monitored events (soundness by construction).
2609.03699.ablations_summary: MPC-Greedy vs MPC-L shows value of horizon; single G15 (FPR 5.08%) vs Vote3 (1.92%) vs Vote3-Guarded (1.79%) shows ensemble and MPC guard mitigate covariate-shift failures; fixed reducers vs dynamic selection shows switching is the main gain.
limitations: Policies only select among existing reducers and performance is tied to theirs
Computational cost; balance among horizon, beam width, and bounds is problem/deployment-dependent
Loss computed against predicted ground truth from unreduced rollouts, not true physical state
Learned policies on resource-constrained hardware are prone to covariate shift
failure_modes: Simple distillation occasionally fails under covariate shift due to information asymmetry (student sees only 15 zonotope features)
Scott's method fails when the zonotope matrix is non-invertible during long executions
Ensemble and guard mitigate but do not fully resolve occasional learned-policy failures
2609.03699.relevance_to_opd: Uses DAgger-style policy distillation from an MPC teacher into a small MLP, but in a robotics runtime-monitoring domain with discrete action outputs and a ranking loss; not LLM on-policy distillation.

2609.05295.title: RISE: Recursive Improvement via Self-Extrapolating Policy Distillation
2609.05295.summary: Extrapolate RLVR trajectory to build self-teacher for on-policy distillation

method.training_loop: Per iter: GRPO rollouts+update θn→θ'n+1; build teacher π_future by extrapolating (θ'n+1−anchor) in weight or logit space with β>1; distill π_future into student via top-K JSD on same rollouts; update EMA anchor; decay β→1
method.loss_formulation: L_{RISE} = E_{y\sim\pi_\theta}[\sum_t D(\pi_\theta(\cdot|s_t) \| sg[\pi_{future}(\cdot|s_t)])], \; \log\pi_{future} = \log\pi_{\theta_n} + \beta(\log\pi_{\theta'_{n+1}} - \log\pi_{\theta_n}) \text{ (logit) or } \theta_{future}=\theta_n+\beta(\theta'_{n+1}-\theta_n) \text{ (weight); D=JSD over top-K+tail}
method.data_source: DAPO Math, OpenR1-Math-46K, Guru STEM mix, Skywork-OR1-Code, ALFWorld, WebShop (prompts with verifiable rewards; rollouts self-generated)
key_components: RLVR (GRPO) phase grounding the update direction
Self-extrapolated teacher (task-arithmetic weight-space or geometric-mixture logit-space, β>1)
OPD phase with top-K JSD on reused student rollouts
Linear β decay schedule (β0=1.2→1)
EMA anchor checkpoint (η=0.1 Qwen, η=1 OLMo)
Stop-gradient teacher refreshed every iteration

2609.05295.novelty: Unlike external-teacher OPD or privileged-conditioned self-distillation (SDPO, OPSD, RLSD, SDAR), the teacher is synthesized from the model's own RLVR training trajectory by extrapolating checkpoint displacement (β>1), requiring no external model or privileged context; teacher is non-stationary and refreshed each iteration, removing ExOPD's static-teacher ceiling.

on_policy_mechanism.evidence_quote: Bothphasesoperateonthesamesetofrollouts—theresponsesy ∼π sampledforRLVRarereusedforOPD,

opd_classification.reasoning: Pure self-distillation with no external model or privileged info—teacher is an extrapolated future self built from the student's own checkpoints—combined with RLVR grounding and a theoretical suboptimality decomposition.

training_setup.compute_budget: single node × 8 GPUs (VeRL), 1 epoch; 1.3–1.6× GRPO wall time
stabilization_tricks: JSD instead of reverse KL (bounded by log2)
top-K (K=100; K=20 code) truncation with renormalized tail bucket
OPD as trust-region projection instead of adopting θ_future directly
token-level IS clip 2.0, no std-normalization in GRPO

key_findings: RISE beats GRPO and all privileged-teacher OPSD baselines on in-domain Math Avg across all settings: +2.7 (Qwen3-8B), +4.8 (Qwen3-1.7B), +8.8 (OLMo3-7B), with OLMo AIME'24 rising 30.2→46.9.
Multi-seed: RISE(weight) 62.4±0.2 vs GRPO 60.1±0.2 on Qwen3-8B; RISE(logit) 49.6±0.4 vs GRPO 45.1±0.4 on Qwen3-1.7B.
Removing RLVR grounding collapses training within 60 steps (MATH-500 → 2.4%, length explodes to 8K cap, reward → 0).
Removing OPD (adopting θ_future directly) gives negligible gains (60.0→60.3 at 8B, 45.4→45.6 at 1.7B), showing distillation is the key.
Safe β range narrows with training: β=2.0 gives +7.3 at step 50 but −15 at step 100; β=1.5 costs 7.7 by step 200.
Compute-matched GRPO-2× gains only +1.9/+0.5 vs RISE's +4.8/+2.7; RISE costs 1.3–1.6× GRPO wall time with no extra sampling.
RISE improves pass@16 as well as avg@16 (AIME'24 1.7B pass@16 +9.6), broadening coverage rather than only sharpening.
Privileged-conditioning GRPO+SDPO underperforms GRPO on Qwen3-8B (55.9 vs 60.0) and Qwen3-1.7B (43.2 vs 45.4).
Agentic tasks: RISE(weight) +9.4 ALFWorld and +10.9 WebShop Acc over GRPO.
2609.05295.ablations_summary: Both phases necessary (no-RLVR collapses, no-OPD gains vanish); β0∈[1.2,1.5] stable with 1.2 best, β0=2.0 diverges; any decay beats fixed β; EMA anchor η=0.1 lifts Qwen3-1.7B Math Avg 46.2→50.2 (logit) but hurts OLMo (56.4→50.1); rollout reuse matches resampling (62.5 vs 62.5) while halving sampling; neither weight- nor logit-space consistently dominates; compute-matched GRPO-2× only marginally helps.
limitations: Relies on training trajectory being sufficiently low-dimensional/near-linear for extrapolation at modest β; principled detection of when extrapolation becomes unreliable remains open
Inherits biases of the RLVR reward: if reward is hackable, extrapolation amplifies the spurious direction
Theoretical bounds are directional (T-dependent prefactor, linearity assumption), not tight certificates
Gains on code are modest due to fast saturation; smallest margin on non-instruction-tuned base model (+1.2)
failure_modes: Extrapolation without RLVR grounding (self-distillation-only displacement) causes degenerate non-terminating generation and reward collapse
Large β (2.0) becomes catastrophic once policy nears optimality (−15 points at step 100)
EMA anchor counterproductive when per-step RLVR directions are already large and stable (OLMo −6.3)
Adopting θ_future directly without OPD yields no consistent improvement

theory.theoretical_claim: Suboptimality decomposition J(π*)−J(π_θ) ≤ teacher gap + T·sqrt(L̄_OPD/2); safe extrapolation range 1<β<2α*/α_n−1 under linear trajectory; RISE iteration contracts bound by γ(β)<1
theory.proof_sketch: Performance difference lemma → Hölder bound via TV → Pinsker + Jensen/Cauchy–Schwarz yield teacher-gap + distillation-error decomposition; under linear φ-trajectory, extrapolated teacher is closer to π* iff β in (1, 2α*/α_n−1), and Lipschitz J gives contraction factor γ(β)=|α*−βα'|/(α*−α').

2609.05295.relevance_to_opd: Directly an OPD method: proposes a new teacher source (self-extrapolated future checkpoint) for on-policy distillation, combined with RLVR in an alternating loop; addresses the teacher-quality bottleneck of external-teacher OPD and privileged self-distillation, and unifies with ExOPD's geometric-mixture view.

2609.05198.title: What Matters in On-Policy Distillation? A Perspective on Data Efficiency and Data Selection
2609.05198.summary: 1-shot OPD works; 8 hard examples match 17K-example full-set OPD

method.training_loop: for step in 279: sample prompt(s) from tiny hard subset; student samples 8 rollouts (T=1.0, ≤7168 tok); teacher scores student prefixes; minimize student-top-16 renormalized reverse KL per token
method.loss_formulation: L_{OPD}^{top-k}(\theta)=\mathbb{E}_{x\sim D_x,\hat{y}\sim\pi_\theta(\cdot|x)}\left[\sum_{t=1}^{T} D_{KL}(\bar{p}_t^{(S_t)}\|\bar{q}_t^{(S_t)})\right],\ S_t=\mathrm{TopK}(p_t,16)
method.data_source: 1,000-example subset of DAPO-Math-17K, ranked by average student/teacher rollout accuracy A_i=(S_i+T_i)/2 over 16 rollouts; Hard = A_i<0.1
key_components: 1-shot OPD
difficulty-driven data selection (hard examples only)
student top-k (k=16) reverse KL
length-controlled analysis of CoT length vs token entropy
per-token KL reduction analysis on structural reasoning tokens

2609.05198.novelty: First systematic data-centric study of OPD: shows OPD is effective from a single example (stable to 2,000 steps), that hard/'unsolvable' (0% train accuracy) examples yield the largest gains via longer CoTs rather than token entropy, and proposes selecting only hard examples so 8 examples match the 17K full-set baseline across four 1.5B–7B models.

on_policy_mechanism.evidence_quote: OPD computes supervision on trajectories sampled from the current

opd_classification.reasoning: Standard on-policy top-k reverse-KL distillation with an external teacher; the contribution is data selection/curriculum (hard examples, CoT length) and data-efficiency analysis, i.e., a data/curriculum technique for OPD.

training_setup.compute_budget: 8×H800 80GB; 279 training steps (1 epoch equivalent); extended runs to 2,000 steps

train: DAPO-Math-17K (1,000-example subset; hard subsets of size 1/4/8/16/64)

key_findings: 1-shot OPD is effective for every sampled example: the 1.5B student improves from 42.4% to 48.0–51.7% average, with the best hard example π973 reaching 51.7% vs 53.7% for the 17K full-set baseline.
Training on 8 selected hard examples reaches 53.6% average, matching the full 17K DAPO-Math baseline (53.7%); scaling to 16 or 64 hard examples gives no further gain (53.3%/53.9%).
Hard examples beat easy and medium ones at fixed size 8 (53.6% vs 51.2% easy, 52.2% medium), even when both teacher and student score 0% on them.

Under length-controlled rollouts (1K/2K caps) the hard-vs-easy gap collapses to 0.5% and -0.9%, versus 3.9% and 2.4% at the 7,168-token default, showing longer CoT, not token entropy, drives gains; raising temperature to inflate entropy gives no gain.
The 7K-rollout model keeps lower per-token KL to the teacher than 2K/4K models across the 16K generation horizon, with the gap widening beyond 4,000 tokens.
Tokens with largest KL reduction are structural reasoning tokens ("Alternatively", "Wait", "Because"); "Alternatively" is absent for easy-trained models and emerges for medium/hard.
1-shot OPD trained for 2,000 steps plateaus after ~300 steps with no overfitting or collapse.
Data efficiency generalizes: 8-shot reaches 59.5% vs 59.6% full-set for DeepSeek-7B, 21.3% vs 22.5% for Qwen3-1.7B-Base, 29.2% vs 30.8% for Qwen3-4B-Base.
2609.05198.ablations_summary: Difficulty (easy/medium/hard), training-set size (1/4/8/16/64), maximum rollout length (1K/2K/4K/7K), student rollout temperature (0.6–1.1), extended training (2,000 steps), and four teacher-student pairs; hardness and CoT length are the key drivers, entropy and data volume beyond 8 examples are not.
limitations: Difficulty-driven selection is an empirical heuristic, not a theoretically optimal training set; finding the optimal set may be intractable.
Difficulty-based selection requires a verifier; in verifier-free domains CoT length is suggested only as a proxy.
Ever-longer rollouts suffer compounding exposure bias that degrades teacher supervision quality; max response length 7,168 is an empirical choice.
failure_modes: Excessively long on-policy rollouts drift the student into out-of-distribution states, degrading the teacher's supervision (exposure-bias trade-off).
Scaling hard examples beyond 8 (to 16 or 64) yields no additional gains.
Length-capped rollouts (1K/2K) erase the advantage of hard examples.
2609.05198.relevance_to_opd: Directly studies the data side of OPD: shows OPD needs very few (even one) prompts, that hard/unsolvable prompts with long CoTs are most effective (unlike GRPO where zero-advantage samples are wasted), and proposes hard-example selection as a data-efficiency technique for OPD.

2609.05111.title: Unifying ICL, SFT, KL-Regularized RL Through a Bayesian Lens
2609.05111.summary: Bayesian/Gibbs-posterior unification of ICL, SFT, KL-RL and OPD

method.training_loop: Theory paper: construct Gibbs posterior q ∝ π_ref·exp(R/β) from reference model + reward; fit π_θ by forward-KL projection (reward/advantage-weighted SFT, RW-ICL, or PPO/GRPO).
method.loss_formulation: L(\theta) = -\sum_{(x,y)} \exp(r(y|x)/\beta) \log \pi_\theta(y|x), \quad \text{i.e. } \min_\theta KL(q_{Gibbs}(\cdot|x) \| \pi_\theta(\cdot|x)),\ q_{Gibbs} \propto \pi_{ref}\exp(r/\beta)
method.data_source: DAPO-Math-17K slice (train 2000 / val 1000 / test 500) for experiments
key_components: Bayes posterior predictive as ICL target
Gibbs posterior closed form of KL-regularized RL
reward-weighted SFT = forward-KL projection
advantage-weighted SFT (AWSFT)
reward-weighted ICL (RW-ICL)
ESS-based cold-start argument for OPD
matched-budget operator-agreement experiments

2609.05111.novelty: Chains existing results (ICL-is-Bayes, RL-as-inference, RWR/AWR) into a single two-step template (posterior design + forward-KL projection), derives a theoretical necessity of SFT cold-start for on-policy distillation via importance-weight ESS collapse, and adds matched-budget update-direction cosine experiments on Qwen3 comparing PPO/GRPO/RW-SFT.

on_policy_mechanism.evidence_quote: Reward-weighted context distillation — a direct on-policy implementation of the RW-ICL objective of Part III — scores 106 of 256, ahead of answer-only SFT (100) and GRPO (97).

opd_classification.reasoning: Primarily a theoretical unification paper; OPD appears as an analyzed instance (cold-start necessity via ESS collapse), and the experimental 'context distillation' uses reward-weighted log-likelihood rather than teacher logit/KL supervision, so it fails C2/C3 as an OPD method but offers theory relevant to OPD.

stabilization_tricks: disabling thinking mode / raising generation budget to fix dead reward signal

key_findings: PPO and GRPO update directions have cosine ≈1.000 on all three seeds in the stable (anchored) regime but collapse to 0.107–0.358 under unanchored stress.
Reward-weighted SFT direction differs from GRPO even when stable (cos 0.1–0.2) and becomes erratic (negative cosines down to −0.477) under stress.
Cold-start failure demo: original generation contract yields raw reward sum 3.0 with 99.2% zero-variance groups; fixing the contract raises reward sum to 181.0 and parse success to 0.846.

Reward-weighted context distillation scores 106/256 (0.414) vs SFT 100 (0.391), GRPO 97 (0.379), warm-start 91 (0.355), base 83 (0.324), but the 95% bootstrap CI [−5.5,+6.25] shows statistical indistinguishability.
Theory: KL-regularized RL optimum is a Gibbs posterior and reward/advantage-weighted SFT is exactly its forward-KL projection.
2609.05111.ablations_summary: Varying only the sampling proposal anchoring (1.0 vs 0.0) flips PPO/GRPO agreement from ~1.0 to ~0.1–0.36; varying only the generation contract (thinking on/1024 tokens vs off/2048) turns a dead reward signal into a usable one; no component ablation of the distillation objective itself.
limitations: Equivalences hold only at the level of objectives/posterior targets and first-order update forms, not identity of practical algorithms.
Experiments are small-scale (256 validation prompts, one seed for E.2–E.3) and characterize mechanism-level behavior rather than benchmark-scale gains.
Operator agreement is measured only on the last two transformer layers.
Whether within-task exchangeability holds for real pretraining corpora is an open empirical question.
failure_modes: Importance-weighted KL projection (off-policy RW-SFT or on-policy distillation) degenerates when the sampling distribution has low support overlap with the high-reward Gibbs posterior (ESS collapse).
Dead reward signal when generation contract truncates reasoning (99.2% zero-variance groups).
Few-shot prompting can degrade RL-tuned reasoning models due to posterior mismatch.

theory.theoretical_claim: KL-regularized RL optimum is a Gibbs posterior; reward/advantage-weighted SFT and RW-ICL are its forward-KL projections; cold start is theoretically necessary for OPD via importance-weight ESS collapse
theory.proof_sketch: Lagrangian stationarity of E_π[r] − βKL(π‖π_ref) under normalization gives π* ∝ π_ref exp(r/β); expanding KL(q_Gibbs‖π_θ) and dropping θ-independent terms yields the exp(r/β)-weighted log-likelihood objective; ESS of weights q_Gibbs/μ collapses without support overlap.

2609.05111.relevance_to_opd: Provides a theoretical framing in which on-policy distillation is one instance of forward-KL projection onto a Gibbs posterior, and argues that SFT cold-start/warm-up is a statistical necessity for OPD pipelines due to importance-weight variance; no new OPD algorithm with teacher-logit supervision is proposed.

2609.06490.title: ORACLE ZOOM: On-Policy Self-Distillation Inspired Reference-Constrained Recursive Image Super Resolution
2609.06490.summary: OPSD-inspired recursive image SR trained on own predictions beyond GT scales

method.training_loop: for each image: recursively zoom+SR with LoRA-adapted OSEDiff; LPIPS to GT at scales<=m; cross-scale projected LPIPS, TOPIQ quality, latent-MSE KL prior to frozen base, EMA consistency at deeper scales; backprop through chain
method.loss_formulation: L = L_{sup} + \lambda_{xscale} L_{xscale} + \lambda_{qual} L_{qual} + \lambda_{prior} L_{prior} + \lambda_{ema} L_{ema}
method.data_source: 1,000 curated images from 4KLSDB training split (short side >= 2048)
key_components: recursive on-trajectory training with backprop through zoom chain
cross-scale ground-truth consistency via aligned reference projection
frozen no-reference quality model (TOPIQ-NR) guidance
KL-constrained latent prior to frozen base SR model (reduces to latent MSE)
EMA consistency at supervision boundary
rank-16 LoRA on SD3 transformer

2609.06490.novelty: Unlike Chain-of-Zoom which only uses VLM caption guidance at deeper zooms, ORACLE ZOOM trains on its own recursive predictions and carries the last available ground-truth image as a projected cross-scale reference beyond the supervision boundary, combined with quality guidance under a KL-bounded latent prior with a provable bound on quality-driven deviation.

on_policy_mechanism.evidence_quote: Recursive SR uses each prediction as the input to the next scale. We therefore retain the computation graph through successive predictions rather than detaching them.

opd_classification.reasoning: Image super-resolution with image (not text) output is out of modality scope, and there is no logit/distributional teacher supervision; the 'KL prior' is a latent MSE anchor to the frozen base SR model, so C2 and C3 fail.

training_setup.compute_budget: single 8-GPU H100 node, 1 GPU for optimization, under one day

benchmarks.name: Aggregate over 7 test sets (CLIPIQA, all scales)

key_findings: Across seven datasets ORACLE ZOOM reaches 0.713 mean CLIPIQA vs 0.621 for CoZ, with 0.199 LPIPS and 0.160 DISTS at 4×.
At 256× CLIPIQA is 0.706 vs 0.579 for CoZ, and an InternVL3.5-38B judge prefers ORACLE ZOOM in 68% (64×) and 78% (256×) of decided comparisons.
Hallucination rate at 64×/256× is 0.21/0.14 for ORACLE ZOOM vs 0.55/0.70 for CoZ.
Removing the KL latent prior raises CLIPIQA to 0.794 but hallucination jumps from 0.303 to 0.907 and P-DISTS degrades from 0.215 to 0.330.
Only a 7.1M-parameter LoRA trained on 1,000 images is needed; inference latency is 1.505s vs 1.486s per step for CoZ.
2609.06490.ablations_summary: L_sup controls 4× fidelity (LPIPS 0.199→0.215 without it); L_xscale controls projected fidelity (P-DISTS 0.215→0.232); L_qual drives quality (CLIPIQA 0.714→0.594); L_prior prevents hallucination (0.303→0.907 without it); L_ema is a lightweight stabilizer; decode-space LPIPS beats latent MSE for 4× supervision; TOPIQ-NR beats HyperIQA and Laplacian as quality model.
limitations: Evaluation beyond 4× cannot measure exact recovery since ground truth is unavailable; projected metrics and VLM judge measure consistency only
Synthetic center-crop recursion does not establish performance for physical camera zoom or arbitrary user regions
Trained on curated 4K photographic set; smaller gains on DRealSR and RealSR with domain-specific degradations
Relies on fixed no-reference quality model and pretrained SR prior which can bias detail type
failure_modes: Without KL prior the quality objective produces repetitive high-scoring but hallucinated textures
Mixed 4× fidelity on real-camera datasets DRealSR and RealSR (CoZ better on some metrics)

theory.theoretical_claim: Bounded quality deviation: KL(ρθ∥ρ0) ≤ ε_prior implies |Q(Î_j) − Q(D(z0_j))| ≤ L_q σ sqrt(2ε_prior/d) under local Lipschitz assumption
theory.proof_sketch: Shared isotropic Gaussian covariance makes KL equal (d/2σ²)·MSE; bounding KL bounds latent RMSE, and local Lipschitzness of the quality score transfers this bound to quality space.

2609.06490.relevance_to_opd: Only nominally related: borrows the OPSD idea of training on model-generated intermediate predictions with privileged training-only information, but in image super-resolution with no distributional teacher; useful only as an example of OPSD terminology spreading to non-LLM generative domains.

2609.22254.title: Teacher Should Think Ahead: Adaptive Continuations for Reliable On-Policy Distillation
2609.22254.affiliation_primary: Institute of Automation, Chinese Academy of Sciences / Ant Group
2609.22254.summary: AC-OPD: adaptive-length teacher continuations from student states to stabilize OPD

method.training_loop: student rollout → score tokens by squared log-ratio → pick K anchors → teacher continues ≤m_max tokens → choose horizon h_i by variance-bias criterion → L_OPD + λ L_branch update
method.loss_formulation: L_{AC-OPD} = L_{OPD} + \lambda L_{branch},\; L_{OPD} = -\mathbb{E}_{x,y^S}\big[\tfrac{1}{T}\sum_t sg[\Delta_t]\log\pi_\theta(y_t^S|c_t^S)\big],\; \Delta_t=\log\pi_T(y_t^S|c_t^S)-\log\pi_\theta(y_t^S|c_t^S),\; L_{branch} = -\tfrac{1}{N_{resp}}\sum_{i\in A_B}\sum_{k=1}^{h_i}\log\pi_\theta(Z^T_{i,k}|C^T_{i,k-1}),\; \lambda=0.5
method.data_source: DAPO-Math-17k prompts (math); Eurus split of UltraInteract (code)
key_components: Teacher Uncertainty Contraction (TUC) observation
squared log-ratio anchor selection
bounded teacher continuations (m_max) from student states
adaptive horizon h_i via Gini-variance vs cumulative-KL-bias criterion
branch CE loss added to reverse-log-ratio OPD trunk loss

2609.22254.novelty: Unlike prior OPD variants that only reshape the next-token signal (reweighting, entropy-aware divergence, reward extrapolation), AC-OPD extends teacher supervision beyond the local query by letting the teacher continue multiple tokens from selected student states, with a theory-derived finite/adaptive continuation length balancing TUC variance reduction against path-divergence bias.

on_policy_mechanism.evidence_quote: Given a prompt x ∼ D, the student generates a length-T rollout

opd_classification.reasoning: Core method is an on-policy distillation objective (student rollouts + teacher log-ratio supervision) augmented with an adaptively-sized teacher-continuation branch loss, backed by a variance-bias theoretical analysis.

stabilization_tricks: adaptive horizon masking of branch tokens
top-K anchor selection by squared log-ratio

key_findings: Teacher Uncertainty Contraction: teacher entropy and Gini impurity decrease along its own continuation from a student prefix (exponential saturation fits R²=0.982 and 0.990), but not along student continuations.
AC-OPD improves over standard OPD by 4.37 Math Avg points and 3.50 Code Avg points in Setting 1 (38.03 / 61.20) and reaches 50.38 / 76.65 in Setting 2.
Fixed continuation length is non-monotonic: peaks at h=8 (64.4 HE+, 57.3 MBPP+) then declines at 12 and 16, consistent with the finite-continuation theory.
Adaptive horizon (mean h=5.74) reaches Code Avg 61.20 vs 58.45 for mean-matched Fixed-6, 60.85 for Fixed-8, and 60.10 for Shuffled Adaptive.
Squared log-ratio anchor selection (61.20) beats Even (58.97) and Random (58.57) anchors by 2.23 and 2.63 points.
Under matched supervised-token budgets AC-OPD outperforms OPD throughout early training, so gains are not explained by extra supervised tokens.
Baseline student values in benchmarks are standard-OPD results (no base-model or teacher scores reported); SFT sometimes beats plain OPD (e.g., AIME24 Setting 1: 23.0 vs 13.3).
2609.22254.ablations_summary: Anchor selection by squared log-ratio > Even/Random (+2.2/+2.6 Code Avg); fixed continuation length peaks at h=8 with degradation at longer horizons; adaptive horizon beats mean-matched Fixed-6 (+2.75), best Fixed-8 (+0.35) and Shuffled Adaptive (+1.10); token-matched comparison shows gains are not from additional supervision volume.
limitations: Evaluation limited to the Qwen3 family
Requires additional teacher-side inference for continuations
failure_modes: Overly long teacher continuations (h=12,16) degrade performance due to accumulated teacher-student path divergence (branch-level exposure bias)
Standard OPD underperforms SFT on some math benchmarks in Setting 1 (e.g., AIME24), motivating the reliability issue

theory.theoretical_claim: Variance-bias decomposition of teacher-branch gradient error: TUC gives variance term A_0/m + A_TUC(1-e^{-η_H m})/(m²(1-e^{-η_H})), path-divergence gives bias ≤ Bκ(m-1); relaxed bound A/m + Bκm minimized at finite m* = sqrt(A/(Bκ)) (Finite-Continuation Principle).
theory.proof_sketch: Conditionally center the sampled branch gradient to split error into branch-sampling variance and bias from replacing student-future contexts with teacher-conditioned contexts; bound variance via assumed geometric entropy contraction and bounded logit Jacobian/dependence (Lemma 4); bound bias via bounded per-step teacher-student KL accumulating with depth (Lemma 5); combine (Theorem 6) and relax to derive the scaling law m* (Corollary 7).

2609.22254.relevance_to_opd: Directly extends the OPD objective: keeps the reverse-log-ratio on-policy trunk loss but adds theory-guided, adaptively-truncated teacher continuations branching from high-disagreement student states, addressing OPD instability from unreliable local teacher signals; related to speculative/interleaved KD and token-weighting OPD variants.

2609.25048.title: Prompt Breadth and Rollout Refresh Interact in On-Policy Distillation
2609.25048.summary: 3×3 study: prompt breadth × rollout refresh interact in OPD data efficiency

method.training_loop: for each phase: sample N-prompt bank -> student snapshot generates responses (M snapshots total) -> teacher scores student top-16 tokens -> dual-clipped PPO-style OPD update (110 updates, 14,080 trajectories)
method.loss_formulation: L_{OPD}(\theta;B)=\frac{1}{\sum_t m_t}\sum_{t\in B}\sum_{j\in C_t} m_t\,\phi(A_{tj}, r_{tj}(\theta)),\; A_{tj}=\mathrm{sg}[\bar p^S_{tj}(\ell^T_{tj}-\ell^S_{tj})],\; r_{tj}=\pi_\theta(j|s_t)/\pi_{old}(j|s_t)
method.data_source: English subset of DAPO-Math-17K (14,107 usable prompts; banks of 8, 48, or 14,080 prompts)
key_components: prompt breadth N as control
rollout refresh M (number of student snapshots generating responses)
student-top-16 reverse-KL-derived surrogate with teacher full-vocab log-probs
dual-clipped PPO term
matched trajectory (14,080) and update (110) counts
inference-budget (4K–32K prefix) re-scoring analysis
fixed-parameter gradient diagnostic (fresh vs stale responses)

2609.25048.novelty: First controlled factorial study separating prompt count from response-generating policy snapshots in OPD at matched trajectory/update budgets; shows the sign of the breadth effect flips with refresh schedule (4.07 pp interaction) and that frozen vs periodic ranking reverses with inference budget.

on_policy_mechanism.evidence_quote: answer depend on the student policies that generate its training responses? We

opd_classification.reasoning: The paper keeps the OPD objective fixed and empirically analyzes data controls (prompt breadth, rollout refresh/freshness) and their failure/trade-off modes rather than proposing a new distillation method.

training_setup.rl_algorithm: pure-KD (dual-clipped PPO surrogate on OPD coefficients, one epoch)

key_findings: With frozen initial-policy responses (M=1), increasing prompt breadth from 8 to 14,080 lowers macro3 accuracy from 21.16% to 19.05%; under per-update refresh (M=110) it raises accuracy from 23.61% to 25.57%, an interaction of 4.07 pp (95% CI [2.00, 6.28]).
Under periodic refresh (M=10), eight prompts reach 24.09% vs 24.51% for 14,080 prompts—a 1,760× breadth change spans only 0.41 pp.
Moving from one frozen collection to ten snapshots gains +2.94/+4.21/+5.45 pp across bank sizes, while ten to 110 snapshots changes accuracy by −0.49/−0.17/+1.07 pp.
Frozen-response models produce parseable below-cap answers only 21–25% of the time at 16K, vs 92.6–96.8% with refresh.
Matched 48-prompt comparisons: periodic refresh raises pass@32 by 12.69 pp (Qwen3-4B teacher) and 22.57 pp (JustRL-1.5B teacher) at 16K.
At a 32K budget the ranking reverses: frozen leads by 4.39 pp (Qwen3) and 2.07 pp (JustRL) while using 1.81× and 1.72× as many response tokens.
Stale (initial-policy) responses induce raw gradient norms 2.53–2.82× those of fresh responses at later checkpoints with sketch cosines of 0.127 and 0.034.
2609.25048.ablations_summary: 3×3 grid over N∈{8,48,Full} × M∈{1,10,110}; two-teacher matched refresh comparison; difficulty-selected vs random 48-prompt bank (23.98 vs 24.22, no gain); Impulse single-update run (10.43, inconclusive); prefix-budget re-scoring at 4K–32K; gradient geometry probe.
limitations: Single Qwen3-0.6B student and competition math only
One training run per cell; intervals capture evaluation not seed variance
Breadth and responses-per-prompt vary reciprocally at fixed trajectory count so inversion cause is not isolated
Token-level compute and wall-clock are not matched across cells
Gradient probe lacks fresh-vs-fresh null distribution and does not identify update mechanism
Only three refresh schedules tested; no continuous refresh threshold
failure_modes: Frozen initial-policy responses (M=1) with broad prompt banks degrade accuracy and yield mostly truncated/unparseable answers at 16K
Periodic-refresh models lose to frozen-response models in accuracy at 32K budgets
Single amplified update (Impulse) fails to reproduce periodic training gains
2609.25048.relevance_to_opd: Directly studies OPD data-efficiency: how the number of distinct prompts and the freshness of student rollouts (which define the states teachers supervise) jointly determine OPD outcomes, informing prompt/rollout scheduling design in OPD pipelines.

2609.07137.title: Flow3D-OPD: Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation for 3D Geometry Generation with Flow-Matching Diffusion Transformer
2609.07137.affiliation_primary: Shanghai Jiao Tong University / Tencent Hunyuan3D
2609.07137.summary: Multi-teacher on-policy velocity-field distillation for image-to-3D flow-matching DiT

method.training_loop: Stage1: semi-policy DPO FT -> 3 DPO teachers w/ Gemini agentic reward. Stage2: student rolls out ODE trajectory; routed frozen teacher supervises per-step velocity; accumulate grads over orient->pose->consist cycle; update.
method.loss_formulation: L^m_{distill}(\theta)=\frac{1}{N}\sum_{j=0}^{N-1} w(t_j)\|v_\theta(x_{t_j})-SG(v_{\phi_m}(x_{t_j}))\|_2^2 ;\; L^{total}_{distill}=\frac{1}{|M|}\sum_{m\in M} L^m_{distill}(\theta) (derived from reverse KL between Gaussian transition kernels)
method.data_source: Curated image-conditioned preference datasets per dimension (orientation 3,661; pose 4,083; consistency 1,063 training samples); ground-truth meshes for semi-policy FT; student rollouts during distillation
key_components: semi-policy preference fine-tuning (GT winner vs. on-policy loser)
agentic VLM verifier (Gemini-3-Flash) with multi-view render, zoom-in, diff overlay, case memory
dimension-specific DPO teachers (orient/pose/consistency)
on-policy reverse-KL distillation reduced to time-weighted velocity-field L2 matching
hard task-routing to a single teacher per mini-batch
gradient accumulation across a full orient->pose->consistency cycle
ODE sampling in OPD stage, SDE in FT stage

2609.07137.novelty: First application of multi-teacher on-policy distillation (following DiffusionOPD/Flow-OPD from image generation) to 3D geometry generation, adding an agentic 3D verifier for DPO teacher training and hard task-routing + gradient accumulation to avoid gradient interference; student surpasses all teachers on average win ratio.

on_policy_mechanism.evidence_quote: At each training step, the student model generates its own

opd_classification.reasoning: Method is genuinely on-policy multi-teacher distillation (student rollouts, frozen teacher velocity-field/KL supervision), but the output modality is 3D meshes from a flow-matching diffusion transformer, not text, so it is out of LLM-OPD scope (Pattern 2).

stabilization_tricks: ODE deterministic sampling in OPD stage
training_setup.warmup_method: semi-policy DPO fine-tuning (GT winners + on-policy losers) plus MSE

benchmarks.name: Average pairwise B-wins vs Hunyuan3D-2.1 (Gemini-3-Flash judge)

key_findings: Flow3D-OPD student reaches 61.0% average B-wins, surpassing all three teachers (53.0/47.9/56.9) and FT (54.9).
Each DPO teacher excels on its target dimension but degrades others (orient teacher: 2.7% A-wins on orientation but 30.8% A-wins on consistency).
Gradient accumulation with hard task-routing beats single-step sequential (61.0 vs 59.8 B-wins) and single-step routed (58.5).
SDE sampling is better in the FT stage (54.9 vs 51.7 B-wins) while ODE is better in the OPD stage (61.0 vs 54.8).
OPD without semi-policy FT gives only 57.3% average B-wins vs 61.0% for the full pipeline.
Distilling from teacher velocity at CFG w=1.0 yields the best student; inference is best at w=3.0.
Improvements hold under an independent GPT-5.5 evaluator (51.4% B-wins) and blind user study (4.40 top score).
2609.07137.ablations_summary: Semi-policy FT stage, hard task-routing, mini-batch gradient accumulation, ODE (vs SDE) sampling during OPD, and CFG scale of the distillation target all contribute; gradient accumulation yields smoother, lower distillation loss.
limitations: Majority of sampled DPO pairs fall below confidence margin, making fully online teacher training inefficient (requires rollout-then-train)
Base model lacks capability for reliable preference learning without prior fine-tuning
failure_modes: Applying DPO directly to the pretrained model degrades performance (48.3% B-wins)
Individual teachers exhibit gradient interference / degrade non-target dimensions
SDE sampling during OPD converges slower with higher loss than ODE

theory.theoretical_claim: Reverse KL between student and teacher Gaussian SDE transition kernels with shared covariance reduces to a closed-form time-weighted squared velocity difference; degenerates to L2 velocity matching under ODE
theory.proof_sketch: Euler–Maruyama discretization gives isotropic Gaussian kernels differing only in mean; KL of equal-covariance Gaussians is ||mu_theta-mu_phi||^2/(2 sigma^2); state terms cancel leaving weighted ||v_theta - v_phi||^2.

2609.07137.relevance_to_opd: Transfers LLM-style on-policy distillation (GKD/MiniLLM reverse-KL on self-generated trajectories) and DiffusionOPD/Flow-OPD to 3D flow-matching DiTs, demonstrating multi-teacher OPD as a substitute for multi-reward RL; out of text-modality scope but methodologically informative for multi-teacher OPD and gradient-interference mitigation.

2609.07103.title: Revisiting Complete Reasoning Traces for Post-Training
2609.07103.summary: E-SFT: trim middle reasoning segments; extends to GRPO and OPD masking

method.training_loop: For each trace: split by \n\n, keep first n and last n steps, drop middle (~20% tokens); SFT on trimmed trace. For GRPO/OPD: mask middle 20% tokens from per-token gradient.
method.loss_formulation: L_{SFT}(\theta) = -\sum_{i=1}^{N} \log p_\theta(y_i, r_i^{trim} | x_i), where r_i^{trim} retains first/last n steps; for OPD/GRPO the per-token loss is masked on the middle 20% of the trajectory
method.data_source: s1K-1.1, OpenThoughts3-1.2M (100K subsample), DAPO-17k (GRPO)
key_components: step-level segmentation at double newlines
endpoint retention (prefix+suffix), middle removal ~20%
attention and segment-ablation analysis of redundancy
middle-token masking for GRPO and on-policy distillation

2609.07103.novelty: Shows via attention/knockout/perplexity analyses that intermediate reasoning steps are redundant, and that a resource-free segment-level truncation (keep endpoints) beats full-trace SFT and several filtering baselines; also transfers the masking idea to GRPO and OPD objectives.

on_policy_mechanism.evidence_quote: a widely used post-training method that trains a studentonateacher’sdistributionoveritsowngen- eratedtrajectories.

opd_classification.reasoning: Core contribution is E-SFT (trace trimming for SFT); OPD appears only as an extension experiment where the middle 20% of student-rollout tokens are masked from the distillation loss, a token-weighting technique rather than a new OPD method.

training_setup.compute_budget: OPD/GRPO: 100 steps; SFT of Qwen2.5-32B on 100K OpenThoughts3 ~20h on 16×H100

key_findings: Retaining prefix+suffix of reasoning traces beats full-trace SFT (75.19 vs 73.51 avg on Qwen2.5-32B; 67.50 vs 65.78 on Qwen3-8B).
Attention on intermediate reasoning steps is weak; replacing middle segments lowers answer PPL (-0.02) while replacing beginning/end raises it (+0.02/+0.04).
Masking the middle 20% in OPD (Qwen3-8B→Qwen3-1.7B) improves avg from 61.2 to 63.4 with step-level masks (+2.2) vs +0.7 for token-level.
Masking the middle 20% in GRPO improves Qwen3-1.7B-Base avg by +8.7 and Qwen3-1.7B by +1.2.
E-SFT outperforms resource-intensive filtering (LLM-based 60.08, PPL-high 74.43, LS-Mixture 71.90 vs 75.19).
GPT-OSS-120B judge prefers E-SFT trajectories in 22% of cases vs 8% for original data.
2609.07103.ablations_summary: Prefix-only or suffix-only retention degrades relative to both; random step removal hurts; step-level masking beats token-level in OPD; performance insensitive to ~20% trim ratio but excessive trimming hurts; benefit depends on base model capacity.
limitations: Effectiveness depends on base model capability; weak models gain little (threshold ~60–65 on general benchmarks for s1K-1.1).
Retained step ratio is a hyperparameter; excessive truncation degrades performance.
Analysis does not determine whether individual steps are truly redundant.
failure_modes: Weak base models cannot infer trimmed segments and see little or no benefit.
Very small models (Llama-3.2-3B) show no average gain.
Removing beginning or ending segments degrades performance.
2609.07103.relevance_to_opd: Shows that masking the middle 20% of student rollout tokens from the OPD loss (Qwen3-8B teacher, Qwen3-1.7B student) improves results, suggesting token/segment weighting can benefit on-policy distillation; but OPD is only an extension of an SFT-focused paper.

2609.09300.title: Video-MOPD: Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation for Video Understanding
2609.09300.summary: Routed multi-teacher on-policy distillation unifies three RL video experts into one 8B model

method.training_loop: for x in D: route to domain teacher by label; student samples y~πθ(·|x); teacher scores same tokens; minimize per-token reverse KL(πθ‖πT^d) on student rollout
method.loss_formulation: L_{Video-MOPD}(\theta)=\sum_{d\in\{v,i,t\}} p_d \mathbb{E}_{x\sim D_d, y\sim\pi_\theta(\cdot|x)}\left[\frac{1}{|y|}\sum_{t=1}^{|y|} D_{KL}\left(\pi_\theta(\cdot|x,y_{<t})\,\|\,\pi_T^d(\cdot|x,y_{<t})\right)\right]
method.data_source: 7,493-sample mixture (2,500 video MCQ, 2,500 image STEM/math, 2,493 temporal grounding) selected via RAIS from public video/image datasets (NeXT-QA, LongVideo-Reason, STAR, LLaVA-Video-178K, Holmes-train, PerceptionTest, CLEVRER, SR-91k, Orsta47K, virl39K, TimeLens2-93K, TimeLens-100K, Ego4D-NLQ)
key_components: Three RL-trained domain experts (General Video, VTG, STEM) from Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct
Deterministic domain-label router selecting one teacher per sample
Token-level reverse-KL on student-sampled trajectories (MOPD)
Reliability-Aware Informative Sampling (RAIS): keep Acc_T=1 examples, prioritize large 1-Acc_S gap
Token-support variants: sampled token vs Teacher/Student/overlap Top-16

2609.09300.novelty: First application of routed multi-teacher on-policy distillation (MOPD) to consolidate heterogeneous video capabilities (general, temporal grounding, STEM) into one VLM, plus RAIS data selection based on teacher consistency and teacher–student gap; shows policy-space consolidation beats parameter averaging by 1.84 avg points.

on_policy_mechanism.evidence_quote: The reverse-KL objective provides dense token-level supervision on trajectories generated by the student itself, allowing each domain expert to guide the student only on samples matched to its specialization.

opd_classification.reasoning: Student generates rollouts, routed white-box teachers give per-token reverse-KL supervision on them, and the paper's contribution is applying multi-teacher OPD to the new video-understanding domain with a data-selection (RAIS) add-on.

training_setup.compute_budget: 4 nodes × 8 A800 GPUs; 2 epochs / 178 updates (duration unspecified)
stabilization_tricks: RAIS reliability filter (teacher Acc=1 across K samples)

key_findings: Video-MOPD-8B raises the 7-benchmark average from 63.68 to 69.12 (+5.4) over Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct.
Largest gains on Video-Holmes (+10.2), TimeLens (+9.2), and MMVU (+5.9).
Policy-space consolidation via MOPD beats parameter averaging of the three experts (67.28 → 69.12, +1.84).
The unified student matches or exceeds its matched expert on several benchmarks (e.g., MMVU 66.80 vs STEM Expert 65.20; Video-Holmes 54.71 vs General Expert 53.89).
Among non-expert baselines the model leads or ties on six of seven benchmarks.
Only 178 updates on 7,493 RAIS-selected samples with 1 generation per prompt suffice for the consolidation.
2609.09300.ablations_summary: Token-support ablation (one epoch): sampled-token supervision is best on VideoMMMU (73.67), Video-Holmes (50.57), TimeLens (61.42); Teacher Top-16 best on MMVU (68.00); Student Top-16 best on Video-MME (73.4); overlap Top-16 best on MVBench (72.88); sampled-token adopted as default. RAIS itself is not ablated.
limitations: Long-form videos with sparse, distant evidence not addressed (deferred to future work).
STEM expert trained purely on static images; video-STEM data scarce.
RL experts limited by current training data, verifiers, and rewards.
failure_modes: Different token-support choices trade off gains across benchmarks; no single support dominates.
VTG Expert alone degrades general benchmarks (e.g., VideoMMMU 58.89 vs 69.11 base), showing specialist interference that must be resolved by consolidation.
Video-MOPD-8B slightly trails the STEM Expert on VideoMMMU/TempCompass and the VTG Expert on TimeLens.
2609.09300.relevance_to_opd: Direct application of multi-teacher on-policy distillation (reverse-KL on student rollouts with domain-routed white-box teachers) to VLM video understanding; demonstrates OPD as a capability-consolidation tool superior to model merging and introduces RAIS teacher-reliability/gap-based data selection for OPD.

2609.08341.title: TV-Regulated OPD: Direction Matters in On-Policy Distillation
2609.08341.affiliation_primary: The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology (Guangzhou)
2609.08341.summary: Sign-only OPD advantage = TV descent; add TV-regulated global scale for stability

method.training_loop: for step k: sample 64 prompts, 1 on-policy student rollout each; teacher scores same prefixes; Δ=log p−log q; A=c_k·sign(Δ); update student; c_{k+1} from EMA of sampled-token TV estimate
method.loss_formulation: L = -\frac{1}{|B|}\sum_{i\in B} sg[A_i]\log q_\theta(a_i|s_i),\; A^{TVR}_{i,k}=c_k\,\mathrm{sign}(\Delta_i),\; c_k=\mathrm{clip}\big((\tfrac{\bar D_{k-1}+\epsilon}{D_{ref}+\epsilon})^\alpha, c_{min},1\big),\; \hat d(s,a)=[1-e^{\Delta(s,a)}]_+
method.data_source: DeepMath-103K prompts (Qwen3-8B pair) and DAPO-Math-17K prompts (JustRL-1.5B pair); student-generated on-policy rollouts
key_components: Sign-TV: replace raw log-ratio coefficient with sign(Δ), shown equivalent to conditional TV descent
Sampled-token unbiased TV estimator [1-e^Δ]_+ using existing teacher log-probs
EMA-smoothed TV-responsive global scale c_k with exponent α and floor c_min
Controlled magnitude ablations (Raw / Sign / Group-Constant / Permuted)

2609.08341.novelty: Unlike vOPD, PowerOPD, OPD+, TIDE which reweight token magnitudes, this paper shows token-wise magnitude allocation gives no consistent benefit; keeping only the sign yields a bounded TV-distance objective, and a single shared TV-estimated scale restores discrepancy-dependent attenuation without per-token weights.

on_policy_mechanism.evidence_quote: Each run generates its own on-policy trajectories as its student evolves.

opd_classification.reasoning: Proposes a new fixed divergence objective (conditional TV via sign coefficient) for sampled-token OPD with an adaptive global scale, plus theory on bounded coefficients and TV estimation.

training_setup.compute_budget: 8 GPUs per run, ~625 steps; total hours unspecified
stabilization_tricks: EMA-smoothed TV-based global scale (β=0.95, c_min=0.1, α=0.5)
one-sided TV estimator −expm1(min{Δ,0}) for numerical stability

train: OpenThoughts (400K, SFT warmup for Qwen3-8B student)

key_findings: Retaining only the sign of the token-level log-ratio (Sign) achieves 36.29% trajectory average vs 35.40% for Raw OPD, 34.67% Group-Constant, 34.35% Permuted on the JustRL 1.5B pair.
The sign-weighted update is exactly a conditional TV descent direction (−2∇D_TV), giving bounded coefficients in [-1,1].
TV-OPD reaches 70.00±1.17 / 58.33±1.67 on AIME 2024/2025 for the Qwen3-8B pair, exceeding Raw OPD (68.33 / 57.08) by 1.67 and 1.25 points.
TV-OPD improves late-stage LateMean from 40.87±0.83 to 43.06±0.10 and reduces PeakDrop from 3.51±1.13 to 2.36±0.49 on the JustRL pair.
Regulator exponent α sweep shows monotonic decline: two-benchmark average 38.13 (α=0.5) → 33.33 (α=4.0).
2609.08341.ablations_summary: Magnitude ablations (Raw/Sign/Group-Constant/Permuted) show sign direction matters and token-wise magnitude allocation gives no consistent benefit; Sign-TV alone matches Raw OPD but lacks late-stage attenuation; adding the TV-based global scale (TV-OPD) gives best aggregate and late-stage retention; larger α over-suppresses the signal and slows optimization.
limitations: Teacher-relative direction does not guarantee policy improvement; a weak or mismatched teacher can guide the student toward undesirable behavior.
TV equivalence is a conditional surrogate with stopped state occupancy; no gradient through rollout distribution and no monotonic sequence-level return guarantee.
Evaluated on a limited set of model pairs, benchmarks, and seeds; evidence supports improved dynamics and late-stage retention but not a higher capability ceiling.
failure_modes: Large α (e.g., 4.0) over-suppresses the distillation signal and lowers accuracy by ~4.8 points average.
Sign-TV without regulation assigns unit magnitude even as teacher and student converge, losing discrepancy-dependent attenuation.
Variable-length active-token pooling is a ratio estimator and not unbiased at finite batch size.
Bounded coefficients do not solve missing token coverage under top-k/nucleus truncation.

theory.theoretical_claim: Sign-weighted sampled-token update equals conditional TV descent (−2∇D_TV) with bounded teacher influence; [1−e^Δ]_+ is an unbiased sampled-token TV estimator with variance ≤1/4; TV closeness preserves positive expected task advantage
theory.proof_sketch: Differentiate D_TV=½Σ|p−q| using score identity ∇q=q∇log q to get E_q[sign(Δ)∇log q]; mass conservation gives TV = Σ[q−p]_+ = E_q[1−p/q]_+; bounded-statistic inequality |E_u f−E_v f|≤(M−m)D_TV yields advantage preservation.

2609.08341.relevance_to_opd: Directly an OPD objective-design paper: replaces the reverse-KL sampled-token log-ratio coefficient with a sign (TV) coefficient and a TV-estimated global scale, addressing variance/instability of standard OPD supervision.

2609.08183.title: NeoHorse-1: Towards Recursive Self-Improvement via Agentic Post-Training with Routing Harness
2609.08183.summary: Routing-harness data flywheel with curriculum SFT and routing-guided on-policy distillation for agent models

method.training_loop: Convert harness trajectories to user-turn examples -> 3-stage routing-score curriculum SFT -> 3-stage routing-scheduled OPD: student rollouts from recorded contexts, fixed teacher top-K reverse-KL -> capability-guided reallocation of next mixture
method.loss_formulation: L_{OPD}(\theta;R) = \frac{1}{\sum_{r\in R} w_r L_r} \sum_{r\in R} w_r \sum_{t=1}^{L_r} D_{KL}(\tilde{P}_{\theta,r,t} \| \tilde{Q}_{r,t}) over top-K student candidates plus one residual bin; SFT: masked token-level CE normalized by supervised token count
method.data_source: ~10^5–10^6 harness-generated agent trajectories from deployed routing harness (OpenSquilla etc.) plus public instruction/reasoning/tool/code/preference data (OASST2, Aya, OpenThoughts3, OpenR1-Math, ToolACE, APIGen, Nemotron-SFT-SWE, HelpSteer2, UltraFeedback)
key_components: user-turn training units with interleaved reasoning/tool-call supervision and masked history
structural validation + six-dimensional semantic evaluation + subscene labeling
router-derived C0–C3 capability-demand scores (hard/soft ordering)
three-stage routing-guided curriculum for SFT
routing-guided on-policy distillation with fixed teacher, top-K+bin coarsened reverse KL, refreshed rollout checkpoints
capability-guided data allocation closing evaluation–selection–update loop

2609.08183.novelty: Uses deployed LLM-router capability-demand predictions (rather than difficulty labels or served-model identity) to schedule both SFT examples and OPD starting contexts in a staged curriculum, and frames the routing harness as a harness-mediated RSI feedback loop; the OPD objective itself follows Agarwal et al. with a top-K + residual-bin coarsening.

on_policy_mechanism.evidence_quote: one assistant response for each context in a batch C drawn from 𝜌 𝑗. The resulting response

opd_classification.reasoning: Student generates rollouts from recorded contexts, a fixed teacher supplies next-token distributions on those rollouts, and the loss is reverse KL; the paper's OPD-specific delta is a routing-score curriculum over starting contexts, so it fits curriculum (§6.2) with an agentic-application flavor, though it is largely a technical report where OPD is one component.

stabilization_tricks: top-K candidate tokens plus residual-mass bin for coarsened distributions
three-stage curriculum reserving low-score contexts for later stages
no optimizer/LR reset between curriculum stages

key_findings: Full agentic post-training (curriculum SFT + routing-guided OPD) lifts the 4B macro-average from 58.94 to 64.87 and the 9B from 65.60 to 69.04 across ten benchmarks.
NeoHorse-1-4B outperforms Qwen3.5-4B on every benchmark and matches or exceeds Qwen3.5-9B base on several, substantially narrowing the 4B→9B gap.
Gains concentrate on harness-based agent and coding tasks (e.g., WorkBuddy +9.79, VitaBench +10.5, HumanEval +9.75 at 4B); instruction following is roughly flat at 9B.
Routing-harness trajectories beat public Toucan tool-agent data by +6.26 avg points under identical curriculum training (τ2-Bench +11.31, HumanEval +8.54).
Scaling unique routing-harness supervised tokens (~2M→10M, log scale) raises the 5-benchmark dev average monotonically from 69.31 to 71.45.
In a PinchBench trajectory the 9B model reduced model requests, execution time, and token usage by ~70.8%, 76.7%, and 83.6% vs the 4B model.
2609.08183.ablations_summary: Only data-side ablations are reported: routing-harness data vs public Toucan data (+6.26 avg) and nested data-scaling subsets (69.31→71.45). No ablation isolates the OPD stage or the routing-guided curriculum versus random ordering; all reported gains are for the full pipeline.
limitations: Validation concentrates on agentic, coding, tool-use, and instruction-following capabilities; broader harness-served capabilities not evaluated.
Results reflect a single pass of the evaluation–selection–update loop; whether gains accumulate across iterations is untested.
Routing signals are not yet well-calibrated difficulty/deficiency estimates; training the router itself is left to future work.
Should be read as an initial RSI prototype rather than a definitive demonstration.
failure_modes: 4B model stops after a single implementation attempt without a test–repair loop (WorkBuddy code repair).
4B model repeatedly retries an unavailable dependency (pandas) instead of adapting strategy (PinchBench).
9B instruction-following benchmarks show a minor decrease after post-training (IFEval 89.46→89.09).
Even NeoHorse-1-9B leaves residual label errors in structured report outputs (Case A).
2609.08183.relevance_to_opd: Applies GKD/Agarwal-style on-policy distillation (student rollouts, fixed teacher next-token distributions, reverse KL over top-K+bin coarsened distributions) to agentic multi-turn tool-use data, contributing a router-derived capability-demand curriculum that schedules OPD starting contexts; however, the teacher is unspecified and OPD is not ablated separately from SFT, so its isolated contribution is unknown.

2609.10321.title: On-Policy Distillation for Vision-Language Model Adaptation, an Effective Paradigm on Low-Quality Multimodal Data
2609.10321.summary: Learned controller builds adaptive teacher/prior/label KD targets for CLIP adaptation

method.training_loop: for each batch: compute T/S/prior logits → controller state (confidence, entropy, disagreement) → bounded actions (mix λ, weight w, temp τ) → KL(q_i‖S); every K steps update controller via validation action-matching
method.loss_formulation: L_OnPoKD = (1/B) Σ_i w_i τ_i^2 KL(q_i ‖ softmax(z_i^S/τ_i)), q_i = λ_i^T softmax(z_i^T/τ_i) + λ_i^P q_i^P + λ_i^H q_i^H; L_policy = α_λ‖λ_i−λ_i*‖² + α_w‖w_i−w_i*‖² + α_τ‖τ_i−τ_i*‖² + α_r R(π_θ)
method.data_source: Base-class training splits of 11 CLIP benchmarks; ImageNet source split for cross-dataset transfer (unlabeled target-domain training images as in PromptKD)
key_components: two-layer MLP policy controller with zero-initialized final layer
sample-wise three-way target mixture (adapted teacher, frozen zero-shot prior, hard label)
bounded actions with auxiliary-mass caps
progress-aware action modulation
validation-feedback action-matching update decoupled from KD loss
novel-class-slice prior injection

2609.10321.novelty: Replaces PromptKD's fixed teacher-centered soft target with a learned, sample-wise and stage-wise target-construction policy that mixes teacher, zero-shot prior, and hard labels, updated from held-out validation reliability rather than RL or meta-gradients, with no inference-time change.

on_policy_mechanism.evidence_quote: During training, a lightweight controller uses reliability cues from the adapted teacher, the student, and the frozen zero-shot prior, together with training progress, to construct adaptive distillation targets.

opd_classification.reasoning: Image-classification KD on CLIP logits: the student produces no autoregressive rollouts (fails C1) and outputs class labels rather than text; 'on-policy' refers only to a target-construction controller, so it is out of OPD scope.

key_findings: OnPoKD raises average base-to-novel HM over PromptKD from 83.73 to 84.62, with a larger novel-class gain (+1.40) than base (+0.30).
Cross-dataset transfer average accuracy improves from 71.33 to 72.66 (+1.33), best on 7 of 10 targets, with largest gains on EuroSAT (+5.69) and DTD (+3.11).
A fixed teacher-prior-label mixture (FixedMix) is consistently weaker than the adaptive policy, e.g. FGVCAircraft HM 43.96 vs 47.66.
Removing validation feedback collapses FGVCAircraft HM from 47.66 to 22.74.
Removing uncertainty cues drops FGVCAircraft HM by 9.69 and EuroSAT HM by 3.30, the most important state signal.
Training overhead is +19–25% time and +51% memory vs PromptKD with no inference-time cost.
2609.10321.ablations_summary: Teacher-only KD and fixed mixtures underperform the learned policy; prior mainly protects novel-class transfer, hard labels anchor cross-dataset transfer, validation feedback is critical on fine-grained data (FGVCAircraft), and the full action space (mix+weight+temp) is needed since adaptive mixing alone collapses FGVCAircraft HM to 25.78; uncertainty cues are the most important state features.
limitations: Small decreases on Caltech101 (-0.57), Food101 (-0.32), UCF101 (-1.07) where PromptKD is already strong, suggesting need for more conservative intervention when teacher and prior are both confident.
Cross-dataset transfer accuracy is less monotonic in hyperparameters and stays sensitive to the intervention scale.
Policy hyperparameters differ between the two evaluation settings.
Training time (+19–25%) and memory (+51%) overhead.
failure_modes: Without validation feedback, target construction becomes unstable on fine-grained classes (FGVCAircraft HM 47.66 → 22.74).
Adaptive mixing alone without weight/temperature control collapses on FGVCAircraft (HM 25.78).
Excessive auxiliary cap (>0.40) or no policy regularization degrades novel-class accuracy.
2609.10321.relevance_to_opd: Uses 'on-policy distillation' terminology but for CLIP image classification with a target-construction controller; no student-generated sequences or text output, so it is only tangentially related to LLM OPD (adaptive target mixing / teacher-reliability weighting ideas).

method.data_source: Synthetic multi-turn role-play dialogues generated by Claude 3.7 Sonnet (character) and Qwen2.5-14B (user) with instruction-injected user behaviors and reverse profile filtering; OPD uses full dataset then a world-setting subset

2609.11127.novelty: Inverts the usual distillation direction (domain-adapted SFT+RL model as teacher, original base as student) to undo catastrophic forgetting, and introduces CDD, a strictly causal exponential token-weight decay based on cumulative top-k forward KL, as an alternative to FiRe-OPD's trajectory filtering, TOPD's future-window OT alignment, and IW-OPD's min-max normalized weights.

on_policy_mechanism.evidence_quote: Unlike offline SFT distillation, the ”online” nature of OPD ensures that distillation always occurs on

opd_classification.reasoning: Core algorithmic contribution CDD is a per-token weighting scheme for on-policy GKD that down-weights positions after prefix drift; the two-stage PG→GKD curriculum and self-teacher setup are secondary.

train: Synthetic role-play SFT dialogues (Claude 3.7 Sonnet + Qwen2.5-14B user simulator)

key_findings: SFT on role-play data collapses BFCL v4 Overall Acc from 24.83 to 12.53 (8B) and parallel-call sub-metrics to ~0; RL does not recover it (12.55).
OPD Stage 1 (K1/PG) with base as student fully restores BFCL v4 to 24.83, matching the base model, while keeping domain Char-Consist. at 90.12.
OPD-PG barely injects world knowledge (Domain Know. 9.52 vs SFT 38.10, 8B); Stage 2 GKD raises it to 32.86.
With CDD, domain Char-Consist. reaches 92.08±1.45 vs 90.02±2.10 without CDD (8B), the best in the pipeline and above M2-HER's 89.22.
On 4B, CDD improves Domain Know. from 17.14 to 20.00 and Mem-Consist. from 45.00 to 58.75 over GKD without CDD.
Reverse profile filtering improves SFT domain Char-Consist. (90.92 vs 89.20 at 8B; 86.78 vs 86.48 at 4B).
2609.11127.ablations_summary: Stage-wise comparison (SFT→RL→OPD1→OPD2 w/o CDD→OPD2 w/ CDD) shows PG-OPD recovers general agent ability but not world knowledge, GKD recovers knowledge, and CDD adds thoroughness/stability (higher char consistency, lower variance); RPF ablation shows small consistency gains; LoRA vs full SFT shows LoRA fails to inject world knowledge.
limitations: No consistent gains when applying the same pipeline to Qwen3.5-9B, attributed to already-high base character consistency and outdated distilled data
Benchmark and RL rewards do not capture subjective experience such as interestingness
Evaluation restricted to a single game/target domain with internal TRACEbench
failure_modes: OPD-PG cannot transfer world knowledge because the required token sequences never appear in the base student's sampling distribution
Plain GKD-OPD overfits and degrades role-playing capability while learning world knowledge
Teacher top-k distributions on student-drifted prefixes become noisy, diluting gradients (motivating CDD)
Stronger base models (Qwen3.5-9B) show no stable improvement under the current pipeline
2609.11127.relevance_to_opd: Applies on-policy GKD and K1-reward OPD in a reversed direction (domain-adapted teacher → same-size base student) to reverse catastrophic forgetting, and proposes CDD, a causal cumulative-KL token weighting that directly addresses the prefix-drift/position-bias problem in OPD discussed by FiRe-OPD, TOPD and IW-OPD.

2609.14636.title: Know When to Stop, Where to Restart: Accelerating Multi-Turn Agentic On-Policy Distillation
2609.14636.affiliation_primary: University of Science and Technology of China / Ant Group
2609.14636.summary: STRIDE: adaptive early stopping + prefix buffer accelerate multi-turn agentic OPD

method.training_loop: for task: reuse cached prefix up to weakest correct turn k*; student rolls out turns, teacher scores per-turn mean log-prob; stop when cumulative Σl̄_k<λ; token-level OPD loss on retained tokens; record l̄_k
method.loss_formulation: L_{OPD} = \mathbb{E}_{x,y\sim\pi_\theta}\Big[-\sum_t \log\pi_\theta(y_t|y_{<t})\cdot r_t\cdot \mathbb{1}_{trainable}(t)\Big],\; r_t=\log\pi_T(y_t|y_{<t})-\log\pi_\theta(y_t|y_{<t})\ (\text{stop-grad})
method.data_source: Synthesized τ2-bench retail/telecom tasks (Gao et al. 2026 pipeline); dapo-math-17k for math; OpenThought3-8B traces for math SFT init
key_components: per-turn mean teacher log-probability l̄_k as online OOD probe
adaptive early stopping when cumulative teacher log-prob < λ
prefix buffer caching correct prefixes (l̄_k > α) and restarting at weakest correct turn k*=argmin l̄_k
data-driven curriculum sliding training window to later turns
token-level OPD (discount 0) with stop-gradient reward

2609.14636.novelty: Unlike fixed-budget truncation (Fast OPD), offline OPD (Lightning OPD), or hand-designed curricula (TCOD), STRIDE detects the action-locked onset of teacher-signal OOD drift online via the cumulative per-turn teacher log-probability and recovers lost late-turn coverage by restarting rollouts from cached weakest-correct-turn prefixes; also provides an empirical analysis showing cross-turn endorsement loss is locked to the first erroneous action rather than turn index.

on_policy_mechanism.evidence_quote: lets the student generate its own training data and

opd_classification.reasoning: Core contribution is compute-efficiency of OPD (student rollouts scored by teacher log-probs with token-level reverse-KL-style loss) via early stopping and prefix reuse that induces a curriculum, grounded in analysis of teacher-signal failure modes in multi-turn agents.

Retail-domain expert teacher + Telecom-domain expert teacher (unspecified Qwen3)

stabilization_tricks: token-level OPD (discount factor zero, O(T^2) variance)
environment observation tokens masked from loss
prefix-quality threshold α=-0.8 to prevent prefix pollution
early-stopping cumulative sum computed only over newly generated turns
FSDP with parameter and optimizer-state offloading
training_setup.warmup_method: SFT (math setting only: 500 steps on OpenThought3-8B; agentic settings use Qwen3-4B/8B directly)

train: τ2-bench retail synthesized tasks (Gao et al. 2026 pipeline)

benchmarks.name: τ2-bench retail (single-teacher, mean@16, λ=-2 w/ PB)
τ2-bench retail (single-teacher, pass@16, λ=-1 w/ PB)
τ2-bench retail (multi-teacher, Qwen3-4B, mean@4, λ=-2 w/ PB)
τ2-bench telecom (multi-teacher, Qwen3-4B, mean@4, λ=-3 w/ PB)
τ2-bench retail (multi-teacher, Qwen3-8B, mean@4, λ=-3 w/ PB)
τ2-bench telecom (multi-teacher, Qwen3-8B, mean@4, λ=-3 w/ PB)

key_findings: On τ2-bench retail, STRIDE (λ=-1 w/ PB) matches full OPD (0.475 vs 0.477 mean@16), exceeds the 30B teacher (0.461), and attains best pass@16 (0.859) at 3.73× speedup; λ=-2 gives 0.483 (+1.3% over baseline) at 2.34×.
Fixed-budget Fast OPD (2.70×) falls below full OPD (0.434 vs 0.477 mean@16); TCOD-F2B (0.437, 2.01×) and turnOPD (0.434, 1.64×) also remain below baseline.
STRIDE reaches baseline final quality in ~2.85h vs 10.65h for 140 steps of full OPD.
Cross-domain multi-teacher training retains 4.51× speedup with retail 0.599 vs 0.590 baseline; telecom best 0.849 vs 0.853 at 3.96×.
With Qwen3-8B student, STRIDE (λ=-3 w/ PB) reaches 0.673 retail / 0.941 telecom vs full OPD 0.625 / 0.882 at 3.05×.
On math, STRIDE outperforms full OPD on AIME 2025 (0.467 vs 0.458) at 5.10× and on AIME 2024 (0.558 vs 0.546) at 3.08×, while Fast OPD averages below full OPD.

Empirical analysis: per-token KL peaks at +0.62 after ~150 tokens then decays to +0.37 within a turn; cross-turn teacher log-prob is flat (+0.07) but drops sharply at the first erroneous action (Cohen's d +0.30 on l̄_k, -0.33 on KL over 267 failed tasks).
2609.14636.ablations_summary: Prefix buffer improves over early-stopping-only at nearly every λ, with larger gains at more aggressive stopping and on harder telecom; without PB all thresholds fall behind baseline after ~60 steps and λ=-1 becomes unstable, while with PB all thresholds track baseline (robust to λ). λ defines a speed–accuracy Pareto frontier. Disabling α (α=-∞) causes prefix pollution and training collapse; α=-0.8 is a critical safety parameter.
limitations: On the harder telecom domain even the best STRIDE configuration falls short of the full-OPD baseline (0.849 vs 0.853).
The appropriate scale of λ depends on token length of the generation unit and must be chosen per task domain.
In single-turn math, α quality filtering is disabled since a single reasoning error does not imply an unusable prefix.
Experiments truncated to fixed step budgets (140/120/160 steps) rather than run to convergence.
failure_modes: Without α filtering, reused prefixes embed mistaken states, early stopping triggers almost immediately, and effective training length collapses.
Early stopping without prefix buffer loses coverage of later turns; aggressive λ=-1 becomes unstable and lags baseline.
Long-trajectory domains (telecom) advance the training window slowly because each rollout covers a smaller fraction before crossing λ.
