Fixed-budget truncation over-truncates valid trajectories and under-truncates OOD ones.

compute_efficiency.teacher_inference_cost: 1× (live teacher forward on retained prefix only; considered cheap relative to rollout)
compute_efficiency.speedup_vs_baseline: 3.73× (retail, matching quality); up to 5.94× multi-teacher; 5.10× AIME 2025
compute_efficiency.memory_footprint: student on 4 GPUs + teacher on 4 GPUs (separate)

2609.14636.relevance_to_opd: Directly an OPD-efficiency paper: proposes online adaptive truncation of student rollouts and prefix reuse to cut the dominant rollout cost of multi-turn agentic OPD while preserving coverage, and characterizes where/why the teacher's token-level signal becomes unreliable (action-locked OOD drift).

2609.15404.title: Who Teaches Which Token? Verifier-Gated Multi-Expert On-Policy Distillation for Scientific Reasoning
2609.15404.summary: Verifier-gated per-criterion expert routing and token-localized multi-teacher OPD

method.training_loop: Sample G rollouts (GRPO); score criteria; probe experts once per prompt; license expert iff verifier gain>δ; mask bottom-10% teacher logprob tokens; add -w_t*KL as token advantage; GRPO update
method.loss_formulation: L(\theta)=L_{PG}(A^{task};\theta)+\lambda L_{PG}(A^{KD};\theta),\; A^{KD}_t=-w_t\hat{k}_t,\; \hat{k}_t=\min\{e^{\Delta_t}-\Delta_t-1,c\},\; \Delta_t=\log\pi_{E_{k_t}}(y_t|x,y_{<t})-\log\pi_\theta(y_t|x,y_{<t})
method.data_source: Dr.SCI collection mixture (WebInstruct-Verified, NaturalReasoning, MegaScience, RaR-Science) with derived criteria bank and verifiers
key_components: criterion-level verifier licensing gate (counterfactual gain Δ' of expert probe vs rollout)
softmax routing over licensed experts per criterion (τ=0.5)
disagreement localization mask: bottom-η (10%) teacher log-prob tokens dilated ±1
verified-gain weights from rubric importance (square-root compressed)
gated reverse-KL as detached additive token-level advantage inside GRPO
four RL-trained LoRA capability experts (quantitative, symbolic, mechanistic, evidence)

2609.15404.novelty: Unlike MOPD (prompt-level domain routing, uniform token weights) and reward/sign-gated OPD that gate against a single task-level verdict, VG-OPD checks per criterion whether each expert actually beats the student under the same verifier before it may teach, and restricts supervision to tokens the licensed expert disagrees on, weighted by rubric importance.

on_policy_mechanism.evidence_quote: them into the student on its own rollouts. Existing recipes assign supervision at

opd_classification.reasoning: Core contribution is token-level weighting/localization of teacher KL on student rollouts, gated by external verifier feedback and fused into a GRPO objective.

training_setup.compute_budget: 8×40GB GPUs (3 training, 1 expert sidecar, 2 judge); 300 steps at ≈147 s/step for 4B
stabilization_tricks: task-reward stream counterbalances non-positive KD advantage to avoid entropy collapse
pitfall criteria and verifier abstentions excluded from gating
fail-open hook zero-fills weights on error
entropy bonus 0.01, reference-KL penalty 1e-3, PPO clip 0.2

key_findings: VG-OPD ranks first on five of seven benchmarks at both 4B and 8B and second (within half a point) on MMLU-Pro and MATH500.

Over rubric-GRPO, the 4B student gains +2.0 on scientific reasoning, +3.3 on domain science, +0.2 on general reasoning (group averages); 8B gains +1.7 and +1.9 and stays within 0.3 on general reasoning.
Dense distillation inside GRPO drags it below its own floor (GRPO+OPSD 51.6, GRPO+MOPD 50.1 vs GRPO 53.0 on scientific reasoning) while GRPO+VG-OPD reaches 55.0.
Standalone VG-OPD without any task reward (53.1/57.3) matches or exceeds the RL-only floor (53.0/56.0) on both science groups.
Coverage-matched random localization is the most damaging ablation (−6.3/−12.1/−5.6), worse than sequence-level or step-level masks.
88% of licensed criteria are taught by the expert of the prompt's own axis; 12% cross axes.
Teacher-disagreement tokens show log-prob decrease 0.186 after training vs 0.130 at highest-surprisal and 0.039 at random positions.
Full pipeline runs at 146.8 s/step vs 94.7 s for RL-only (+55%).
2609.15404.ablations_summary: Random localization −6.3/−12.1/−5.6 (sci/domain/general), random routing −5.7/−4.0/−3.8, w/o gate −4.4/−1.6/−0.5, uniform weighting −3.6/−2.1/−0.8, sequence-level mask −2.5/−3.3/−0.7, step-level mask −3.5/−2.8/−2.8; finer assignment wins both standalone (OPSD 51.3→MOPD 52.3→VG-OPD 53.1) and inside GRPO.
limitations: Finite set of text-only scientific benchmarks (physics, chemistry, biology, medicine, math); other domains and modalities (figures, molecular structures, experimental data) not covered.
Students limited to 4B and 8B; scaling to stronger students not systematically verified.
Training data mixture is non-commercially encumbered.
No stronger external teacher by construction; teacher-anchored GRPO baseline instantiated with substituted privileged teacher.
failure_modes: Thinking-mode start saturates: no expert can be trained to outscore the student under criterion verifiers, so the gate licenses almost nothing.
Distillation stream alone (A^KD ≤ 0) can continually suppress probability mass and accelerate entropy collapse without the task-reward stream.
LLM judge has 39% false-trigger rate on penalty items, requiring pitfall criteria to be excluded from gating.
Dense/indiscriminate distillation (MOPD, OPSD) inside GRPO lowers accuracy below the RL-only floor.

theory.theoretical_claim: Prop. 1: e^{Δ_t}−Δ_t−1 ≥ 0 with expectation equal to per-position reverse KL, so A^KD ≤ 0 pointwise and total teacher pressure is bounded by s̄·ΣKL_t ≤ ΣKL_t (MOPD)
theory.proof_sketch: e^u ≥ 1+u with equality iff u=0; E_{y_t∼π_θ}[e^{Δ_t}]=1 by full support of softmax policies and E[Δ_t]=−KL_t, giving E[k̂_t]=KL_t; sign follows from w_t ≥ 0 and clamp only lowers k̂_t.

2609.15404.relevance_to_opd: Directly extends multi-teacher on-policy distillation (MOPD) with verifier-gated per-criterion teacher eligibility and disagreement-localized token-level reverse-KL supervision fused into GRPO; provides evidence that placement of teacher signal matters more than amount.

2609.15313.title: Reducing the Output-Mode Gap in Speech Language Models via Joint-Output On-Policy Distillation
2609.15313.summary: Self-teacher OPD closes S2T vs S2TS internal-text accuracy gap in speech LLMs

method.training_loop: Sample S2TS joint trajectories from student; at each text position, frozen base in S2T mode conditions on text-only projection of prefix, gives top-k soft targets; CE on text vocab + non-text preservation vs frozen S2TS reference
method.loss_formulation: L = L_T + L_pres, \quad L_T = \mathbb{E}_{z,i}[\mathrm{CE}(q_i, p_i)], \quad L_pres = \text{weighted reference-to-student CE/KL on non-text (acoustic/control) positions}
method.data_source: 27,847 prompts from Tulu 3 and NaturalReasoning, speech synthesized with flite SLT voice; S2TS trajectories sampled from initial student
key_components: history projection P_T (text-only view of student prefix for S2T teacher)
text-vocabulary-restricted soft top-32 teacher targets (JO-OPD-Soft)
non-text preservation loss vs frozen S2TS reference
trajectory refresh (regenerate from updated student across stages)

2609.15313.novelty: Unlike X-OPD/CORD/X3-OPD which use text-conditioned teachers with matched text inputs, JO-OPD keeps the speech input fixed and uses the model's own S2T policy on a text-only projection of student-generated interleaved histories, restricts distillation to the text vocabulary, and adds a preservation regularizer for acoustic/control tokens; it also identifies and quantifies the output-mode gap (OMG).

on_policy_mechanism.evidence_quote: stronger S2T policy into joint generation using student-generated

opd_classification.reasoning: Student-generated S2TS trajectories (C1) are supervised by soft top-k text distributions (C2) via CE/KL (C3) from the same frozen base model in a different output mode, i.e., self-distillation with asymmetric (text-projected) context, applied to speech LLMs.

stabilization_tricks: non-text preservation loss (weight 0.05 Step-Audio 2; controller 1 / codec 10 Baichuan-Audio)

key_findings: Output-mode gap (S2T minus S2TS internal-text accuracy) is 42.87 pp on Spoken-MQA and 29.72 pp on GSM8K for Step-Audio-2-mini, and 12.41 / 10.39 pp for Baichuan-Audio-Instruct.
JO-OPD-Soft reduces Step-Audio 2 OMG from 42.87 to 16.26 pp on Spoken-MQA and 29.72 to 13.04 pp on GSM8K with S2T accuracy nearly unchanged (75.32→75.18).
Matched Self-SFT worsens S2TS(T) (32.45→23.61) and Response-SFT barely helps (31.60), while JO-OPD-Soft reaches 58.92 on Spoken-MQA.
Soft top-32 targets beat one-hot (JO-OPD-Hard) by 17.97 points on Spoken-MQA and 4.32 on GSM8K.
Spoken-answer (ASR) accuracy on Spoken-MQA rises 7.49 points (28.67→36.16) for Step-Audio 2 and 2.92 for Baichuan-Audio.
Under explicit CoT on human-recorded VoiceBench-BBH, OMG widens from 8.2 to 19.0 pp for the base model; JO-OPD-Soft cuts it to 5.8 pp (+14.7 S2TS(T)).
S2TS(T) accuracy scales with training prompts: 36.95 (2k), 49.71 (8k), 58.92 (27,847).
Refreshing trajectories from the updated student across 4 stages improves S2TS(T) by 2.57 (Spoken-MQA) and 2.73 (GSM8K) points over static initial-student trajectories.
2609.15313.ablations_summary: Soft vs hard targets: +17.97/+4.32 S2TS(T). Full-vocabulary distillation keeps internal-text accuracy (~60.70) but collapses spoken-answer accuracy from 36.16 to 11.20; removing non-text preservation drops it to 29.74. Training-set size monotonically improves S2TS(T); trajectory refresh adds ~2.6 points.
limitations: Training-scale trend under one-epoch training conflates more data with more optimization updates.
Gains on Baichuan-Audio are modest (OMG reduced by 2.92 and 0.61 pp; spoken-answer gains ~1.5 pp over Response-SFT).
Step-Audio 2 shows little spoken-answer change on GSM8K despite large internal-text gains.
Main experiments use fixed trajectories from the initial student rather than continuous on-policy sampling.
failure_modes: Full-vocabulary supervision (no text-vocabulary restriction) destroys spoken-answer accuracy (36.16→11.20) despite good internal text.
Removing the non-text preservation loss degrades speech-generation fidelity (S2TS(S) 36.16→29.74).
Self-SFT on student's own S2TS trajectories reduces S2TS(T) accuracy (32.45→23.61).
Internal-text improvements do not always transfer to spoken answers (Step-Audio 2 GSM8K S2TS(S) flat).
2609.15313.relevance_to_opd: Applies on-policy (student-trajectory) distillation with a self-teacher whose context is a text-only projection of the student's interleaved history, extending OPD to speech LLMs and introducing output-mode gap as a target; contributes vocabulary-restricted soft targets and preservation regularization as stabilization for multi-stream outputs.

2609.16937.title: Beyond Token-Local Imitation: Reward-Compatible Temporal Credit Assignment for On-Policy Distillation
2609.16937.summary: γOPD: discounted temporal credit for OPD plus bounded reward mixing

method.training_loop: Sample prompts, rollout student responses (1/prompt), verify reward R; compute per-token ∆_t=logπθ−logπ*; discounted return-to-go advantage; RBM normalize+softsign+R; policy-gradient update
method.loss_formulation: g_\gamma(\theta) = -\mathbb{E}_{x\sim D, y\sim\pi_\theta}\left[\sum_{t=1}^T \hat A_t^{(\gamma)} \nabla_\theta \log\pi_\theta(y_t|h_t)\right],\; A_t^{(\gamma)} = -\sum_{t'=t}^T \gamma^{t'-t}\Delta_{t'},\; \hat A_t^{(\gamma)} = \frac{A_t^{(\gamma)}}{\frac{1}{T}\sum_k |A_k^{(\gamma)}| + |A_t^{(\gamma)}|} + R(x,y)
method.data_source: DeepMath-103K (difficulty ≥6) for math; Eurus-RL-Code (25K) for code
key_components: Unified temporal-credit view: token-level OPD = stop-gradient truncation of sequence-level reverse-KL gradient
Discount factor γ interpolating token-level (γ=0) and sequence-level (γ=1) OPD credit
Horizon-independent variance bound σ²/(1−γ)²
Reward-Compatible Bounded Mixing (RBM): mean-abs normalization + softsign + verifiable reward {−1,1}
veRL + vLLM implementation, multi-teacher routing by domain

2609.16937.novelty: Unlike prior token-level OPD (local ∆_t only) or sequence-level estimators (full return-to-go with horizon-dependent variance), γOPD introduces a discounted return-to-go over teacher log-ratios with a proven horizon-independent variance bound, and RBM guarantees sign(Â_t)=R(x,y) so the verifier decides reinforce/suppress while the bounded teacher credit only modulates magnitude, at ~0.1% extra compute.

on_policy_mechanism.evidence_quote: It provides dense teacher supervision on trajectories sampled from the

opd_classification.reasoning: Core contribution is a new OPD surrogate objective (discounted teacher log-ratio credit) augmented with verifiable RL rewards via bounded mixing, satisfying student rollouts, teacher logit supervision, and reverse-KL-derived loss.

training_setup.rl_algorithm: REINFORCE-style policy gradient with reverse-KL token advantages + verifiable reward (veRL)
stabilization_tricks: discount factor γ=0.99 on future log-ratio credit
softsign bounding of teacher advantage to (−1,1)

key_findings: Vanilla distillation (Qwen3-4B-Math→Qwen3-4B): γOPD reaches 69.49 avg acc vs 67.04 for vanilla OPD and 68.10 for the teacher, surpassing the teacher; relative gain over strongest baseline 2.30% AvgAcc, 1.80% AvgPass.
Size-mismatch (→Qwen3-1.7B): γOPD achieves 56.51 avg acc vs 53.86 best baseline (AOPD), relative gains of 4.92% AvgAcc / 2.06% AvgPass, though still below the 68.10 teacher.
Multi-teacher (Math+Code teachers → Qwen3-4B): TotalAvg 66.00 vs 64.36 best baseline (ExOPD) and 63.82 teacher; best on HumanEval+ (89.02) and LCB (28.14).
Ablation: temporal discounting alone +2.04 on AIME avg; removing γ from full method drops gain from +3.91 to +2.00; naive reward mixing adds only +0.05 without bounded normalization.
γ=1 (sequence-level) yields much larger gradient norms and rapid entropy collapse; γ=0.99 performs best, above γ=0.9 and γ=0.
Theorem 3.3: Var(A^(1)) ≤ (T−t+1)²σ² (horizon-dependent), Var(A^(γ)) ≤ σ²/(1−γ)² (horizon-independent).
γOPD adds only 0.1064% training time and 0.00046% memory over vanilla OPD.
Token visualizations show A^(0.99) concentrates negative credit on the erroneous formula derivation instead of unrelated tokens.
2609.16937.ablations_summary: On AIME24/25 avg (vanilla OPD 53.65): γ only 55.69 (+2.04); γ+Mix 55.74 (+2.09); Mix+Norm without γ 55.65 (+2.00); full γ+Mix+Norm 57.56 (+3.91). γ sweep on 1.7B student: γ=1 unstable (entropy collapse), γ=0.99 best. Overhead profiling: 610 ms/step extra vs 573,669 ms per OPD update.
limitations: Experiments limited to models with fewer than 10B parameters due to computational constraints
Fixed discount factor; adaptive or entropy-aware discounting left to future work
failure_modes: γ=1 (undiscounted sequence-level credit) produces large gradient norms and rapid entropy collapse on long reasoning trajectories
Naive (unbounded) reward mixing yields only marginal gains (+0.05) since teacher advantage magnitude can dominate the bounded reward
In size-mismatch setting all students including γOPD remain below the teacher

theory.theoretical_claim: Token-level OPD gradient equals sequence-level reverse-KL gradient with stop-gradient on prefix distribution (Props 3.1/3.2); discounted credit has horizon-independent variance bound σ²/(1−γ)² vs (T−t+1)²σ² for sequence-level (Thm 3.3)
theory.proof_sketch: Expand reverse KL, apply score-function identity, drop t'<t terms by conditional zero-mean of score; variance bound via L2 triangle inequality and geometric series in γ.

2609.16937.relevance_to_opd: Directly an OPD methods paper: it reinterprets standard token-level OPD as a truncated sequence-level reverse-KL gradient, proposes a discounted credit-assignment objective with variance guarantees, and integrates RLVR rewards via bounded mixing, benchmarking against ExOPD, REOPOLD, AOPD, TOPD and RL baselines.
comparable_papers: ExOPD (Yang et al. 2026a, Learning beyond teacher: generalized OPD with reward extrapolation)
AOPD (Jia et al. 2026, Asymmetric on-policy distillation)
REOPOLD (Ko et al. 2026, Relaxed on-policy distillation)
TOPD (Zhang et al. 2026, Are full rollouts necessary for OPD?)
Fu et al. 2026 (Revisiting on-policy distillation: failure modes and simple fixes)

2609.16459.title: OPD-Aha: From Linguistic Momentum to Visual Reflection in Multimodal On-Policy Distillation
2609.16459.summary: Real–null intra-teacher contrast reconstructs privileged OPD target, eliciting visual reflection

method.training_loop: for batch: student samples 8 rollouts on full image; frozen teacher (copy of init student) scores prefix w/ privileged crop I+ and mean-RGB null I0; q_t=softmax((1+β)log p+ − β log p0); minimize JSD(q_t, p_student) on top-100+tail; update
method.loss_formulation: L_{OPD-Aha} = \frac{\sum_t M_t \, D_{dist}(q_t, p^S_t)}{\sum_t M_t}, \quad q_t(v)=\frac{p^+_t(v)\exp(\beta u_t(v))}{\sum_w p^+_t(w)\exp(\beta u_t(w))}, \quad u_t(v)=\log p^+_t(v)-\log p^0_t(v)
method.data_source: Vision-OPD-6K (6,241 fine-grained perception training examples with localized evidence crops)
key_components: privileged multimodal on-policy self-distillation (teacher = frozen copy of student with evidence crop)
visual null I0 = mean-RGB replacement of privileged crop
intra-teacher real–null visual preference signal u_t = log p+ − log p0
KL-regularized target reconstruction via exponential tilt with strength β
JSD distillation on student top-100 tokens + tail bucket along unchanged student rollout

2609.16459.novelty: Identifies supervision collapse in privileged OPD (erroneous student prefixes drag teacher to agree with student hallucination) and replaces the fragile teacher–student discrepancy with a same-teacher real-vs-null-image contrast as the source of the distillation target, which selectively suppresses image-inconsistent continuations and induces emergent 'wait/actually' reflection without any explicit reflection supervision.

on_policy_mechanism.evidence_quote: The student optimizes this objective along its own unchanged rollout.

opd_classification.reasoning: Core contribution is a new adaptive per-token distillation target (β-tilted reconstruction from real–null teacher contrast) applied to student's own rollouts with JSD loss, within a privileged-information self-distillation setup for multimodal LLMs.

teacher.name: Qwen3.5-4B (frozen copy of initial student, with privileged evidence crop)
Qwen3.5-9B (frozen copy of initial student, with privileged evidence crop)

stabilization_tricks: KL-regularized target reconstruction anchored to privileged teacher (β controls departure)
distribution support restricted to student top-100 tokens plus one tail bucket
JSD (symmetric) divergence instead of forward/reverse KL

key_findings: OPD-Aha beats Vision-OPD on all six fine-grained benchmarks: Avg6 76.4→80.4 (+4.0) at 4B and 78.2→81.4 (+3.2) at 9B.
Teacher recovery of the correct answer drops from 75.8% with 0% erroneous prefix to 6.0% with 90% retained, and the teacher's decision margin flips negative near the response midpoint.
Reconstructed target maintains over an order of magnitude (up to 17.2×) higher correct-answer probability than the standard privileged target at late-prefix states.
Reconstruction from the real–null contrast (Avg6 78.8 at β=1) far outperforms reconstruction from teacher–student discrepancy (76.9) vs standard target (76.4).
Increasing β from 1 to 4 consistently raises Avg6 (≈78.8→80.4) with a transient response-length spike (~500 tokens) that stabilizes.
Vision-OPD degrades 4B zero-shot reasoning below base on all 8 metrics (e.g., MathVerse 73.6→71.0), while OPD-Aha improves over base on all (75.7).

Reflection emerges because erroneous continuations are suppressed more than reflection tokens, not because reflection probability rises; after reflection, prefix support falls and visual support rises after a short delay.
JSD gives best Avg6 (80.40 at 4B, 81.43 at 9B); forward KL at 9B collapses to 75.23 while reverse KL reaches 80.80.
2609.16459.ablations_summary: Real–null intra-teacher signal (78.8) >> teacher–student discrepancy signal (76.9) > standard privileged target (76.4) at β=1; JSD best divergence but reverse KL also retains gains; all four visual nulls (Gaussian noise 79.8, mismatched image 79.6, black 80.3, mean RGB 80.4) yield similar gains; log-prob vs probability-space reconstruction comparable (78.8 vs 78.7); shuffling token-wise visual preference or using irrelevant crops destroys correction; larger β reverses more hidden wrong teacher preferences (later prefix quartiles require higher β, median threshold 2.24→5.55).
limitations: Later prefix states require stronger reconstruction β; correction weakens as linguistic momentum grows or visual separation shrinks
Reconstruction requires two teacher forward passes (real and null image) per student rollout
Decision-margin separation after reflection remains relatively weak (Appendix B.2)
failure_modes: Standard privileged OPD supervision collapses when erroneous student prefixes make teacher and student converge on the same hallucination
Forward KL at 9B underperforms substantially (75.23 vs 81.43 JSD)
Nonzero u_t is not necessarily corrective; a fixed β may be insufficient for very late erroneous prefixes

compute_efficiency.teacher_inference_cost: 2× teacher forwards per rollout (real crop + visual null), teacher is a frozen copy of the student

theory.theoretical_claim: Exponential-tilt target is the unique global optimum of the KL-regularized visual-alignment objective; explicit β threshold for reversing erroneous teacher preference; expected visual alignment and KL departure increase monotonically in β (derivatives equal Var[u_t] and β·Var[u_t])
theory.proof_sketch: Lagrangian of βE_q[u_t] − KL(q‖p+) with simplex constraint; stationarity gives q ∝ p+ exp(βu_t); strict concavity of −KL plus linearity of alignment term yields uniqueness; pairwise log-odds comparison yields β threshold (Eq. 13); differentiating the exponential family gives variance identities.

2609.16459.relevance_to_opd: Directly extends privileged-information on-policy self-distillation (Vision-OPD line) for multimodal LLMs: diagnoses a failure mode of the teacher–student discrepancy under on-policy prefixes and proposes an alternative distributional target derived from an intra-teacher contrast, distilled via JSD on the student's own rollouts.

2609.18321.title: Trajectory Learnability for Offline On-Policy Distillation with Imperfect Teachers
2609.18321.summary: Learnability-weighted trajectory reweighting for offline OPD under imperfect teachers

method.training_loop: Student ρ generates trajectories once; store frozen-teacher targets + teacher outcome; train π+ on teacher-successful records; score failed trajectories by log π+ − log ρ; tier into weights; run weighted reverse-KL offline OPD
method.loss_formulation: L_{LWD}(\theta)=\sum_{i=1}^{N} w_i \sum_{t=1}^{T_i} d_{i,t}(\theta),\quad d_{i,t}=D_{KL}(\pi_\theta(\cdot|s_{i,t})\|\pi_T(\cdot|s_{i,t})),\quad w_i=1 \text{ if } c_i=1,\ \omega_{b_i} \text{ if } c_i=0
method.data_source: DAPO-Math-17K (math) and 30K function-generation subset of EpiCoder-300K (code); student-generated trajectories with stored Qwen3-8B teacher targets
key_components: offline records of student trajectories + frozen teacher targets + independent teacher outcome label
successful-only learning to obtain reference checkpoint π+
token-level learnability signal ℓ_{i,t}=log π+(a|s) − log ρ(a|s), clipped to [−4,4], 33-token moving average
trajectory-level mean/variation standardized within teacher-failed set, mapped to low/mid/high tiers
bounded tier weights (0.15/0.25/0.35) scaling the original token-level OPD loss

2609.18321.novelty: Unlike ReNIO/FiRe-OPD/RA-OPD which reweight using student–teacher probabilities, rewards or continuation-based reliability estimates, LWD uses a cheap successful-only reference update and likelihood changes on stored tokens to grade how much teacher-failed supervision to retain, requiring no new rollouts and preserving token-level OPD structure in an offline setting.

on_policy_mechanism.evidence_quote: generated; only the subset used for this auxiliary distillation is selected by the teacher outcome.

opd_classification.reasoning: Core contribution is a trajectory-level weighting scheme applied to the reverse-KL OPD loss on student-generated (offline-collected) trajectories with frozen teacher token distributions, i.e., a weighting/efficiency technique for OPD.

training_setup.compute_budget: 2 GPUs × 10.98 wall-clock hours ≈ 21.90 GPU hours (vs 10.64 for Lightning-OPD, 36.28–47.69 for online OPD)
stabilization_tricks: global scale so average failed-record weight = 0.25

key_findings: At 4B, LWD improves the offline Lightning-OPD baseline on all five benchmarks: +2.7 AIME24 (66.4→69.1), +2.0 AIME25, +1.6 HMMT25, +1.9 LCB v5, +1.7 LCB v6, and is best among all online/offline methods on every benchmark.
Teacher-failed supervision should be neither fully retained nor discarded: average math score is 55.0 (full), 55.5 (zero), 56.4 (shared reduced), 57.1 (learnability-based).
Trajectory-level tiered weighting (57.1 avg) beats token-level (55.4/56.2), span-level (56.1/56.6) and continuous trajectory weighting (56.7).
LWD uses 2 GPUs and 21.90 GPU hours vs 3 GPUs and 36.28–47.69 GPU hours for online selective OPD methods; per-step cost is unchanged (2.14 vs 2.13 min/step).
At 1.7B, LWD is best on all three math benchmarks but online OPD variants remain slightly stronger on code (7.5–7.6 vs 6.2 on LCB v5).
2609.18321.ablations_summary: Failed-case weighting ablation: full 55.0 < zero 55.5 < shared reduced 56.4 < learnability-based 57.1 avg. Granularity ablation: tiered trajectory weighting is most consistent (57.1) vs token/span/continuous variants (55.4–56.7); dense span gives best single HMMT25 (43.1) but is inconsistent.
limitations: Code teacher-success labels measure format validity (normal termination and program extraction) rather than functional correctness.
The successful-only stage roughly doubles offline training cost (10.64→21.90 GPU hours) relative to Lightning-OPD.
Learnability signal does not label tokens as correct nor estimate the utility of the teacher target; first-order interpretation is approximate.
failure_modes: Token- or span-level learnability weighting reshapes token-level OPD supervision and is inconsistent across benchmarks.
At the 1.7B scale on code generation, online OPD variants remain slightly stronger than LWD.
Low learnability can occur exactly where the student deviates and corrective teacher supervision is still useful.

compute_efficiency.speedup_vs_baseline: ~1.7–2.2× fewer GPU hours than online OPD (21.90 vs 36.28–47.69); ~2× more than Lightning-OPD
compute_efficiency.memory_footprint: 2 GPUs (no separate teacher GPU during training)

theory.theoretical_claim: First-order expansion: trajectory-mean learnability ℓ̄_i ≈ Δθᵀ∇_θ f_i(θ_ρ), i.e., alignment between the successful-only update and the direction increasing stored-trajectory likelihood
theory.proof_sketch: Define f_i(θ)=(1/T_i) log π_θ(τ_i|x_i) and Δθ=θ_+−θ_ρ; Taylor-expand f_i around θ_ρ to obtain ℓ̄_i = Δθᵀ∇f_i(θ_ρ) + O(‖Δθ‖²), while the exact identity ℓ̄_i=(1/T_i) log[π_+(τ_i|x_i)/ρ(τ_i|x_i)] holds since both score the same autoregressive sequence.

2609.18321.relevance_to_opd: Directly extends offline on-policy distillation (Lightning-OPD): student-generated trajectories with stored frozen-teacher reverse-KL targets, adding trajectory-level supervision weighting to handle imperfect teacher supervision without additional rollouts.

2609.18310.title: SEA-LION-v4.8: A Technical Report
2609.18310.summary: SEA-LION-v4.8: Nemotron-3 CPT + async SFT/on-policy distillation for SEA languages

method.training_loop: CPT on 150B SEA tokens; then async loop: env interaction → student response → token-exact capture → teacher top-k reverse-KL + SFT loss → update → new rollouts
method.loss_formulation: L = L_SFT(D_SFT) + KL(p_student || p_teacher_topk) on student trajectories τ ~ p_θt (reverse KL, top-k teacher logits)
method.data_source: 150B-token CPT corpus (SEA-Instruct, reasoning/code, bilingual parallel); post-training prompts from aisingapore/SEA-Instruct-2602; online trajectories from ~3,000 agent environments (≥100k sessions)
key_components: continued pre-training with WSD no-decay on Nemotron 3 Nano/Super
asynchronous decoupled pipeline: environment-agent orchestrator, Conductor token-exact capture, SGLang serving/reward fleet, AutoModel trainer
online on-policy distillation with reverse KL over teacher top-k (Nemotron-3-Ultra-550B-A55B teacher)
joint SFT + OPD training stream
staleness window of 32 with token-level versioning
post-training checkpoint merging with Nemotron 3.5 Lightning / Nemotron 3 Super

2609.18310.novelty: Model release / system report: applies existing reverse-KL on-policy distillation at scale via an asynchronous, decoupled agent-environment training system for Southeast Asian language adaptation of Nemotron 3 MoE models; no new distillation objective is proposed.

on_policy_mechanism.evidence_quote: Unlike conventional offline distillation, these trajectories are not generated once and stored as a fixed dataset. Instead, the current student model generates new trajectories throughout training.

opd_classification.reasoning: System/model-release technical report that uses off-the-shelf reverse-KL on-policy distillation (student rollouts + 550B teacher top-k logits) as a component but proposes no novel distillation algorithm or objective (Pattern 4).

training_setup.compute_budget: 30B: 16 train + 48 reward + 8 serving H200 × 12h (1200 steps); 120B: 48 train + 48 reward + 16 serving H200 × 24h (1600 steps); CPT: 32×H200 × 114.23h (30B) / 186.65h (120B)
stabilization_tricks: staleness window: train only tokens with staleness ≤32, mask others
top-k teacher outputs compressed/binarized, only unmasked positions scored
pack rollouts with off-policy reference answer from same prompt in same batch
joint SFT loss on offline data
post-training model merging with Nemotron 3.5 Lightning / Nemotron 3 Super

train: 150B-token CPT corpus (SEA-Instruct, OpenMathInstruct2, Nemotron-sft, Reasoning-Base, code, Finetranslations parallel, Megawika)

benchmarks.name: SEA-HELM overall SEA score (30B-A3B vs Nemotron 3 Nano)
SEA-HELM overall SEA score (120B-A12B vs Nemotron 3 Super)

key_findings: 30B-A3B improves overall SEA-HELM from 46.89 (Nemotron 3 Nano) to 51.57; 120B-A12B improves from 49.30 to 63.44.
Largest gains in low-resource scripts: 120B Burmese 4.98→31.35, Tamil 21.83→56.35, Thai 56.61→68.66, Vietnamese 55.31→70.36.
30B Tamil NLU jumps from 19.38 to 75.26; 120B Tamil NLU from 17.89 to 80.04.
120B-A12B shows broader, more consistent gains across Cultural, Instruction Following, Knowledge, NLR, NLU than 30B-A3B.
Post-training system sustains ~3,000 concurrent agent instances and >100,000 interaction sessions with reverse-KL top-k OPD from a 550B-A55B teacher.
Reported deltas conflate CPT + SFT/OPD + merging; no isolated OPD ablation.
2609.18310.ablations_summary: No ablations isolating OPD vs SFT vs CPT vs merging; only comparisons against Nemotron 3 Nano/3.5 Lightning/3 Super baselines.
limitations: Original Nemotron tokenizer retained; Khmer, Lao, Tamil require ~5× more tokens, limiting adaptation efficiency
Filipino not explicitly in CPT corpus; gains rely on cross-lingual transfer
Gains not uniform: cultural, generation, safety, knowledge, multi-turn tasks show language-dependent trade-offs
Evaluation covers only seven SEA languages
failure_modes: Burmese and Tamil remain weak in absolute terms, especially at 30B (Burmese 10.61)
30B model regresses vs baselines on some Cultural (Thai, Vietnamese), Knowledge (Malay, Thai), Safety (Indonesian, Malay) and Multi-turn (Malay, Thai) tasks
Safety scores of 0.00 persist for Burmese and Tamil at 30B
2609.18310.relevance_to_opd: Large-scale production deployment of on-policy distillation (reverse KL over teacher top-k, student-generated agentic trajectories, 550B MoE teacher → 30B/120B MoE students) with an asynchronous decoupled infrastructure; useful as an applied/system reference for OPD at scale rather than a methodological contribution.

2609.20784.title: RetireOPD: Self-Retiring On-Policy Distillation for Agentic Reinforcement Learning
2609.20784.summary: Adaptive online retirement of a GRPO-trained privileged-skill teacher in joint GRPO+OPD agent training

method.training_loop: Phase1: train skill-conditioned teacher w/ GRPO; Phase2: student rollouts → GRPO + λ·reverse-KL to frozen teacher; every W steps check discrepancy stagnation & SR ratio → drop OPD, continue GRPO
method.loss_formulation: L_{student}(\theta)=L_{GRPO}(\theta)+\lambda L_{OPD}(\theta),\; L_{OPD}=\mathbb{E}_{y\sim\pi_\theta}\frac{1}{|y|}\sum_t D_{KL}(\pi_\theta(\cdot|x,y_{<t})\|\pi_T(\cdot|x,c^+,y_{<t})),\; \Delta_t=\log\pi_T(y_t|x,c^+,y_{<t})-\log\pi_\theta(y_t|x,y_{<t});\; retire\ when\ \rho_m\ge\delta \wedge \eta_m\ge\gamma
method.data_source: ALFWorld and WebShop environments with environment rewards; SkillBank from SkillRL as privileged skill context (keyword-matching retrieval)
key_components: Privileged teacher construction (skill-conditioned GRPO-trained teacher, frozen)
Joint GRPO + reverse-KL OPD on student-generated trajectories (sampled-token approximation)
Adaptive Retirement criterion: discrepancy-change ρ ≥ δ and relative competence η ≥ γ
Post-retirement GRPO-only training

2609.20784.novelty: Unlike SDAR/OPSD which share one policy for teacher and student, RetireOPD decouples and RL-trains the skill-conditioned teacher before distillation; unlike fixed annealing (ATOD) or two-stage schedules, it decides the global OPD→RL transition online from teacher-student discrepancy stagnation and student/teacher success-rate ratio, removing the teacher entirely.

on_policy_mechanism.evidence_quote: Theteacherprovidessupervisiondirectlyonstatesvisitedbythestudentanddoesnotgeneratea

opd_classification.reasoning: Core contribution is an adaptive curriculum/schedule for when to remove on-policy KL teacher supervision (plus building a reliable privileged-information teacher), with student rollouts, teacher logit supervision, and reverse-KL loss all present.

stabilization_tricks: sampled-token single-sample Monte Carlo estimate of reverse KL
window-averaged discrepancy (W=5) and two-window averaged success rate to avoid transient-triggered retirement

key_findings: RetireOPD improves ALFWorld success over GRPO by +17.0/+18.8/+14.1 points on Qwen2.5-1.5B/3B/7B and WebShop accuracy by +19.0/+14.0/+11.8.
The student surpasses its own skill-conditioned teacher in every setting (e.g., 3B: 93.8% vs teacher 79.7% on ALFWorld; 77.3% vs 64.8% on WebShop).
Unoptimized skill-prompted teachers are unreliable: 3B/7B reach only 28.9%/23.4% on ALFWorld with skills; after GRPO training they reach 79.7%/90.6%.
Retaining OPD throughout training yields 82.8% vs 92.2% with adaptive retirement (3B ALFWorld); GRPO-only gives 75.0%.
After the retirement point, continuing GRPO alone raises SR from 76.6% to 93.8%, while continued joint training plateaus and switching to pure OPD degrades.
Retirement step is robust: stays within ±5 steps for γ∈[0.80,0.96] and δ∈[−0.10,0.04]; SR ranges 89.1–92.2% across threshold settings.
Adaptive retirement beats ATOD-style linear annealing, which plateaus later in training.
Retirement point varies from step 50 to 90 across models/tasks (n*=60–90), so no single fixed schedule fits all.
2609.20784.ablations_summary: Teacher construction: RL-trained skilled teachers vastly outperform prompted ones and yield stronger students; with retirement the Skill-3B vs Skill-7B teacher gap shrinks (92.2 vs 91.4). Retiring criteria: removing either the stagnation or competence criterion drops SR from 92.2 to 89.0; no retirement gives 82.8; no OPD gives 75.0. Threshold sensitivity (γ, δ) shifts retire step 55–95 with SR 89.1–92.2. Adaptive retirement outperforms linear annealing.
limitations: Method requires an extra teacher training phase with GRPO before distillation
Retirement relies on validation success-rate monitoring and hyperparameters γ, δ, W
Evaluated only on Qwen2.5 Instruct models (1.5B–7B) and two text agent environments
failure_modes: Pure OPD/OPSD without rewards plateaus at low ceilings (e.g., OPSD 14.1–32.8% ALFWorld)
Distilling from larger unoptimized skill-prompted teachers (OPD-3B/7B/14B) performs poorly
Keeping teacher supervision after the student internalizes skills constrains reward optimization (gradient conflict)
Teacher assigns strong negative scores to task-correct student actions late in training (Figure 9)

theory.theoretical_claim: First-order analysis: non-decreasing teacher-student KL discrepancy implies ⟨g,h⟩ ≥ λ‖h‖² (local GRPO-OPD gradient conflict), and under conflict teacher exit yields ηλ⟨g,h⟩ larger first-order return improvement than joint update
theory.proof_sketch: Expand J(θ+ηΔ) to first order with Δ=g−λh; dD/dt=⟨g,h⟩−λ‖h‖²; compare J(θ_exit)−J(θ_joint)=ηλ⟨g,h⟩+O(η²).

2609.20784.relevance_to_opd: Directly addresses privileged-information self-teacher OPD for multi-turn agents (joint GRPO+reverse-KL OPD on student rollouts) and contributes an online criterion for when to stop distillation, plus evidence that PI teachers must be RL-trained to be reliable.

2609.20511.title: When EOS Tokens Disagree: Understanding Length Inflation in On-Policy Distillation
2609.20511.affiliation_primary: University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill
2609.20511.summary: EOS-token mismatch causes OPD length inflation; semantic EOS aggregation fixes it

method.training_loop: for step: student samples 4 responses/prompt on 16 prompts; teacher scores sampled tokens; A_t=logπE−logπθ (EOS tokens aggregated into shared 'stop' action); policy-gradient update
method.loss_formulation: g_t = A_t \nabla_\theta \log \pi_\theta(y_t|s_t),\; A_t = \log \pi^E(y_t|s_t) - \log \pi_\theta(y_t|s_t);\; \text{Fix 3: } \bar\pi(\text{stop}|s_t)=\sum_{e\in E_{EOS}} \pi(e|s_t)
method.data_source: DAPO-Math-17K prompts; student on-policy rollouts
key_components: sampled-token OPD (reverse-KL per-token signal on student rollouts)
Fix 1: shared-set decoding (insufficient)
Fix 2: teacher-side EOS probability mapping to canonical student EOS
Fix 3: semantic EOS class (aggregate termination-equivalent tokens into one stop action)
Fix 4: canonical single-EOS action space with renormalization
stage-wise analysis across K2-Horizon pretrain/midtrain/SFT/final checkpoints
template and grader sensitivity analysis

2609.20511.novelty: Identifies termination-token mismatch between base students and post-trained teachers (even with identical declared EOS sets, e.g. Gemma 3) as a direct cause of OPD length inflation, shows decoding-set alignment alone is insufficient, and systematically compares four probability-level termination alignments across Qwen3, Llama, Gemma; also reveals a residual late-stage re-inflation not explained by EOS mismatch and proves local OPD omits a nonnegative stopping-logit pressure relative to trajectory-level reverse KL.

on_policy_mechanism.evidence_quote: We use sampled token OPD. Student responses are generated on policy, and the distillation signal at each generated token is given by the teacher and student log probability difference on that token.

opd_classification.reasoning: The paper's core contribution is diagnosing a failure mode (EOS mismatch-induced length inflation) of sampled-token OPD and comparing objective-level termination corrections, i.e. an analysis of OPD failure modes with a stability fix.

training_setup.compute_budget: 4× NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 (96GB) per experiment, 200 steps (400 for K2 Pretrain-to-Final)

benchmarks.name: Avg@16 macro-average over AIME24/AIME25/AMC23 (Qwen3-1.7B-Base ← Qwen3-4B, DAPO grader)

key_findings: Under vanilla OPD, Qwen3-1.7B-Base student's probability on its native <|endoftext|> EOS falls from ~0.8 to near zero while it assigns ~1e-11 to teacher-preferred <|im_end|>, causing responses to hit the 7,168-token budget.
Inflated responses contain the correct answer early (e.g., after 462–1,094 tokens) then emit 7,098–7,730 redundant tokens (86.6–94.4% of the response).

Fix 1 (adding teacher EOS to decoding stop set) tracks vanilla OPD and fails; Fixes 2–4 (probability-level alignment) keep length/clipping near teacher reference and prevent termination-probability collapse.
Gemma 3 PT/IT share the same declared EOS set yet the student prefers <eos> while the teacher prefers <end_of_turn>; semantic aggregation recovers termination without forcing surface-token agreement.

K2-Horizon Pretrain-to-Final shows late-stage (Phase 3) re-inflation and termination collapse even with semantic EOS correction, indicating mechanisms beyond EOS mismatch; midtrain/SFT initializations show no collapse.
Original DAPO grader underestimates Qwen3-4B teacher at 6.28% Avg@16 vs 24.34% with format-compatible parsing; OPD accuracy gains persist despite severe length inflation under TTRL evaluation.
2609.20511.ablations_summary: Four termination-handling strategies compared on Qwen3: shared-set decoding is insufficient; teacher-side EOS mapping, semantic EOS class, and canonical single-EOS action space behave similarly and mitigate inflation. Semantic EOS is validated on Llama 3.2 and Gemma 3 (Llama retains larger residual gap). Non-interference check on K2-Horizon midtrain/SFT shows correction is inert when termination already aligned. Template ablation: DAPO-trained models produce shorter responses; TTRL evaluation yields higher measured accuracy; length and accuracy partially decoupled.
limitations: EOS mismatch is an important but not exhaustive explanation; late-stage K2-Horizon re-inflation persists under semantic correction and its mechanism is left to future work.
Experiments limited to single-turn math reasoning; semantic EOS classes may not transfer to multi-turn/agentic settings where special tokens have distinct control-flow semantics.
Prompt-template/grader analysis limited to Qwen3 with three templates and two graders; generalization to Llama/Gemma not established.
Full-vocabulary OPD not evaluated due to computational cost.
failure_modes: Vanilla sampled-token OPD when student and teacher place termination mass on different EOS tokens: student EOS suppressed, teacher EOS not transferred, budget saturation with repetition.
Late-stage re-inflation in K2-Horizon Pretrain-to-Final even after EOS alignment: termination probability collapses again.
Early transient length growth after EOS correction, pronounced in Llama 3.2 and Gemma 3; Llama accuracy remains near zero throughout training.
Termination improvements do not necessarily yield downstream accuracy gains (Gemma/Llama/K2 show modest, model-dependent changes).

theory.theoretical_claim: Proposition 1: local sampled-token OPD applies weakly less upward pressure to the stopping logit than the trajectory-consistent reverse-KL update, with gap Δ*_e(s) − Δ^OPD_e(s) = p_θ(s) C_θ(s) ≥ 0
theory.proof_sketch: Trajectory-level reverse-KL coefficient A*_t = log πE/πθ − V_θ(f(s_t,y_t)) differs from local OPD by the successor KL; via softmax coupling ∂logπ(y)/∂z(b)=1{y=b}−π(b), the expected update difference on the stop logit is π(e|s)[C_θ(s) − V_θ(†)] = p_θ(s)C_θ(s) since V_θ(†)=0; vanishes as V_θ→0.

2609.20511.relevance_to_opd: Directly studies sampled-token OPD (Thinking Machines-style reverse-KL on student rollouts), diagnosing an implementation-level failure mode (termination-token mismatch) that produces length inflation, and provides objective-level corrections; complementary to prior OPD length-inflation analyses (Luo et al., Li et al., Zhao et al., Fu et al.).

2609.23038.title: Spatial-Interactor: Learning Spatial Reasoning through Interaction with the Observable Physical World
2609.23038.summary: Interaction-trajectory curriculum + privileged on-policy self-distillation for VLM spatial reasoning

method.training_loop: Stage1: SFT on L1/L2 transition QA. Stage2: for each prompt sample G=8 student rollouts; snapshot teacher (same weights + privileged trace z) scores same prefixes; GRPO reward + λ_t·forward-KL on reasoning tokens + β·KL(ref)
method.loss_formulation: L_{OPD} = L_{answer} + \beta L_{KL\text{-}ref} + \lambda_t L_{process},\; L_{process}=\mathrm{KL}\big(sg[\pi_{\theta^-}(\cdot|x,z,y_{<t})] \,\|\, \pi_\theta(\cdot|x,y_{<t})\big) \text{ on teacher top-100 support, reasoning tokens only}
method.data_source: LSI-108K (simulated AI2-THOR/ProcTHOR/HSSD/Replica/SIMS-V + real ScanNet/ScanNet++/MultiScan/ARKitScenes/RoomTour3D/BridgeData V2) plus 80K public spatial QA (VSI-590K, MindCube, VSTI-Bench)
key_components: three-level curriculum (L1 passive world-state, L2 active self-state, L3 long-horizon)
LSI-108K verifiable QA dataset
privileged state-transition trace z from frozen VLM annotator
on-policy same-prefix distillation with stop-gradient snapshot teacher conditioned on z
forward KL on teacher top-k support, reasoning tokens only
verifiable GRPO answer reward + frozen SFT reference KL
linearly decayed process-loss coefficient

2609.23038.novelty: Instead of static spatial QA, uses interaction triplets (O_t, a_t, O_{t+1}) as direct supervision for state transitions, and adds a privileged-information self-teacher (same policy snapshot given segment-level transition descriptions) that supervises the student's own on-policy CoT via KL, isolated against a matched GRPO baseline.

on_policy_mechanism.evidence_quote: OPD supervises reasoning prefixes sampled by the current student policy.

opd_classification.reasoning: Student generates on-policy rollouts, a privileged-information self-teacher (policy snapshot conditioned on training-only transition trace) provides forward-KL supervision on the same student prefixes, combined with GRPO verifiable reward; the teacher is distinct from the reference-KL anchor, though the process weight is small (λ=0.05) and gains over GRPO are modest.

stabilization_tricks: stop-gradient snapshot teacher refreshed each update (not EMA)
forward KL restricted to teacher top-100 non-special tokens, renormalized
process loss masked to reasoning tokens only
λ_t schedule: 0.05 fixed 100 steps then linear decay to 0 at step 1200

train: LSI-108K (L1/L2: 82,596 examples for SFT; L3: 10,712 RoomTour + 10,783 VSTI-Bench long-horizon for OPD)

benchmarks.name: Overall, Qwen2.5-VL-7B (Full SFT+GRPO vs Full SFT+OPD)
VSI-Bench Route Planning, Qwen2.5-VL-7B (GRPO vs OPD)
VSTI-Bench Camera Displacement, Qwen2.5-VL-7B (GRPO vs OPD)

key_findings: Spatial-Interactor improves Overall by 16.4–25.0 points over Base across Qwen2.5-VL-3B/7B and Qwen3-VL-4B/8B; the 8B model reaches best Overall 65.9.
Starting from the same Full-SFT checkpoint (58.4), GRPO reaches 59.2 while OPD reaches 60.1, with OPD exceeding GRPO by 5.1 on Route Planning and 3.1 on Camera Displacement.
OPD adds 1.0–1.4 Overall points over the SFT checkpoint on four held-out cross-benchmarks for every backbone.
During OPD, mean on-policy task reward rises 6.8–8.9 points and divergence between plain and privileged branches falls 27–56% while rollout entropy stays nonzero.
Inference-time ordered 4-segment trace raises frozen SFT camera-displacement score from 32.6 to 35.4; shuffled trace gives 33.8, 8 segments give 35.3.
Frame shuffling drops Spatial-Interactor-3B/7B by 6.6/7.0 points vs 0.9/0.8 for Base, indicating stronger use of temporal order.
Closed-loop: WalkerBench success 7.0→14.0 with mean actions 17.71→6.52; ESI-Bench 32.9→41.2.
2609.23038.ablations_summary: External-data SFT 35.1→56.0; adding interaction L1/L2 data →58.4 (+1.4–3.9 per benchmark); GRPO →59.2; OPD →60.1 with largest gains on long-horizon tasks. Sequential L1→L2 curriculum is the only configuration improving all four held-out benchmarks (44.1→49.8). Trace order matters more than segment count.
limitations: Future work needed on adaptive trajectory segmentation (fixed four uniform intervals used)
More diverse real interactions needed
SpatialLadder remains strongest on SPBench-MV
Privileged trace and teacher usable only in training; requires a frozen strong VLM annotator
failure_modes: OPD gain over matched GRPO is small in Overall (0.9 points) with λ=0.05 process weight
Several ESI-Bench categories regress vs Base (Connectivity 53.3→40.0, Long-Term Navigation 20.0→6.7, Inclined Plane 16.7→6.7, Traversable Passage 40.0→20.0)
Most cross-benchmark transfer comes from SFT; OPD adds only 1.0–1.4 points
2609.23038.relevance_to_opd: A privileged-information on-policy self-distillation variant for VLMs: the teacher is a stop-gradient snapshot of the student given training-only transition descriptions, supervising the student's own reasoning tokens via forward KL inside GRPO; extends PI-teacher OPD (Self-distilled reasoner, Uni-OPD, Vision-OPD) to long-horizon spatial video reasoning.

2609.23697.title: Distill What You Trust: Reliability-Aware Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation
2609.23697.affiliation_primary: University of Science and Technology of China / Tencent
2609.23697.summary: Label-free token-level teacher weighting for multi-teacher OPD via RL displacement

method.training_loop: Sample y~π_θ(x); at each prefix compute each teacher's centered log-ratio vs shared pre-RL ref, norm ρ, calibrate r=ρ/μ_k, power-normalize to w_k,t; minimize Σ_t Σ_k w_k,t KL(p_θ||q_k)
method.loss_formulation: L_{MOPD}(\theta;w) = E_{x\sim D, y\sim\pi_\theta(\cdot|x)}\left[\frac{1}{|y|}\sum_{t=1}^{|y|}\sum_{k=1}^{K} w_{k,t} D_{KL}(p_{\theta,t}\|q_{k,t})\right],\; w_{k,t}=\frac{(\rho_{k,t}/\mu_k)^\gamma}{\sum_j(\rho_{j,t}/\mu_j)^\gamma},\; \rho_{k,t}=\|\log\frac{q_{k,t}}{q_{ref,t}}-\overline{\log\frac{q_{k,t}}{q_{ref,t}}}\|_2
method.data_source: SINGLECAP (7,458 prompts sampled from OpenMOPD: 1,540 math, 1,870 code, 4,048 IF) and MULTICAP (math/code prompts augmented with verifiable instruction constraints following MathIF)
key_components: RL displacement from shared pre-RL reference as local reliability proxy (centered log-ratio L2 norm)
Offline per-teacher calibration constant μ_k estimated once on unlabeled student rollouts
Power normalization with sharpness γ to simplex-valued token-level teacher weights
Reverse-KL multi-teacher OPD objective with weights treated as constants (no gradient through allocation)
No domain labels, router, or auxiliary model required

2609.23697.novelty: Replaces example-level, label-dependent one-hot teacher routing in MOPD/Open-MOPD with label-free, state-dependent token-level supervision allocation derived from each specialist's KL displacement from the shared pre-RL reference, with a theoretical link between displacement and the RL soft advantage contrast.

on_policy_mechanism.evidence_quote: On-policydistillation(OPD)trainsastudentonitsownrolloutsbyqueryingtheteacheratstudent-generatedprefixes

opd_classification.reasoning: Student generates rollouts, K white-box RL-specialist teachers provide per-token distributions on those prefixes, and the loss is a per-token adaptively-weighted reverse KL mixture across teachers, making it an adaptive multi-teacher OPD objective.

stabilization_tricks: weights sum to one per token so total supervision mass and update scale unchanged
allocation weights treated as constants (no gradient through allocation)

key_findings: On SINGLECAP, TrustMOPD reaches 30.04±0.47 Overall (+5.15 over init), only 0.14 below label-based MOPD (30.18±0.25) and 2.09 above the strongest label-free baseline (Uniform), raising recovery ratio from 54.4% to 91.5%.
On MULTICAP, TrustMOPD reaches 30.41±0.60 Overall (+5.52), 2.45 above the best label-free baseline (Random), raising recovery ratio from 54.5% to 98.0%.
Without labels, math/code/IF teachers receive mean weights 0.69/0.65/0.99 on their own domains, and the correct-teacher margin is positive for 98%/91%/100% of rollouts.
Random token-level weights independent of the prefix perform no better than uniform weighting, indicating the value lies in conditioning on the student's generation state.
Replacing RL displacement with confidence, negative entropy, or teacher-student KL reduces Overall by 1.63–2.08 (SINGLECAP) and 1.48–3.06 (MULTICAP).
Removing calibration μ_k costs 1.28 points on MULTICAP (0.31 on SINGLECAP); response-level allocation costs 0.92 (0.05 on SINGLECAP).
Transfers to DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-7B (+7.49 SINGLECAP, +6.30 MULTICAP) and to independently sourced prompts (+4.58, +4.30).
2609.23697.ablations_summary: RL displacement is the best reliability proxy versus confidence/entropy/teacher-student KL; per-teacher calibration and token-level (vs response-level) allocation matter mainly on multi-capability prompts; γ sweep (3–9) beats Uniform everywhere, with MULTICAP peaking at γ=7 (5.52) and dropping to 4.87 at γ=9.
limitations: Assumes all teachers are RL fine-tunes of the same shared pre-RL reference so displacement is well-defined.
Excessive allocation sharpness (large γ) can amplify errors in ρ and suppress complementary teachers on MULTICAP.
Gains decrease when training prompts come from sources other than the teachers' RL training distribution.
Code-teacher margins are more dispersed than math/IF, indicating weaker alignment for code.
failure_modes: Over-concentrated allocation (γ=9) degrades MULTICAP performance despite higher concentration
Single-teacher distillation harms out-of-domain capabilities (e.g., IF teacher lowers math to 16.41 and code to 15.60)
Teacher-student divergence is unreliable as a reliability signal since it varies with student capability and training stage

theory.theoretical_claim: Theorem 1: if a teacher is the converged optimum of finite-horizon KL-regularized RL from π_ref with coefficient β_k, the centered log-ratio d_k,t(v) equals the mean-centered optimal soft utility contrast (Q*_k(s_t,v)−Q̄*)/β_k and ρ_k,t its L2 norm over β_k; Corollary 1: dividing by frozen μ_k cancels the KL scale so allocation favors the specialist with largest utility contrast relative to its calibrated baseline.
theory.proof_sketch: Uses the closed-form of the KL-regularized optimal policy π_k ∝ π_ref exp(Q*/β_k); taking log-ratio and centering over the vocabulary removes the state-dependent log-partition term, leaving the centered utility scaled by 1/β_k.

2609.23697.relevance_to_opd: Directly extends multi-teacher on-policy distillation (MOPD/Open-MOPD) with a label-free, state-dependent token-level allocation of reverse-KL supervision across white-box RL-specialist teachers, addressing teacher selection at each student-visited state.
comparable_papers: MOPD: Multi-teacher on-policy distillation (Ma et al., 2026)
TIP: Token importance in OPD (Xu et al., 2026)

2609.23435.title: Tool-Augmented On-Policy Distillation for LLM Domain Adaptation in Sequence-Based Omics Tasks
2609.23435.summary: OmicsBench reasoning benchmark + tool-agent-privileged on-policy self-distillation (TA-OPD)

method.training_loop: for batch: student samples response to (instruction, sequence); frozen same-init teacher sees agent answer+evidence; per-token r_t=logπ_T−logπ_S (k1); policy-gradient update student
method.loss_formulation: L = -\mathbb{E}_{y\sim\pi_\theta}\Big[\sum_t \big(\log \pi_T(y_t|x,\text{priv},y_{<t}) - \log \pi_\theta(y_t|x,y_{<t})\big)\Big] \text{ (sampled-token } k_1 \text{ reverse-KL estimator, policy gradient)}
method.data_source: TA-OPD-10K: 10,069 records from Biology-Instructions training split with Biomni (DeepSeek-V4-Flash) agent answers+evidence filtered by answer-label consistency gate
key_components: OPSD-style same-weight frozen teacher with privileged information
tool-augmented Biomni agent (DeepSeek-V4-Flash) generating answers + biological evidence as privileged context
answer-label consistency gate + minority-class oversampling
sampled-token k1 log-ratio estimator with policy-gradient optimization
OmicsBench with Rubric Recall (RR) evaluation

2609.23435.novelty: Extends OPSD (privileged ground-truth answers) by feeding the teacher tool-derived agent evidence (BLAST, JASPAR, ViennaRNA, PubMed) instead of only labels, enabling API/black-box agents to contribute to OPD without exposing token probabilities, and applies OPD to multi-omics sequence reasoning for the first time; also introduces the first multi-omics reasoning benchmark with instance-specific rubrics.

on_policy_mechanism.evidence_quote: The student receives the task instruction and biological sequence and generates its own response. Both models then calculate the probability of each generated token given the task input and the earlier tokens in that response. The teacher also sees the agent's answer and evidence. We compute the distillation signal for each token as the teacher's log probability minus the student's and update only the student weights.

opd_classification.reasoning: Student samples its own responses, a frozen same-initialization teacher conditioned on privileged tool-agent evidence supplies per-token log-prob (reverse-KL k1) supervision, making it privileged-information self-distillation applied to a new scientific domain.

stabilization_tricks: answer-label consistency gate on privileged info

eval: OmicsBench (EMP, Prom, TFBS, Mod, ncRNA, EC)

key_findings: TA-OPD raised Avg Rubric Recall at all five Qwen3.5 sizes, from +0.14 pp at 0.8B to +16.02 pp at 27B (9.63%→25.66%).
Mean predictive scores improved on 4/6 tasks at 0.8B, 5/6 at 2B and 4B, and 6/6 at 9B and 27B.
Prom MCC rose by 15.94, 20.50, 34.97 and 33.13 pp at 2B, 4B, 9B and 27B; EMP gained +28.89 pp at 9B and +34.04 pp at 27B.
TA-OPD 27B exceeded the unadapted Qwen3.5-397B reference on 5/6 predictive tasks and in Avg Recall (25.66% vs 11.64%).
Gains in predictive score and Avg Recall across the five sizes were strongly correlated (Pearson r=0.99, Spearman ρ=1.00).

Benchmark evaluation of 17 LLMs shows 'reasoning degeneration': scientific LLMs rank high on prediction (e.g., ChatNT 86.86 MCC on EMP) but ~0% RR, with r=−0.29 between reasoning and prediction within scientific LLMs.
2609.23435.ablations_summary: No component ablations reported; only scaling across five model sizes (0.8B–27B) and comparison to unadapted models and a 397B reference. Authors discuss but do not ablate the answer-label consistency gate and class oversampling.
limitations: Evaluation covers only six sequence tasks
Post-training experiments limited to models up to 27B parameters
High cost of constructing and validating evidence-grounded reasoning data
RR measures expert-verifiable evidence, not internal reasoning; rubrics may omit valid unanticipated evidence; benchmark overlap cannot be fully excluded
failure_modes: EC (enzyme function) scores remained low and 27B EC RR decreased from 0.36% to 0.16%
0.8B EMP score decreased after TA-OPD (3.28→2.31 MCC) and 2B TFBS decreased
Mod AUC changed little despite RR gains
Tendency toward longer responses during TA-OPD training (length inflation risk)
Answer-label consistency filter favors questions the agent already solves and can skew class proportions
2609.23435.relevance_to_opd: Direct OPD paper: extends OPSD (privileged-information self-distillation) by using tool-augmented agent outputs as the teacher's privileged context, shows OPD can transfer black-box API agent reasoning into a local student via a same-init teacher, and demonstrates OPD scaling (0.8B–27B) in a new scientific reasoning domain (multi-omics sequences).

2609.25176.title: Qwen-Audio-3.1-Realtime: Towards Reliable Agentic Voice Interaction
2609.25176.summary: Audio LM tech report with M2-OPD (text-teacher + multi-teacher on-policy distillation) and GRPO tool-use

method.training_loop: Core-Cocktail SFT → Multimodality OPD (student samples audio-conditioned y; text teacher on text prompt + frozen audio ref score each prefix) → domain GRPO specialists → Multi-Teacher OPD consolidation → GRPO in executable envs
method.data_source: million-hour-scale paired audio-text data; text-equivalent prompts for Multimodality OPD; domain-specific audio data; self-evolving executable tool environments seeded from open-source tool/MCP definitions
key_components: Core-Cocktail SFT (parameter reconciliation with source Text LLM)
Multimodality OPD: Text Teacher q_T(·|x_t,y<j) + frozen Audio Reference q_ref(·|x_a,y<j) on student trajectories
Multi-Teacher OPD: GRPO-trained audio-domain experts supply token-level distributions on student trajectories
Self-evolving executable environments with dialogue/milestone/turn-level GRPO rewards
Full-duplex conversational policy alignment

2609.25176.novelty: Cross-modal OPD where the teacher receives the text-equivalent prompt while the student is conditioned on audio, combined with a frozen audio-reference distribution and a multi-teacher consolidation stage that merges GRPO-trained domain specialists into one deployable AudioLM; also self-evolving executable environments with multi-granularity GRPO rewards.

on_policy_mechanism.evidence_quote: The Text Teacher does not provide a pre-generated answer; it scores

opd_classification.reasoning: The report applies on-policy distillation with token-level teacher distributions on student-generated audio-conditioned trajectories to a new cross-modal (text-teacher→audio-student) domain and multi-teacher consolidation, but is primarily a system/tech report with no explicit loss formula or OPD ablations.

teacher.name: Frozen Audio Reference (copy of Audio Student)
GRPO-trained audio-domain experts (empathy, pragmatic intent, acoustic scenes)

stabilization_tricks: frozen Audio Reference distribution during Multimodality OPD
parameter reconciliation with source Text LLM before SFT
invalid rollouts resampled rather than assigned zero reward

train: domain-specific audio data (empathy, pragmatic intent, acoustic scenes)
self-evolving executable tool environments seeded from open-source tool/MCP definitions

benchmarks.name: Full-Duplex-Bench v1.5 Background Speech Respond rate

key_findings: Overall task success on the half-duplex S2T τ-Voice adaptation rises from 78.4% (3.0) to 82.0% (3.1).
On FDB v1.5 Background Speech, response rate falls from 73.0% to 13.0% and resume rate rises from 0.26 to 0.87.
Multilingual BBA macro-average rises 6.4 points to 88.1, with largest gains on Arabic, Thai, and Vietnamese.
FLEURS macro-average WER falls from 9.01 to 3.98; LibriSpeech clean/other reach 1.19/2.31.
LongBench v2, MiniLongBench, and Long-AMC improve by 6.76, 4.40, and 8.04 points.
Multi-turn attack success rate falls by 54.50 points (Chinese) and 40.00 points (English).
WebSearch1K mean query count falls from 4.37 to 1.05 (76.0% relative), but retrieval-triggering F1 drops 2.26 points.
Voice Harness hybrid routing (with 3.0 foreground) reaches 91.04% task success and lowest overall latency 4.729s.
2609.25176.ablations_summary: No controlled ablations; authors state ablations are needed to attribute changes to Core-Cocktail SFT, either OPD path, environment evolution, or rollout granularity. Only release-level 3.0 vs 3.1 comparisons and a system-level routing comparison (4 execution paths) are given.
limitations: Release-level comparisons do not isolate individual training components; no ablations of OPD paths
Most comparisons descriptive; no confidence intervals, repeated-seed tests, or contamination analyses
EVA-A covers 200 of 213 sessions with a configuration differing from official setup
τ-Voice uses half-duplex S2T adaptation, not comparable to official full-duplex S2S
Voice Harness evaluation uses 3.0 foreground, not the released 3.1 model
Duplex evaluation needs real-recording and deployment-condition coverage
Human red-team study limited to 50 sessions; 3.1 at 92.00% vs GPT-Realtime-2 96.00%
failure_modes: Multimodality OPD applies only when task information can be represented in text; emotion/pragmatic/acoustic tasks need audio-conditioned supervision
Retrieval-triggering F1 decreases (60.87→58.61) after GRPO count penalty
Daily Chat Spoken score decreases (4.016→3.965) while Rubric increases
EVA-A Mean decreases (70.50→66.26); FDB v3.0 ArgAcc and Pass@1 slightly lower than 3.0
Adult content safety category is lower than GPT-Realtime-2 by 0.90 points
2609.25176.relevance_to_opd: Applies on-policy distillation (citing Lu 2025) to an audio LM: student samples audio-conditioned trajectories and receives token-level distributions from a text teacher (given the text-equivalent prompt), a frozen audio reference, and multiple GRPO-trained domain experts; demonstrates cross-modal and multi-teacher OPD in a production pipeline but without explicit loss or ablations.

2609.24244.title: Look Where It Counts: A Free, Label-Free Visual Evidence Signal for Fine-Grained Vision–Language Reasoning
2609.24244.summary: Label-free crop-peakedness signal for MLLM grounding; gated self-OPD negative result

method.training_loop: Per step: pick z+ crop by argmax peakedness under EMA teacher; sample G on-policy rollouts; score per-token gap Δ_k=logπ(y|z+)-logπ(y|z-); normalize to weight w; weighted reverse-KL/JSD to sg[EMA teacher | z+]; update θ, EMA θ̄
method.loss_formulation: L_{SEG} = \frac{1}{G}\sum_g w^{(g)} \frac{1}{T_g}\sum_k D\big(\pi_s(\cdot|x,y^{(g)}_{<k}) \| sg[\pi_t(\cdot|x,z^+,y^{(g)}_{<k})]\big),\; w^{(g)}=sg[clip(1+(p^{(g)}-\mu_x)/(\sigma_x+\epsilon),0,2)]
method.data_source: High-resolution VQA images (HR-Bench matched distribution) with label-free grid-crop discovery; no answer labels or bounding boxes
key_components: contrastive evidence gap Δ_k (per-token log-likelihood ratio z+ vs z-)
answer-peakedness label-free region discovery over 16-crop grid
EMA self-teacher with privileged crop view (stop-gradient)
trajectory-level evidence gate (group-normalized, clipped to [0,2])
per-token gate variant (TOKEN)
reverse-KL / top-k JSD distillation on on-policy rollouts

2609.24244.novelty: Unlike V-Zero (external teacher + oracle crops) and Vision-OPD (ungated EMA self-teacher), SEG-Distill is simultaneously teacher-free, gated, label/verifier-free, contrastive and does crop discovery; the paper's main novelty is the training-free peakedness-based region discovery and the finding that the gap complements confidence, plus an honest negative on converting the gap into OPD training gains.

on_policy_mechanism.evidence_quote: Given G on-policy rollouts for a prompt x, the grounding scores p(g) are normalized within the group and mapped to a bounded stop-gradient weight.

opd_classification.reasoning: SEG-Distill samples student rollouts on-policy and distills via reverse-KL/JSD toward a stop-gradient EMA self-teacher conditioned on privileged crop information (PI-based self-distillation), with trajectory/token gating; the training result is negative, making it also a failure-mode analysis.

stabilization_tricks: group-normalized gate weights centered at 1 and clipped to [0,2]
fixed self-teacher at initialization (not continually updated in probes)

train: HR-Bench matched high-resolution distribution (label-free, crops discovered by peakedness)

benchmarks.name: V*Bench direct_attributes (Qwen3-VL-8B, inference-time peakedness crop, training-free)

key_findings: Training-free peakedness-based crop selection localizes the target 4.4–5.1× above chance (hit 0.800–0.922 vs 0.180) and lifts V*Bench direct_attributes accuracy from ~70% to ~85% (0.704→0.852 on Qwen3-VL-8B).
Random (0.714) and center (0.687) crops do not help over no-crop (0.704), while anti-selected crops give 0.678, showing the selection direction is causal (+17.4 pts).
The contrastive gap is complementary to confidence: combined AUC 0.926/0.992/0.979 vs confidence-alone 0.854/0.922/0.866, and it flags confidently-wrong answers at AUC 0.97–1.00.
Effects vanish on the relative_position control split (discovery 2.1–3.0× chance, negative lift over confidence); a tight selected crop even beats the oracle bbox there (0.803 vs 0.724).
SEG-Distill training (Qwen2.5-VL-7B, LoRA, 300 steps) fails to beat base on HR-Bench: base 0.717 > NONE 0.712 > SEG 0.707 > TOKEN 0.691; more gating monotonically hurts.
2609.24244.ablations_summary: Crop-selection ablation shows only peakedness-selected crops help (0.852 vs 0.704 no-crop, 0.714 random, 0.678 anti-selected). Gate-design ablation for SEG-Distill (none/trajectory/per-token) shows more gating consistently degrades accuracy, with per-token gating cratering on relative_position (0.658); on low-res GQA (Δ≈0) all arms equal base.
limitations: Discovery needs 16 forward passes per example (16-crop grid)
Evaluated on a single benchmark (V*Bench) with multiple-choice-letter scoring and fixed 1280px downsizing
No IoU/grounding metrics or comparison against attention/Grad-CAM/CRG baselines
Training probes use the self-teacher fixed at initialization rather than continually updated
Training experiments only at pilot scale (7B, LoRA, 300 steps)
failure_modes: Converting the gap signal into training gains fails: no SEG-Distill variant beats base at pilot scale
Per-token gating reinforces crop-induced errors on spatial (relative_position) questions because a tight crop destroys global context
Signal vanishes on global-context questions that do not depend on fine-grained detail

theory.theoretical_claim: OPD framed as negative-free stop-gradient self-distillation (SimSiam-like) with view asymmetry; gap as counterfactual estimate of region influence

2609.24244.relevance_to_opd: Proposes a teacher-free, label-free gated on-policy self-distillation (SEG-Distill) using an EMA self-teacher with privileged crop view and contrastive evidence gating, extending V-Zero/Vision-OPD; reports an honest negative result showing that a validated inference-time grounding signal does not translate into OPD training gains at pilot scale, highlighting a failure mode of privileged-information self-OPD.

2609.24141.title: CLOOPD: Closing the Learner Loop in On-Policy Distillation
2609.24141.summary: Reuse frozen teacher-scored OPD batches via adaptive-α waypoint and multi-pass actor updates

method.training_loop: student samples 8 rollouts/prompt; teacher logprobs scored once; adaptive α waypoint under K3≤0.02; freeze A0; actor pass E1, re-forward, E2 (E3 optional by token-priced marginal realization)
method.loss_formulation: g_{\alpha,t} = \log(1-\alpha+\alpha e^{\ell^T_t-\ell^S_t}),\; R_t = g_{\alpha,t} + \frac{\sum_{j>t} g_{\alpha,j}}{\max(L-t,1)},\; A_0 = \text{prompt-normalized } R_t;\; \text{PPO actor update on frozen } A_0 \text{ for } k \text{ passes}
method.data_source: DAPO-Math-17k prompts; student-generated rollouts scored by Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507 teacher
key_components: adaptive-α proximal (TOP-D) waypoint selection on 32-point log grid under external-K3≤0.02 and reward-tail Q0.05≥-0.5
frozen teacher-scored transaction (responses, teacher logprobs, A0)
multi-pass actor realization (E1/E2/E3) with re-forwarding
Teacher-Signal Realization (TSR) and advantage-aligned marginal realization M_k
Token-Priced Marginal Realization (TPMR) allocator for E3 under hard actor-token budget
separate teacher-token vs actor-token accounting

2609.24141.novelty: Separates teacher-signal acquisition from student-side realization: instead of one actor update per teacher-scored batch (GKD/TOP-D/TrOPD), reuses the frozen batch for 2–3 measured actor passes with adaptive-α waypoint feasibility, turning PPO-epoch count into an explicit, instrumented teacher-efficiency variable.

on_policy_mechanism.evidence_quote: movesdistillationontostudent-generatedtrajecto- riesandqueriestheteacheronprefixesthestudent actually visits (Agarwal et al., 2024).

opd_classification.reasoning: Core contribution is compute/teacher-token efficiency by amortizing each teacher-scored student batch over multiple actor passes, with an adaptive-α waypoint objective as secondary component.

training_setup.compute_budget: 8×H20 node, 300 steps (131.5–288.1 GPU-h per arm); 8×A100-80GB ablations 50–150 steps
stabilization_tricks: internal K3/ESS/finite-value/watchdog safety checks before E3
hard E3 actor-token cap and pace constraint

benchmarks.name: Five-benchmark Macro (AIME24/25/26, AMC23, MATH-500)
benchmarks.metric: generation-level accuracy (%), baseline = TOP-D one-pass anchor at step 300

key_findings: At ~292M teacher-scored tokens, macro accuracy rises from 15.41 (TOP-D) to 17.78 (CLOOPD-Fixed2), 17.28 (TPMR), 18.47 (Random), and 19.36 (CLOOPD-Fixed3); vanilla OPD reaches 10.50.

CLOOPD-Fixed3 at step 100 reaches 15.35 macro, nearly matching TOP-D at step 300 (15.41) with 67.2% fewer teacher-scored tokens (95.9M vs 292.5M), comparable actor tokens (287.8M vs 292.5M), and 28.0% fewer GPU-hours (94.7 vs 131.5).
Adding a third frozen-signal pass (Fixed2→Fixed3) adds 1.58 macro points with no additional teacher scoring.
All four CLOOPD policies beat TOP-D on every one of the five benchmarks.
Fixed α=0.3 violated the external-K3 0.02 target at 12/12 stress-probe checkpoints for each of 3 seeds; adaptive α recorded 0/12 violations.
A100 2×2: E2 raises 3-AIME avg from 2.29→2.95 under fixed α but 1.77→3.65 under adaptive α; Fixed3 reaches 4.27 at step 50.
Spearman correlation between E2 and E3 marginal-realization LCB per token was 0.9309, supporting E2 as a ranking signal for E3.
2609.24141.ablations_summary: Adaptive α and second pass (E2) interact: strongest together (3.65 AIME avg, 59.4% above fixed-α E1 anchor); E3 adds 0.62 AIME avg on A100 and 1.58 macro on H20; budget-matched random E3 (18.47) outperforms TPMR (17.28), showing most value comes from exposing depth rather than the specific allocation rule; adaptive α eliminates all trust-envelope violations.
limitations: Only one student–teacher pair, two hardware programs, and a single OPD implementation evaluated
Transfer of realization-depth frontier to other model families, datasets, or training stacks not established
Allocation policies and token budgets calibrated for reported runs; different hardware prices or safety thresholds may change rankings
Finite checkpoint grids and generation-level exact verification; broader scaling and uncertainty analyses left as future work
failure_modes: Fixed α=0.3 exceeds external-K3 trust target on all stress probes, making depth reuse unsafe without adaptive waypoint
Adding optimizer work without controlling teacher gap leaves target unchanged (limited gains under fixed α)
TPMR online allocator underperforms budget-matched random allocation on macro accuracy (17.28 vs 18.47)
Extra passes are not free: GPU-hours rise from 131.5 (TOP-D) to 288.1 (Fixed3) at equal step count

compute_efficiency.speedup_vs_baseline: 3.05× fewer teacher tokens (95.9M vs 292.5M) at matched quality; 28.0% fewer GPU-hours

2609.24141.relevance_to_opd: Directly extends OPD (GKD/TOP-D lineage) by amortizing teacher-scored student rollouts over multiple actor passes with an adaptive KL-feasible waypoint, addressing teacher-inference cost—the dominant compute bottleneck in on-policy distillation.

2609.26355.title: PACT: From Credit Assignment to Critic Alignment
2609.26355.summary: Unique token-credit theorem; OPD teacher as implicit critic; PACT actor-then-critic

method.training_loop: for k: rollout D_k~π_k; critic V̂ gives credits; B actor updates → π_{k+1}; forward pass for ρ=π_{k+1}/π_k; critic BCE on masked target ρ·R
method.loss_formulation: L_{PACT}(\phi) = \frac{\sum m \odot \mathrm{BCE}(\hat V_\phi(D_k), \rho \odot R)}{\sum m},\ \rho = \mathrm{sg}[\exp(\ell_{new}-\ell_{old})],\ m=\mathbb{1}\{\rho_{min}\le\rho\le\rho_{max}\}
method.data_source: DAPO-Math-17k subset (3,200 problems) with OpenCode agent harness; OpenSWE with Codex agent via Harbor; verifier outcome rewards
key_components: Unique representation theorem for token-level credit (Completeness, Prefix Consistency, Neutrality)
Actor-then-Critic update order
Importance-sampling-corrected critic targets (current-token ratio, masked to [0,6])
Sigmoid critic trained with soft BCE instead of MSE
GAE with λ=1

2609.26355.novelty: Proves credit is uniquely V_i−V_{i−1} under three axioms, shows ideal-teacher OPD gradient equals (1/β)·credit policy gradient (teacher = implicit critic) and RLOO gradient-equivalence, derives credit sparsity bound, and proposes critic synchronization with the updated actor via IS-corrected BCE targets—unlike PPO/VAPO/SAO which train critic aligned to the old policy.

on_policy_mechanism.evidence_quote: Therefore, trajectories sampled before the actor update can be used to train a critic for the updated actor

opd_classification.reasoning: No teacher model is used in training (verifier rewards + learned critic), but Theorem 2 provides a theoretical analysis identifying the ideal OPD teacher as an implicit critic whose expected gradient matches the unique token-level credit.

stabilization_tricks: TIS with ratio range [0,2] for train/rollout mismatch

key_findings: Token-level credit satisfying Completeness, Prefix Consistency, Neutrality is uniquely C_i = E[R|F_i] − E[R|F_{i−1}], a martingale difference.
Under a KL-regularized ideal teacher, the OPD update direction equals (1/β) times the policy gradient induced by the unique credit, so the teacher acts as an implicit critic (Theorem 2).
RLOO's response-level baseline yields the same expected token-level policy gradient as the unique credit (Theorem 3).
Expected number of credits with |C_i|>ε is bounded by 1/(4ε²) independent of length, so intermediate critic errors in GAE with λ<1 can dominate; λ=1 removes them.
PACT reaches 72.87% average on four math benchmarks with Qwen3.5-4B, beating GRPO by 8.80 and PPO(λ=1) by 13.16 points; PPO(λ=0.95) collapses to 26.31%.
PACT achieves 67.4% pass@1 on SWE-bench Verified with Qwen3.6-35B-A3B vs 65.4 GRPO, 65.0 PPO, 63.6 SAO.
Critic-target importance correction improves average math accuracy from 67.74% to 72.87% (+5.13).
2609.26355.ablations_summary: Removing critic-target IS correction (PACT w/o IS) drops average math accuracy from 72.87 to 67.74 and destabilizes training; fixed-policy critic pretraining shows BCE-trained critics converge faster with lower BCE/MSE loss and larger value separation Δ± than MSE-trained critics at both 4B and 35B-A3B scales; PPO λ=1 far outperforms λ=0.95 (59.71 vs 26.31).
limitations: Uniqueness result is conditional on the three proposed regularity conditions; other axioms may yield other credit notions.
Credit notion is statistical (conditional expectation), not causal/counterfactual.
Characterizes what credit should be but does not solve exact estimation in practical LLM RL.
failure_modes: Exact continuation importance ratio has high variance for long responses, requiring a one-step current-token surrogate and ratio masking.
PPO with λ=0.95 undergoes policy collapse in long-horizon training due to intermediate critic errors.

theory.theoretical_claim: Unique credit representation C_i=V_i−V_{i−1}; ideal-teacher OPD gradient = (1/β)·E[Z_t C_t]; RLOO gradient unbiasedness; credit sparsity bound Var(R|F_0)≤1/4
theory.proof_sketch: Existence via telescoping martingale differences; uniqueness since finite-horizon martingale determined by terminal value. Ideal teacher solves KL-regularized problem giving q*∝p·exp(Q/β), so log-ratio = Q/β − logZ; score-function identity removes logZ and V_{t−1}, yielding credit-gradient equivalence.

2609.26355.relevance_to_opd: Provides a theoretical bridge showing that the OPD teacher's log-density-ratio signal, under an ideal KL-regularized teacher, is proportional to the unique token-level credit—i.e., the teacher is an implicit critic; PACT itself is an RL actor-critic method without any teacher distillation.

2609.28845.title: LastOPD: Taming Collapse in Latent On-Policy Distillation
2609.28845.summary: Last-layer latent alignment crossfaded into token-level OPD avoids latent collapse
