method.training_loop: for step t: student samples 4 responses/prompt on 32 prompts; teacher scores same prefixes; L = alpha(t)*reverse top-16 KL + beta(t)*last-layer latent MSE, latent fades to 0 over 10 steps
method.loss_formulation: L_t = \alpha(t) L_{OPD} + \lambda_{rep} \beta(t) L_{rep}, \alpha(t)=\min(1,t/T_w), \beta(t)=\max(0,1-t/T_w), L_{OPD}=\frac{1}{|M|}\sum_{t\in M} D_{KL}(R_{V_{k,t}}(p_{\theta,t}) \| R_{V_{k,t}}(p_{T,t})), L_{rep}=\frac{1}{|M| d_T}\sum_t \|\nu(g_\psi(z_t^S)) - sg[\nu(z_t^T)]\|_2^2
method.data_source: DAPO-Math-17k prompts, student on-policy rollouts (~7.9k rollouts over 62 steps)
key_components: reverse top-k (k=16) token-level OPD on student rollouts
last-layer (pre-LM-head) latent alignment with small trainable MLP projector
10-step linear crossfade from latent to token loss
frozen teacher, no layer pairing, projector discarded at inference

2609.28845.novelty: Unlike OPRD/LOPD/PHF which align depth-paired intermediate layers for the whole run, LastOPD diagnoses early-gain/late-collapse and alignment-behavior mismatch in latent OPD, restricts latent supervision to the last-layer state shared by both LM heads, and keeps it on only during a 10-step crossfade into token-level OPD.

on_policy_mechanism.evidence_quote: hastheteacherscoreeverytokenitgenerates, soeverycorrectionlandsonacontextthestudent

opd_classification.reasoning: Core contribution is a training-schedule (curriculum) that crossfades a white-box latent term into standard token-level reverse-KL OPD on student rollouts, motivated by an analysis of collapse failure modes.

stabilization_tricks: 10-step linear crossfade of latent weight to zero
latent term only at last-layer state

key_findings: LastOPD improves MATH-500 over token-only OPD by 5.55 (58.95 vs 53.40) and 4.02 (53.45 vs 49.43) points with Qwen3-4B and Qwen3-8B teachers.
Latent-only OPRD-Bridge lifts validation MATH-500 from 25.4 to 46.2 in 10 steps, then collapses to 11.3 with no recovery, ending below the untrained student.
Projected cosine alignment keeps rising (0.97→0.98) while MATH-500 falls ~35 points; final last-layer CKA is 0.570 for token-only OPD vs 0.546 for LastOPD despite LastOPD scoring higher.
LastOPD reaches token-only OPD's final score in about half the steps (passes 51.9 by step 30) and holds near 57 through 150 steps.
Eight-dataset mean improves over token-only OPD by 3.93 and 2.10 points; best@N mean 51.2 and 50.6 vs 47.2 and 45.9.
On the same-lineage pair (diagonal CKA 0.983), continued latent supervision (OPRD-Vanilla 87.22) beats crossfading (LastOPD 83.42).
2609.28845.ablations_summary: Hard switch at step 10 drops to 50.45 (below token-only 53.40); fade-only 50.90; raise-token-only 54.15; hold latent 10 steps + raise token 55.73; always-on 53.77; windows of 5/15 steps give 54.62/54.47; reversed projector 50.00; Gram-matrix loss 46.23; +KL to initial policy 58.55; massive-dimension mask barely moves LastOPD (59.72→59.35) but hurts all always-on recipes; raising latent weight to 1000 collapses LastOPD-always (33.90) but not LastOPD (57.57).
limitations: Fixed 10-step fade shared across all pairs costs up to 0.58 points on the eight-dataset mean for the same-lineage pair where continued latent supervision is better.
MATH-500 is used both for diagnostics and for choosing T_w, so only the other seven datasets are independent evidence.
Each cell is a single run at the final checkpoint; only math domain and Qwen3/1.5B pairs tested.
failure_modes: Latent-only supervision across depth-paired layers collapses the student below its starting point (MATH-500 12.12) after an early peak.
Better latent alignment does not indicate better behavior; the most aligned model is the worst performing.
Hard switch from latent to token loss is worse than never using the latent term.
Masking massive-activation dimensions or remapping layers by CKA ridge does not prevent collapse.
Always-on latent term with large weight (1000) brings back collapse.
2609.28845.relevance_to_opd: Directly an OPD method: reverse top-k KL on student rollouts from a frozen larger teacher, augmented with a short-lived last-layer latent alignment; provides empirical diagnosis of when latent supervision helps and harms within on-policy distillation.

2609.28778.title: Reward-Tilted On-Policy Distillation for Acoustic Grounding in Audio-Language Models
2609.28778.summary: Teacher audio-present/absent log-prob contrast reshapes OPD target for ALMs

method.training_loop: for batch: student samples response on (audio, question); frozen teacher scores each prefix with and without audio; r=logp_M-logp_∅; q∝p_M·exp(αr); update student via reverse-KL(p_S‖q)+gated CE on gold answer
method.loss_formulation: L = \frac{1}{B}\sum_i [L_{ce,i} + \lambda g_i \frac{1}{L_i}\sum_t D_{KL}(p^M_{S,t} \| q_{\alpha,t})],\quad q_{\alpha,t}(v) \propto p^M_{T,t}(v)\exp(\alpha(\log p^M_{T,t}(v)-\log p^{\emptyset}_{T,t}(v)))
method.data_source: 10,000 audio multiple-choice QA examples randomly selected from AudioMCQ-StrongAC-GeminiCoT
key_components: student-generated on-policy rollouts
frozen teacher scored with and without audio
full-vocabulary log-probability contrast reward r_t(v)
reward-tilted (exponentially reweighted, normalized) teacher target q_α,t
reverse-KL distillation to reshaped target
gated gold-answer cross-entropy loss (gate=teacher correct with audio)
rank-64 LoRA training

2609.28778.novelty: Unlike Vanilla OPD (matches teacher's audio-conditioned distribution) and CAAD (audio contrast but on pre-generated teacher responses with forward KL), RT-OPD applies the same frozen teacher's audio-present/absent log-prob contrast along student-generated trajectories to reshape the vocabulary-level teacher target before reverse-KL; unlike G-OPD it contrasts the teacher with itself (no audio) rather than with a separate reference model, and unlike Visual-Advantage OPD it reshapes token distributions rather than weighting trajectories/token groups.

on_policy_mechanism.evidence_quote: RT-OPD applies the contrast along student-generated trajectories and uses it to reshape the teacher's next-token distribution before reverse-KL distillation.

opd_classification.reasoning: Student generates rollouts online, a frozen white-box teacher provides per-token distributions, and the loss is a reverse KL to a reward-tilted (contrast-reshaped) teacher target, making it a new reward-augmented OPD objective.

stabilization_tricks: gated distillation only when teacher answers correctly with audio

key_findings: RT-OPD outperforms Vanilla OPD and CAAD on all three benchmarks for both students; Macro-3 63.08 vs 62.00 (Ke) and 62.26 vs 60.79 (Qwen).
Largest gains over Vanilla OPD occur on MMAR: +2.3 points for Ke and +3.0 for Qwen.
Mizar-3B (Ke-Omni-R-3B + RT-OPD) reaches 72.72% on MMAU, highest among compared 3B models, and Macro-3 63.08 close to the 7B teacher's 63.47, exceeding the teacher on ADQA-clean (56.45 vs 54.85).
On-policy RT-OPD beats an off-policy variant (pre-generated teacher responses) by 0.84 (Ke) and 1.02 (Qwen) Macro-3 points.
Audio-contrast reshaping beats plain teacher sharpening (τ=0.5) on all three benchmarks and a G-OPD-style model-reference contrast in Macro-3 for both students.
Under silenced/replaced audio, RT-OPD shows larger accuracy drops than Vanilla OPD (e.g., MMAR silence −22.46 vs −19.16), suggesting greater reliance on acoustic evidence.
2609.28778.ablations_summary: Removing the audio contrast (Sharpening) costs ~1.7 (Ke) / ~1.25 (Qwen) Macro-3; using a frozen-initial-student reference instead of audio-absent teacher (Model ref.) costs ~1.7 / ~0.8; using a different recording as reference (Unmatched) costs ~0.4 / ~0.1; replacing on-policy rollouts with pre-generated teacher responses (Off-policy) costs 0.84 / 1.02; α=0 recovers Vanilla OPD, which is 1.08 / 1.47 worse.
limitations: No explicit limitations section; evaluation restricted to audio multiple-choice QA benchmarks with a single 7B teacher and 3B students
Protocols and parameter-count conventions differ across models on the MMAU leaderboard, complicating external comparisons
failure_modes: On MMAU the 'Unmatched' reference variant slightly exceeds RT-OPD for both students (72.84 vs 72.72; 72.26 vs 72.18) and 'Model ref.' exceeds it for Qwen (72.31 vs 72.18)
Audio-perturbation drops are not uniformly larger for RT-OPD (e.g., ADQA-cl. silence −31.29 vs Vanilla −31.74), so the grounding effect is suggestive rather than consistent

compute_efficiency.teacher_inference_cost: 2× (teacher forward pass with audio and without audio per student rollout)

theory.theoretical_claim: Reverse KL to the reward-tilted target decomposes as D_KL(p_S‖p_T) − α·E_{v∼p_S}[r_t(v)] + log Z_t, i.e., standard OPD plus an expected audio-contrast reward term and a gradient-free normalizer; α=0 recovers standard OPD
theory.proof_sketch: Substitute q_α,t ∝ p_T·exp(αr) into D_KL(p_S‖q); the log-partition Z_t is constant for a fixed prefix and does not affect student gradients.

2609.28778.relevance_to_opd: Directly extends GKD/MiniLLM-style reverse-KL on-policy distillation to audio-language models by reshaping the white-box teacher's per-token target with a modality-contrast reward, and empirically confirms on-policy beats off-policy distillation in this setting.

2609.28385.title: When and Where to Trust the Teacher: Unifying On-Policy Distillation and GRPO Through Entropy-Calibrated Credit Assignment
2609.28385.summary: UECR-GRPO fuses verifier reward and OPD teacher log-ratio pre-normalization, entropy-calibrated token credit

method.training_loop: for each batch: sample G=8 responses from π_old; verifier R_task; teacher/old log-prob gap δ per token; R_U=R_task+α·mean(δ); group-normalize; ECR redistributes task credit via tanh(δ)·exp(-H_T) zero-sum; clipped PG + ref-KL
method.loss_formulation: L = L_{PG}(A^{final}) + \beta_{ref} L_{low-var-KL},\quad A^{final}_{i,t} = A^{task|U}_i(1+\rho q_{i,t}) + \alpha A^{T|U}_i,\quad R^U_i = R^{task}_i + \alpha \frac{\sum_t m_{i,t}\delta_{i,t}}{\sum_t m_{i,t}},\ \delta_{i,t}=\log\pi_T(y_{i,t}|s_{i,t})-\log\pi_{old}(y_{i,t}|s_{i,t})
method.data_source: DeepMath-103K (difficulty 5–7 for 1.7B; sampled difficulty 6–8 subset for 4B)
key_components: Path-Utility Unification (PUU): verifier reward + length-normalized teacher-to-old log-ratio combined before group normalization
Gibbs-optimal path distribution from joint KL-regularized objective
Entropy-Calibrated Redistribution (ECR): signed teacher–old gap direction tanh(sδ/2τ_δ)
Full-vocabulary teacher entropy confidence c=exp(-H_T/τ_H)
Response-wise zero-sum projection preserving total task credit and token sign
Clipped GRPO-style PPO update with low-var reference KL

2609.28385.novelty: Unlike DistilledRL (multiplicative teacher ratio after normalization, zero when verifier ties) and ATOD (additive token OPD after normalization), teacher evidence enters the response utility BEFORE group normalization so it can alter response ranking; token-level redistribution is entropy-attenuated and constrained by a zero-sum projection that exactly preserves each response's verifier-credit budget and sign.

on_policy_mechanism.evidence_quote: Astrongerteacherscoresthestudent’sownprefixesandthereforesuppliesdensefeedback

opd_classification.reasoning: Student generates rollouts, a frozen stronger teacher scores their realized tokens with per-token log-probs and full-vocab entropy, and this OPD signal is the central object fused with RLVR reward in one GRPO update—an RL-augmented OPD objective with entropy-based token weighting.

training_setup.compute_budget: unspecified (8 GPUs implied by GPU0–7 memory logging; 515 steps for 1.7B, 160 steps for 4B)
stabilization_tricks: low-var reference KL (coef 0.001) in actor loss only

key_findings: UECR-GRPO reaches 17.21% average Avg@12 with Qwen3-1.7B, +0.89 pp over the strongest baseline (ATOD-aligned 16.32) and +5.76 over Vanilla GRPO (11.45).
With Qwen3-4B student, average is 65.09%, +0.56 pp over DistilledRL (64.53), though it trails the best baseline on AIME25, AMC23, HMMT25-Nov.

Teacher scores distinguish 84.3–98.4% of verifier-degenerate groups, but conflict with verifier correctness on 39.1–50.8% of correct–incorrect pairs and agree with a blinded process judge only 56.8% of the time.
Ablation: PUU joint normalization raises 3-benchmark avg from 18.19 (separate norm) to 20.28; full ECR raises it to 25.62.
82.4% of top-10% teacher gaps occur in the highest teacher-entropy quartile; entropy calibration reduces their mean magnitude by 37%.
At α=1, no correct–incorrect ordering inversions over 451 mixed groups and 22,811 pairs in the offline audit.
Full ECR yields positive invalid-minus-valid weight gap D=0.0048, beating all 100 entropy-shuffle controls (mean 0.0024).
2609.28385.ablations_summary: On Qwen3-1.7B (3-benchmark avg): task-only GRPO 17.22 → separate norm 18.19 → PUU joint norm 20.28; adding ECR: w/o entropy 21.11, w/o projection 25.17, full UECR-GRPO 25.62. Both pre-normalization unification and each ECR component (entropy gating, zero-sum projection) contribute; entropy removal hurts most.
limitations: Retraining-based sensitivity to α, ρ, τ_δ, τ_H remains future work; only offline fixed-rollout audits are provided.
Offline audits (PUU signal geometry, ECR localization) do not estimate gradient contributions or causal accuracy gains.
α sensitivity audit limited to held-out AMC 2023 with group sizes 12/24 rather than training groups of 8; responses truncated at 8,192 tokens.
Data-hygiene screening and checkpoint-selection rules still require confirmation from completed runs.
Aggregate gains do not imply uniform per-benchmark improvement.
failure_modes: Teacher preference can favor incorrect paths or style: conflicts with verifier on 39.1–50.8% of correct–incorrect pairs.
Vanilla GRPO beats the method on HMMT25-Nov (1.7B) by 0.84 points; 4B student trails baselines on AIME25, AMC23, HMMT25-Nov.
Large α (checkpoint-wise 7.6–11.5) causes ordering inversions in ≥10% of mixed groups.
Teacher additional response-level variation decays from 86% at step 30 to 21% at step 515.

theory.theoretical_claim: Gibbs-optimal path distribution Q*∝exp(R_task/β)P_T^{α/β}P_0^{1-α/β} for joint KL-regularized verifier+teacher objective; exact PUU advantage decomposition; closed-form zero-sum projection preserving task-credit budget and sign
theory.proof_sketch: Token log-ratios telescope to path log-density ratio (Lemma 1); maximizing E_Q[U]-βKL(Q||P_0) equals βlogZ-βKL(Q||Q*) so Q* is unique (Prop 1); shared denominator gives A^U=A^{task|U}+αA^{T|U} by linearity (Prop 2); Lagrangian of strictly convex weighted least squares gives q=½c(d-μ^c) with zero sum, and |q|≤1, ρ<1 keeps weights positive with mean one (Props 3–4).

2609.28385.relevance_to_opd: Directly extends on-policy distillation into an RLVR hybrid: student rollouts are scored per-token by a frozen teacher, and the paper studies when (verifier-tied groups, response ranking) and where (token-level, entropy-gated) to trust the teacher signal, positioning itself against KDRL, G-OPD, DistilledRL, ATOD, reward-gated and sign-gated OPD.

2609.28145.title: RL Starts before RL: On Policy Distillation for Better Reinforcement Learning
2609.28145.summary: Empirical study: OPD as pre-RL preparation beats SFT→RL and direct RL

method.training_loop: Stage1: student samples responses; teacher gives full next-token dists at student prefixes; minimize RKL (or FKL). Stage2: GRPO RL with verifier from OPD checkpoint.
method.loss_formulation: L_{RKL}(s)=D_{KL}(p_s \| q_s),\; L_{FKL}(s)=D_{KL}(q_s \| p_s),\; p_s=\pi_\theta(\cdot|s),\; q_s=\pi_T(\cdot|s)
method.data_source: OPD: 100K OpenMathInstruct prompts (text), 100K OpenMMReasoner prompts (VL); RL: 17K DAPO-Math (text), 16K DeepMath/OlympiadBench/MMK12-VisionR1 (VL)
key_components: on-policy distillation with full teacher distributions at student-generated prefixes
reverse-KL vs forward-KL objective comparison
student- vs teacher-generated trajectory source (OPD vs TFD)
downstream GRPO RL with final-answer verifier
behavioral diagnostics: Pass@k, top-20 JS divergence, top-1 agreement, lexicon-conditioned entropy

2609.28145.novelty: First systematic evaluation of OPD as a preparation stage for RLVR (rather than an end-point), showing post-RL rankings differ from pre-RL rankings (FKL overtakes RKL on student trajectories), and attributing the benefit to distributional alignment plus retained uncertainty rather than Pass@k coverage.

on_policy_mechanism.evidence_quote: In OPD→RL, the student first matches full teacher distributions at its own generated prefixes using reverse KL.

opd_classification.reasoning: The paper proposes no new distillation objective; it is an empirical analysis / decision framework arguing OPD recipes (objective, trajectory source) should be selected by performance after subsequent RL.

stabilization_tricks: RL runs monitored for collapse via reward/entropy/generation logs

benchmarks.name: Text 8-benchmark average (after RL: Base→RL vs OPD→RL)
VL 20-benchmark average (after RL: Base→RL vs OPD→RL)

key_findings: OPD→RL reaches 59.18 (text) and 63.02 (VL) averages, exceeding direct RL by 7.28 and 1.34 points and SFT→RL by 11.70 and 1.69 points.
In text, OPD improves the initial average by only 0.54 points (36.48→37.02) but gains 22.16 points during RL vs 15.42 for Base and 9.73 for SFT.
Pre-RL Pass@k does not explain the benefit: text Base and OPD have Pass@64 of 80.37% vs 79.98% yet finish at 51.90 vs 59.18; SFT has highest Pass@1 (29.33%) but lowest final average.
OPD has lower top-20 JS divergence from teacher (0.01468 vs 0.01701 Base, 0.01720 SFT in text) while SFT has slightly higher top-1 agreement (94.25% vs 93.82%).
OPD retains lexicon-conditioned entropy near Base (1.048 vs 0.971 text; 0.629 vs 0.622 VL) while SFT collapses to 0.242/0.214.
On student trajectories RKL leads before RL (60.66 vs 60.17) but FKL leads after RL (64.87 vs 63.02, +1.85, higher on 14/20 tasks); on teacher trajectories RKL stays ahead (61.90 vs 59.20).
OPD beats teacher-trajectory distillation (TFD) after RL under either objective (63.02/64.87 vs 61.90/59.20).
2609.28145.ablations_summary: Four-way VL comparison of trajectory source (student vs teacher prefixes) × objective (RKL vs FKL) with full teacher distributions: FKL best for student-prefix OPD after RL (+4.70 during RL), RKL best for teacher-prefix TFD; all OPD variants beat TFD after RL; SFT with hard targets is worst after RL in text. Diagnostics show FKL has higher entropy (0.952 vs 0.629) and lower JS (0.06234 vs 0.06431) than RKL.
limitations: Analysis does not independently vary teacher distributional alignment and retained uncertainty, so their individual contributions and interaction are unresolved.
Only existing distillation objectives are examined; no new objective designed for subsequent RL is proposed.
Each trajectory-source/objective variant has a single distillation run and single RL run; seed variability is not estimated.

RL runs continue until collapse and checkpoint selection criterion is not specified; run lengths are not equal and preparation costs are not accounted for, so comparisons are not at fixed compute budget.
failure_modes: SFT→RL finishes below direct RL in text (47.48 vs 51.90) despite higher pre-RL accuracy, showing SFT preparation can hurt downstream RL.
Selecting the objective by pre-RL accuracy picks RKL, which underperforms FKL after RL on student trajectories.
FKL on teacher-generated trajectories yields the worst post-RL result (59.20).
OPD→RL regresses or ties on a few VL tasks (e.g., WeMath 62.10 vs 62.67 Base→RL; MMLongBench-Doc slight drop during RL).
2609.28145.relevance_to_opd: Directly studies standard OPD (GKD/MiniLLM-style RKL/FKL on student rollouts with full teacher distributions) as a pre-RLVR initialization stage, showing OPD checkpoints are better RL starting points than SFT or base and that objective choice should be judged post-RL; provides behavioral diagnostics (JS alignment, retained entropy) explaining why.

2609.28554.title: Pistis Technical Report
2609.28554.summary: IDRL: interleave top-k JSD on-policy distillation with SAPO RL in one loop

method.training_loop: From SFT ckpt: for step s: if (s mod 10)<5 and s<S*: sample y~π_θ, minimize top-50 JSD(β=0.5) vs frozen 27B teacher; else SAPO RL step w/ verifiable reward + PAS; after S* pure RL
method.loss_formulation: L_s(θ) = -1[Π_s=RL] J_RL(θ) + α 1[Π_s=OPD] L_OPD(θ), L_OPD = E_{x~D,y~π_θ}[1/|y| Σ_t D_JSD(β)(π_T(·|x,y<t) ∥ π_θ(·|x,y<t))] with top-k restriction and residual term log(1/(1-β))(1-Σ_{v∈V_t}π_θ(v))
method.data_source: ~3.2M multimodal SFT QA pairs (teacher-generated reasoning + agentic trajectories); ~30K RL queries (STEM/visual reasoning, grounding, TIR, search) from open-source and proprietary data
key_components: Interleaved Distillation and RL (IDRL) periodic schedule with switch to pure RL at S*
Top-k (k=50) generalized JSD OPD objective with analytic residual mass term (no renormalization)
SAPO smooth-gated policy gradient with verifiable rewards
Step-level Positive-Advantage Suppression (PAS) for agentic credit assignment
Cold-start SFT to bridge student–teacher distribution gap in multimodal OPD
Pistis-Auto-Harnessing (PAH) inference-time harness optimization

2609.28554.novelty: Rather than running OPD and RL sequentially or as a static weighted sum, IDRL alternates one objective per gradient step (5 OPD / 5 RL steps per cycle) and shows via first-order analysis that summing creates a harmful cross-term g_R^T g_D while interleaving never forms it; also introduces a top-k JSD with analytic residual for student mass outside teacher top-k, and shows cold-start SFT is required for multimodal OPD.

on_policy_mechanism.evidence_quote: Weuseon-policydistillationtotransferteacherbehaviortothestudentunderthestudent’sownsampledcontexts.

opd_classification.reasoning: Core method interleaves student-rollout JSD distillation from a separate frozen 27B teacher (C1-C3 satisfied) with verifiable-reward RL, making it an RL-augmented OPD objective with theoretical gradient-conflict analysis and a multimodal/agentic application.

training_setup.rl_algorithm: SAPO (GRPO-style group-relative advantage with smooth sigmoid gate)
stabilization_tricks: Generalized JSD (β=0.5) instead of reverse KL
Top-50 teacher vocabulary restriction with residual mass term
Alternating OPD/RL steps to avoid gradient conflict
Switch to pure RL after entropy plateau (S*=300 Thinking / 100 Agentic)
SAPO smooth trust region with asymmetric temperatures τ_pos=1, τ_neg=1.05
Positive-Advantage Suppression on ineffective tool-call steps
Cold-start SFT on teacher responses before OPD

train: ~30K RL queries (STEM/visual reasoning, grounding, TIR, search)

key_findings: IDRL reaches 74.7 average over 18 agentic benchmarks vs 74.0 pure RL, 73.4 pure OPD, 74.1 sequential OPD→RL, and 74.1 joint RL+OPD from the same SFT checkpoint (73.7).
Reverse KL and top-5 JSD OPD collapse entropy, whereas top-50 JSD raises and sustains higher entropy with smoother gradient norms.
Direct OPD on multimodal Geo3K gives only +0.7 (65.0→65.7); cold-start SFT on teacher outputs is needed for stable, consistent OPD gains.
PAS improves the 18-benchmark average by 0.4 (74.7 vs 74.3), with the largest gains on Search-Oriented (+1.2) and Multimodal Reasoning (+0.9).
Pistis-9B-Agentic improves over Qwen3.5-9B by 8.4, 8.0, 3.2, 11.4 points on BrowseComp-VL, MMSearch, VDR-testmini, LiveVQA.
Pistis-27B-Thinking grounding average 80.5 exceeds Qwen3.8-27B by 8.6 points; non-grounding average 82.3 vs 82.4.
PAH improves VDR-testmini from 26.8% to 28.6% at fixed 15-interaction budget, and transfers to Seed-2.1-turbo (+1.4) and GPT-5.5 (+4.0).
2609.28554.ablations_summary: OPD objective: RKL and JSD-5 collapse entropy/unstable gradients, JSD-50 stable (adopted). Scheduling: interleaved IDRL (74.7) beats joint RL+OPD (74.1) in all five categories, sequential OPD→RL (74.1) in four of five, pure RL (74.0), and pure OPD (73.4). PAS adds ~0.4 avg, mostly on long-horizon tasks. Cold-start SFT is necessary for multimodal OPD to avoid initial collapse.
limitations: IDRL applied only to 9B variants; 27B variants use pure RL and serve as teachers
Results support interleaving but do not establish that reduced gradient interference or improved exploration alone explains downstream gains
OPD upper-bounds the student at teacher capability, requiring a switch to pure RL
PAH validated only within multimodal search; transfer to coding/Claw-Style unvalidated
Process-level weaknesses persist: intent mis-binding, confirmatory tool use, loosely coupled retrieval and reasoning
failure_modes: Direct OPD on multimodal models drops sharply at start without cold-start SFT due to low student–teacher distribution overlap
Reverse-KL OPD and narrow top-5 JSD cause entropy collapse and gradient-norm spikes
Pure RL undergoes steady entropy collapse and late-stage gradient spikes
Summed RL+OPD objective produces gradient conflict (g_R^T g_D<0) and noisier training
Pistis remains weaker than baselines on MMMU, MMVP, ChartQA and BLINK (−7.1 vs Qwen3.8-27B)

theory.theoretical_claim: First-order analysis: summing RL and OPD gradients yields ΔJ_RL≈η(‖g_R‖²+αg_R^Tg_D) with a shared cross-term that can reverse improvement when g_R^Tg_D<−‖g_R‖²/α, whereas interleaved single-objective steps give non-negative first-order improvement; JSD identity D_JSD=H(M)−βH(π_T)−(1−β)H(π_θ) links OPD to entropy preservation
theory.proof_sketch: Write RL gradient as mode-seeking policy gradient and OPD ascent as mass-covering score-weighted term −(1−β)π_θ log(π_θ/M); on over-confident tokens signs oppose, so aggregated gradients conflict; Taylor-expand each objective under the summed vs alternating update to expose the cross-term.

2609.28554.relevance_to_opd: Proposes a scheduling alternative to joint KL-regularized RL: alternating GKD-style top-k JSD on-policy distillation from a stronger frozen teacher with verifiable-reward RL, with analysis of gradient conflict, entropy preservation, and multimodal cold-start requirements; directly extends GKD/Thinking-Machines OPD to MLLMs and agentic tasks.

2609.29464.title: TS-OPD: Reconciling ASR and QA in Speech Language Models via Task-Specific On-Policy Distillation
2609.29464.affiliation_primary: Nankai University / Xingchen AGI Lab, China Telecom
2609.29464.summary: Dual-teacher task-routed on-policy KD reconciles ASR and QA in speech LLMs

method.training_loop: for speech x: student samples ASR traj (prompt c_ASR) and QA traj (prompt c_QA); ASR teacher scores ASR traj, QA teacher scores QA traj; forward-KL update adapter only
method.loss_formulation: L_{TS-OPD} = \lambda \frac{1}{N}\sum_{t=1}^{N} D_{KL}(p_t^{ASR} \| p_t^{\theta,ASR}) + (1-\lambda) \frac{1}{M}\sum_{t=1}^{M} D_{KL}(p_t^{QA} \| p_t^{\theta,QA})
method.data_source: Emilia English speech (8k hours for teachers; 100–1000 hours, mainly 500h, for distillation) with ASR transcriptions and Qwen3-4B CoT QA responses as targets
key_components: pre-specialization QA teacher (π_QA = A1, also student init)
post-specialization ASR teacher (π_ASR = A2, full-param ASR fine-tuned)
task-specific trajectory routing (each on-policy trajectory supervised only by its corresponding teacher)
top-128 forward KL on student-visited states
adapter-only student update with frozen encoder/LLM

2609.29464.novelty: Uses the model's own pre- and post-ASR-specialization checkpoints as complementary QA/ASR teachers, and routes task-conditioned student rollouts to only the matching teacher (vs. shared-trajectory OPD where both teachers supervise every rollout), which they show removes teacher interference and λ-sensitivity.

on_policy_mechanism.evidence_quote: TS-OPD performs distillation on the student's own trajectories. At decoding step t, the student-visited states are

opd_classification.reasoning: Student generates own ASR/QA rollouts (C1), two white-box teachers provide per-token distributions on student-visited states (C2), forward-KL loss (C3); contribution is a dual white-box teacher signal-routing scheme applied to speech LLMs.

teacher.name: π_ASR (A2: Whisper-large-v3 + Qwen3-4B SLM, full-param ASR fine-tuned)

student.name: π_θ (initialized from A1: Whisper-large-v3 + Qwen3-4B SLM, adapter-only trained)

teacher.name: π_QA (A1: Whisper-large-v3 + Qwen3-4B SLM, QA adapter-trained)

student.name: π_θ (initialized from A1: Whisper-large-v3 + Qwen3-4B SLM, adapter-only trained)

stabilization_tricks: adapter-only update with frozen encoder and LLM
cosine LR schedule, lr 1e-5, one epoch

train: Emilia (English, ~8k hours; 100–1000h subsets for distillation, 500h main)

key_findings: TS-OPD (B1, 500h, λ=0.5) reduces basic ASR WER from 14.19% to 10.03% while raising QA accuracy from 42.57% to 45.07%, the best QA score among all systems.
Full-parameter ASR fine-tuning (A2) achieves the best WER (9.16%) but collapses QA to 2.86%; ASR-only OPD (B3) similarly reaches 9.96% WER but 1.89% QA.
Shared-trajectory OPD (B2) underperforms task-specific routing on all metrics (10.92 vs 10.03 WER; 42.73 vs 45.07 QA).
TS-OPD with 500h of distillation data beats joint ASR+QA adapter training (A4) on the full 8k-hour corpus (10.03 vs 13.44 WER; 45.07 vs 44.29 QA).
TS-OPD is robust to λ in [0.1,0.9] (QA varies ~1 pt), whereas ST-OPD collapses QA to 23.97% at λ=0.55.
Scaling distillation data from 100h to 1000h lowers basic WER 11.32%→9.82% and contextual WER 7.10%→5.88% while QA stays ~45%.
2609.29464.ablations_summary: Removing the QA teacher (B3) destroys QA (1.89%); using both teachers on shared trajectories (ST-OPD, B2) partially preserves QA (42.73%) but with worse ASR (10.92 WER) and strong λ-sensitivity; task-specific routing (TS-OPD) gives near-B3 ASR (10.03) with best QA (45.07) and λ-robustness.
limitations: λ comparison between TS-OPD (300h) and ST-OPD (500h) is not a strictly controlled absolute comparison
ContextASR-Bench samples longer than 30 seconds are excluded due to encoder input-length constraints
Only the speech adapter is updated in the student; a gap to the full-parameter ASR teacher remains (10.03 vs 9.16 WER)
failure_modes: λ=1 (QA supervision removed) causes QA capability to collapse
Shared-trajectory OPD suffers conflicting teacher signals and sharp QA degradation as λ increases beyond 0.5
NE-FNR on contextual ASR worsens relative to the QA-only model (12.28→16.82)
2609.29464.relevance_to_opd: Directly extends on-policy distillation (GKD-style forward KL on student rollouts) to speech LLMs with a dual-teacher, task-routed variant that uses pre-/post-specialization checkpoints as teachers to fight catastrophic forgetting; provides an OPD-vs-OPD ablation (shared vs task-specific routing) and λ/data scaling curves.

2608.19181.title: Beyond Teacher Likelihood: Group-Calibrated On-Policy Distillation for Long-Context Reasoning
2608.19181.summary: OPD advantage calibrated by group-normalized verifier–teacher disagreement residual

method.training_loop: for each prompt: sample G=8 student rollouts; verifier reward R; teacher log-probs → token OPD adv A_t; ρ=z(R)−z(mean A); A'_t=A_t+β(1+tanh(u_t/2))ρ; clipped PPO update
method.loss_formulation: A_t^{(i)} = \log\pi_T(y_t|x,y_{<t}) - \log\pi_{\theta_{old}}(y_t|x,y_{<t});\ s^{(i)}=\frac{1}{T}\sum_t A_t^{(i)};\ \rho^{(i)}=z(R^{(i)})-z(s^{(i)});\ u_t=\frac{A_t-s}{\sigma_A};\ c_t=1+\tanh(u_t/2);\ A'^{(i)}_t=A^{(i)}_t+\beta c_t^{(i)}\rho^{(i)},\ \beta=0.10;\ \text{then clipped PPO surrogate with } A'_t
method.data_source: GoLongRL subset: 9,527 prompts ≤32K tokens across nine long-context task families with native binary/graded verifiers
key_components: vanilla OPD token advantage (teacher−student log-prob, expectation = −reverse KL)
within-group z-score normalization of verifier rewards and trajectory-level OPD scores
signed teacher–verifier disagreement residual ρ = z(R) − z(s)
Relative-Advantage-based Credit Assignment (RACA): c_t = 1 + tanh(u_t/2)
clipped PPO-style token-level actor objective with calibrated advantages
zero-variance guards reducing to vanilla OPD

2608.19181.novelty: Unlike prior verifier-aware OPD (SCOPE routing, MOPD peer conditioning, Uni-OPD outcome-class margin, SG-OPD sign gating, reward-weighted trajectory selection), GC-OPD keeps the teacher pass unchanged and adds a response-specific residual between group-normalized graded verifier rewards and group-normalized trajectory-level OPD scores, preserving graded within-group differences, then distributes it across tokens via bounded relative-OPD-advantage credits without step labels or extra sampling; also diagnoses length-dependent teacher–verifier disagreement in long-context tasks.

on_policy_mechanism.evidence_quote: On-policy distillation (OPD) trains a student on its own responses using dense

opd_classification.reasoning: Core method modifies the OPD advantage by adding an RL-style verifier-reward residual (group-normalized, GRPO-inspired) to the dense teacher log-prob signal and distributes it via token weighting, i.e., an RL-augmented OPD objective.

stabilization_tricks: group/token std thresholds τ=1e-6 (fallback to vanilla OPD / unit credit)
residual coefficient β=0.10 selected on held-out set

key_findings: GC-OPD raises five-benchmark averages of Qwen3-4B from 29.08 (raw) / 39.31 (vanilla OPD) to 40.47 and Qwen3-8B from 35.12 / 43.56 to 44.65, the highest among OPD, ExOPD, Uni-OPD, PowerOPD, FiRe-OPD under a shared 100-step setup.

Trajectory-level OPD scores become less aligned with verifier rewards as prompts lengthen: MTE pairwise disagreement rises from 40.6% (<8K) to 64.0% (32–64K) and preference gap drops from +0.35 to −0.37; HRR goes from 35.2% to 60.2% and +0.65 to −0.35.
Signed residual beats controls on Qwen3-8B: Additional OPD term 43.60 (+0.04), direct group-normalized reward 44.19 (+0.63), GC-OPD residual 44.65 (+1.10).
RACA token allocation (44.65) outperforms uniform (44.28) and absolute-OPD credit (43.93).
Largest gains over vanilla OPD concentrate on CorpusQA (32.22→37.99 for 4B; 39.82→43.77 for 8B), i.e., evidence-aggregation tasks.
A single residual coefficient β=0.10 selected on a 231-example HRR holdout works for both model scales.
GC-OPD adds no extra teacher or student forward pass beyond vanilla OPD.
2608.19181.ablations_summary: On Qwen3-8B, adding another credit-modulated OPD term gives +0.04, adding group-normalized verifier reward directly gives +0.63, and the signed residual gives +1.10; for token allocation, uniform credit gives +0.72, absolute-OPD-magnitude credit +0.38, RACA +1.10 — residual calibration is the main contributor, RACA adds a further gain.
limitations: Main results table alone does not isolate task-specific mechanisms; gains are not uniform across tasks (Frames and LBv1QA show smaller or model-dependent changes).
Disagreement diagnostics use fixed responses and characterize signal disagreement rather than causal effects of task type or context length; prevalence is task-dependent.
Baselines are implementations of each method's principal mechanism under the shared setup, not exact reproductions of original recipes.
Coefficient holdout contains only the High-Recall Retrieval task family.
Only two Qwen3 students and one Qwen3 teacher evaluated; work in progress preprint.
failure_modes: GC-OPD underperforms vanilla OPD on LBv1QA for Qwen3-4B (55.80 vs 57.10) and slightly on Frames/MRCR for 4B.
When within-group verifier or OPD variance is near zero (e.g., all rollouts same reward), the residual is zero and the method reduces to vanilla OPD.
Absolute-OPD credit (sign-discarding) can assign large credit to strongly negative OPD tokens and yields weaker gains (43.93).

theory.theoretical_claim: Signed residual ordering is verifier-consistent under strict teacher–verifier disagreement: if R(i)>R(j) and s(i)<s(j) then ρ(i)−ρ(j)>0 (Eq. 8); token OPD advantage expectation equals negative reverse KL (Eq. 2)
theory.proof_sketch: ρ(i)−ρ(j) = (R(i)−R(j))/σ_R − (s(i)−s(j))/σ_s; both terms positive under the strict disagreement, so the difference is positive.

2608.19181.relevance_to_opd: Directly extends vanilla OPD (Agarwal et al.) for long-context tasks by combining dense reverse-KL token advantages from a Qwen3-30B-A3B teacher with GRPO-style group-normalized verifier rewards via a disagreement residual and token-level credit assignment; belongs to the verifier-aware / RL-augmented OPD line alongside SCOPE, MOPD, Uni-OPD, SG-OPD.

2608.26550.title: SPEAR: Distilling Domain-Adaptive Reasoning Skeletons via Sequential Symbolic Alignment in Reinforcement Learning
2608.26550.summary: Training-free LCS-based symbolic process reward for RL-based sequence-level distillation

method.training_loop: For each query: student samples G rollouts (GRPO/Dr.GRPO/DAPO); extract domain symbolic anchors from student <think> and pre-collected teacher rationale; reward = I_fmt*(R_acc + 0.5*LCS-F1); policy-gradient update
method.loss_formulation: J(\theta)=\mathbb{E}_{q\sim D,o\sim\pi_{\theta_{old}}}[\min(r(o)\hat A,\text{clip}(r(o),1-\epsilon,1+\epsilon)\hat A)],\ R_{spear}=I_{fmt}\cdot(R_{acc}+\lambda R_{reason}),\ R_{reason}=\frac{2|LCS(A_s,A_t)|}{|A_s|+|A_t|}
method.data_source: GSM8K, MATH, GPQA (main+extended), CommonsenseQA training splits with DeepSeek-V3.2 (deepseek-reasoner API) teacher rationales
key_components: domain-adaptive symbolic anchor extraction Φ (regex LaTeX/assignments for math, dependency-parse verb-object tuples for science, noun-chunk state-action anchors for commonsense)
LCS-F1 order-aware alignment reward between student and teacher anchor trajectories
gated composite reward I_fmt*(R_acc + λ R_reason), λ=0.5
plug-in to GRPO / Dr. GRPO / DAPO
spaCy en_core_web_sm (~12MB) instead of neural PRM

2608.26550.novelty: Replaces neural PRMs and token-level divergence with a training-free, rule-based process reward: teacher and student reasoning traces are projected into domain-specific symbolic milestone sequences and aligned with an order-aware LCS-F1, extending process supervision beyond math/code to science and commonsense with ~1.9% step overhead vs 30% for a 7B PRM.

on_policy_mechanism.evidence_quote: To ensure the reward is computable efficiently during real-time RL rollouts, we use a dynamic programming approach where the LCS alignment

opd_classification.reasoning: Student does generate on-policy rollouts (C1), but the black-box API teacher provides only a scalar rule-based reward from pre-collected rationales (no logit/distributional supervision, fails C2) and the objective is a GRPO/PPO reward loss rather than a KL divergence (fails C3); it is an RL-with-teacher-derived-reward paper.

training_setup.compute_budget: 4×A100-80GB; full SPEAR run on Qwen3-4B MATH took 23h42m (169.74 s/step)
stabilization_tricks: strict format gate I_fmt on <think>/<answer> tags
dense partial-credit process reward to prevent gradient collapse early in training
LCS-F1 harmonic mean to penalize verbose or prefix-only trajectories
uniqueness constraint on science anchors to prevent reward inflation via repetition

key_findings: SPEAR improves over the corresponding outcome-only RL baseline by ~1.94–2.29% on average across GRPO, Dr. GRPO, DAPO for both Llama-3-8B-Instruct and Qwen3-4B, versus +0.16–0.45% for Logic-RL.
Against Qwen2.5-Math-PRM-7B, SPEAR is only 0.32 pts lower on MATH but 3.37 pts higher on GPQA on average; against VersaPRM (8B) SPEAR is +0.26 on MATH and +0.51 on GPQA.
SPEAR adds only 1.87% time per step vs 30.04% for a 7B neural PRM (169.74 s vs 216.67 s; GRPO 166.62 s) with zero extra neural reward parameters.
Removing the accuracy reward causes the largest drop (30.60→25.40 MATH, 31.82→26.77 GPQA), so final-answer supervision remains the dominant signal; λ=0 drops to 28.40/29.80.

Replacing symbolic anchors with raw-token LCS-F1 reduces accuracy by 2.37 pts, Jaccard (unordered) by 2.21 pts, generic surface anchors by 2.77 pts; mismatched domain extractors reduce MATH by 2.47 and GPQA by 4.72 pts.
SFT distillation hurts commonsense (Qwen3-4B 83.95→80.90; Llama 75.67→74.75) while RL-based distillation improves it; SFT remains competitive on GPQA (Llama 33.83 beats plain RL baselines).
A moderate cold-start SFT fraction (30%) before SPEAR-RL gives the best MATH result on Qwen3-4B; more SFT degrades subsequent RL.
Commonsense state-transition extractor transfers to AlpacaEval 2.0, improving LC win rate over GRPO/Dr.GRPO/DAPO by 1.61/1.12/1.74 pts.
2608.26550.ablations_summary: Accuracy reward is the dominant component (largest drop when removed); format gate gives consistent smaller gains; process weight λ=0.5 best for MATH, 0.75 for GPQA, 1.0 degrades; symbolic anchors beat raw-token LCS (+2.37) and order-aware LCS beats Jaccard (+2.21); domain-specific extraction beats generic markers (+2.77) and mismatched extractors fall below outcome-only RL in 5/6 settings.
limitations: Symbolic anchor extraction and exact subsequence matching may fail to credit semantically equivalent but structurally different reasoning paths, especially open-ended tasks
Assumes teacher-generated rationales are reliable, though they may contain redundant or suboptimal steps
Rule-based regex/dependency-parsing pipelines are sensitive to parsing errors and formatting inconsistencies
Only sequence-level on-policy distillation explored; token-level reverse-KL distillation not studied due to compute constraints
Teacher provides a single reference trajectory, so correct alternative paths can be under-credited
failure_modes: Smallest gains on CommonsenseQA where anchors poorly capture natural-language variation
λ=1.0 over-emphasizes reasoning alignment and degrades performance
Mismatched domain extractors fall below outcome-only RL baselines
Math-specific PRM outperforms SPEAR slightly on MATH
Case study: lexical divergence (remove methylene unit vs add carbon unit) causes anchor mismatch even when reasoning is equivalent

compute_efficiency.speedup_vs_baseline: 1.87% step overhead vs 30.04% for 7B PRM (≈1.28× faster than PRM-based reward)

2608.26550.relevance_to_opd: Self-described 'sequence-level on-policy distillation' via RL: student rollouts are scored against pre-collected black-box teacher rationales using a rule-based LCS-F1 process reward rather than teacher logits/KL, so it is an RL-with-teacher-derived-reward alternative to token-level OPD (explicitly leaves reverse-KL OPD to future work); relevant as a black-box / external-feedback contrast point.

2609.02998.title: Verify Before You Distill: Prompt-Level Teacher Gating for On-Policy Distillation
2609.02998.affiliation_primary: AllSpark Team (institution not stated in text)
2609.02998.summary: Verifier-gated prompt-level admission of teacher signal in OPD, GRPO fallback otherwise

method.training_loop: Per prompt: student samples G=4 rollouts; teacher concurrently generates K_T=3 probes scored by verifier; if pass rate ≥ τ use per-token reverse-KL OPD advantage, else GRPO advantage; PPO-clip update
method.loss_formulation: \hat A^{TGOPD}_{i,t} = g(x)\hat A^{OPD}_{i,t} + (1-g(x))\hat A^{GRPO}_{i,t},\; g(x)=\mathbb{1}[q_T(x)\ge\tau],\; \hat A^{OPD}_{i,t}=\beta\,\mathrm{sg}[\log\pi_T(y^i_t|x,y^i_{<t})-\log\pi_\theta(y^i_t|x,y^i_{<t})],\; L=-\mathbb{E}\big[\tfrac1G\sum_i\tfrac1{|y^i|}\sum_t \min(\rho_{i,t}\hat A_{i,t},\mathrm{clip}(\rho_{i,t},1-\epsilon,1+\epsilon)\hat A_{i,t})\big]
method.data_source: DAPO-Math-17K (math), CodeI/O input-output prediction (code), Nemotron-Cascade 2 filtered prompts (IF)
key_components: verifier-scored teacher probes (K_T=3) estimating prompt-level reliability q_T(x)
hard reliability gate g(x)=1[q_T(x)≥τ], τ=2/3
dense reverse-KL OPD advantage when gate open
verifier-grounded GRPO fallback (no std normalization) when gate closed
asynchronous probing in idle teacher window (slime framework, IcePop/TIS)

2609.02998.novelty: Unlike distributional reliability proxies (EOPD, TrOPD, REOPOLD) or trajectory/token-level outcome gates (RG-OPD, RLSD, SPOT), TGOPD verifies teacher correctness via repeated verifier-scored teacher rollouts at the prompt level BEFORE admitting dense supervision, routing exclusively to OPD or GRPO (never blending), and exploits otherwise-idle teacher GPU capacity in asynchronous OPD to do so.

on_policy_mechanism.evidence_quote: On-policy distillation (OPD) trains a student on its own rollouts while a stronger teacher provides token-

opd_classification.reasoning: Core method is on-policy reverse-KL distillation from a frozen teacher on student rollouts, augmented with a verifier-based gate that routes unreliable prompts to GRPO (RL-augmented OPD), with a compute-efficiency angle via idle-teacher probing.

training_setup.compute_budget: 4B: 5×8-GPU nodes (40 GPUs); 35B: 7×8-GPU nodes (56 GPUs); duration unspecified (MOPD runs 199 steps)

key_findings: TGOPD beats Vanilla OPD in all six domain–scale settings; 7-benchmark averages 56.67 (4B, +2.10 over Vanilla OPD) and 63.53 (35B, +1.09), and beats the strongest baseline TrOPD by 0.16 and 0.87.
On 35B LiveCodeBench TGOPD reaches 64.0 (+4.0 over base, +3.8 over Vanilla OPD, +1.3 over the code teacher) while TrOPD/RG-OPD/RLSD-style fall below base.
Teacher confidence poorly predicts prompt-level reliability (AUROC 0.51 code, 0.73 math); in low-reliability regime the teacher's top-confidence answer is wrong 84% (code) / 61% (math).

Probing idle teacher capacity raises teacher-node GPU utilization from 9.8% to 78.9% (4B SOPD) and cluster utilization from 51.5% to 69.5%, with 5.9% mean step-time increase in a matched 35B code run.
Gate threshold sweep (K_T=5) shows inverted-U with peak at τ=3/5 (AIME26 73.1, AIME25 64.4, HMMT 58.0), τ=5/5 falls below Vanilla OPD on HMMT-Feb (52.0 vs 54.3).
In multi-domain OPD, TGOPD improves averages by +1.14 (4B) and +0.95 (35B) at 199 steps.
2609.02998.ablations_summary: Gate threshold: broad optimum around a majority vote (τ≈3/5–2/3); too strict discards useful teacher signal. Closed-gate policy: both GRPO fallback and mask-only beat ungated baseline in all four settings; GRPO fallback beats masking on single-domain math (+1.15 at 4B, +0.60 at 35B) and on OJBench, but masking is better on 4B multi-domain (−0.43), so the fallback choice is setting-dependent. 79–85% of audit-rejected math prompts have mixed-outcome student groups, so GRPO fallback yields non-zero advantages.
limitations: Requires an automatic verifier; not directly applicable to open-ended tasks
Binary hard routing decision; uncertainty-aware gates left to future work
Comparison with std-normalized GRPO fallback left to future work
Probing is not strictly free: 5.9% increase in mean step time in matched 35B code run
GRPO fallback is not uniformly better than mask-only closed-gate policy
failure_modes: Overly strict gate (τ=5/5) rejects useful teacher signal and underperforms Vanilla OPD on HMMT-Feb (52.0 vs 54.3)
Gate-closed prompts with all-correct or all-incorrect student groups produce zero GRPO advantage and no update
Slight regressions on some benchmarks (35B IFBench 43.7 vs Vanilla OPD 44.2; 4B LCB −0.48 in MOPD)

compute_efficiency.teacher_inference_cost: 1× scoring + K_T=3 probe decodes per prompt, mostly overlapped with idle teacher window
compute_efficiency.memory_footprint: separate teacher node (1/5 of cluster at 4B, 1/7 at 35B)

theory.theoretical_claim: q_T(x) is an unbiased Binomial(K_T, R_T(x))/K_T estimator of teacher reliability R_T(x)=E[r] with variance R_T(1−R_T)/K_T
theory.proof_sketch: Probes are i.i.d. draws from π_T with binary verifier reward, so K_T·q_T ~ Binomial(K_T, R_T); expectation equals R_T for any probe budget.

2609.02998.relevance_to_opd: Directly an OPD method paper: it addresses the mode-seeking reverse-KL failure mode of confidently wrong teachers by verifier-gating teacher admission per prompt and falling back to RLVR (GRPO), while improving systems efficiency of asynchronous OPD via idle-teacher probing.

2609.02548.title: Learn from Whoever Is Right: Answer-Verified Multi-Teacher Distillation for Multi-Domain LLMs
2609.02548.summary: Answer-verified multi-teacher on-policy self-distillation (MT-SDPO) for multi-domain LLMs

method.training_loop: Offline: verify each frozen teacher's private answer per sample → eligible set. Online: student samples G=8 rollouts; correct peer→self-anchor; incorrect→verified teachers' sanitized critiques; EMA self-teacher reads [anchor;feedback] context; JSD distill to student; EMA update.
method.loss_formulation: L_{MT-SDPO} = \frac{1}{Z}\sum_{i,j,t} m_i^j M_{i,t}^j w_{i,t}^j D_{JSD}\big(p_{\theta,i,t}^j \,\|\, q_{\bar\theta,i,t}^j\big), \; q_{\bar\theta,i,t}^j = sg[\pi_{\bar\theta}(\cdot|x_i,c_i^j,y^j_{i,<t})]
method.data_source: SciKnowEval L3 Science Q&A (chemistry, materials science, physics), balanced, ~9:1 train-test split; 1,953 training questions
key_components: rollout-specific self-anchors
answer-verified teacher eligibility (per-sample, domain-agnostic)
lexical sanitizer against label leakage
privileged context read only by EMA self-teacher
masked importance-weighted symmetric JSD on student top-100 support
frozen domain teachers discarded at deployment

2609.02548.novelty: Replaces MOPD's domain-label routing with per-sample answer-verified eligibility so any correct teacher (even cross-domain) may supervise, aggregates all eligible teachers' text feedback with SDPO's self-anchor into a single privileged EMA self-teacher; matched teacher correct on only 52.9% of samples vs 65.7% with any verified teacher.

on_policy_mechanism.evidence_quote: Among the routes to this problem, we study on-policy integration, which keeps the teachers frozen and lets one student learn on its own rollouts, so what remains open is which teacher supervises which rollout.

opd_classification.reasoning: Student generates on-policy rollouts and is trained via token-level JSD toward a privileged-information EMA self-teacher whose context contains self-anchors and verified external teachers' textual feedback (external teachers give black-box text, not logits).

training_setup.compute_budget: 8×H100 80GB per run, 100 updates (4 GPUs policy + 4 GPUs frozen teachers for teacher methods)
stabilization_tricks: clipped PPO proximal + truncated importance-sampling ratios (clip 2.0)
top-100 truncated support with tail mass

train: SciKnowEval L3 Science Q&A (chemistry, materials, physics)
eval: SciKnowEval L3 Science Q&A held-out (79 per domain, avg@16)

key_findings: Domain-matched teacher is correct on only 52.94% of training samples; admitting any verified teacher raises coverage to 65.69%, recovering 27.09% of what matched routing misses.
On Qwen3-8B, MT-SDPO gains +4.64 Macro and +14.79 Worst-domain over Multi-Domain PT and cuts domain gap from 20.96 to 5.30 (74.7%), beating Domain Routing by 2.90/2.05 points.
MT-SDPO on Qwen3-8B surpasses the three-model matched-teacher reference by 3.79 Macro and 11.15 Worst-domain with one deployable model.
Removing verification (all three unverified teachers) loses 6.56 Macro and 8.94 Worst-domain vs full MT-SDPO and falls 1.92 below initialization.
GRPO with the same verifier as scalar reward widens the Qwen3-8B gap from 20.96 to 21.76 while MT-SDPO shrinks it to 5.30.
Qwen3-1.7B/4B flatten domain gap (49.6%/41.5%) mostly by strong domains falling; Macro improves only at 8B and on OLMo-3-7B.
On Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct with balanced initialization, no online method improves (negative result).
2609.02548.ablations_summary: On Qwen3-8B: w/o Cross-Domain (verified domain routing) 65.08 Macro/61.79 Worst; w/o Aggregation (single eligible teacher) +1.03 Macro/+0.47 Worst but gap widens 5.14→7.99; full aggregation adds +1.00/+1.82 more and restores gap to 5.30; w/o Verification drops to 60.55/55.14. MT-SDPO uses retained teacher feedback on only 5.64% of rollouts vs 23.07% for Domain Routing.
limitations: 34.31% of training samples admit no correct teacher, bounding any method on this pool
Balanced initializations (Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct) leave little headroom; online phase does not pay off
Exact-match verification only; extension beyond exact-answer settings requires a different eligibility signal
Lexical sanitizer cannot catch every label paraphrase or certify semantic validity of feedback
Verification tests one cached completion, not the later critique nor general competence
Training trajectories are non-monotonic; comparison fixed at step 100
failure_modes: Strong domains regress at Qwen3-1.7B/4B (−11.86 and −13.85 points) while weakest gains only 4.19/1.97
Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct: Macro −3.22, Worst −6.80, gap widens 8.15→14.95
SDPO alone peaks at step 50 then loses >7 Macro points by step 100
Unverified all-teacher feedback draws on incorrect answers in 50.21% of teacher-sample pairs and degrades below initialization
2609.02548.relevance_to_opd: Extends SDPO-style privileged-information on-policy self-distillation to multi-teacher capability integration; direct successor/competitor to MOPD, replacing domain routing with per-sample verified teacher eligibility while retaining one deployable policy and frozen black-box teachers.

2609.08337.title: Distillation as Probability Transport: Routed On-Policy Distillation
2609.08337.summary: RouteOPD: OPD as explicit excess-to-deficit token probability transport

method.training_loop: for prompt: student samples 4 responses; teacher scored at each visited state; build top-k union, compute excess/deficit masses; sample m routes (a,b); Huber loss on pairwise log-odds vs bounded-potential targets; AdamW update
method.loss_formulation: L^{(t)}_{RouteOPD} = M_t \, \mathbb{E}_{(a,b)\sim q_t^- \times q_t^+}[h_\kappa(\Delta_t(a,b) - \hat{D}_t(a,b))], \; \Delta_t(a,b)=[\log\pi_\theta(b|s_t)-\log\pi_\theta(a|s_t)]-[\log\pi_{old}(b|s_t)-\log\pi_{old}(a|s_t)], \; \hat{D}_t(a,b)=\phi_{B_t}(g_t(b))-\phi_{B_t}(g_t(a))
method.data_source: DAPO-Math-17K prompts; student-generated on-policy rollouts (4 per prompt, T=1.0, max 16,384 tokens)
key_components: top-k union support (k=32) with renormalized teacher/student distributions
excess-source / deficit-destination decomposition of TV disagreement
independent product coupling with m=2 sampled routes
pairwise log-odds objective with direct-logit locality
bounded shared teacher potential (tanh) for cycle-consistent targets
demand-concentration adaptive transport budget B_t in [log1.2, log1.5]
Huber loss with kappa=1

2609.08337.novelty: Reframes sampled reverse-KL OPD as under-specified probability transport (scalar credit leaves redistribution to softmax geometry) and replaces it with explicit source-to-destination routes with cycle-consistent bounded targets and adaptive budget, unlike prior OPD work that only reshapes the scalar target/magnitude (PowerOPD, TOP-D, RG-OPD) or selects where/when to distill (TIP, TRACE, PACED).

on_policy_mechanism.evidence_quote: The teacher is scored once at every student-visited state. Routed methods reuse these scores and therefore do

opd_classification.reasoning: Proposes a new distillation objective (routed pairwise log-odds transport replacing sampled reverse-KL) applied to teacher logits on student rollouts, with an adaptive-budget variant and sparse efficiency analysis.

training_setup.compute_budget: 24×NVIDIA H20 GPUs per run, one learner epoch on DAPO-Math-17K (~300 steps)

key_findings: RouteOPD improves the four-benchmark Avg@16 over sampled reverse-KL OPD by 2.19–3.61 points across four settings (macro +2.70 [2.28,3.13]).
RouteOPD exceeds full-vocabulary reverse-KL by +1.24 [0.90,1.58] and fixed-mid routing by +1.20 [0.89,1.51] on average.
Teacher-deficit destinations (64.43) beat rank/frequency-matched (63.72) and random-background (62.72) destinations under matched fixed-mid routing.
Routing fidelity rises from 35.4% (sampled-RKL) to 90.4% and full-vocabulary background leakage falls from 68.3% to 13.8% on a frozen 1,024-state bank.
Shared bounded potential eliminates 27.6% four-cycle violations from independent edge clipping and lowers target MAE from 0.091 to 0.052 with adaptive budget.
Adaptive budget advantage over fixed-mid grows with teacher-deficit concentration: −0.10, +0.40, +1.30, +2.70 points across four bins.
Sparse k=32, m=2 routing reaches 65.53 Avg@16 at 2.5% end-to-end overhead vs 65.61 at 12.5% for full-vocabulary routing.
On AIME24, RouteOPD repairs 42 sampled-RKL failures (34 reasoning errors) while losing 21, with correct share rising from 48.1% to 52.5%.
2609.08337.ablations_summary: Destination identity (teacher-deficit 64.43 vs permutation 63.72 vs random 62.72), two-sided pairwise update (64.43 vs source-only 63.55 / destination-only 63.84), shared potential vs independent clipping (0% vs 27.6% cycle violations), adaptive vs fixed budgets (65.53 vs 64.12–64.43, reversed 63.88), support size k=32 at Pareto knee, m=2 optimal (m=4/8 drop to 62.48/61.12).
limitations: Token-level comparisons require exact tokenizer/vocabulary ID compatibility between teacher and student; incompatible pairs are excluded.
Checkpoint correlation between routing signature and accuracy is not treated as causal identification.
Zero background leakage is not expected because softmax normalization and shared parameters move unrelated probabilities.
Ideal logit-level target completion (100%) is attenuated to 88.1% by shared parameters and optimizer state.
Evaluated only on mathematical reasoning benchmarks.
failure_modes: Adaptive budgeting gives no gain (−0.10) in states with diffuse teacher-deficit demand.
Increasing sampled routes m beyond 2 reduces Avg@16 (65.53 → 62.48 at m=4, 61.12 at m=8) despite lower loss variance.
High teacher entropy makes destinations less specific, lowering fidelity (94.1% → 85.6%) and raising leakage (8.7% → 20.5%).
Independent edge clipping produces cycle-inconsistent, jointly unrealizable targets (27.6% violations).

compute_efficiency.speedup_vs_baseline: 1.0× (2.5% end-to-end overhead vs sampled-RKL at k=32, m=2)
compute_efficiency.memory_footprint: +2.0 GB peak over sampled-RKL (66.2 vs 64.2 GB)

theory.theoretical_claim: Sampled RKL OPD implicitly redistributes released mass via student softmax geometry (Prop. 1); product coupling preserves excess/deficit marginals, is max-entropy, and the m-route estimator is unbiased (Prop. 2); pairwise log-odds gradient e_b − e_a gives direct-logit locality (Prop. 3); shared bounded potential yields positive, bounded, jointly integrable targets while independent clipping can violate cycle consistency (Prop. 4).
theory.proof_sketch: Log-softmax identity ∇_z log π(a) = e_a − π gives the negative gradient |A|[π_old − e_a]; equal totals of positive/negative parts of p_S − p_T give M_t = TV; independence of the joint maximizes entropy and linearity gives unbiasedness; log-partition cancels in the pairwise difference; monotone ℓ_δ gives D* ≥ 0 and bounded ϕ_B gives D̂ in [0,B_t), realized simultaneously by shifting z_v by ϕ_B(g_t(v)).

2609.08337.relevance_to_opd: Directly a core OPD method paper: replaces the standard sampled reverse-KL OPD objective with an explicit routed probability-transport objective on teacher logits scored at student-visited states, and provides mechanism diagnostics (routing fidelity, leakage) for OPD updates.

2609.10154.title: CompassOPD: Cross-Family On-Policy Distillation via Within-Family Likelihood Shifts
2609.10154.affiliation_primary: Institute of Information Engineering, Chinese Academy of Sciences
2609.10154.summary: Cross-family OPD via within-family teacher likelihood shift with student anchor

method.training_loop: for step: student samples y~π_θ(x); align text units; score with strong teacher T and weak same-family ref R; A=sg[(ℓ_T−ℓ_R) − α(logπ_θ−logπ_ref)]; policy-gradient update
method.loss_formulation: L = -E_{y\sim\pi_\theta}[\,\mathrm{sg}[\Delta_{T,t} - \alpha(\log\pi_\theta(y_t|c_t)-\log\pi_{ref}(y_t|c_t))]\,\log\pi_\theta(y_t|c_t)],\quad \Delta_T=\ell_T(z|c)-\ell_R(z|c);\ \ J=E_{z\sim\pi}[\Delta_T]-\alpha D_{KL}(\pi\|\pi_{ref})
method.data_source: DAPO-Math and DeepScaleR-Preview prompts for on-policy training; OpenThoughts-114k with teacher-regenerated responses for cold-start SFT
key_components: decomposition of cross-family OPD signal into cross-family offset O and within-family shift ΔT
removal of offset: use ΔT = ℓ_T − ℓ_R from strong teacher and weak same-family reference
frozen student initial policy anchor −α(logπ_θ − logπ_ref)
text-space cross-tokenizer alignment into shared units with span-averaged log-likelihoods
MoE self-reference: same teacher checkpoint with reduced expert activation as R
teacher-trajectory SFT cold start shared by OPD and CompassOPD

2609.10154.novelty: First to identify that standard cross-family OPD is dominated by a pre-existing offset between a weak teacher-family model and the student (70% direction agreement between 0.8B and 35B teachers), masking capability-sensitive supervision; proposes transferring only the within-family likelihood shift (strong minus weak same-family model) anchored to the student's initial policy, and shows an MoE teacher can serve as its own reference by reducing expert activation, removing the need for a separate reference checkpoint.

on_policy_mechanism.evidence_quote: OverviewofCompassOPD.Givenstudent-generatedtrajectories,thestrongteacherT anditswithin-family

opd_classification.reasoning: Proposes a new fixed OPD objective (within-family likelihood shift advantage plus KL anchor to initial student policy) on student-sampled rollouts with white-box teacher log-likelihoods, motivated by an analysis of why cross-family OPD fails.

key_findings: CompassOPD improves average reasoning accuracy over standard cross-family OPD by up to 5.50 points (Granite4.1-3B: 30.86 vs 25.36), and by 2.14 (Qwen3-4B) and 1.81 (OLMo-3-7B).
Cross-family OPD plateaus while same-family OPD improves steadily; a 16.7-point teacher gap (Qwen3.5-35B-A3B vs 4B) yields only 0.1-point difference in distilled Qwen3-4B students.
Qwen3.5-0.8B agrees in OPD update direction with Qwen3.5-35B-A3B on 70.0% and with Qwen3.5-4B on 71.8% of aligned units, revealing a shared cross-family offset.
Restoring the removed offset (β from 0 to 80%) monotonically degrades Granite4.1-3B accuracy, erasing most gains over OPD.
With fixed 0.8B reference, accuracy scales with teacher size: 35B-A3B 30.86, 9B 29.50, 4B 28.65, 2B 26.50, all above OPD's 25.36.
MoE self-reference (Qwen3.5-35B-A3B with ~2B active params as R) gives 28.79 avg, +3.43 over OPD without a separate reference checkpoint.
Anchor strength α=0.5 is best; α=0 is worse and α>1 declines due to over-regularization.
Improves over OPD in 20/21 student-benchmark combinations (Qwen3.5 teacher) and 13/14 (Qwen3/Mistral teachers).
2609.10154.ablations_summary: Removing the cross-family offset is the key contributor (restoring it monotonically removes gains); the frozen-student anchor adds further improvement at α=0.5 but hurts when too strong; larger teacher–reference scale separation yields stronger supervision; MoE reduced-activation self-reference recovers most of the benefit (28.79 vs 30.86 with dedicated 0.8B reference).
limitations: Not evaluated on very large student/teacher models due to computational constraints.
failure_modes: Standard cross-family OPD plateaus after limited early gains and does not benefit from stronger teachers.
CompassOPD requires a low-capability same-family reference; performance degrades when teacher approaches reference scale (2B teacher: 26.50).
Excessive anchor strength (α>1) restricts student updates and lowers performance.
Positions where consistent text boundaries cannot be aligned are excluded from the loss.

compute_efficiency.teacher_inference_cost: 2× (strong teacher + reference scoring per rollout; MoE self-reference uses two forward passes of same checkpoint)

theory.theoretical_claim: Closed-form optimal policy of reference-regularized objective: π*(z|c) ∝ π_ref(z|c) exp(ΔT(z,c)/α); objective equals α log Z − α KL(π∥π*)
theory.proof_sketch: Define Z(c)=Σ_z π_ref exp(ΔT/α); substitute log(π*/π_ref)=ΔT/α − log Z into J = E_π[ΔT] − α KL(π∥π_ref), yielding J = α log Z − α KL(π∥π*), maximized iff π=π*.

2609.10154.relevance_to_opd: Directly extends the sampled OPD (Thinking Machines) formulation to cross-family/cross-tokenizer teachers by reformulating the token-level advantage as a within-teacher-family likelihood shift plus a KL anchor to the initial student; identifies a failure mode of cross-family OPD and provides a reference-based fix.

method.training_loop: teacher writes questions under simple prompt (no filtering) → student samples 4 rollouts/prompt → frozen teacher prefill gives top-16 log-diffs → reverse-KL policy-gradient update

key_components: teacher self-generated training questions (no seeds, no filtering)
on-policy student rollouts with top-k reverse-KL teacher supervision
signal coverage metric (fraction of teacher correction exposed by visited states)
domain-labeled prompts for multi-teacher OPD obtained for free from generating teacher
base-template (no-question) OPD extension

opd_classification.reasoning: Standard OPD (student rollouts + teacher top-k reverse KL) with the contribution being data efficiency: OPD needs almost no prompts and can run on teacher-self-generated questions, plus analysis of why.

stabilization_tricks: top-k (k=16) truncated distributions on student side
thinking mode disabled to match non-thinking teacher

benchmarks.name: Six-math-benchmark macro average (RL-tuned pairing, R1-Distill-1.5B ← JustRL-1.5B)
Six-math-benchmark macro average (larger-parameter pairing, Qwen3-1.7B ← Qwen3-30B-A3B)

key_findings: Eight prompts match the full 17k DAPO dataset: 56.3 vs 56.4 on the RL-tuned pairing and 49.9 vs 47.4 on the larger-parameter pairing; a single prompt stays within 3.6 points.
DAPO, DeepMath and ORZ differ threefold in initial teacher–student KL (0.268/0.089/0.132) and in pass rate (0.461/0.620/0.689) yet produce nearly indistinguishable OPD curves.
Signal coverage for a single problem rises from 0.114 at 1 trajectory to 0.507 at 4096, while going from 8 to 1k problems adds only +0.079 coverage.
Training on DeepCoder (competitive programming) recovers 96% and 92% of the in-domain math gain at |D|=1k, indicating OPD transfers a mode of reasoning rather than knowledge.
Self-generated questions (|D|=64) reach 56.61 vs 56.41 real data on the RL-tuned pairing and 49.16 vs 47.36 on the larger-parameter pairing.
In three-domain MOPD, 1k self-generated questions close 98.5% of headroom (Total 31.31) vs 96.6% (31.18) with 7,458 real examples.

Self-generated questions track the teacher's own post-training data on initial student top-k KL (0.32 vs 0.26), top-k overlap (0.72 vs 0.72) and overlap mass (0.023 vs 0.019), unlike DeepMath/ORZ/DeepCoder.
Base-template (no question) OPD recovers 62.1% of the gap on the RL-tuned pairing but only 2.3% on Qwen3-1.7B and 25.9% under MOPD, tracking the student's self-QA rate (62.0%/0.1%/11.8%).
2609.14193.ablations_summary: Data quantity tiers |D|=1/8/64/256/1k/17k show saturation at 8 prompts (single teacher) and at ~1k under MOPD (75.6/84.8/91.3/98.5%); dataset swaps (DeepMath, ORZ, DeepCoder) show insensitivity to difficulty, information content and even domain; self-generated vs real data; base template vs self-generated vs real.

Training-dynamics analysis confined to the RL-tuned pairing since the larger-parameter teacher's post-training data is unavailable.
MOPD checkpoints selected on the reported benchmarks with no held-out selection set.
Self-generated data slightly behind real data on code in MOPD (80.0% vs 88.0% recovery).

2609.14193.relevance_to_opd: Directly studies the data side of OPD, showing extreme data efficiency and that OPD can be run with no external corpus by having the teacher generate its own prompts, in both single- and multi-teacher settings; complements algorithmic OPD work and One-shot OPD.

2609.14708.title: Lightning Weave: Improving the Accuracy–Efficiency Frontier of Reasoning Models through Capability Composition
2609.14708.summary: Compose multiple anchor-pair policy shifts into one tilted KL target on cached student rollouts

method.training_loop: Sample 4 rollouts/prompt from initial student π_b once; cache; score each (post,pre) anchor pair log-ratio on cached states; build tilted target q_w∝π_b·exp(Σw_i r_i/α); minimize KL(π_θ‖q_w) on cached states
method.loss_formulation: L_{joint}(\theta;w)=\alpha\,\mathbb{E}_{s\sim d_{\pi_b}}[D_{KL}(\pi_\theta(\cdot|s)\,\|\,q_w(\cdot|s))],\quad q_w(a|s)=\frac{\pi_b(a|s)}{Z_w(s)}\prod_i\Big(\frac{\pi_i^+(a|s)}{\pi_i^-(a|s)}\Big)^{w_i/\alpha}
method.data_source: 3,200 math prompts from Skywork-OR1-RL-Data (DAPO format); 3,200 code prompts from KlearReasoner-CodeSub-15K; 4 student responses/prompt (12,800 cached trajectories)
key_components: anchor-pair policy shift (log π+ − log π−) as dense token reward (DOPD)
offline caching of student trajectories and anchor scores (Lightning OPD)
Tilted-Target DOPD: explicit target q ∝ π_b exp(r/α) with fixed point
statewise weighted composition of multiple anchor shifts
cross-tokenizer alignment via byte-level prefix projection with atomic-mapping mask
finite-candidate (top-16 + other) target with squared log-residual surrogate

2609.14708.novelty: Unlike online DOPD (which serves 2K anchor models live) and the naive cached surrogate (whose regularizer does not vanish at the intended target), Lightning Weave defines an explicit exponentially tilted target on cached student states with a provable fixed point, and composes multiple independently trained specialists' policy shifts (accuracy- and efficiency-oriented) into one joint target at shared student token states without requiring parameter compatibility, yielding a controllable Pareto frontier.

on_policy_mechanism.evidence_quote: Allanchorsscorethesamecachedstudenttrajectories,whichare

opd_classification.reasoning: Student-generated rollouts (cached from the initial student) receive token-level logit-derived supervision from external anchor pairs via a new fixed tilted-target KL objective; caching also gives a compute-efficiency contribution.

training_setup.compute_budget: 8×H100; 7.17–11.55 GPU-hours per composition (vs 15.49–19.66 for Online DOPD)
stabilization_tricks: Tilted-target construction with explicit fixed point (zero loss/gradient at target)
clamp residual masses below 1e-8 and log arguments below 1e-30

key_findings: On Qwen3.5-4B, Lightning Weave raises HMMT 2025 accuracy from 59.2% to 64.0% with 10.7% fewer tokens and LiveCodeBench v5 from 41.7% to 54.2% with 9.6% fewer tokens.
On Qwen3-4B, average accuracy improves by 4.02 points while response tokens drop 19.7%; AES 0.41 vs 0.23 (Klear-only) and −0.09 (DECS-only).
Lightning Weave achieves the highest AES across all five student backbones, outperforming both single-anchor policies.
Sweeping the Klear–DECS weight ρ_DECS traces an empirical Pareto frontier; ρ=0.625 reaches 84.9% AIME 2024 with 15,048 tokens, beating SimpleSD, Art, PromptCoT 2.0 and model interpolation.

Tilted-Target matches Online DOPD (avg acc 59.94 vs 59.96 Klear-only; 59.92 vs 60.93 two-anchor) while beating Naive Offline by 1.51 and 3.85 avg points for Klear and DECS, and using 17.6% fewer tokens in the two-anchor setting.
Statewise composition beats Data Mixture on all five benchmarks with 3.8–8.7% fewer tokens; sequential composition is strongly order-sensitive.
Three-anchor Klear+DECS+MiMo-RL composition reaches the highest AES of 0.42 on Qwen3-4B.
Offline pipeline cuts GPU-hours per composition by 1.70–2.18× vs Online DOPD and 4.58× amortized over five compositions.
2609.14708.ablations_summary: Tilted-target correction is comparable to online DOPD and clearly better than the naive cached surrogate (which drifts, e.g., Klear-only tokens balloon to 20,289 and AES −0.15); statewise joint-target composition (AES 0.41) beats data mixture (0.29) and both sequential orders (0.31/0.37); additional anchors (MiMo-RL) shift the operating point predictably toward the added capability.
limitations: Experiments limited to models below 10B parameters; larger-scale benefits not established.
Requires access to matched anchor pairs (post-trained specialist and its pre-anchor checkpoint), which may be unavailable for new tasks.
Efficiency gains are smaller than methods optimized exclusively for efficient reasoning.

Theory assumes full action distribution and fixed cached states; finite-candidate surrogate and cross-tokenizer alignment are approximations, and cached states may not cover states after large policy change.
failure_modes: Naive offline cached surrogate lacks a fixed point and continues pushing after the shift is absorbed, producing longer outputs and lower accuracy (e.g., Klear-only NaiveOffline AES −0.15).
Combining two accuracy anchors (Klear+MiMo-RL) increases accuracy but substantially increases tokens (18,577 vs 15,723 base on Qwen3-4B).
Sequential composition is order-sensitive; last-applied anchor dominates the outcome.
Positions where a student candidate does not map atomically to an anchor token are masked (up to 6.2% of positions lost).

theory.theoretical_claim: Exponential-tilting identity: the tilted distribution q ∝ π_b exp(r/α) is the unique maximizer of the per-state KL-regularized DOPD objective; the tilted-target KL loss equals the negative regularized objective up to a constant and has zero loss and zero gradient at π_θ=q (fixed point), unlike the cached sampled-KL surrogate (counterexample given); multi-anchor target is a product of weighted policy ratios with permutation/baseline/scale invariances.
theory.proof_sketch: Expand KL(p‖T_r) using log T_r = log b + r/α − log Z, giving αKL(p‖T_r) = αKL(p‖b) − Σp r + α log Z; Gibbs' inequality yields uniqueness; gradient of KL at equality reduces to ∇Σπ=0; a two-action counterexample shows the cached estimator exp(ℓ)−1−ℓ under b-sampled actions has nonzero derivative at the exact target.

2609.14708.relevance_to_opd: Directly extends the OPD/DOPD family: it uses student-generated trajectories with dense token-level logit-ratio supervision from external anchor pairs, contributes a new fixed tilted-target KL objective with a provable fixed point for offline (cached) OPD, and demonstrates multi-teacher capability composition for the accuracy–efficiency frontier.

2609.23989.title: ACLArena: Agent Continual Learning in Multi-stage Post-training
2609.23989.summary: Benchmark + analysis of agent continual learning; proposes Mixed OPD and MLE

method.training_loop: Sequential SFT/RL stages → MMOPD: student (final ckpt) rolls out on balanced mixed prompts; domain-owning frozen teacher ckpt scores tokens; mixed rev-KL + entropy-gated top-q fwd-KL
method.loss_formulation: L_{MOPD,t} = D_{KL}(\pi_{i+1}(\cdot|h_t)\|\pi_i(\cdot|h_t)) + \gamma \mathbb{1}(H^{tea}_t>\alpha)\sum_{v\in S^q_t}\tilde\pi_i(v|h_t)\log\frac{\tilde\pi_i(v|h_t)}{\pi_{i+1}(v|h_t)};\; L_{MMOPD}=\mathbb{E}_{k\sim U(K)}\mathbb{E}_{x\sim D_k,\hat y\sim\pi_\theta}[\sum_t L_{MOPD,t}(\pi_\theta;\pi_k)]
method.data_source: DAPO-Math-17K, NaturalQuestions, τ3-Bench (retail), IFTrain; 3,000 prompts per domain for OPD; student rollouts in agentic environments
key_components: Sequential multi-stage post-training pipeline (Math→Search→E-commerce→IF)
Mixed OPD (MOPD): reverse KL + entropy-gated top-q forward KL
Multi-teacher routing by prompt domain tag (no logit ensembling)
Self-distilled fine-tuning (SDFT) from filtered oracle trajectories
Model merging via task vectors
Mixture of Low-Rank Experts (MLE): SDFT backbone + per-stage LoRA RL experts routed by environment context
Model-level (PCA/cosine) and token-level (entropy-split consistency) diagnostics

2609.23989.novelty: First controlled comparison of multi-teacher OPD, SDFT, and model merging for agent continual learning; introduces token-selective Mixed OPD that injects forward-KL only at high-teacher-entropy tokens to fix reverse-KL collapse on agentic tasks; proposes MLE (SDFT + routed LoRA RL experts) to mitigate forgetting.
