opd_classification.reasoning: MOPD is an adaptive per-token objective switching between reverse KL and top-q forward KL based on teacher entropy, applied to student rollouts scored by frozen white-box teacher checkpoints; paper also analyzes OPD failure modes in agentic continual learning.

teacher.name: Seq-Math / Seq-Search / Seq-E-commerce / Seq-IF (four Qwen3-8B stage checkpoints)

stabilization_tricks: teacher routing by domain tag instead of logit averaging
masking environment tokens (tool observations, simulated-user turns)
GSPO sequence-level clipping for RL stages

key_findings: Sequential training causes non-monotonic forgetting: AIME26 drops from 25.83 to 6.04 after the E-commerce stage and NQ from 45.2 to 14.6, only partially recovering (10.21, 33.5) after IF.
MMOPD on Seq-Final recovers AIME26 10.21→21.25, NQ 33.5→45.2, single-hop 44.9→53.7, multi-hop 25.0→32.8 while largely preserving IF-Eval (84.8→84.6) and τ3-Telecom (45.9).
Vanilla reverse-KL OPD collapses on agentic search (truncate ratio → 100%, valid ratio → 0); forward-KL is stable but weak; Mixed OPD trains stably and sharpens decisions.
Single-teacher MOPD lifts student NQ from 14.6 to 48.4, surpassing the search teacher (45.2).
SFT updates are 3–7× larger in relative magnitude than RL/MMOPD updates; SDFT moves farthest in parameter space (cross-init update cosine 0.77).
Token-level: ~94% of positions are low-entropy (H<0.5) and stay ~0.997 consistent across stages; high-entropy positions drop to ~0.68.
MLE (SDFT + LoRA RL experts) achieves 49.7 NQ, 32.9 τ3-Retail, 85.0 IF-Eval, 42.4 GPQA, best on single-/multi-hop search and τ3-Mock among consolidation methods.
Isolated per-domain RL increments are mutually near-orthogonal in weight space (|cos| ≤ 0.004).
2609.23989.ablations_summary: Single-teacher MOPD (Table 3) shows strong search recovery beyond teacher; Appendix C shows reverse-KL-only OPD collapses and forward-KL-only underfits while mixed OPD is stable; SDFT from Seq-Final beats from Base and Balanced-Mix beats Random-Mix on average; model merging weight sweeps only shift trade-offs (uniform best avg 31.63).
limitations: Experiments limited to Qwen3-8B-Base and a fixed four-stage curriculum; generalization across model families and training orders unclear.
MLE routes by observable environment context; untested when context is ambiguous, changes mid-interaction, or requires combining multiple specializations.
failure_modes: Vanilla reverse-KL OPD collapses on agentic search: teacher assigns very low probability to critical connective/termination tokens (advantage ≈ −10), truncation rises to 100%.
Pure forward-KL OPD is stable but cannot learn critical decisions (limited distillation capacity).
MMOPD slightly degrades MMLU (79.5→79.2), τ3-Retail (29.6→27.7) and IF-Bench (30.8→30.5).
SDFT recovers search but sharply degrades E-commerce (τ3-Telecom 45.9→21.7) and IF-Eval (84.8→53.6).
2609.23989.relevance_to_opd: Directly studies multi-teacher on-policy distillation as a capability-consolidation stage in agentic continual learning, proposes an entropy-gated mixed reverse/forward-KL OPD objective, documents reverse-KL collapse on agentic tasks, and compares OPD against SDFT and model merging under controlled settings.

2609.26708.title: Train Where the Quantized Model Goes: On-Policy Distillation for Low-Bit Reasoning
2609.26708.affiliation_primary: Institute of Automation, Chinese Academy of Sciences
2609.26708.summary: OPD stage after QAD recovers long-form reasoning in sub-3-bit quantized LLMs

method.training_loop: Init from QAD ckpt; per step: 8 prompts, sample G completions via quantized fwd path (vLLM); frozen BF16 teacher scores tokens; loss = GRPO adv term + β·reverse-KL; update BF16 master weights
method.loss_formulation: L_{OPD}(\theta) = -\mathbb{E}[\sum_t \hat{A}(x,\hat{y}) \log \pi_\theta(\hat{y}_t|x,\hat{y}_{<t})] + \beta \mathbb{E}[\sum_t \log \frac{\pi_\theta(\hat{y}_t|x,\hat{y}_{<t})}{\pi_T(\hat{y}_t|x,\hat{y}_{<t})}], \beta=1
method.data_source: Math phase: GSM8K train, MATH L1–3 train, DAPO-Math; Code phase: MBPP train, KodCode (prompts only; completions sampled by student)
key_components: QAD (EdgeRazor mixed-precision) initialization at 2.79/1.88 effective bits
Student rollouts through deployment quantized forward path (BF16 master weights updated)
Frozen BF16 teacher (student's own full-precision copy) providing per-token reverse-KL on student prefixes
Group-relative advantage (GRPO-style) verifier rewards for math answer / code test execution
Two-phase math-then-code schedule with checkpoint selection every 20 steps

2609.26708.novelty: First to apply on-policy distillation to extreme low-bit (sub-3-bit) quantization recovery; diagnoses quantization-amplified exposure bias (95% budget exhaustion, 70% repetitive loops on MATH-500 after QAD) as the cause of reasoning collapse, and shows that sampling through the quantized forward path with the model's own BF16 copy as teacher recovers trajectory control far more efficiently than continued teacher-forced QAD under matched step budgets and 2×/3× budgets.

opd_classification.reasoning: Core method is OPD (student quantized rollouts + reverse-KL from frozen full-precision teacher + verifier reward) applied to a new domain—low-bit quantization recovery—with the distillation term dominating the loss.

training_setup.compute_budget: OPD stage: 57 GPU-hours / 14h wall-clock (Qwen3-4B W1.88, 260 steps); 11 GPU-hours / 2.8h (Falcon3-1B W2.79, 245 steps); QAD init 820 and 253 GPU-hours respectively
stabilization_tricks: QAD initialization before OPD (RTN start has nothing worth sampling)
Checkpoint selection every 20 steps by validation
BF16 master weights with quantized rollout path

eval: QA9 (ARC-Easy, ARC-Challenge, HellaSwag, SocialIQA, OpenBookQA, PIQA, WinoGrande, TruthfulQA, MMLU)

benchmarks.name: MATH-500 avg BF16 retention (4 models × 2 widths)

key_findings: After QAD, sub-3-bit models retain 86% of BF16 on QA9 but only 27% on MATH-500 and 16% on AMC23; retention falls monotonically with required generation length.
QAD Qwen3-0.6B W2.79 exhausts the decoding budget on 95% of MATH-500 problems and ends in repeated 8-grams 70% of the time (BF16: 27% and 12%); OPD cuts these to 53% and 17%.
OPD raises average BF16 retention from 35.3% to 69.7% on MATH-500 and 66% to 91% on HumanEval across four models at 2.79 and 1.88 bits, while QA9 retention rises from 88.1% to 92.1%.
OPD beats continued teacher-forced QAD in all 16 matched-budget comparisons; for Qwen3-1.7B W2.79 MATH-500 reaches 45.6% vs 23.2%.
OPD's share of GSM8K recovery grows at lower precision, from 11% to 73% for Qwen3-4B; at 1.88 bits GSM8K goes 17.36→64.59 and MBPP 11.6→48.7.
OPD stage costs 57 GPU-hours vs 820 for QAD on Qwen3-4B W1.88 (14–23× fewer), yielding up to 42× more GSM8K points per thousand steps.

Self-teacher (student's own BF16 weights) matches or beats 4B/8B teachers for students ≥1.7B; only Qwen3-0.6B needs a larger (1.7B) teacher because its BF16 pass@4 (62%) barely exceeds the quantized student (36–39%).
Extending QAD to 2× and 3× the matched budget yields no further gain; QAD 3× still trails OPD phase-1 by 8.9–18.1 GSM8K points.
With β=1 the distillation term dominates the loss while the policy-gradient term stays near 0.05; policy entropy drops from ~10 to 0.35 nats/token within 30 steps.
2609.26708.ablations_summary: OPD vs continued teacher-forced QAD under matched checkpoints, corpora, steps, LR and samples: OPD wins all 16 comparisons (Table 4); 2×/3× QAD budgets do not close the gap (Table 9). Teacher choice (Table 8): self BF16 teacher suffices for ≥1.7B students (e.g., Qwen3-1.7B W1.88: +18.88 GSM8K self vs +15.62/+15.84 for 4B/8B); 0.6B needs 1.7B teacher (+13.87 vs +2.80 self). β fixed at 1 in all runs, not tuned.

Reproduced QAD deviates from released recipe (effective batch 768 vs 1024/1536; KV cache at 16 bits)

Falcon3-1B shows only modest gains (e.g., MATH-500 16.0→19.2 at W2.79)
failure_modes: Self-distillation fails when the full-precision teacher is barely stronger than the quantized student (Qwen3-0.6B: +2.80 GSM8K vs +13.87 with 1.7B teacher)
Teacher-forced QAD continued past matched budget can degrade (Qwen3-0.6B W2.79 3× run falls below 1× baseline)
AMC23 recovery remains weak on small models (e.g., Qwen3-0.6B W2.79 4.69 vs BF16 7.81; Falcon3-1B W2.79 drops 5.00→2.50)

2609.26708.relevance_to_opd: Direct OPD paper: student generates rollouts through its deployment quantized path, frozen full-precision teacher gives per-token reverse-KL on student prefixes, augmented with GRPO verifier rewards (β=1, distillation dominates loss). Extends OPD (GKD/MiniLLM/Thinking Machines recipe) to the new domain of sub-3-bit quantization recovery, framing quantization as an amplifier of exposure bias and showing self-teacher (BF16 copy) OPD suffices.

2609.29142.title: Not Every Token Is Worth Distilling: Selective Supervision for Direct-OPD
2609.29142.summary: JSD-based state masking (top-10%) for Direct-OPD weak-to-strong transfer

method.training_loop: for step: student samples rollouts; compute teacher & reference top-K probs; score states by teacher–reference JSD; keep top-10% per response; apply Direct-OPD log-ratio reward + KL-to-init only on kept states
method.loss_formulation: J_{S2D-OPD}(\theta)=E_{x\sim D,(s_t,y_t)\sim\pi_\theta}[\Delta_t(y_t|s_t)-\alpha D_{KL}[\pi_\theta(\cdot|s_t)\|\pi_{stu}(\cdot|s_t)] \mid m_t=1],\ \Delta_t(v|s_t)=\log\frac{\pi_T(v|s_t)}{\pi_{ref}(v|s_t)},\ m_t=1\{t\in TopK_{t}(\tilde d_t,\lceil\rho|T|\rceil)\},\ \tilde d_t=D_{JS}(\tilde\pi_T\|\tilde\pi_{ref})
method.data_source: Skywork-OR1-RL-Data (math subset) prompts; student-generated rollouts
key_components: Direct-OPD log-ratio reward (post-RL teacher vs pre-RL reference)
top-K=16 student candidate set with residual token
teacher–reference JSD scoring per state
per-response top-10% state retention mask
adaptive KL anchor to initial student
mass-invariance construction (Prop. 1)

2609.29142.novelty: First to show Direct-OPD's log-ratio reward is invariant to the probability mass behind the policy shift (while JSD/KL vanish), and to use teacher–reference JSD to mask low-divergence states, yielding gains over dense Direct-OPD at zero extra forward passes; differs from OPD2's sign-gating and TIP/TA-OPD's teacher–student disagreement criteria by ranking on teacher–reference divergence.

on_policy_mechanism.evidence_quote: which ranks student-sampled states by their teacher–reference JSD and masks Direct-OPD supervision at low-divergence states

opd_classification.reasoning: Core contribution is a token/state-selection (masking) rule for on-policy distillation supervision, motivated by a theoretical probability-mass mismatch analysis.

training_setup.compute_budget: 8×H200, 300 training steps per configuration, single run each
stabilization_tricks: adaptive sign-based KL coefficient controller (α0=2.5, ε=0.01, [0.5,2.5])
top-K=16 candidate support with residual token
per-response state selection (mask independent of batch)

benchmarks.name: Held-out Test Avg (mean over 8 settings, vs dense Direct-OPD)

key_findings: S2D-OPD with top-10% JSD retention improves held-out Test Avg over dense Direct-OPD in 7 of 8 teacher–student settings and ties in the eighth (mean gain 0.95 points, 95% CI 0.40–1.54, p=6.4e-4).
Random 10% of states reaches 51.2 peak validation vs 51.3 for dense Direct-OPD, showing dense supervision is largely redundant; the top-JSD bin reaches 52.9.
Gain in peak validation accuracy is approximately log-linear in mean training JSD of retained states (R²=0.97 over 11 subsets).
Training only on the three lowest-JSD bins degrades the student below initialization and the two lowest bins collapse.
Masking helps more under the lower-JSD QuestA pair (1.0–1.7 pts) than JustRL (0.0–1.2 pts), suggesting gains come from filtering harmful low-divergence supervision.
Forward KL, reverse KL, and JSD selection all beat dense Direct-OPD from step 160 onward; retention rate 5–20% changes peak accuracy by <1 point (52.2–53.0).
S2D-OPD avoids Direct-OPD's late-stage collapse on Qwen3-4B (final 71.6–74.1 vs 67.2) without extra forward passes.
2609.29142.ablations_summary: JSD percentile bins show graded utility (top bin > random 10% ≈ dense; bottom bins harmful/collapse); divergence measure (JSD vs forward/reverse KL) and selection scope (response vs batch) have little effect; retention ratio 5–20% robust; top-16 token overlap analysis shows top-JSD bin increases teacher overlap while preserving reference overlap.
limitations: JSD scores magnitude of teacher change, not correctness; adverse RL shifts are retained as readily as corrections
JSD is blind to what the student needs (depends on student only via top-K set)
Scale/scope limited: 1.5B teachers, students up to 8B, math reasoning only
Single training run per configuration; CI reflects problem resampling, not seed variance
failure_modes: Training exclusively on low-JSD states drives student below initialization and collapses
Retained states can reinforce teacher errors (e.g., incorrect parity judgment, Fig. 11)

theory.theoretical_claim: Mass invariance: Direct-OPD log-ratio reward and gradient stay fixed and nonzero as candidate mass ε→0 while JSD and both KLs scale as ε and vanish; JSD upper-bounds TV distance (D_TV ≤ sqrt(2 D_JS)) hence teacher behavioral change
theory.proof_sketch: Construct teacher/reference as εt, εq on student top-K and (1−ε)b on the shared tail; the common factor ε cancels in every log-ratio so the reward/gradient are ε-free (nonzero since t≠q, top-K ⊊ V), while the shared tail contributes zero to divergences and ε factors out on the candidate set; Pinsker on each KL term of JSD gives the TV bound.

2609.29142.relevance_to_opd: Directly extends Direct-OPD (weak-to-strong on-policy distillation of RL-induced policy shifts) with a divergence-based token/state selection rule, contributing to the token-weighting/selective-supervision subfield of OPD and to theoretical understanding of log-ratio reward failure modes.

2608.20334.title: Exploring the Performance Frontier of Compact Unified Image Generation Models
2608.20334.summary: Swift-Image: compact 6B/3B unified T2I+editing DiT via parallel RL and multi-teacher OPD

method.training_loop: Progressive pretrain(256→1024px) → CT → SFT → parallel DiffusionNFT RL experts → multi-teacher on-policy distillation into mixed-RL student → pruning 6B→3B + DMD2 few-step distillation
method.loss_formulation: L = L_{diff} + \lambda_{KD} \| v_{3B}(z_t,t,c) - sg(v_{6B}(z_t,t,c)) \|_2^2
method.data_source: Internal capability-centric T2I/TI2I corpus (Wang et al. 2026), human-verified SFT subset, rubric-based online rewards
key_components: 6B parallel single-stream DiT with Qwen3-VL-8B encoder and FLUX.2 AE
progressive coarse-to-fine curriculum (500K/200K/10K steps)
parallel expert RL with DiffusionNFT and task-routed rewards
multi-teacher on-policy distillation (DiffusionOPD/DanceOPD style) for expert consolidation
Prompt Enhancer trained with SFT + renderer-grounded GRPO
structural pruning 6B→3B with velocity KD
few-step DMD2/CDM distillation with dynamic backward simulation

2608.20334.novelty: Not a new distillation algorithm; contribution is a training-engineering recipe combining parallel expert RL with multi-teacher OPD, pruning, and few-step distillation to push a 6B image generator to leading open-source editing scores under 243K GPU hours.

on_policy_mechanism.evidence_quote: We initialize a shared student from the mixed-task policy and distill each on-policy sample from its domain-matched expert, combining generalist balance with specialist strength.

opd_classification.reasoning: Output modality is images (diffusion transformer), out of OPD text-LM scope, and the paper is a system/recipe report applying existing DiffusionOPD/DanceOPD rather than proposing a new distillation objective.

training_setup.rl_algorithm: DiffusionNFT (diffusion RL) for renderer; GRPO for Prompt Enhancer
stabilization_tricks: CFG-enabled rollout with CFG-free policy optimization
parallel expert RL to avoid gradient interference
late-stage biased stopping in backward simulation
decoupled re-noising below stopping noise level
QK RMSNorm + Sandwich Norm + Tanh-gated modulation

train: internal capability-centric T2I/TI2I corpus (Wang et al. 2026)
synthesized PE data (Universal/Reasoning) verified by Gemini 3.1 Pro/Claude/GPT-Image

benchmarks.name: Editing Overall Table 1 (6B w/ PE API)

key_findings: RL + multi-teacher OPD improves Swift-Image-6B editing overall from 3.98 to 4.16, with REDEdit rising 3.98→4.34 and PiPractical 3.69→3.92.
Few-step distilled Swift-Image-6B-Turbo (8 steps) reaches 4.20 overall, slightly exceeding its 50-step RL teacher at 4.16.
Swift-Image-6B with API-based Prompt Enhancer achieves 4.41 overall, best among open-source editors and third overall including proprietary models.
Pruned 3B model incurs nearly no loss (4.15 vs 4.16 overall) and outperforms FLUX.2-klein-4B.
Prompt Enhancer lifts CPI-Intelligent from 2.26 to 4.23 (6B) and Pi-ExpertVerse-T2I from 2.49 to 4.63.
Parallel single-stream DiT improves inference efficiency ~10% with minor quality cost; block-shared modulation frees parameters for attention/MLP.

Refined Muon optimizer scheme not yet integrated into formal pre-training
Kimi-Attn residual and conditional feature-reuse degradation not fully understood

Joint few-step distillation of T2I and editing yields a student worse at both

2608.20334.relevance_to_opd: Applies multi-teacher on-policy distillation (citing GKD, MOPD, DiffusionOPD, DanceOPD) to consolidate RL expert diffusion models into one image generator; illustrates OPD transfer to non-text modality but is out of LLM-OPD scope and contributes no new distillation objective.

2608.20554.title: aiXamine: Unified Black-Box Evaluation of Cross-Dimensional Trade-offs in LLM Safety, Security, and Privacy
2608.20554.summary: Black-box SSP evaluation platform; finds off-policy distillation collapses robustness

method.training_loop: No training. Evaluate 121 LLMs on 46 tests / 9 services; score with rule/judge ensembles; aggregate; compare base vs R1/IDA-distilled models and probe hidden-state cosine similarity.
method.loss_formulation: L_{KL}(\theta)=E_{x\sim D}E_{y\sim p_\theta(\cdot|x)}[D_{KL}(p_T(\cdot|x,y)\|p_\theta(\cdot|x,y))] (on-policy, Eq.1) vs L_{off}(\theta)=E_{(x,y)\sim TeacherGen}[-\log p_\theta(y|x)] (Eq.2)
method.data_source: public safety/security/privacy benchmarks (46 tests, 221,882 samples); evaluated models are off-the-shelf
key_components: SSP three-layer taxonomy (Safety&Reliability, Security&Robustness, Privacy&Fairness)
46 tests across 9 services with unified [0,1] scoring
multi-judge ensemble (GPT-oss-120B, LLaMA Guard 1-4, moderation APIs)
stakeholder-profile weighting and Dirichlet ranking robustness
distillation-induced robustness collapse analysis (Appendix D + hidden-state cosine similarity)

2608.20554.novelty: First joint safety/security/privacy black-box study of 120+ LLMs revealing safety tax, privacy orthogonality, and the first robustness-focused characterization of off-policy (R1-style) distillation causing entropy collapse and adversarial brittleness, contrasted with on-policy-corrected (IDA) distillation.

on_policy_mechanism.evidence_quote: the on-policy KL correction [1] is omitted due to vocabulary mismatches between teacher and student, causing the student to overfit exact teacher trajectories

opd_classification.reasoning: The paper trains nothing and proposes no OPD method; it is an evaluation platform whose Appendix D analyzes the failure mode of omitting on-policy KL correction in strong-to-weak distillation, i.e. a failure-mode/theoretical analysis relevant to OPD.

benchmarks.name: Adversarial Robustness (Llama3.1-8B: base vs IDA-distilled; R1-distilled=2.6)
OOD Robustness (Llama3.1-8B: base vs IDA-distilled; R1-distilled=10.0)
Overall SSP score (Llama3.1-8B: base vs IDA-distilled; R1-distilled=50.9)

key_findings: R1-style off-policy distillation reduces adversarial robustness on Llama3.1-8B from 56.9 to 2.6 and OOD robustness from 79.4 to 10.0, while IDA distillation retains 38.7 / 89.4.
R1-distilled models have near-orthogonal last-layer representations vs. base (cos=0.094±0.161 Llama, 0.069±0.206 Qwen) whereas IDA retains 0.834±0.013 / 0.532±0.048 (Cohen's d=6.5, 3.1).
Safety tax: Over Refusal correlates negatively with Jailbreak Robustness (r=-0.39) and Safety Alignment (r=-0.22).
Privacy is near-orthogonal to other dimensions (mean |r|=0.13); GPT-5 loses 21.73 privacy points vs GPT-4o despite +3.84 overall.
Overall trustworthiness plateaus around ~4B params (Qwen3.5: 59.0 at 0.8B → 73.4 at 4B → ~76 at 27B).
Jailbreak Robustness is the most fragmented service (avg std 17.8, generalization gap 47.0 points).
Rankings are perspective-sensitive: mean pairwise Kendall's τ=0.455 across six stakeholder profiles; GPT-4o swings 13 rank positions.
2608.20554.ablations_summary: No training ablations; comparative analysis contrasts R1 (off-policy, no on-policy KL correction due to vocabulary mismatch) vs Cogito/IDA distillation on the same base models, and two judges (GPT-oss-120B vs Gemma3-27B) agree with Pearson r=0.985.
limitations: English-only tests
Black-box evaluation only; gradient-based attacks and mechanistic interpretability out of scope
Judge reliability on implicit/culturally specific harms; binary safe/unsafe framing
failure_modes: Off-policy distillation without on-policy KL correction (R1-style, vocabulary mismatch) causes entropy collapse and near-zero adversarial/OOD robustness
Safety alignment increases over-refusal (safety tax)
Privacy regresses across model generations in 5 of 7 families

theory.theoretical_claim: Off-policy CE on teacher-generated sequences drives H[p_θ(·|x)]→0 (entropy collapse), sharpening decision boundaries so small perturbations δx cause large output shifts; on-policy KL correction on student samples prevents this
theory.proof_sketch: Cross-entropy L_off is minimized when p_θ(y|x)→1 on exact teacher tokens, collapsing predictive entropy; without feedback on its own trajectories the student's support drifts from the teacher, yielding sharp, poorly calibrated boundaries (Appendix D).

2608.20554.relevance_to_opd: Provides empirical and informal theoretical evidence that omitting the on-policy KL correction (Agarwal et al. GKD) in strong-to-weak distillation catastrophically harms adversarial robustness, motivating on-policy/robustness-preserving distillation; not an OPD method itself.

2608.22788.title: TailSieve: Partial-Rollout-Guided Tail Routing for LLM Rollouts
2608.22788.summary: Partial-rollout-guided tail routing to cut long-tail rollout makespan in LLM RL

method.training_loop: Each rollout step: groups unfinished at partial-rollout cutoff → tail candidates for next step; regenerate them on low-concurrency tail replicas, fresh groups on bulk replicas; hierarchical controller adjusts isolation size q and replica split m; GRPO update
method.data_source: DeepScaleR math prompts and KodCode-Light-RL-10K coding prompts
key_components: offline makespan analysis (tail isolation with load balancing)
top-k tail isolation policy
partial rollout as training-free tail filter
hierarchical controller (inner completion-time balance, outer marginal-capacity balance)
route-specialized speculative decoding (MTP / DFlash)

2608.22788.novelty: Unlike predictor-based dispatch (StreamRL, Seer) it needs no length predictor, and unlike partial-rollout/tail-batching systems (APRIL, CoPRIS, RollPacker) it does not reuse trajectories or consolidate tails into separate rounds; it jointly controls isolated workload and replica split and proves top-k isolation is within 4% of the offline optimum.

on_policy_mechanism.evidence_quote: responsesremaininterleavedwithineveryupdatebatch,andallconsumedresponsesaresampledfromscratch

opd_classification.reasoning: Systems paper on rollout routing/scheduling for synchronous GRPO training; there is no teacher model and no distillation loss (KL disabled), OPD is only cited as a motivating use case, so C2 and C3 fail.

key_findings: TailSieve achieves up to 1.67× routing-only speedup over uniform group routing (Qwen3.5-35B-A3B on KodCode) and up to 2.59× with route-specialized MTP/DFlash.
Best-k tail isolation stays within 4% of the exact offline makespan optimum across 100 rollout groups, within 1% for 72% of them.

Partial-rollout filter captures 85%/93%/95% of ground-truth long-tail groups at cutoff ρ=5%/10%/25%; prompt identity explains 64.8% of response-length variance and tail-ranking AUC exceeds 0.95 across checkpoints.
In 30-step GRPO on Qwen3.5-2B, routing-only reduces generation time from 119.34s to 82.49s (1.45×) and with MTP to 46.61s (2.56×), with comparable reward and downstream accuracy.
Hierarchical controller converges to q=4 and m=2 from different initial allocations.
2608.22788.ablations_summary: Fixed-replica-allocation variant (outer loop disabled) gives 1.14–1.56× vs 1.11–1.67× for full TailSieve; route-specialized speculation beats symmetric speculation under matched budget; speedups shrink as concurrency N grows from 64 to 256.
limitations: Gains are strongest only when long-tail requests determine baseline makespan; weaken when tail workload is small, tail route overloaded, or isolation loses concurrency advantage.
Suffix decoding was not effective due to modest acceptance and ragged query lengths breaking CUDA-graph replay.
Allocation changes introduce short composition transitions; bias analysis assumes an idealized stationary policy and prompt-conditioned selector.
No official DFlash implementation for Qwen3.5-2B.
failure_modes: Weak-tail workloads where tail is not the bottleneck
Tail-dominated workloads that overload the tail replica
High-concurrency regimes where speedup diminishes (e.g., 1.122× at N=256)
Controller reverted to uniform routing after step 8 in Qwen3.5-2B RL run

theory.theoretical_claim: Optimal min-max rollout routing equalizes replica completion times (tail isolation with load balancing); marginal-capacity balance condition for replica split; routed batches are unbiased estimators of same-policy length distribution under stable allocation
theory.proof_sketch: Contradiction argument: shifting infinitesimal work from slower to faster replica strictly reduces max completion time; implicit differentiation of inner-loop equilibrium yields α* = γ_tail λ_bulk /(γ_tail λ_bulk + γ_bulk λ_tail); identical-distribution of consecutive pools plus prompt-conditioned selector gives E[P̂_B(A)] = P_π(A).

2608.22788.relevance_to_opd: Infrastructure paper: accelerates long-tail rollout generation for synchronous RL/OPD pipelines, explicitly citing OPD as a beneficiary, but contributes no distillation method or teacher signal.

FarSkip-Collective
feedback-driven SFT data curation
DPO with load-balancing disabled
IF-specialized GRPO+DAPO RL
Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation (MOPD) with domain router
Rollout Routing Replay (R3)
truncated importance sampling

no KL penalty, no entropy bonus

key_findings: IF-specialized RL alone raises IFEval from 77.1 to 84.1 but regresses AIME25 from 73.2 to 65.2 and GPQA from 62.7 to 60.9.
MOPD recovers most of the IF gain (IFEval 83.7) while keeping DPO-level math/code/MMLU, giving the best 11-benchmark ablation average of 75.7 vs 75.0 (DPO) and 74.0 (IF-RL).

Disabling load balancing during DPO reduces top-1 expert routing drift from 54% to 5% of tokens (top-6 Jaccard 0.42→0.94).

2609.00791.ablations_summary: Table 14: DPO 75.0 avg → IF-RL 74.0 (IFEval +7.0, math/GPQA regress) → MOPD 75.7 (IFEval 83.7, math preserved). Architecture: Gated MLA +0.47 avg over MLA; FarSkip maintains accuracy (50.38 vs 50.33). Feedback-driven SFT curation +1.5 avg.

failure_modes: IF-specialized RLVR alone causes catastrophic forgetting on math/reasoning (AIME25 −8 points).
MoE train/inference routing mismatch between SGLang and Megatron requires R3 replay and TIS to stabilize RL.
2609.00791.relevance_to_opd: Provides a large-scale, fully open case study of multi-teacher on-policy distillation (MOPD) used as a capability-integration stage in an MoE model: student on-policy rollouts scored by domain-routed frozen teachers (IF-RL expert and the DPO self-anchor) with token-level reverse KL, showing OPD can merge RL-specialist gains without forgetting; also documents MoE-specific stabilization (R3, TIS) for on-policy distillation.

2609.08368.title: Miles v0.1: Production-Level Post-Training
2609.08368.authors_first: RadixArk (core contributors: Tom Chen et al.)
2609.08368.summary: Full-stack production RL post-training system with OPD as one recipe

method.training_loop: loop: SGLang engines roll out trajectories (async) -> buffer -> Megatron/FSDP trainer computes GRPO/PPO loss (opt. teacher reverse-KL folded into advantage) -> weight sync to engines
method.loss_formulation: A_t \leftarrow A_t - \beta\,[\log\pi_{student}(x_t) - \log\pi_{teacher}(x_t)];\; \text{then standard policy-gradient (GRPO/PPO) update}
method.data_source: terminal-bench-2 coding tasks (case study); DAPO prompts (OPD/true-on-policy examples)
key_components: SGLang rollout engines with session affinity routing
fully asynchronous RL with staleness-bounded data buffer
Token-In-Token-Out (TITO) session server
Rollout Routing Replay (R3) for MoE
FP8/MXFP8/NVFP4 low-precision contracts
optimizer state streaming and actor offload
three weight-sync transports (NCCL broadcast, P2P RDMA, disk-delta)
LoRA RL
on-policy distillation as advantage penalty (one-sample or top-K reverse KL)
true-on-policy bitwise rollout-trainer alignment
Miles-Diffusion port

2609.08368.novelty: A system/engineering report: novel infrastructure (TITO sessions, async buffer, P2P weight transfer, precision contracts, true-on-policy alignment) rather than a new distillation objective; OPD is implemented following Lu (2025) and Li et al. (2026) as a shipped recipe.

on_policy_mechanism.evidence_quote: On-policy distillation (OPD) [40] trains a student model on its own trajectories while a stronger teacher model supplies the learning signal.

opd_classification.reasoning: System paper (Pattern 4): Miles implements existing OPD (per-token reverse-KL folded into GRPO/PPO advantages) as one of many supported recipes but proposes no new distillation algorithm or objective.

training_setup.compute_budget: 64×GB300 for GLM-5.2 RL case study (100 steps, median 263s/step); OPD run compute unspecified

key_findings: Fully async agentic GRPO on GLM-5.2 744B-A40B over 64 GB300 GPUs achieves a median step time of 263s over the first 30 steps with 96% prefix-cache hit rate.
P2P RDMA weight transfer cuts update time from 58.30s to 8.48s for GLM-5 744B-A40B (16 nodes/side) and 53.28s to 7.23s for Kimi K2 1T-A32B (−86.4%).
OPD alone (reward=0, reverse-KL penalty in advantage) shortens Qwen3.5-35B-A3B responses on DAPO from 14,070 to 6,132 tokens (−56%) with accuracy 84.0%→85.2%, within ~1.6-point standard error.
Optimizer state streaming cuts Qwen3-30B-A3B actor offload from 24s to 5.2s and reload from 8.9s to 1.3s.
True-on-policy alignment yields exactly zero rollout-trainer log-prob difference for Qwen3 0.6B/4B dense models at a throughput cost.
Train–inference KL in the GLM-5.2 run averages 0.0369 over 100 steps, corrected by TIS.
2609.08368.ablations_summary: No formal ablations; component-level measurements: P2P vs broadcast weight sync, optimizer streaming offload times, streaming reward path cutting LTX-2.3 rollout time 157.4s→87.6s, OPD-only run showing length reduction without reliable accuracy change.
limitations: MXFP8 and NVFP4 recipes remain Beta and tested on few models
P2P weight transfer covers only certain model families; slower than broadcast on single node
disk-delta limited to Megatron; incompatible with colocation, LoRA, PD disaggregation
session server does not support image/video inputs (no VLMs through TITO)
true-on-policy alignment covers only dense Qwen3 0.6B/4B and only sampled-token log-probs
GLM-5.2 results from a single run; reward rise cannot be separated from run-to-run variation
top-K OPD variant available with served teacher only; teacher must share student tokenizer
failure_modes: OPD 1.2-point accuracy change lies within evaluation standard error — no demonstrated accuracy improvement
loose TITO message matchers can silently merge divergent tool-call histories
R3 routing tensors (~60MB per 32K-token trajectory) impose large memory overhead and have limited effect under async RL
P2P transfer up to ~70% slower than broadcast on single-node deployments
2609.08368.relevance_to_opd: Provides production infrastructure for running OPD at frontier scale (served/in-process teachers, top-K reverse-KL estimates, multi-teacher routing, token-exact trajectories) but contributes no new OPD algorithm; useful as an implementation reference and for its OPD-shortens-responses observation.

2609.11929.title: SenseNova-U1.5: Towards Native Unified Visual Intelligence
2609.11929.summary: 8B native unified vision model; multi-expert on-policy velocity distillation

method.training_loop: Stages1-3 pretrain/SFT; Stage4 train 4 RL experts (GRPO); Stage5 student samples own ODE trajectory, routed frozen expert gives velocity target, MSE
method.loss_formulation: L_{OPD} = E[ \| v_\theta(sg(\hat{x}_{\theta,t}), t, c) - v_m(sg(\hat{x}_{\theta,t}), t, c) \|_2^2 ]
method.data_source: Internal + public text-to-image, editing, interleaved corpora; RL prompts from HPSv3++, Pick-a-Pic, Flow-GRPO, Linear-DPO; 25,600 samples per domain for OPD
key_components: encoder-free VAE-free NEO-unify MoT backbone
spatially coupled PixelShuffle+3x3 conv decoder
resolution-aware noise conditioning up to 4K
four task-specific RL experts (aesthetic, OCR, editing, infographic)
hard-routed multi-expert on-policy velocity-field distillation
Beta-scheduled query-timestep curriculum from Beta(2,5) to Beta(5,2)
CFG-aware velocity target with stop-gradient

2609.11929.novelty: Replaces joint reward optimization with specialize-then-unify: four independently RL-trained experts are consolidated into one native pixel-space unified model via hard-routed on-policy velocity distillation along student-generated denoising trajectories, plus a spatially coupled decoder replacing independent patch MLP.

on_policy_mechanism.evidence_quote: Bydistillingalongthestudentmodel’sowngenerationtrajectories,thisprocesstransfersexpertcapabilitiesintoasingleunifiedpolicywhilepreservingtheircomplementarystrengths.

opd_classification.reasoning: Output modality is images (pixel-space flow matching) and the distillation loss is MSE on velocity fields, not a token-level distributional divergence; also a system/model-release paper.

stabilization_tricks: freezing understanding branch, final three generation layers, output head
single queried timestep per trajectory with early termination

key_findings: SenseNova-U1.5 reaches 0.92 on GenEval, best among open-source models, vs 0.91 for SenseNova-U1.
ImgEdit overall improves from 3.90 (U1) to 4.59, leading all listed models including closed-source.
With prompt enhancement, Qwen-Image-Bench-EN overall rises to 60.22 (52.82 without), best open-source.
BizGenEval average jumps from 39.7/61.7 (U1) to 72.2/88.4 with PE.
VBVR-Pro-Bench overall 68.2 surpasses Nano-Banana-Pro (56.4) and GPT-Image-2 (50.7).
Understanding benchmarks largely preserved (MMLU-Pro 86.67, IFEval 93.35) despite added generation training.
OPD stage: 800 optimizer steps, batch 128, 25,600 samples per domain, four frozen experts hard-routed.
2609.11929.ablations_summary: No ablation isolating the on-policy distillation stage or individual experts is reported; comparisons are only against the prior SenseNova-U1 model and external baselines, with CoT and prompt-enhancement variants shown.
limitations: Gap to strongest proprietary systems remains on IGenBench and infographic generation
Translation-related and reasoning-intensive edits remain challenging on WeEdit
Spatial editing benefits less consistently from CoT on RISEBench
Uni-MMMU-GaU performance drops relative to SenseNova-U1-SFT (29.6 vs 35.0)
failure_modes: Knowledge-intensive BizGenEval without PE scores only 4.8/23.4
Sliding puzzle task on Uni-MMMU-GaU scores 0.0
2609.11929.relevance_to_opd: Applies the OPD idea (student-generated trajectories, frozen experts supervising at student states) to pixel-space image generation via multi-expert velocity-field regression; useful as an example of OPD-style capability consolidation in non-text generative models, but the output modality is images and the loss is MSE, so it falls outside LLM OPD scope.

2609.23377.title: One to More, More to One: Category-Aware Iterative Expert Training for Software Engineering Agents
2609.23377.summary: Category-routed same-origin SWE experts via RRE, merged by multi-teacher OPD

method.training_loop: Label tasks A/B/C → per-category Agentic-miniRL + Repair SFT (RRE loop) → freeze 3 experts → student (base) rolls out; label-routed teacher log-ratio + ReLU-gated extrapolation advantage → PG update
method.loss_formulation: L_{MOPD}(\theta) = -\frac{1}{B_{valid}}\sum_i \frac{1}{|S_i|}\sum_{s\in S_i}\sum_{t\in s} \mathrm{clip}(A_t^{MOPD},-5,5)\log\pi_\theta(y_t|h_t),\; A_t^{MOPD}=\sum_k m_k(x)[-d_{t,k}+(\lambda_k-1)\max(e_{t,k},0)],\; d_{t,k}=q_t-\log\pi_{T_k}(y_t|h_t),\; e_{t,k}=\log\pi_{T_k}(y_t|h_t)-\log\pi_{ref}(y_t|h_t)
method.data_source: ~32K synthetic executable SWE tasks from merged PRs/issues (3,048 selected with base pass rate 0–0.5) + 3,675 SWE-rebench V2 tasks (6,723 total); MOPD uses 2,769 category-labeled records upsampled to 4,956
key_components: SWE Labeler (hierarchical evidence-grounded taxonomy, Domain L1 → A/B/C routing)
Agentic-miniRL (RLOO, K1-in-reward, MiniRL behavior correction, turn-aware reduction)
Refresh–Repair–Expand (RRE) self-improving expert loop with Repair SFT on own verified trajectories
Label-routed multi-teacher on-policy distillation (MOPD)
ReLU-gated reward extrapolation (ExOPD variant, λ=1.25)
Reward-integrity / anti-hacking protocol

2609.23377.novelty: Applies multi-teacher OPD within a single domain (SWE) using observable task-category labels for routing; teachers are same-origin RL experts (no external trajectory teacher); adds ReLU gate to ExOPD extrapolation so only positive teacher–reference log-prob gaps contribute; introduces category see-saw diagnostics (G_sim, SSG) and RRE iterative expert development.

on_policy_mechanism.evidence_quote: The student π_θ generates the complete trajectory, so teachers are queried only on prefixes the student actually visits, following the on-policy distillation setting of MOPD [Ma et al., 2026].

opd_classification.reasoning: Student generates its own long-horizon SWE trajectories, frozen expert teachers supply per-token log-prob (reverse-KL estimator) supervision on those tokens, and the loss is a pure distillation advantage (no environment reward); core contribution is applying/adapting MOPD+ExOPD to the SWE agent domain with label routing and a ReLU-gated extrapolation term.

training_setup.compute_budget: MOPD: 32 devices student optimization + 32 rollout + 16 per teacher (×3) + 16 reference (128 devices); RL: 32 train + 32 inference devices; duration unspecified
training_setup.rl_algorithm: RLOO-based Agentic-miniRL for experts; pure-KD vanilla policy gradient with teacher log-ratio advantage for MOPD
stabilization_tricks: truncated importance sampling [0,5] and sign-aware proximal mask (RL)
asynchrony bound of one policy update

train: ~32K synthetic executable SWE tasks (RepoLaunch envs, 3,048 selected)

key_findings: Final MOPD policy reaches 58.04% on Pro-618 (+5.39 pp over base 52.64%) and 59.00% on SWE-bench Multilingual (+2.78 pp).
MOPD beats Pooled RL (55.50%) by 2.54 pp and Balanced RL (55.34%) by 2.70 pp on Pro-618 Full, with positive lifts in all three categories (min lift 1.53 / 2.04 pp).
MOPD recovers 80.8% / 111.1% / 84.8% of expert A/B/C gains in a single model; on B the student exceeds its expert by 0.50 pp.
RRE develops experts from +1.81/+0.66/+0.68 pp (initial RL) to +7.84/+4.48/+5.61 pp on Pro-A/B/C; first Repair SFT gives the largest adjacent-stage gain (+3.77/+1.50/+2.89 pp).
During initial expert RL, 839 of 2,769 training records (30.3%) regress despite mean gains; Repair SFT recovers 69.8%/73.0%/61.3% of repaired regressed records to base or above.
During MOPD, training rollout score rises from 45.51% to 56.91% while student–teacher KL falls 43.0%.
Balanced RL matches Pooled RL overall with 1,548 vs 6,723 instances but does not eliminate the category see-saw (avg SSG 1.18 vs 1.05).
2609.23377.ablations_summary: No component ablations; stage-wise RRE results act as a progression study (initial RL → Repair SFT → expanded RL → second SFT each add gains). Authors note ReLU gating was needed because ungated extrapolation had comparable positive and negative components that cancelled, leaving net extrapolation well below the imitation term. Authors explicitly acknowledge they do not isolate contributions of each optimization component, replay choice, or routing granularity.
limitations: Hard routing assigns each task to a single category though SWE tasks can span categories
Training multiple experts and running K+1 teacher/reference forwards adds substantial compute; best K may vary with data, base model, budget
Same-origin teachers may be too similar to add signal or too distant after heavy specialization
Benchmark pass rates do not fully measure patch quality; test-driven rewards invite evaluator hacking and brittle specs
Controls do not eliminate pretraining memorization or all weak-verifier failures
Pro-618 results cannot generalize to unexecuted full SWE-bench Pro
Component contributions not isolated; single-run trajectories include evaluation variability
failure_modes: Expert-gain recovery uneven: category A retains only 80.8% of its expert's gain (1.51 pp below expert)
On SWE-bench Multilingual, category C shows no gain over base and MOPD scores 2.47/6.17 pp lower than Pooled/Balanced RL on unassigned instances
Initial category-specific RL alone yields only modest target-category gains below the Pooled RL endpoint
Ungated extrapolation term nearly cancels across tokens (positive and negative components comparable)
2609.23377.relevance_to_opd: Direct application of multi-teacher on-policy distillation (MOPD + ExOPD reward extrapolation) to long-horizon agentic SWE, with teachers being same-origin RL experts routed by task labels and a ReLU gate on the extrapolation term; demonstrates OPD consolidating specialist experts into one deployable agent with 80–111% gain recovery.

2609.24432.title: 1% of Tokens Can Be Enough: On Gradient Estimation in On-Policy Distillation
2609.24432.summary: IER: gradient-reliability score for sparse token selection in OPD

method.training_loop: Student samples rollouts; teacher+student top-K logits per prefix; compute IER (Fisher-SNR of one-sample RKL gradient); rank/combine with usefulness; apply sampled reverse-KL on top-α% tokens
method.loss_formulation: L = E_{s~π_θ}[ Σ_{j∈S} (log π_θ(a_j|s) - log π_T(a_j|s)) ], S = top-α% tokens in rollout batch ranked by IER = ‖g‖²_{F+} / E_p[‖ĝ_{b*}-g‖²_{F+}] = Var_p[ρ] / (E_p[(ρ-b*)²L]-Var_p[ρ]), combined via s_OR=1-(1-u)(1-r) or s_AND=u·r
method.data_source: DAPO-Math-17k prompts (math); RaR-Medicine prompts (medical); student-generated rollouts
key_components: information-efficiency ratio (IER) from Fisher-geometry signal/noise decomposition
optimal variance-minimizing scalar baseline b*
top-K candidate-set approximation of IER (K=16)
soft-OR / soft-AND combination with usefulness scores (Prefix, Entropy, TIP, TA-OPD, CA-SoftOR)
batch-level token budget (0.1%–80%) with sampled reverse-KL objective

2609.24432.novelty: Prior sparse-OPD selectors (TIP, TA-OPD, Prefix, entropy) score token usefulness; this paper introduces an orthogonal axis—reliability of the one-sample reverse-KL gradient estimate—derived in Fisher information geometry with an optimal control-variate baseline, and shows 0.1%–1% token budgets can match full OPD.

on_policy_mechanism.evidence_quote: On-policydistillation(OPD)obtainsteachersupervisionatprefixesgeneratedbythestudent.

opd_classification.reasoning: Core contribution is a token-selection/weighting criterion (IER) for sparse OPD that retains the sampled reverse-KL objective, backed by a theoretical signal-to-noise analysis.

training_setup.compute_budget: 8 GPUs (type unspecified); 50 rollout rounds math, 100 rollout rounds medical
stabilization_tricks: missing-logit fill value -12 on candidate set
at least one token retained per response
optimal scalar baseline b* in IER

key_findings: IER scores are extremely heavy-tailed: fewer than 0.1% of tokens have IER>1, i.e., estimated noise exceeds signal for most tokens.
IER alone at 0.1% budget approaches full OPD on AIME26 (58.9 vs 59.9) and HMMT26 (34.1 vs 34.7) for the Nemotron pair and exceeds full OPD on 3/4 benchmarks for Qwen3-4B→Qwen3-1.7B.
TIP+IER-AND at 0.1% budget reaches 19.4/16.3/11.7/14.4 on AIME25/26, HMMT25/26 for Qwen3-1.7B vs full OPD 14.4/12.5/8.7/13.4.
On HealthBench, IER at 0.1% (≈1 token per trajectory) scores 45.25 vs full OPD 45.77, while Prefix at 0.1% gives 38.30 (no improvement over student 38.23); Prefix+IER-OR lifts it to 44.98/19.49.
Higher token budgets (up to 80%) do not monotonically improve performance; 1%–5% with usefulness+IER matches or beats full OPD in several settings.
IER adds only 2.2–2.5% step time and ≤2.17 GiB (0.92%) peak memory vs full OPD.
In thinking-on mode, TIP alone can underperform full OPD and even the student, whereas TIP+IER-AND generally improves.
2609.24432.ablations_summary: IER standalone is competitive with usefulness selectors; combining via IER-OR helps most for weak selectors (Prefix) and tiny budgets (0.1%/1%), IER-AND helps most with TIP/TA-OPD; combinations with Entropy are inconsistent in math; sensitivity over budgets 0.1%–80% shows non-monotonic gains; Sampled RKL min/max baselines strong on Nemotron pair but degrade to near-random on Qwen3 pair.
limitations: Gains vary across selectors and settings; no selector is universally best.
Both usefulness scores and candidate-set IER are approximations with no selection guarantee.
High IER does not imply usefulness, gradient magnitude, or task alignment.
Sparse supervision does not yield proportional compute savings since full trajectories are still generated and scored.
Adaptive per-prefix sampling budget K left as future work.
failure_modes: IER-OR/IER-AND combined with Entropy can reduce math performance (e.g., Entropy+IER-OR 1% AIME25 49.7 vs Entropy 53.6 on Nemotron pair).
Higher token budgets can degrade performance when noisy-gradient tokens are included.
Thinking-on mode: TIP alone can fall below the student baseline.

theory.theoretical_claim: Theorem 1: under Fisher (F+) geometry, squared signal of one-sample reverse-KL gradient equals Var_p[ρ], noise equals E_p[(ρ-b)²L(a)]-Var_p[ρ], optimal baseline b*=E_p[ρL]/E_p[L]; Corollary 1: IER^-1 is the relative MSE of the K=1 estimator and relative MSE with K samples is 1/(K·IER)
theory.proof_sketch: Show g = p⊙v_s = F v_s with v_s the centered log-ratio, so ‖g‖²_{F+}=Var_p[ρ]; ‖φ_a‖²_{F+}=(1-p_a)/p_a=L(a); combine with unbiasedness for noise; minimize quadratic in b.

2609.24432.relevance_to_opd: Directly extends sparse on-policy distillation by adding a gradient-estimation-reliability axis (IER) to token selection, showing full OPD can be matched with 0.1%–1% of supervised tokens under the standard sampled reverse-KL objective.

2609.26375.title: KwaiMind Technical Report
2609.26375.summary: E-commerce image editing system with agent data engine, RLHF, and DiffusionOPD

method.training_loop: CT on 1.8M pairs → SFT on 234.9K pairs → mixed offline/online Diffusion-DPO → DiffusionNFT online RL with task rewards (separate teachers) → DiffusionOPD consolidation on student trajectories
method.loss_formulation: L_{OPD} = \mathbb{E}_{k\sim p(k)}\mathbb{E}_{x_{0:N}\sim p_{S_k,\theta}}\left[\sum_{j=0}^{N-1} \frac{\|\mu_{S_k}(x_{t_j};\theta)-\mu_{T_k}(x_{t_j})\|_2^2}{2\bar\sigma_j^2}\right]
method.data_source: Agent-curated ~1.8M editing pairs from ScaleEdit-12M, X2Edit, AnyEdit, and proprietary Kwai data; platform CTR logs for reward model
key_components: agent-based data engine (Filter/Generation/Caption/Coordinator agents)
MMDiT editor based on Qwen-Image-Edit-2511
mixed offline+online Diffusion-DPO
DiffusionNFT online RL with VLM judge + CTR/OCR/consistency rewards
DiffusionOPD multi-teacher on-policy consolidation
Ecom-Bench 11-task benchmark

2609.26375.novelty: Domain-specific e-commerce editing pipeline: multi-agent data curation, three specialized reward models (CTR, coarse-to-fine text, fine-grained consistency), separate RL teachers consolidated via existing DiffusionOPD, plus a commercial benchmark with CTR ranking; no new distillation objective is proposed.

on_policy_mechanism.evidence_quote: we distill the teachers into a single student along trajectories generated by the student itself

opd_classification.reasoning: Output modality is images (diffusion image editor), out of scope; and the paper is a system report applying the existing DiffusionOPD method rather than proposing a new distillation algorithm.

stabilization_tricks: offline DPO warm-up with λ_on annealed 0→0.5
gated SSIM regularizer against text reward hacking

key_findings: KwaiMind achieves best open-source scores: 4.15 ImgEdit, 6.29 GEdit, 3.75/3.73 REDEdit EN/CN, 3.67 Ecom-Bench, vs base Qwen-Edit-2511 at 3.83/5.97/3.43/3.43/3.18.
CTR reward optimization raises the fraction of generated images with predicted CTR above the original from 12.16% to 37.41%.
Online A/B test with CTR-based image selection yields ~2.44% relative CTR increase.
Vision-only CTR reward model reaches 57.1 pairwise accuracy on CreativeRanking vs 56.2 for CAIG and 50.2 for GPT-4o; ~70% on held-out internal pairs.
Specialized RL teachers are consolidated into one editor via DiffusionOPD to avoid cross-task interference and catastrophic forgetting.
2609.26375.ablations_summary: CTR reward model ablations: bucket-then-rank training is the main source of ranking ability; SigLIP2-giant vs base gains only ~0.2 points; soft gap-aware weighting beats hard filtering of near-tie pairs; overly fine buckets add label noise. No ablation of the DiffusionOPD consolidation stage is reported.
limitations: Closed-source systems (GPT-Image-2, NanoBanana-2) remain stronger on visual quality
Weaker on Outpaint and Product Extract than some baselines
Robustness on compositional and multi-reference edits needs improvement
CTR ranking score does not represent measured CTR
failure_modes: Viewpoint changes and fine-grained appearance edits remain difficult
Outpaint scores below Flux.2-dev; Product Extract below Joy-Image-Edit
2609.26375.relevance_to_opd: Applies DiffusionOPD (per-step reverse-KL reduced to Gaussian mean-matching on student-generated denoising trajectories) to consolidate multiple RL-trained diffusion teachers into one student; an application of on-policy distillation in the image-generation domain rather than an LLM OPD contribution.

2609.27421.title: Counterfactual Constraint-Conditioned On-Policy Distillation for Multi-Constraint Instruction Following
2609.27421.summary: Leave-one-out counterfactual teacher scoring adds per-constraint token shaping to OPD

method.training_loop: for batch: student samples y~π_θ(·|q,C); frozen teacher forced-scores y under full C and each C\{c_i}; δ_i=ℓ(C)-ℓ(C\{c_i}); r_t=-KL̂(t)+λ·clip(Σδ_i,-c,c); ratio-clipped PPO update
method.loss_formulation: r_t = -\hat{KL}(t) + \lambda\,\mathrm{clip}\Big(\sum_{i=1}^{|C|}[\ell(C;t)-\ell(C\setminus\{c_i\};t)],-c,+c\Big),\quad \hat{KL}(t)=\log\pi_\theta(y_t|h_t)-\log P_T(y_t|h_t);\ \ell(A;t)=\log P_T(y_t|q,A,y_{<t});\ optimized\ via\ ratio\text{-}clipped\ PPO
method.data_source: HIR-16K multi-constraint instruction-following corpus (16,968 samples, 5–17 constraints each); student rollouts generated online
key_components: sampled-token reverse-KL OPD reward (PPO backbone)
leave-one-out counterfactual teacher forced-scoring (|C|+1 teacher passes per rollout)
per-constraint log-likelihood shifts δ_i(t) summed over constraints
symmetric hard clip (c=5.0) of aggregate shift
additive shaping term with λ=2.0 on top of vanilla OPD reward
frozen GRPO-IR-tuned teacher, no external verifier during distillation
constraint subsampling ratio ρ for compute savings

2609.27421.novelty: Inverts the supervision direction of rubric-RL/OPD: instead of enriching the teacher or adding external verifier rewards, it ablates each constraint from the frozen teacher's prompt and uses the resulting per-token leave-one-out log-likelihood differentials as a dense per-constraint token-level shaping signal added to vanilla sampled-token OPD, reducing exactly to vanilla OPD when the aggregate shift is zero; Möbius analysis shows LOO cardinality-weights higher-order constraint interactions unlike a single full-vs-empty contrast (LA) or single-constraint anchors (NAO).

on_policy_mechanism.evidence_quote: trains a student to match a teacher distribution on the student’s own rollouts

opd_classification.reasoning: Proposes a new fixed OPD objective: student rollouts scored by a frozen white-box teacher with a sampled-token reverse-KL reward plus a teacher-derived counterfactual per-constraint token-level shaping term, optimized with PPO.

training_setup.compute_budget: 32 GPUs (96GB each) in a Ray cluster; CC-OPD trained 1,500 verl-steps (=12,000 gradient steps); wall-clock unspecified
stabilization_tricks: symmetric hard clip of aggregate counterfactual shift (c=5.0)
bounded shaping contribution λc per token
no critic/GAE, single PPO epoch per mini-batch

key_findings: CC-OPD attains the highest 7-benchmark average among all student-training methods: 51.4% on Qwen2.5 (+2.5pp over strongest ExOPD, +3.8pp over vanilla OPD 47.6) and 64.3% on Qwen3 (+1.5pp over Teacher-TopK RKL).
A 1.5B CC-OPD student surpasses its own 7B GRPO-IR teacher on MulDimIF by +2.8pp overall (72.9 vs 70.1) and +6.3pp on the hardest Level-4 split (59.4 vs 53.1).
On the same-size Qwen3-4B pair the student exceeds its teacher on five of seven benchmarks (e.g., IFBench 37.6 vs 32.5).

CC-OPD matches vanilla OPD's smoothed MulDimIF peak in 15.2× fewer gradient steps (16.6× on Level-4), using ≈30% of OPD's total FLOPs on Qwen2.5 and ≈53% on Qwen3 despite 4.63× per-step teacher overhead.
Leave-one-out (LOO) counterfactual beats Leave-All (50.5), Random-Subset (50.5), and No-context-Anchor-Only (48.7) variants on average (51.4), with NAO −6.5pp on MulDimIF and −14.1pp on Level-4.
Self-CC-OPD (teacher = frozen student init) beats DR-CFG by +0.9pp on Qwen3-4B (61.9 vs 61.0) but only +0.2pp on Qwen2.5-1.5B (37.7 vs 37.5).
Sum aggregation outperforms top-k=2 and top-k=1 on MulDimIF overall (72.9 vs 71.7/71.0 on Qwen2.5; 76.2 vs 73.7/74.4 on Qwen3).
All 14 (λ,c) grid cells improve over vanilla OPD; λ=2, c=5 is the joint optimum with unimodal λ curve and IFBench dropping 2.0pp at λ=4.
Constraint subsampling ρ=0.10 still gives +1.8 to +4.4pp over OPD; IFBench improves monotonically from 25.6 (ρ=0.10) to 28.2 (ρ=1.00).
Empirically the teacher's constraint response is non-additive: relative L1 residual between LOO and LA is 0.918 and sign disagreement is 31.9% of tokens on 15,450 HIR-16K samples.
2609.27421.ablations_summary: LOO counterfactual structure is the key: it beats LA (+0.9pp avg), RSS (+0.9pp), and NAO (+2.7pp; −14.1pp on MulDimIF L4). Sum aggregation beats top-k=1/2. λ=2, c=5 is a joint optimum with benign neighborhood; every grid cell still beats vanilla OPD. Subsampling ρ<1 retains most gains on aggregate metrics but dense ρ=1.0 matters on constraint-stressed IFBench and MulDimIF L4. Self-distillation variant works but gains are teacher-scale dependent.
limitations: Trained only on HIR-16K and two Qwen-family pairs; generalization to other corpora, non-Qwen families, multi-turn or system-prompt settings untested
Requires a white-box teacher with per-token log-probability access under multiple counterfactual prompts; generation-API-only teachers out of scope
Evaluated only with the sampled-token reverse-KL OPD objective; other OPD objectives untested
Counterfactual prompt construction assumes constraints can be cleanly excised by byte-aligned span deletion; structured/templated constraint formats may need different construction
Each sample needs |C|+1 teacher forward passes, increasing per-step compute, memory, and latency vs single-pass OPD
Self-distillation comparison across only two settings is insufficient to establish how LOO signal usefulness scales with teacher size
failure_modes: NAO (single-constraint anchor) variant substantially underperforms (−6.5pp MulDimIF, −14.1pp L4), discarding inter-constraint interactions
Over-strong shaping (λ=4) degrades IFBench by 2.0pp and MulDimIF vs λ=2
Tight clip / weak shaping corner (λ=0.5,c=1) under-uses the counterfactual signal
Self-CC-OPD on Qwen2.5-1.5B gives only marginal gain over DR-CFG and loses on four of seven benchmarks
Mean aggregation changes relative scale across samples with varying |C| and was not tuned; ρ=0.50 slight non-monotone regression on MulDimIF overall

compute_efficiency.teacher_inference_cost: (|C|+1) forced-scoring passes per rollout (~8× teacher passes; 4.63× per-step overhead on Qwen2.5 pair)
compute_efficiency.speedup_vs_baseline: 15.2× fewer gradient steps to match OPD peak; ≈3.3× fewer total FLOPs at iso-accuracy on Qwen2.5 (≈30%), ≈1.9× on Qwen3 (≈53%)
compute_efficiency.memory_footprint: unspecified (teacher frozen, student only updated; extra teacher passes noted to increase memory)

theory.theoretical_claim: Möbius decomposition: LOO sum weights order-k constraint interaction coefficients by k while Leave-All weights them uniformly and NAO truncates to order 1; exponential-tilt / product-of-experts interpretation of the implicit target q*(v|h_t) ∝ P_T(v|h_t) exp(λΔ_c(v,t))
theory.proof_sketch: Treat teacher log-prob f_t(S) of realized token as set function on Boolean lattice of constraint subsets; Möbius inversion gives f(S)=Σ_{T⊆S} m(T); then δ_LA=Σ_{T≠∅} m(T), δ_LOO,i=Σ_{T∋c_i} m(T), so Σ_i δ_LOO,i=Σ|T|m(T); residual Σ(|T|−1)m(T) is nonzero iff higher-order interactions exist. Maximizing λE_q[Δ_c]−KL(q‖P_T) yields the unique exponential-tilt solution.

2609.27421.relevance_to_opd: Directly extends sampled-token reverse-KL OPD (GKD/MiniLLM/Thinking-Machines-style PPO reward) with a teacher-derived counterfactual token-level shaping term for multi-constraint instruction following; demonstrates student-surpasses-teacher OPD, compares against ExOPD, EOPD, Teacher-TopK RKL/SRKL (DistiLLM), and rubric-RL, and provides a self-distillation variant.

2609.29518.title: CataOPD: Catalytic On-Policy Distillation for Large Language Model Reasoning
2609.29518.summary: Black-box teacher as catalyst: hints elicit verified student trajectories, then weighted NLL internalization

method.training_loop: For each q: sample G rollouts (GRPO); if all-failed, self-rescue m more samples; if still failed, up to H teacher-hint rounds elicit a verified student trajectory; weighted NLL on q-only
method.loss_formulation: L = L_clip(θ) + c_KL R_ref(θ) + λ E_{D_int}[ -Σ_t m_t w̃_t log π_θ(y*_t|q,y*_<t) / Σ_t m_t ],  w_t = 1+β clip(sg[log π_θ(y*_t|[q;c],y*_<t) − log π_θ(y*_t|q,y*_<t)],0,b_max)
method.data_source: 1,280 questions each from MetaMathQA, GSM-Plus, Big-Math, Omni-MATH, NuminaMath-CoT, MATH, DeepMath-103K, OpenMathReasoning (10,240 total)
key_components: Self-Rescue Routing (extra on-policy sampling on all-failed groups)
Catalytic-Guided Self-Resolution (GPT-5.4-mini method-level hints, answer withheld, up to H rounds)
Barrier-Weighted Internalization (token weights from guided-to-unaided log-prob gaps)
GRPO dual-clip objective with KL to reference policy

2609.29518.novelty: Unlike OPD/OPSD that distill teacher (or privileged-self) token distributions, CataOPD never uses teacher trajectories or logits as targets: the black-box teacher only provides hints to make a correct student trajectory reachable, and the student's own guided-vs-unaided log-prob gap selects which tokens to upweight during catalyst-free internalization; all-failed groups are routed first to extra self-sampling before any teacher call.

on_policy_mechanism.evidence_quote: The teacher is used only as a training-time catalyst for guided recovery, not as a trajectory target.

opd_classification.reasoning: Student rollouts are on-policy (C1) but the API teacher supplies only text hints, not logit/distributional supervision (fails C2), and the internalization loss is barrier-weighted NLL on student trajectories plus GRPO with a KL anchor to π_ref (fails C3); it is closest to a black-box-teacher, RL-augmented OPD variant.

training_setup.compute_budget: 8×H100 80GB, single server; 80 training steps, 1 epoch over 10,240 questions
stabilization_tricks: mean-normalized token weights to avoid loss-scale drift

key_findings: CataOPD achieves the best 8-benchmark average on all three backbones (67.87 / 72.66 / 71.48 for Qwen2.5-3B / 7B / Qwen3-1.7B), beating GRPO (65.92 / 71.88 / 69.34) and exceeding the GPT-5.4-mini teacher's 67.29.
OOD macro-average improves over the best baseline by +2.93 / +1.17 / +1.95 points on Qwen2.5-3B / 7B / Qwen3-1.7B under catalyst-free inference.

Hard-problem gains exceed overall gains: Blind +18.81/+24.70 and Hard +24.65/+22.79 vs Overall +3.78/+4.92 on Qwen2.5-3B/7B; Pass@8 retention is 99.8%/99.9% with 49.5%/56.7% of base-unsolved questions newly solved.
Self-Rescue recovers 16.5–19.0% of all-failed groups without teacher calls; total recovery is 23.9% / 36.0% / 36.4% for Qwen3-1.7B / Qwen2.5-3B / 7B.
Self-Rescue reduces teacher cost: 10.1 calls and 16.2K input tokens per verified target vs 17.6 calls and 33.1K tokens without it (Qwen2.5-3B).
Barrier mass is highly concentrated: top 10% of tokens carry 85.0% of barrier mass, top 20% carry 96.2%.
2609.29518.ablations_summary: On Qwen2.5-3B, removing Self-Rescue Routing causes the largest drop on every benchmark (e.g., MetaMath 88.28→62.50, GSM+ 87.50→37.50); removing Barrier weighting ranks second (MetaMath →81.25, OmniMath →30.47); removing catalytic Guidance yields smaller but consistent losses (MetaMath →87.50, OmniMath →32.81).
limitations: Requires a rule-based verifier, so limited to tasks with reliable answer checking (math, code).
Catalytic guidance depends on the training-time teacher; prompt constraints cannot fully eliminate answer leakage, and guidance quality varies across teachers/problems.
Self-rescue and catalytic sampling add training-time rollout cost, especially on hard queries; efficiency on larger models and longer tasks unevaluated.
failure_modes: Questions with no verified candidate within H catalytic rounds are excluded from internalization (64–76% of all-failed groups remain unrecovered).
Without self-rescue routing, performance collapses well below GRPO (e.g., GSM+ 37.50 vs 86.72).
Self-distillation baselines (OPSD, OPCD, ROPD) degrade Qwen3-1.7B on DeepMath/OpenMath below base.

theory.theoretical_claim: Self-rescue miss probability decays as (1−p)^m ≤ exp(−mp); H-round guided retry succeeds w.p. 1−∏(1−p_ℓ)>0 if any round has p_ℓ>0; barrier weighting gives above-mean-barrier tokens larger first-order update coefficients than uniform NLL
theory.proof_sketch: Prop.1: i.i.d. Bernoulli draws yield geometric first-success time; Prop.2: chain rule over conditional round success probabilities; Prop.3: normalized weights w̃_t=(1+βb_t)/(1+β b̄) >1 iff b_t>b̄, first-order Taylor expansion of one gradient step.

2609.29518.relevance_to_opd: Self-labelled OPD but a boundary case: black-box API teacher provides only text hints to expand student reachability; supervision is verifier + barrier-weighted NLL on student's own verified trajectories, with no teacher-logit KL. Relevant to §5.2 black-box OPD, §4.3 RL-augmented OPD, and token-weighting (§6.1) discussions, and as a comparison point vs OPSD/SDPO/OPCD/ROPD/RLCSD.
